Published posthumously in 1571 by Sigismund Feyerabend, it outlines the "natural light" of reason and the spiritual mysteries of the universe.</summary>

# To the Most Illustrious, High-
### Born Prince and Lord, Lord Augustus, Duke of Saxony, Arch-Marshal of the Holy Roman Empire and Elector, Landgrave in Thuringia, and Margrave of Meissen, etc., my most gracious Lord.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter 'D' featuring intricate foliate and scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>
Most Illustrious, High-born Elector, most gracious Lord: After Almighty God willed to be known through the creation of the entire firmament, the elements, and all creatures, He made Man and placed him in Paradise, so that he should diligently explore and consider all these things, and thereby recognize, praise, and honor his Creator, so that He might ultimately make him a partaker of His Divine glory, nature, and essence. For this reason, Man is God’s most beloved creature, even above the angels. For He created Man in His own image, but not the angels. Furthermore, when Lucifer and his company fell away from God out of pride, He did not receive the apostate spirits back into grace, but cast them from Heaven into eternal damnation. But when Man—for whose sake He created everything—was led into apostasy by the cunning serpent, whereby he fell into damnation, God had such mercy that He gave His only Son into death for him. Who can sufficiently contemplate or express this love? Since this is so, Man should rightly be recognized as the noblest creature and be held in high honor by everyone; not only because he is a <term>Microcosmus</term> <note>original: "Microcosmus"; a "little world" or miniature universe, reflecting the structure of the entire cosmos within the human body</note>

# Preface.

...must be and is a <term>miracle of the world</term> <note>original: "miraculum Mundi"</note>; but much more so because God created him in His own image, which <term>Moses</term>, out of high emotion, repeats in <term>Genesis</term> <note>original: "Genesi"</note> and says: "In the image of God created He him." For these reasons, the dear, highly-enlightened, experienced, and Christian <term>philosopher</term> <note>original: "Philosophus"</note> <term>Theophrastus Paracelsus</term> wrote this <term>work</term> <note>original: "Opus"</note> from the true ground. He did not set his foundation upon the sand, but upon the right cornerstone, the Holy Spirit, who told us of the creation of the world and of Man through <term>Moses</term> in the Holy Scriptures. Without this, the <term>philosopher</term> must wander about in the darkness against the walls. Therefore, he must take from the <term>theologian</term> <note>original: "Theologo"</note> the first and true <term>principle of "let it be done"</term> <note>original: "Principium fiat"; referring to God's creative command in Genesis</note>, through which God created everything out of nothing; which <term>Theophrastus</term> then publicly confesses in this <term>philosophy</term> as a Christian.

But so that the lovers of <term>Theophrastus</term> may see at the very beginning what they shall have in this <term>philosophy</term>, I will briefly and most simply indicate its contents for the sake of the beginning <term>disciples of Theophrastus</term>.

Since there are four ways that are set before Man, and he is engaged in four ways, Man should know in which way he lives, acts, or wanders, so that he may recognize his own works. These four ways <term>Theophrastus</term> calls the four <term>astronomies</term> <note>original: "Astronomias"; here meaning systems of knowledge or celestial influences</term>: the first is of Nature; the second of God; the third of Faith; and the fourth of Satan. In the first three, Man should remain and constantly exercise himself. But the fourth way he should not walk, nor use, but only recognize it, so that he knows how [to guard]...

# Preface.

But before Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus (1493–1541), the famous physician and alchemist.</note> explains these four paths, he first describes, as a philosopher in the first book, the essence of the Natural Man; thereafter he explains natural Astronomy <note>original: "Astronomiam"</note> with its nine members and gifts <note>original: "Membris vnd Donis"</note>. Accordingly, in the second book, he primarily describes the Eternal Heavenly Man of the new birth, so that the old natural, mortal man does not love Nature too much, but rather sees what he is, and knows how to conduct himself so that he loves the Heavenly more than the Earthly. He should also know what such a newborn man through Christ is capable of here on Earth, and then also in eternal life. Therefore, he first recounts the entire essence of the soul: what it is, from whence it comes, what its properties are, and its actions and omissions. Secondly, the union of the body and the soul, how the two are one. Thirdly, concerning the origin of the birth of the immortal flesh. And fourthly, concerning the joining together of the mortal and immortal flesh into one image <note>original: "Bildtnuß"</note>. After this, he recounts what Celestial Astronomy <note>original: "Coelestis Astronomia"</note> is, and how the members of natural astronomy may also be used in this. In the third book, he treats the Astronomy of Faith. In the fourth, the Infernal <note>original: "Infernaliſchen," referring to the lower or hellish realms</note> Astronomy.

Now, as far as both men are concerned—the Natural and the Heavenly—all faculties <note>academic disciplines or professions</note> should rightly consider this well, so that they do not hold him for a beast, but for the noblest creature, as one made in the image of God.

# Preface.

<note>The author argues that man is unique among creatures because of his physical composition.</note> made above all other creatures, because of the **matter**. For man was not made out of nothing, like heaven and earth, but was made out of a matter—that is, out of the great world—for which reason he is also called the *Microcosm* <note>original: "Microcosmus"; meaning "little world," the idea that man contains the entire universe within himself</note>. For everything that exists substantially in heaven and earth is also in man spiritually; that is, the starry body and the elemental **corporeality** <note>original: "Corporalitet"</note> shall dwell within the image of God—that is, in man—with their **powers** <note>original: "virtutibus"</note> and **essences** <note>original: "essentijs"</note>. But so that the nature of man may be better understood, *Theophrastus* <note>Referring to Theophrastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus (1493–1541)</note> recounts the order of creation as it was described by Moses in the Bible.

First, when there was nothing, God created through His Word a **Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> which was the **great mystery** <note>original: "mysterium magnum"; in Paracelsian thought, the primordial chaos or first matter from which all things were separated</note> and a beginning of all things. For this **Body**, He also created its living spirit, which accomplished its effects out of and through the **Body**, just as God ordained within that same **Body**. Out of this **Body**, God created the elements and everything that comes from them. He also gave them a spirit as a ruler, which drove out of them everything that is within them: such as all kinds of fruit from the earth; to the water, that it gives fish; to the air, its fruit; to the fire, that it burns; and from the heavens, the course of the sun, moon, and all stars.

After all this, God concluded in His divine counsel on the sixth day, after He had created all kinds of animals, that He also wished to make a human being in His image, so that he might learn to recognize his Creator from all **creatures** <note>original: "Creaturen"</note> and serve Him. Therefore, He did not take a simple clay <note>original: "Laimen"</note>, but rather a **corporeal mass** <note>original: "corporale massam"</note> and an extract of the **fifth essence** <note>original: "fünfften wesens" or Quintessence; the purest part of matter</note> of the four elements and of the entire **firmament**, and made two bodies out of it: one visible and material from the visible world, to be a house for the soul, so that he might eat, drink, and multiply into the na-

<summary>This preface explains the Paracelsian concept of man as a Microcosm, created not from nothing but from the "mysterium magnum" and the quintessence of the four elements. It describes the hierarchical order of creation, positioning man as the culmination of the universe designed to recognize and serve the Creator.</summary>

# Preface.

And although this <term>Massa</term> <note>The "massa" refers to the primordial "clump" or raw material of creation</note> was not flesh and blood, yet Man received his flesh and blood solely from it. But that the Holy Spirit called this mass <term>Limum terrae</term> <note>Latin: "the slime or mud of the earth"</note> and not <term>Coelorum</term> <note>Latin: "of the heavens"</note>, even though it was also taken from the Heavens, happened for this reason (as <insert>Theophrastus Paracelsus</insert> says): because the Earth is the foundation of all creatures, and the Center into which all creatures go. From this, Adam was to be formed in the image of God; but what this image of God truly was, though much has been written of it, no one can know except God Himself. 

However, because God made Man according to His image, He wished to have him eternally; therefore He made him not only from the <term>fifth essence</term> <note>The "quintessence," the purest and most potent part of a substance</note> of perishable creatures, but also out of the creation of the spirit. For there had to be something in man that was also invisible and like unto God, for the sake of which the image was made; not so that he would be a beast, but a Man, and live according to that same image in the will of God, and not according to the will of flesh and blood, for the sake of the eternal—which is why God does and reveals so much to man. 

But that which was to be like God is the Soul, which makes Man complete; not from the <term>Limo</term> <note>The earthly mud</note>, but from God Himself. For Moses says that God breathed a living breath into the nostrils of the form of Adam, and so Adam became a living soul. Now, the birth of the Soul is thus: when a child is conceived in the flesh, that is, born in the seed, in that same fleshly conception a Word goes out from God, which gives the flesh its soul, which makes the Man eternal.

# Preface.

Thus the soul is a breath from the mouth of God / and is the center within man / for her seat is in the heart / and she is the heart in the midst of man / and all other spirits, good and evil, dwell within her.

So there are now three operations <note>German: "wirckungen"; refers to the distinct ways the different parts of a human function or act upon the world</note> in man / the first is of the visible body / from the elements / such as eating / drinking / and other necessities / all of which, if it falls into excess, should not be attributed to Heaven / which creates no vice / but to the flesh and blood / which through vice drives the good spirit away from itself / and sets Satan in its place. The second operation is of the invisible body / which is received from Heaven / and is in man the human reason / earthly wisdom and art / in which body the natural light alone operates / for the sidereal spirit <note>The "sidereal spirit" refers to the astral or starry influence that Paracelsian philosophy believed governed the mind and intellect</note> teaches man everything that the natural light is capable of / so that he may recognize / and reveal all natural mysteries <note>original: "Mysteria"</note> of the elements and of the firmament / for which purpose man was created / so that nothing remains hidden. The third operation is of the soul and of the Spirit of God / which alone teaches us Divine virtue / and teaches us to recognize God and His Kingdom / and to understand the prophets / and the entire Bible / and without this Spirit we understand nothing heavenly or spiritual / everything is earthly / and everything that we do toward God / and God toward us / happens through the soul of man / which is invisible / but the works that follow from her make her visible.

Whoever does not use the **light of nature** <term>Light of Nature: The "Lumen Naturae," or the divine wisdom implanted in the natural world, which allows humans to understand the properties of plants, minerals, and stars through reason and experience.</term> learns all arts falsely. Therefore, those who write of natural things and forget their **Creator** / from whom the light of nature has its origin / they cannot write the truth. Thus, the physician should not trust them, nor rely solely on the means of Nature, but rather on the will and blessing of God.

The **Astronomy of nature** has ten branches <term>Branches: original "membra," literally "members" or parts of a body of knowledge.</term> / as **Theophrastus** has set them in tables with their specific types <note>original: "Speciebus"</note> / **Magic**, **Necromancy**, **Spirit-divination** <note>original: "Nectromantiam"; likely a variant of necromancy or communication with the spirits of the dead.</note>, **Astrology**, etc. These names will offend many / especially when they read that Theophrastus assigns these branches not only to natural astronomy, but also to Heavenly astronomy and the astronomy of faith. 

Now, let everyone consider well what Theophrastus intended to be understood in his writing. The natural branches may be used for harm as well as for benefit. If we cause harm, we misuse them to our own ruin; therefore, we should not do harm, but manifest ourselves through them and serve our neighbor for the honor of God. Theophrastus also indicates how the aforementioned branches may be applied <note>original: "accommodiern"</note> in the other Astronomies. But because of their potential misuse, no one should condemn these branches as devilish arts and sorcery. Otherwise, we would have to forbid **wine** and **beer** / do away with gunsmiths and knifesmiths along with many other things and trades. We would even have to burn the entire **Bible** / since all heresy has drawn its foundation from it. But the slan[derers]— <note>original: "Calum-"; likely "Calumniatoren" (slanderers).</note>

The **third Astronomy** is that of **Faith**—that the powers which proceed from faith, and all means, are fully and perfectly present through deeds and works. However, faith is of two kinds: **good** and **evil**. The good is a gift of **God**; the evil comes from **Satan**. Each has its own works. This Astronomy is lacking here in this work <note>original: "Opere," the Latin word for a book or composition.</note> and has not yet come to light; it perhaps remains hidden with a good friend.

The Devil also has not only his signs, but also his "saints." The wisdom which he did not lose <note>A reference to the theological idea that fallen angels retained their natural intellectual powers even after being cast out of heaven.</note>, he uses only to deceive and seduce mankind; and he has his order among his spirits no less than the angels in Heaven. We, Maximilian the Second, by the grace of God, Elected Roman Emperor, at all times Increaser of the Empire <note>This title, "mehrer des Reichs," is a translation of the Latin "semper Augustus," a standard title for the Holy Roman Emperor</note>, in Germany, of Hungary, Bohemia, Dalmatia, Croatia, and Slavonia, etc. King; Archduke of Austria; Duke of Burgundy, Styria, Carinthia, Carniola, and Württemberg, etc.; Count of Tyrol, etc.; publicly acknowledge with this letter and make known to everyone: that the honorable and learned Michael Toxites, teacher of medicine <term>Medicina: the art and science of healing</term>, our and the Empire’s dear and faithful subject, has humbly approached us and made it known: how he has for some time now compiled and composed several books in philosophy <term>Philosophia: the study of fundamental nature, knowledge, and reality</term> and medicine with particular great diligence, toil, and labor, as well as heavy expense; and he hopes daily to compile and compose even more of them, which he intends to allow to be released publicly in print for the benefit, good, and welfare of all. At the same time, however, he has the concern that perhaps others might undertake to reprint these same books of his, and thus he would not only be denied compensation for his spent costs, diligence, toil, and labor—as would be fair—but it might also result in significant disadvantage and harm to him. And for that reason, he has humbly called upon and petitioned us that we would graciously deign to provide for him in this matter with Imperial grace and <term>Freedom: in this context, a 'Freyheit' refers to a legal monopoly or copyright privilege granted by the sovereign</term>. Therefore, we have considered such humble prayer, as well as the particular skill and experience for which he is praised to us; and for that reason, with well-considered mind, good counsel, and certain knowledge, we have granted this special grace and given freedom to the aforementioned Doctor Michael Toxites. We do this and grant it to him also herewith by Roman Imperial Power knowingly, by virtue of this letter, in this manner: that for ten years following the next edition <note>original: "Aedition"</note> of each book, no book printer or anyone else, whoever they may be, shall or may in any way reprint the books which the said Michael Toxites shall release in print in philosophy and medicine, without his permission and consent; nor shall they transport, carry about, or sell such reprinted copies. And we command thereupon all and every one of our and the Empire’s subjects and faithful—as well as those of our Kingdoms, hereditary Principalities, and Lands—of whatever dignity, standing, or essence they may be, and especially all book printers, book distributors, and book sellers, wherever and in which cities and places they are settled and resident in the Holy Empire and in our said Kingdoms, hereditary Principalities, and Lands, collectively and each one in particular, earnestly with this letter: and it is our will that you let the said Michael Toxites remain peacefully in possession of this Imperial Grace and Freedom, and that you do him no grievance, entry, or hindrance therein, neither with reprinting nor in any other way. This is as dear to all of you and each one as it is to avoid our and the Empire’s heavy displeasure and punishment, and in addition a penalty: namely, ten marks of refined gold <note>A significant financial penalty intended to deter "pirate" printers</note>, which everyone who willfully acts against this shall be liable to pay, half to us and our and the Empire’s Treasury, and the other half to the aforementioned Michael Toxites without fail. In addition, he has full power to seize into his own hands—without hindrance from anyone—the reprinted books, wherever and in whatever places he or his authorized messengers and commanders can find them throughout the Holy Empire and also our Kingdoms, hereditary Principalities, and Lands, and to deal and proceed with them as he pleases, and he shall have committed no outrage or forfeit therein. Preface

# Of Philippus Theophrastus Paracelsus
## regarding the entire Sagacious Philosophy <term>Sagacem Philosophiam: a term Paracelsus uses for "wise" or "insightful" philosophy that understands the hidden workings of nature</term> of the Great and Small Worlds <term>Great and Small Worlds: the Macrocosm (the universe) and the Microcosm (humanity)</term>.

<image-desc>Large historiated initial 'D' decorated with intricate scrolling foliage and floral motifs in the woodcut style.</image-desc>So that you may first understand what is to be known and treated in Sagacious Philosophy, I have seen fit—and indeed considered it a reasonable necessity—to explain the whole nature <note>original: "Religion," here referring to the essential character, duties, or "bond" of created things</note> of all creatures, and upon what foundation and art they are placed according to the Order. If this is to be understood correctly and recognized well at its core, it is necessary that it be divided into its species <note>original: "Species," meaning distinct categories or types</note>, so that it might be more easily understood. And although these same divisions are not maintained in such a way by other philosophers, it must not be omitted here. 

First, I must praise this "sagacious art" because God has given, and continues to give, all art and everything natural to man through the firmament <note>The "firmament" refers to the heavens and the stars, which Paracelsus believed transmitted physical and mental qualities to Earth</note>. Thus, the firmament is the light of nature <term>natural light: the innate wisdom and reason found in the physical world, distinct from the light of divine revelation</term>, and man receives what is natural from the firmament. Furthermore, I must praise it because of its great usefulness, as every natural art springs from it. 

The great art of medicine, which was wonderfully created by God, takes its cornerstone—for recognizing man's illness, his health, and death—to the extent of half its necessity from this art of astronomy. Where this is lacking, the patient is misled by his physician. For the physician who does not know astronomy cannot be called a perfect physician, since more than half of all illnesses are governed by the firmament. 

Furthermore, this noble art does not only perfect medicine through astronomy, but also, concerning eternal wisdom, it provides the understanding to distinguish useless wisdom from the eternal, and to recognize one from the other; otherwise, it remains an entire error. For it is a necessary point and article that there are many who write of eternal wisdom, but are not themselves born of eternal wisdom. So that every person may be understood and recognized by what source he speaks from, or from where his wonders <term>prodigia: extraordinary signs or omens</term> spring, it is necessary to properly uncover the foundation, for there is more to it than just the two noble points mentioned. Note further that the art of astronomy allows us to recognize and reveals the secret—

# Preface

...nature <note>original: "heit," likely completing "Beschaffenheit," meaning the constitution or character</note> of the innate heart, and what nature has born as good or evil within man. For the reason is that man is made from the Great World <term>Great World: the macrocosm or the universe</term> and bears its nature within himself. Therefore, since there is one nature from the earth and the firmament <note>The "firmament" refers to the celestial sphere and its influence on the physical world</note>, and another from heaven, it is necessary to discover what speaks from each one. Whether this is not a great treasure, I leave for everyone to recognize, since the other virtues and arts flow and come from the stars.

For everything that the Light of Nature <term>Light of Nature: the innate wisdom and reason found in the physical world, distinct from divine revelation</term> teaches man comes from the nature of the stars. Pay attention to this point: that all natural arts and wisdom are given to man by the stars, and nothing is excepted; rather, all things are given by the stars. We are the pupils of the stars, and the stars are our teacher. Therefore it is necessary, since the stars deal so much with us, to follow them. Thus God has ordained in the Light of Nature that we should learn from it—namely as if from our father, from whom we were made and created.

Therefore, it is a matter of great necessity—since such error and folly have occurred that those whose cornerstone <note>original: "Eckstein"</note> should be the astronomers actually reject them—it is necessary that their folly be brought to light. For the false prophets destroy this art because it reveals them too clearly. From such folly in rejecting the cornerstone, the false physicians take their origin; the erring also know their origin, as do those who are ignorant of the Light of Nature and lack knowledge of this art. What is not surrounded by folly or falsehood? There are those who conduct their lives according to this mystery—even though a law exists in human life and the art within it is not considered—yet these lawmakers do not recognize on what foundation and cornerstone that same law is set. They do not know it because they do not know what the Light of Nature teaches, nor what God teaches, nor from what source the mortal or the eternal springs. Thus they do not understand themselves; for mere opinion and belief are distinguished from true knowledge and ability through this art. That is, all things should happen with great reason; *Astronomy* teaches what belongs to its part. In divine conduct, one learns from God; but what serves the mortal part, that one learns from the firmament.

So that I do not make this preface too long for you, you should know that there are many who boast of being astronomers, whose simplicity and lack of understanding come from their own pride <note>original: "aus ihrem eignen hals," literally "out of their own neck," a German idiom for speaking without authority or from one's own imagination</note>. High-sounding names are much sought after, but the pearl <note>original: "Perlin," referring to the "pearl of great price" or the essential truth of the matter</note> is neglected. Thus I will briefly reveal to you the art of *Astronomy* in nine parts; when these are joined together, then the *Astronomer* is...

# Preface

A ij

...born. As I recounted in the beginning, I must again point out those same **categories** <note>original: "Species"</note>, so that it may be precisely understood how **Astronomy** is a mother of all other arts. Where the **Astronomer** ends, there the true Physician begins, there the true Philosopher begins, there Justice begins, there eternal Wisdom begins; there all arts begin. These are the elements of those things of which I have spoken, to uncover the nine articles. 

And mark this all well: where **Astronomy** ends, the excellent religions begin, and without **Astronomy** no art can be fully completed. Following it, Divine Wisdom begins; following it, the **Light of Nature** <term>Light of Nature: the innate wisdom and reason found in the physical world, distinct from divine revelation</term> begins. For first we should properly recognize the natural light; only then are we fit to recognize all things that God further works through man. 

Now, concerning this, know that each is the other’s enemy, and each wants to yield nothing to the other—just as the vain and frivolous want to judge all things without foundation or knowledge. They do not consider that they all act from one Father; that is, they all exist before God, one like the other. This example demonstrates it: they do not recognize in Nature that seven kinds of smiths are born from iron, and each is legitimate in his own part. 

See, friends, what great simplicity and folly exists in clever people, when such things are revealed. The **Astrologer** <note>original: "Astrologus"</note> will not let the **Magus** <note>original: "Magum"</note> be, nor the **Diviner** <note>original: "Diuinatorem"</note>, nor the **Necromancer** <note>original: "Nicromanticum"</note>, nor the **Signator** <note>original: "Signatorem"</note>, nor the **Uncertain** <note>original: "Incertus"</note>; he only lets the **Manualist** <note>original: "Manualem"</note> remain. 

But the **Magus** does not let the **Astrologer** or the **Manualist** remain, nor the **Signator**. The **Signator** despises all the other six; the **Diviner** keeps silent against the other six. The **Necromancer** is ignorant of the foundation of the others. The **Uncertain** holds himself to be the best. The **Manualist** makes use of instruments and attaches himself a little bit to everything. Thus, the **Inanimate** <note>original: "Inanimata," referring here to things without life, like minerals or stones</note> are completely excluded, and they are not considered according to the content of the **Light of Nature**. 

And although the foundation of the other **categories** has not been established with earnestness—so that they might be thoroughly understood in their essence—this is the best: that each individual part be perfect in itself, and let the others, his sisters, remain as good as they themselves are. Wood does not require only one kind of art, until each piece comes to that place where it belongs. One art consumes the wood in the stove; another works its wood into a chair; another art into a knife handle; another into slipper soles; another into window frames, etc. Is not each art right to work its wood? So also are the eight parts right to work...

# Preface

...the stars. Though each star is different from the next, yet each—in the gift given to it—is naturally and essentially a perfect art that God wills to exist. He does this so that there is not just one single thing on earth among men, but a great variety. Although there is only one Wisdom and one Art, it is nevertheless applied in many different ways. For God wishes to be seen as wondrous in His saints—that is, among His scholars. 

However, this variety exists only in the arts. Towards God, regarding eternal life, it is not so; there, there is only one way, one art, one teaching, one manner, one essence, one dwelling, one protection, and one God. But in the **Light of Nature** <term>Light of Nature: The innate source of human reason and sensory knowledge, distinct from the light of divine revelation</term>, there are many ways to work that light: among craftsmen, in the arts, and in other academic faculties and religions. 

**Theology** <note>original: "Theologia"</note>, however, is not contained within these various ways. There is only one **Theology** in the person to whom it is given; it fills them entirely, and they remain on a single path and track. In the same way, every other art should be perfect within itself: the **Astrologer** <note>original: "Astrologus"</note> in what belongs to him, the **Magician** <note>original: "Magus"</note> in his own, and likewise the **Diviner** <note>original: "Diuinator"</note>, the **Necromancer** <note>original: "Necromantist"</note>, the **Signator** <term>Signator: A practitioner who interprets the "signatures" or physical marks in nature that reveal an object's hidden purpose</term>, the **Uncertain** <note>original: "Incertus," referring to the *Ars Incerta*, a form of divination involving dreams or the imagination</note>, the **Manualist** <note>original: "Manualis," likely a reference to chiromancy or hand-reading</note>, and the **Generative** <note>original: "Generatiuus," one who understands hereditary traits and procreation</note>. It is a noble thing for one who has grasped **Genealogy** <note>original: "Genealogiam"</note> or lineage within one’s mind and brought it all together; such a person recognizes the wondrous works of God and can point out the **mighty works** <term>mighty works: from the Latin 'magnalia', referring to the great secrets or powerful deeds of God hidden within the natural world</term> and even operate through them.

This is what I have deemed good to explain: the specific parts of **Astronomy**, describing their foundation and truth. I do this so that these useless studies—which mockingly and shamefully consume our noble time—might be forgotten and cast out, along with other useless courtesies and habits in which the youth of today are occupied and raised. For in my time, these vanities have increased beyond measure. 

Understand that there are two types of wisdom in this world: one eternal and one mortal. The eternal springs directly from the light of the Holy Spirit; the other springs directly from the **Light of Nature**. That which comes from the light of the Holy Spirit has only one **category** <note>original: "Speciem"</note>: it is righteous, flawless wisdom. But that which comes from the **Light of Nature** has two **categories**: good wisdom and evil wisdom. The good attaches itself to the eternal, while the evil attaches itself to the damnable. 

This is a matter for an **Astronomer** <note>original: "Astronomo"</note> to consider deeply and to measure: that God said:

-> I regret that I have made man. <-
<note>original: "Mich reuwet / daß ich den Menschen gemacht hab." A reference to Genesis 6:6-7.</note>

The cause of this is found in **Astronomy**, which indicates such regret. It is found in the fact that God made man in His own image and ordained His image for **Paradise** <note>original: "Paradeiß"</note>, and not for this world. From this it follows that God felt regret because His image does not live in Paradise, but must live a mortal life in the world...

...must. For had man remained in Paradise, then **Philosophy** <note>original: "Philosophia"</note> might well consider that God would have created a different nature for the world. Since man is now born from the **Light of Nature** <term>Light of Nature: The source of human reason, craft, and understanding inherent in the natural world, distinct from divine revelation</term>, it follows that man knows good and evil—not from flesh and blood, but from the stars within flesh and blood. This is the treasure, the natural **highest good** <note>original: "Summum bonum"</note>. 

Is it not a treasure for a man to know how to recognize Eternal Wisdom from that which is mortal, given that he is the **Image of God** <note>original: "bildtnus Gottes"</note>? Through this understanding, he realizes that the natural, compared to the Eternal, serves for nothing. Therefore, he should seek further, in accordance with that Image, to separate mortal wisdom into good and evil. That is to say, he may now accept the evil or the good, yet he knows where the evil leads and he also knows to whom the good returns. 

Now, I consider it a great good when a separation occurs between each individual essence and the others, so that one can pick out that which is good. First the eternal wisdom, then the mortal—but keeping the good and letting the evil fall away. For wisdom does not compel you; you alone compel yourself. 

Although it is no less blessed to write about—and more than blessed to learn—eternal Wisdom (which I do not venture to address here), I shall focus only on the mortal wisdom, which I can fully complete through **Astronomy** <note>original: "Astronomey"; in this context, it refers to the study of how the stars influence human nature and the "Light of Nature"</note>. Should I not be capable of this—and everyone else too—so that we may preserve the eternal light within us and also testify to the natural light within us? And thus, by walking in the eternal light according to God's highest will so that our light shines before all men, I would otherwise be grieved that the earth should even bear me. 

But if it should be thought that I do not act rightly—as those desperate ones suggest, who are themselves **fanatics** <term>fanatics: "Schwermer," a term used during the Reformation for religious radicals who were seen as untethered from reason or tradition</term> in matters of eternal faith, and who despise and judge their Lords—how then could the Light of Nature remain uninjured by them? 

Take note: God will not hold it against me. For in the **Creation** <note>original: "Schöpffung"</note> there are two who have created, each together with the third in Person and the one Godhead. The first, as the **Father** <note>original: "Vatter"</note>, created man from the bottom up. The other, as the **Son** <note>original: "Sohn"</note>, from the top down. Since we are created by these two, the first was established by God the Father, through the power of the **Holy Spirit** <note>original: "heiligen Geistes"</note>, for the Natural Light. Therefore, if they learn and live from the natural light, they receive the same from the Holy Spirit. The new creature [is brought] through the Holy Spirit into the eternal light of life—that is, to bring the Image of God back to where it came from. Thus the Image falls back into God's hand,

# Preface

...and the flesh back into the earth. If I now write of the **Light of Nature** <term>Light of Nature: For the author, this is the divine spark within creation that grants humans reason and the ability to understand the physical world, medicine, and the stars</term>—which comes from the Father—why should the Son hate or envy me? Since I take the Son’s wisdom for myself, yet both have one undivided Spirit and are not at odds within themselves. For man is two-fold: in one part **mortal** <note>original: "Toͤdtlich"</note>, in the other eternal. Each part takes its light from God—the mortal and the eternal—and there is nothing that does not take its origin from God. 

Why then should the Father's light be recognized and judged as heathenish, and I as a pagan? Especially when I am a Christian and walk in the Christian light—both the old and the new. For if the Father and Son are one, how can I honor two separate lights? I would be judged as idolatrous, but the number One sustains me. And if I love two and give to each its own light, as God has ordained for each, how then can I be a pagan? 

Now, the body cannot be nourished with the food of the soul, nor the soul with bodily food, but each has its own proper needs. If I give to each part that which should be given to it, should I for that reason be called a pagan or a **renegade** <term>renegade: The original uses the term "Mammaluck" (Mamluk), which in this period was a common slur for an apostate or someone who had betrayed their faith</term>, or be excluded from the number of Christians? Where is it proven to me that the Light of Nature is not eternal? Rather, through the eternal, I must become eternal. Should I not be able to unite the soul’s transitory light with the eternal? Yet body and soul remain together; who cannot use two lights, as stated above? Since God has made two essences in man—the earthly and the eternal—and they are wedded together until the resurrection, when the earthly is returned to the earth and the eternal to the Kingdom of God. 

I write as a Christian and am no pagan; a **German** <note>original: "Teutscher"</note>, no **foreigner** <note>original: "Welscher," a term typically used for those of Romance/Latin descent, often carrying a pejorative sense of "outsider"</note>; an **interpreter** <note>original: "Interpres"</note>, no sophist, etc.

Furthermore, take note of how two lights are mentioned: an eternal and a mortal. The eternal accomplishes its transformation in the soul, the mortal in the body. The mortal light works in the **Light of Nature**, the eternal in the eternal. For thus has the divine **providence** <note>original: "Fuͤrsichtigkeit"</note> of the world stood: that to the mortal body its labor be given to pass the time that we must consume on earth, so that other idle thoughts might be left aside, and that we might walk in the Light of Nature according to God’s will, and provide the natural light to our natural body, and take up the natural art for ourselves, and experience the wondrous works of God through nature. And although he should not rejoice in that same light alone, but also...

<meta>This page continues the "Preface" (Vorred) from the previous section. # Preface

...in the light that belongs to the **image of God**. And so, man should live in two lights, and neither hinders the other; rather, they are married together like husband and wife. 

Now, what enmity should there be here between the **mortal** and **eternal physician**? As an example: the mortal physician makes the sick healthy, and the **apostle** makes him healthy as well. That the apostle surpasses the natural physician is due to the **New Birth** <term>New Birth: A theological concept referring to spiritual regeneration (John 3:3), which the author believes grants powers beyond the physical world</term>. But the Godhead does not allow the **Light of Nature** <term>Light of Nature: The divine wisdom found within the physical world and human reason</term> to be rejected because of this. And although the apostle brings the dead back to life—which the natural physician cannot do—the natural physician recognizes that his art is but a **footstool** compared to the eternal art. 

The prophets prophesied things that it was not possible for the **astronomer** <note>original: "Astronmo"</note> to find or fathom in even the smallest part. But how does that harm astronomy? Because she cannot speak of what she does not know, should astronomy be despised for what she *does* know? How could such a thing be justified? Even if the prophets have said much, what does that take away from astronomy? Even if astronomy has said much, what harm does that do to the prophets? One side speaks from above downward, the other from below upward, and both are righteous within their own light. 

Even though the apostles and saints have healed many, has not much more been left to **medicine** <note>original: "Artzney"</note>—specifically for those who were not healed by the saints and apostles? Is it not also worth considering that while the apostles and saints raised the dead and made the lame walk, they are not with us at all times? Therefore, we lack their works. If medicine were to be worth nothing, then the saints would have to fill its place. But since the saints are not present and those miracles do not occur, medicine must take their place—just as happened in **Jericho** <note>This refers to the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30–37), who used physical bandages and oil to heal a victim on the road to Jericho</note> with the wounded man, who was cured by medicine and not by saints. Thus, the Light of Nature is an administrator for the saints. 

What harm is it to the natural tongue that the **tongue of fire** <note>original: "Feuwrin geredt," referring to the Holy Spirit's gift of tongues at Pentecost</note> has spoken? Or what does the fiery tongue take away from the natural one? They are just like a husband and wife who together bear a child; it cannot happen without both. So too, both lights are given to us to dwell within one man. 

Therefore, I will conclude this preface and proceed with my intention to explain what the nine parts of astronomy are, testing them sufficiently, and explaining their power and strength. The explanation in this preface was given so that I may defend myself as a Christian—that I should not be called a **sorcerer** <note>original: "Zauberer"</note>, a pagan, or a liar in this book. I wish to bear witness through my writing that I am a Christian, and

# Preface

...and let the false Christians prattle with their false leaven <note>A biblical metaphor (from Matthew 16:6) referring to corrupting influences or hypocritical teachings</note>. And so God has seen fit for me to describe **Astronomy**, as follows hereafter. And although I write in the **Mortal Light** <term>Mortal Light: The temporary, physical knowledge available to humans during their earthly life, as opposed to eternal spiritual revelation</term>, I intend now to satisfy and sate the mortal body with all that is in the **Natural Light** <term>Light of Nature: The divine wisdom embedded within the physical world and human reason, which allows people to understand the created universe</term>, with which God has gifted me. To speak with fiery tongues is not my gift—that is, to describe the nature of those tongues <note>The author is referring to the miracle of Pentecost (Acts 2), where the Apostles were granted the ability to speak in many languages to spread the Gospel</note>. 

For even though I am not gifted to write here from the **School of Pentecost**—which school alone teaches the eternal and within the eternal, and not in the mortal world, though both are married together—yet I have the grace and gift of that same Spirit who proceeds from the Father into the **Natural Light**, just as He otherwise proceeds through the Son from the Father into the **Eternal Light**. 

For I wish to testify by means of Nature that there are many among men who are regarded as gods or saints, but who should be held as more wretched than a corpse <note>original: "Cadauer"</note>. For it is simply so: the Devil initiates his **satanic virtues** <note>In this historical context, "virtue" (Tugendt) refers to an inherent power or effective property; the author is warning against the deceptive powers of evil</note> so that he may turn man against God. 

Therefore, it is necessary to learn the **Right Light**, so that those same satanic powers may be struck from us. I hope to be found herein with equal truth, in as much as the Mortal Light is given by God through the Spirit, who may enlighten and perfect our work and labor, our **natural talents** <note>original: "Ingenia"</note>, and our **teaching** <note>original: "Doctrin"</note>. Amen.

### The First Chapter.
#### Primarily, an instruction to recognize the beginning /
#### how the Stars and Man stand toward one another /
#### and are united.

So that it may be presented to you: First, regarding the beginning of all things, it is necessary to take up the work of the first creation—how Heaven and Earth and all creatures were created. Note that same order thus: First the Body, after the Body the Governor, after that the sentient Body, after that its King who governs it, and thereafter a King who governs Man. Understand it in this way: First, a body was created of the upper and lower spheres, so that the Firmament has a bodily essence, as do the elements in both Heaven and Earth. The **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note> was the beginning of all things. After that, its living Spirit was created for that same Body, which accomplishes its work out of the Body and through the Body, which God then ordained within it. Thus, the days of creation and the ordering of all creatures came to an end. After all this, Man was made by God Himself in His image. Therefore, understand further what the Spirit is that governs in the creatures, and what the Spirit is that governs Man. Regarding such governing—how each one rules the other—note this: First, the **Elements** <note>original: *Elementa*</note> were created, and the elements are nothing but a **Subject** <term>Subject: Used here in the sense of a *subiectum*—a physical vessel, foundation, or "matter" that acts as a container for a higher force</term> through which something is to be accomplished; that is, they are the things in which the **Living Force** <term>Vivum: The vital, active principle or life-force implanted by God into physical matter to animate it</term> is placed. 

This motion is what governs the body; thus there is a Governor and a ruler in the elements who drives out of them what is within them. This drives the Fire so that it must burn, drives the Earth so that it must yield fruit, drives the Water so that it must sustain fish, drives the Air across the whole earth, drives the Sun and Moon and all the stars in their course. This is the essence from which the Body goes into its action and is compelled; and as the essence is, so the Body is used—except for what **art** <note>In Paracelsian terms, "art" (*Kunst*) usually refers to human intervention, such as Alchemy or Medicine, which can work with or redirect natural forces</note> reserves. And although there is a distinction there between the creatures and Man—

This provides the third and fourth rulers <note>In Paracelsian thought, these "rulers" are the internal forces or spirits that govern biological and mental functions.</note> over Man, which do not exist over the cattle. That which is reason in the Divine image is what separates Man from other creatures.

Thus, **Predestination** <note>original: *Praedestination*; in this context, it refers to a natural "pre-ordering" or the inherent purpose and lifespan fixed by God for every created thing, rather than the theological concept of salvation.</note> is fulfilled in every **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note>. In Man—as one who is made by God with diligence out of the highest Divine art—it concerns the **Elements** <note>original: *Elementen*</note>; and in cattle and other things, according to what each one is, so it has its predestination from God, belonging where it is meant to be, so that every creature must fulfill that which is predestined within it.

Thus, the sentient flesh must fulfill that for which it is ordained; the elements must give forth that which lies within them. Nevertheless, Man, as the last created by God, is also assigned a ruler who drives him—just as animals are driven into natural action—toward that which God wishes to have from him and which should happen through him. That same ruler drives these things out of him, with nothing excepted, according to whether he is capable and inclined toward good or evil.

Furthermore, regarding other rulers and essences, as far as they concern the Divine image—which then makes a Man different from the natural—it is not proper for me to write of the natural here. I will therefore omit the eternal in Man here, for it is not my purpose to write of it in this place.

Thus, it should now be understood that, firstly, there is a body of which the **Astronomer** <note>original: *Astronomus*; for Paracelsus, an astronomer is not just a star-watcher but a scientist who understands how celestial forces influence the "sidereal" or "astral" spirit of man.</note> does not speak. It is **Elemental** <note>original: *Elementisch*</note> and belongs to the earthly philosophy of the elements. But over the natural **Spirit** <note>original: *Spiritum*</note> in the body, the Astronomer has the power and authority to speak; for the body belongs to the elements, but the spirit that is given to the elemental body is married to and embodied from the **Firmament** <note>The "Firmament" here refers to the belt of stars and planets that provides the "sidereal" or "star-like" spirit to living things.</note>.

And so, **Philosophy** <note>original: *Philosophia*</note> divides into two parts: into the essence of the spirit, and secondly into the essence of the body—that is, into the *Corpus* and *Spiritum*. Therein, note what the Heavenly Operations accomplish—that is, what the **Ethereal spirits** <note>The subtle, non-physical forces of the heavens.</note> act upon and do. I wish here to describe those same powers and virtues that God has given within them, such as:
* The body of the elements
* The body of the cattle
* The body of Men
* The body of the stones
* The body of the metals
* The body of the herbs
* and others of the like.

These are all bodies and *Corpora* that do not concern the **Sidereal spirit** <note>original: *Syderischer geist*; the "star-spirit" or astral body that mediates between the physical flesh and the divine soul.</note>. For the body of the elements is set into four bodies; the body of the cattle into many hundreds of species; the body of Men into one body. There are four elements, but of the animals, no number has been found, for it is impossible to know them all.

# The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus (1493–1541).</note>

Therefore, I wish to write nothing of those things, but only what concerns **Man**, so that the **Natural spirit** <note>original: *Natūrlich geist*; in Paracelsian thought, this is the "astral body" or "sidereal spirit" that connects the human body to the stars and governs instincts and physical life.</note> may be understood and recognized. Thus, in Man there is only one body, one essence, and one kind, and only one body comes from Man. But because he may run into so many **Species** within human reason—as many species of cattle as there are in all lineages—it is therefore necessary that snake-men, toad-men, sow-men, cock-men, and lion-men be described. For many types of **Bodies** <note>original: *Corpora*</note> come out of the elements, and many types of **spirit** come out of the **Firmament** <note>The heavens or the sphere of the stars.</note>. If the Firmament then enters into a person in the manner of a lion, or into a sow-man, and the body is like a sow, then that person will be no human being, but only an animal. The image is not in the animal; the form is not that of a sow alone, but the behaviors are also those of a sow. But in the **Divine Image** <note>original: *Göttlicher Bildtnus*; the "Imago Dei," the eternal part of man.</note> there is only one spirit, of which it is not my purpose to speak here. Rather, my intention is to speak of the **ruler** who governs the body. And this ruler is called the **Stars** <note>original: *Gestirn*</note>, from which the whole of **Astronomy** <note>In this period, "Astronomy" encompassed both the physical movement of stars and "Astrology," the study of their influence on the earthly world.</note> flows. Even if I have spoken here in a **Heathen** <note>Pagan or non-Christian.</note> manner—as it might be viewed by many—it is nevertheless not hidden from me; although I call Man an animal, I well know the distinction between Man and the animals, which lies solely in the **Image** and in the **Spirit**. I must point this out by the Highest; because I point out the **Light of Nature** <note>original: *Liecht der Natur*; the divine wisdom revealed through the study of the natural world, distinct from the light of grace or revelation.</note>, should I be despised? The **Father** made it, who also taught the **Son**; if the Son is pleasing, then the Father’s work in other things is also pleasing. Where has Man sustained himself from the elements and from the stars in the Son? Never; but only in the Father. Therefore, if they give me space to write of the works of Him who taught the Son, let the others remain without disparaging me. Thus I say: Man as an animal has a ruler as an animal; Man as an image of God also has a ruler as an image of God. This ruler [of the animal side] does not keep the name "ruler"—that is the ruler of the body according to the animal way. And although there are **two rulers** in the body of Man, here we are to note only the **mortal** one, for he comes to an end through death. I write of the mortal one, and it is just as necessary to know this as any other thing, for we should walk in the **works of God**, not in the fantasies of men. # The First Book /

To help you understand this more clearly: there are two bodies in Man—one from the elements, the other from the stars. Therefore, these two bodies must be recognized as distinct. Through death, the elemental body and its spirit enter the pit <note>the grave</note>, while the ethereal bodies are consumed in their firmament, and the spirit of the Image <note>The "Imago Dei" or the divine spark within humanity.</note> goes to that which the Image is. Thus, everyone dies in that, or out of 그 that which they are made, and into that same thing they are buried.

So death separates three spirits from one another within Man. I have decided to write here not of the spirit of the Image, but only of the natural body. However, the spirit of the Image remains with the other two, for they are Men. Astronomy <note>In the 16th century, "Astronomy" included what we now call astrology—the study of how the heavens influence human life.</note> has much to say about these, because the spirit exists within the image of Man, whether they be good or evil. And where the Image of God is not, there this spirit is also absent, because a human being is created by God for that spirit.

For the two shall not be divided from each other—the Man and the Image—and it is intended that Man should live according to the Image, and so persevere and conclude his life. In this way, the Image should have nothing of the animal within it. But because of the natural side, the human body <note>original: *Corpus*</note> is driven into the natural light, separate from the Image; and each spirit shall rule where it resides and is ordained.

And so long as each remains in its power <note>original: *Potenz*</note>, it is in its predestination <note>original: *Praedestination*; its divinely appointed path</note> according to the will and order of God. That is to say, the two—Man and the Image—should not be separated from each other, for in both lies the predestination, undivided.

The reason I mention this is that the ruler of the four elements is known to the philosopher; likewise, the ruler in animals is known to the astronomers. Just so, the ruler of the natural man is revealed to astronomers through magic <note>original: *Magice*; here meaning the study of hidden natural forces</note> and not through astrology <note>original: *Astrologice*</note>, or other branches of astronomy. For Magic alone has the authority to speak here.

But the spirit of the Image is hidden from all astronomy; it belongs to those who speak in God and from His light and spirit. Therefore, the astronomer can speak nothing of Christ, nor of His apostles and prophets. For what concerns the Image is not commanded to astronomy. Christ is supernatural and above nature. Nature is beneath Him; He is the Second Person of the Trinity <note>original: *secunda Persona der Trinitet*</note> and the creator of all things. He creates for Himself a new heaven whenever He wishes. Therefore, the astronomer says nothing of the prophecy of Christ and the prophets, nor does he deal with the Book of Revelation <note>original: *Apocalipsin*</note>. For there is a distinction to be noted: Christ and His followers proclaim the times of the nations <note>original: *Tempora nationum*; the historical and prophetic ages of humanity</note>, while the astronomer proclaims the times of nature <note>original: *Tempora naturae*; the cycles and seasons of the physical world</note>. There is a great difference between them.

### Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus, Page 3

Take good note of this, and note it very well, you natural philosophers <note>original: *Naturales*; those who study the laws of nature</note> and theologians. And although I write of the mortal being, the eternal is even more. *   **Sulphur** <note>The principle of combustibility and growth.</note>

*   In the **Mind** <note>original: *Gemüth*; one's disposition or inner temperament.</note>
*   In **Wisdom**
*   In **Art** 

And they are both set into Life. Thus, I proceed with the Natural, and what I have revealed so far is for the sake of those things one must guard against—especially anyone who wishes to deal in the works of God.

Thus stand the creatures in the world, and all creatures are divided into two parts: into the perceptible and the imperceptible. The perceptible is divided into two kinds: into reason and unreason, and yet both are animal-like. Thus, humans know with understanding what they ought to do, and according to what they do, they are aware of their own end; this is not present in the irrational animal. Therefore, humans have judgment and the power of completion, which is not in the beasts. 

In this way, all senses are governed by the stars as by a ruler, who is set over every understanding: to the human as a human, and to the cattle as cattle. And as far as the human is concerned, there are two kinds: the reason of the human in arts, mind, and wisdom comes from the stars; but the nature of the beast is only for eating and drinking and fulfilling its kind. Blood is that which comes from the elements. Thus, there are two workings in Man: one of the Light of the Firmament, in natural wisdom, arts, and reason—these have no other father, for God has created the medium in the natural light. And furthermore, there is another from the elements, such as unchastity, eating, drinking, and the like, which concerns flesh and blood; and what is thus born in flesh and blood should not be attributed to the stars <note>original: *Gestirn*</note>. For the Heavens give no unchastity, and they make no one greedy. Just as fire falls from the flint, in which it is not seen, so it also falls from the stars into the flesh and blood, which is its tinder—but it does not fall into the things that affect flesh and blood [exclusively]; rather, it only gives birth within man to those things concerning wisdom, art, etc., for from the Heavens come only wisdom and art. Thus, the tinder of the flesh is divided into two parts: the part that lives without reason, and the part that lives in reason. To each part is given its predestined sensuality, each according to its quality, nature, and essence. All this is received from the stars and the elements, as has been mentioned. Thus, each part receives its essence according to what has been given to it; what is of the flesh is animalistic and belongs to all animals; what is of the stars is human; and what is of the spirit of God is according to His image, etc.

As was just mentioned regarding how the upper stars work in Man, you should now understand that in the stars are all **faculties** <note>original: *Facultates*</note>, all arts, all crafts, all wisdom, all reason, as well as what belongs to folly and others. From this, it follows that nothing can be in man unless it has been given to him by the Light of Nature <term>Light of Nature: The innate intelligence and instincts provided by the physical world, distinct from divine revelation.</term>; and what is in the Light of Nature is the working of the stars, and in the stars is the school from which all the mentioned subjects are learned. For instance, the first **ascendant of Venus** <note>original: *ascendens Veneris*</note> taught **music** <note>original: *Musicam*</note>; the first **ascendant of Mars** <note>original: *ascendens Martis*</note> taught the **smith's arts** <note>original: *fabrilia*</note>. Note further how such **ascendants** rose in **Venus**; they also gave other **melodies**. Likewise, other **ascendants of Mars** have also given other **inventions** in the **smith's arts**. You should also note that had **Venus** not existed, no **music** would have been invented; likewise, had **Mars** not been, the **smith's arts** would not have been invented. Thus, the stars teach us all the arts that are on Earth, and if they did not work within us, but we were to do it of our own accord, no art would ever be invented—so much is given to the stars in relation to man. Since the heavens have been arranged in different figures from Adam's time until now, the years of discovery will be found...

# Of what Humanity was made / what the *Slime* <note>original: *Limus*; referring to the "dust of the ground" or primordial clay from which Adam was created in Genesis 2:7.</note> is / and what properties that same Mass possessed.

Firstly, regarding the origin of humanity, it is necessary to know from what they were made; and although the ancient **Philosophers** do not consider this, nor do the **Theologians**, **Jurists**, or even **Physicians**, such a failure should not be counted as wisdom among them. For the **Philosopher** should consider this first of all—from whence humanity comes—and thus lay the **cornerstone** <term>Cornerstone</term><note>original: *Eckstein*; the foundational principle upon which all other knowledge in a specific field must be built.</note> for the others. Likewise the **Theologian**, so that he may know what the body is, what in it is mortal, and what is eternal, so that he does not damn the body to the Devil. And the **Jurist**, so that he knows that a human being is not a **sow**, but a nobler creature; thereafter he should know how to judge him as a human, and not as a **calf**. And the **Physician** must also know this beginning, so that he does not treat a person like cattle at a **butcher’s bench** <note>original: *Fleischbencken*; a metaphor for physicians who treat the body as mere physical meat without spiritual or divine context.</note>, but rather considers the **Divine image** <note>original: *Göttliche bildtnus*</note> in order to proceed correctly with medicine. For if one knows how humanity is made, one also learns to recognize through that same knowledge that man is of the same essence and property as that very thing from which he was made. 

Now they may judge and grasp the understanding of what that substance is from which humanity comes, which is itself noble and highly esteemed and held by all people; it is only right that humanity be held even higher. Furthermore, I say plainly that the Physician should be the first to know this, yet I have heard very little of such knowledge from them. To describe this, it is necessary that, before all things, **Holy Scripture** be used, which in this place provides the beginning for all **Philosophers** and **Naturalists** <note>original: *Naturalibus*; those who study the natural world or physical sciences.</note>, and shows that without this beginning, all philosophers are employed and led in vain. That is to say: if a philosopher is not born out of **Theology**, he has no cornerstone upon which he may place his philosophy; for truth proceeds from Theology, and without it, nothing may be found.

Thus, I have resolved—before I describe humanity itself—to show the origin of all **created things**, so that the subsequent origin of humanity may be better recognized. Although describing such a thing takes its start from that which proves itself—that is, from what it is—both it and humanity are recognized through the **creation**, which then describes how humanity was made. For all **created things** <note>original: *Creata*</note> are letters and books for describing the origin of humanity. That is: if one wishes to know ancient histories, one must take them from the

Rather, he was made from a material <note>original: *Zeug*; stuff or substance.</note>, whereas all other creatures were made from nothing, born only from what the **Word** gave and created. Of this I must speak. For the scripture proves that God took the **slime of the earth** <term>Slime of the Earth</term> <note>original: *Limum terrae*; the primordial clay of Genesis.</note> like a mass <note>original: *Massam*</note>, and from that same mass He formed and made Man. As the scripture further proves, Man is ash and powder, dust and earth; this is sufficient proof that Man is made from *something*, and that "something" was the **slime of the earth** <note>original: *Limus terrae*</note>. 

And although he has a different form and **body** <term>Body</term> <note>original: *Corpus*</note> than the slime—possessing flesh and blood, bone, etc., which is different from clay and filth—he nevertheless becomes that again which he once was, as is clearly proven by sight. For powder and dust are a material and a **matter** <term>Matter</term> <note>original: *Materia*</note>; whatever comes from them is not made from nothing, but from a material. How that material is shall be discussed, so that it may be known that Man is made from powder or dust, and that same dust is the **slime of the earth** <note>original: *Limus terrae*</note>, and the **slime of the earth** is the **Greater World** <term>Greater World</term> <note>original: *maior Mundus*; the macrocosm or the entire universe.</note>. 

And thus Man is made of heaven and earth—that is, out of the upper and lower creations. Therefore, Man is a **subject** <term>Subject</term> <note>original: *subiectum*; the primary focus of study.</note> of the **Philosophers**, because he is made from the **slime of the earth**; and since the slime is taken from the heavens, he is also a **subject of Astronomy** <note>original: *subiectum Astronomiae*</note>. Thus, **Astronomy** and **Philosophy** cannot be separated from one another.

-># The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus<-

That **islands** <term>Islands</term> <note>original: *Infulen*; a reference to the then-recently discovered Americas and other distant lands.</note> have been found and are still hidden, so that it might be believed they descend from **Adam**, cannot be confirmed—that Adam's children reached these hidden islands. Rather, it is well to consider that these same people are from another Adam. For it is difficult to conclude that they are related by flesh and blood; and it is also worth considering that had Adam remained in **Paradise** <term>Paradise</term> <note>original: *Paradeiß*.</note>, perhaps another Adam would have been created. Yet perhaps not in the **image of God** <note>original: *Bildtnus Gottes*.</note>, as those of the new islands are. There are many kinds of animals scattered here and there upon the Earth; perhaps there are also many kinds of people, of which more follows later to be explained.

Therefore, note that we are from the **slime** <term>Slime</term> <note>original: *Limo*; in Paracelsian thought, this is the "Limus Terrae," an extract of all created things.</note>, and thus we contain everything mortal within us from that slime. In the same way—as the example demonstrates—that we receive **eternal wisdom** from the **Holy Spirit**, who is sent to us through **Christ** from the Father, so too is all **natural wisdom** given to us naturally through the **stars** <term>Stars</term> <note>original: *Gestirn*; Paracelsus uses this term to describe the celestial influence that grants human intelligence and skill.</note> from the Father. In order that such wisdom and art might be fulfilled, and the wonder-works of God made manifest, Man was created for this purpose. After he was driven out of Paradise, he contemplated the knowledge of his misery; being mindful of the foresight for his descendants, he did not lie with **Eve** for a hundred years. To such an extent did the paradisiacal life differ from the worldly; and henceforth he experienced misery in his own wisdom and the future of his children. 

Thus we must live from the world in a virtuous way, just as the **new birth** <note>The spiritual rebirth through faith.</note> must have its refuge in the wisdom of Christ and take its nourishment from Christ. Furthermore, Man is also from the Earth; that same man enjoys the fruit of the Earth, the bird in the air, the fish in the sea, and is powerful over serpents and the **basilisk** <term>Basilisk</term> <note>original: *Basiliscus*; a mythical king of serpents. Paracelsus uses it here to symbolize man's intended dominion over even the most dangerous parts of nature.</note>. When God thus desired to make a man, He did so by forming him from the **slime** and leading him into Paradise, wherein he broke the commandment and was led back into the **slime of the earth** <note>original: *Limum terrae*.</note>, to endure that same property and nature of the world, and to suffer with it, as follows hereafter.

After God had created all creatures and **elements** <term>Elements</term>, all stars and creations, and everything stood according to His will, He finally undertook to make Man in such a form. He extracted the essence of the four elements together into one piece; He also extracted from the **stars** the essence of wisdom, of art, and of reason, and thus placed both essences—of the elements and the stars—together into a **mass**...

Thus, two **Bodies** <note>original: *Corpora*.</note> were made out of this Mass: the **Sidereal Body** <term>Sidereal Body</term> <note>The "astral" part of man, influenced by the stars.</note> and the **Elemental Body** <term>Elemental Body</term> <note>The physical part of man, composed of the four elements.</note>. And according to the **Light of Nature** <note>A key Paracelsian concept referring to innate human reason and the understanding of the natural world.</note>, it is called the **Fifth Essence** <term>Fifth Essence</term> <note>original: *fünffte wesen*; also known as the Quintessence, the purest extract of the elements.</note>; that is, the Mass was extracted and the **Firmament** <term>Firmament</term> <note>The heavens or the sphere of the stars.</note> and the **Elements** <note>original: *Elementa*.</note> were brought into it as one. Thus, from this it follows: that which is drawn from four is the fifth, yet the four are within it just as surely as they are in the Mother.

Regarding this, note that the Fifth Essence is the entire foundation and core of all beings and properties of the whole world. This is to say: into the hand of God came all nature, power, and property, and every essence in the upper and lower **Globe** <note>original: *Globo*; referring to the celestial and terrestrial spheres.</note>. All of these together God held in His hand **actually** <note>original: *realiter*.</note>, and out of them He formed Man after His **image** <note>original: *Bildtnus*.</note>. For when God performs a work, it is not in the manner of a **goldsmith**; rather, it is a work beyond all natural powers. The material for such was the greatest and noblest material of all His creatures: the **Secret** <term>Arcanum</term> <note>original: *Archannut* [Arcanum]; a hidden, powerful essence.</note> and being in His hand.

It is a great thing to consider: while all other things were made from nothing, Man alone was not; and God Himself made him according to His image, not from common **mud** <note>original: *Koth*; can also mean filth or refuse, emphasizing the humility of material substance.</note>, but from the extract of all creatures. And although he is indeed mud and a **dust** <note>original: *Pulffer*.</note> that the wind blows and tosses to and fro, yet all that out of which he is made is likewise "mud." For there is nothing there that is permanent; and so into the Fifth Essence came all the nature of the whole world—the sentient and the non-sentient—and was grasped together in one fist, into one Mass. This was done by Him who created Heaven and Earth, and out of that same Fifth Essence, which the Scripture calls **Slime of the Earth** <note>original: *Limum Terrae*.</note>.

Out of this **Slime** <note>original: *Limo*.</note>, the Creator of the world made the **Little World** <note>original: *kleine Welt*.</note>, the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosm</term> <note>original: *Microcosmum*; the idea that the human being is a miniature map of the entire universe.</note>, which is Man. Thus Man is the Little World, having all the properties of the world within him. Therefore he is the Microcosm; therefore he is the Fifth Essence of the Elements and of the **Stars** <note>original: *Gestirns*.</note> or Firmament, in the upper sphere and in the lower globe. Thus the **Great World** <note>The Macrocosm or the universe at large.</note> is a father to the Little World. Therefore, in the Little World there is the nature of **dragons**, the nature of **snakes**, the genus of **vipers** and **adders**, and also the nature of **wolves**, of **sheep**, etc. Also of all elements, as well as **health** and **sickness**. For every child takes after the nature of its father.

However, that the Microcosm is different from the Great World in its substance, form, and figure—this the Creator brought about so that he might have flesh and blood, and mobility within the same, according to all that from which he is made, each according to his **conception**...

For every son eats and drinks from his father and lives in his father. But because the **Basilisk** <term>Basilisk</term> <note>original: *Basiliscus*; a mythical creature whose gaze was lethal, used here as a metaphor for spiritual poison or corruption within nature.</note> is also found in the **fifth essence** <term>fifth essence</term> <note>original: *fünfften wesen*; the *Quinta Essentia*, the purest and most potent form of a substance, which contains the blueprints of all qualities.</note>, along with other poisonous, evil natures and properties, the Law was given so that we do not suck the poison of that same Basilisk into ourselves, but rather gather the honeycomb from nature. And take good note of what Christ said: "**Offspring of vipers**" <note>original Latin: *Progenies Viperarum*; a reference to Matthew 12:34.</note>, and more of the like; you should understand that the nature of every animal was present in the **slime of the earth** <note>original Latin: *Limo terrae*; the primordial material from which man was formed.</note>. And thus the damned are separated and divided from the blessed, good fifth essence—whence it came—back into their **species** <note>original Latin: *Species*.</note>, just as they were before. And note also that Christ says: I do not want them to be converted, lest I should make them blessed. That is, he does not want to make saints out of snakes, dragons, lions, wolves, and foxes, but rather put them in their stall.

However, although the Law is given to us in nature—which is the way of the Lord—it means that even if you were born with an evil nature like **Judas** <note>referring to Judas Iscariot as a symbol of an "evil birth" or predestined betrayal.</note>, you may still overcome that evil birth through the Image. For we are gods if God draws us to be His son. But Judas did not succeed in this. Therefore, let each person look at what **predestination** <note>original Latin: *Praedestinatio*; the doctrine that a person's ultimate fate is determined by God or their inherent nature.</note> does in the wolf and in the lamb. Yet sinners should take the good unto themselves, for in this way the Basilisk may become a lamb; this is where God wants us to be, and He has given us the power to arrive there through our conduct here on earth. But what shall be fulfilled regarding the damned and the **predestined** <note>original Latin: *Praedestinierten*.</note> is not my intention to describe here; well I know that the sinner is heard. As for what a sinner is, I will let that rest, as it is easily understood by everyone. It is because of both the **predestined** <note>original: *Praedestinierten*; those whom God has chosen or set on a specific path.</note> and the sinners that the law was given to us, the commandments established, and authority and the power of the sword handed over—namely, so that the **Basilisk** <term>Basilisk</term> <note>original: *Basiliscus*; in Paracelsian thought, this legendary serpent represents the poisonous, destructive potential within human nature that must be restrained.</note> might not spread too much poison. The discarded Body is as much weaker as the Fifth Essence within it is more concentrated; and since it was taken from the discarded Body, the World is diminished by that much. It was not entirely extracted, as a **medicine** <note>original: *Artney*.</note> is extracted, but only as much as was necessary for Man to exist. Enough remained so that what is left behind may still lead a life, receive nourishment, eat and drink, and possess that which pertains to the Heavens within its reason.

Thus, it is necessary to describe the manner of Adam and Eve's making, and thereafter that of the two children born from them. As has been sufficiently stated, they came from the **Slime of the Earth** <note>original: *Limo terrae*; the primal mud or dust of the ground used in creation.</note>, as a beginning of the whole world, through the Highest Artist, who is God Himself.
