But concerning Eve, know further that his wife was taken and made out of Adam himself, and was not born. He extracted the man, not the woman; but from the man, He made the woman, so that a **Concordance** <note>original: *Concordātz*; a state of fundamental harmony, unity, or agreement between two things.</note> might exist. In the same way that the man is from the Great World and cannot and may not leave it, so the woman is from the man, and cannot leave him either. For had the woman, Eve, been made from a different **material** <note>original: *Massa*</note>, their mutual desire would not have existed. But since they are of one blood and one flesh, it follows that they cannot leave one another. Furthermore, this is to be understood regarding their children, of whom there is more need to speak. # The First Book #

### D ii ###

But so that Eve’s nature may also be understood: she was made from Adam, out of his side—she belongs to his side. Yet her nature is **microcosmic** <term>Microcosmic</term> <note>original: *Microcosmisch*; from the idea that a human being is a "little world" containing the essence of the entire universe.</note>, just like the man’s—and even more so, because there is a distinction between women and men. This distinction is found in the fact that God gave humans the **procreative power** <note>original: *geberend Krafft*.</note> and placed it in man and woman, each according to their natural essence. They differ from one another only insofar as one is a man and the other a woman. Otherwise, however, they are of the same kind of **Machine of the World** <term>Machine of the World</term> <note>original: *Machinae mundi*; the universe viewed as a grand, divinely designed mechanism.</note>. 

Therefore, to write of children: they are no longer made directly by the hand of God, but are commanded to be born through the creatures of Nature. This is how God wills it to be from now on; therefore, He has joined man and woman together so that they shall procreate, and no one may separate them. Thus, from here on, it is necessary to explain the children born of women and men. For the hand of God made the first human and gave him his wife, who was **unborn** <note>Referring to the biblical account of Eve being created from Adam's rib rather than being born of a mother.</note>; thereafter, humanity was handed over to the order of Nature. 

This means a process has been established within Nature through which humans are no longer "made" [directly], but shall be born, one from the other. For only Adam belonged [directly] to God’s [handiwork]. The reason I point this out is that, as mentioned, man is composed of the **Elements and the Stars** <note>original: *Elementen und des Gestirns*.</note>. And just as the first man was made of these, so too is every child born of them—just like the father and mother—earthly and stellar. This happens not through the direct hand of God, but through birth. 

For God has ordained that Nature, rather than His own hand, should henceforth bring forth His children naturally. In the same way, a grain of corn is sown in a field; that grain **decays** <note>original: *faulet*; in early modern biology, the "putrefaction" or breaking down of a seed was seen as the essential first step for new life to sprout.</note> and produces more grain, far more than its original number. This happens through the power and the union that the grain and the **Great World** <note>The Macrocosm or the universe at large.</note> have with one another. Thus was the beginning first created, and then handed over to Nature. 

Therefore, in the same way I have just described, you should also understand the procreation of humans. The first grain was created; those that followed grew through the elements and the stars. It is the same with the human form: nothing can be born without this **decay** <note>original: *faulung*.</note>, and all things must be directed toward **digestion** <term>Digestion</term> <note>original: *digestion*; here referring to a biological or alchemical ripening process within the body.</note> until the appointed time of **nativity** <note>original: *natiuitet*; birth.</note>. 

So it is with man, who cannot be born otherwise than as the grain in the field. His seed is the **sperm** <note>original: *sperma*.</note> which God has ordained, and the field is the **womb** <term>Womb</term> <note>original: *matrix*; the generative environment or uterus.</note> in which the "digestion" must occur. After the decay, the human being comes to be; and this decay happens through the influence of the Great World—through the elements and the stars in the father and mother, acting as the instruments which Nature uses for this purpose...

# The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus [Paracelsus]

I reveal this chapter to you concerning the origin of mankind as it has been recorded: that God created two types of creatures, the **substantial** and the **non-substantial** <note>original: *Substantialem/ vñ nit Substantialem*</note>. Know then the reason: that God desired to have a creature that would be tangible, having blood and flesh. This same blood and flesh is taken from the **Body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note> of the four elements, transformed from that same substance into the substance of man—much like one who takes a white thing and makes it black, green, or red, etc. For all things are like "white" in the hand of God; He may make of them what He will. This is not like humans, who can make nothing else out of wood but must let it remain wood, or metals remain metal, stones remain stone, etc. God, however, can make bread out of stone; thus He can transform the four elements into flesh and blood.

Therefore, take note as has been mentioned: that man, in terms of his substance, is an **extract** <term>extract</term> <note>original: *außzug* — in Paracelsian thought, this refers to a "quintessence" or a refined distillation of the physical world.</note> of the four elements, and this same extract became an artist within blood and flesh. Since this was the Divine intention, God also created and ordained man's seed in such a way as to make "Sons of God" out of Adam's children, according to His will, as He desired to have them in blood and flesh. And the **residue** <note>original: *Residuum* — the leftover material after an extraction.</note> remained as a **subject** <note>original: *Subiecto*</note> to this extract; that is, the **fifth essence** <term>fifth essence</term> <note>original: *fünfft wesen* — the "quinta essentia," the purest part of a substance that governs the other four elements.</note> must use the others from which it comes. And because man is made from them, and made in the image of God by God Himself, he is therefore powerful over the four elements from which he is made; they must be obedient to his image, and he is lord over them. It is not that the **primordial slime** <term>primordial slime</term> <note>original: *Limus* — refers to the "dust of the ground" from Genesis, which Paracelsus views as a complex extract of the whole universe.</note> is the master, but rather that which is made from it is the master—the son over the father.

Now take note of the aforementioned indication: that the "true man" is the **Firmament** <term>Firmament</term> <note>original: *Gestirn* — literally "the stars." Paracelsus believes the human mind and talents are an "astral body" derived from the heavens.</note>. For neither hands nor feet make a man; rather, natural wisdom and natural art alone make the man. Therefore, man should not seek within his physical body that which the body merely possesses. For whatever concerns the physical body is nothing; rather, he should take up that which is invisible and intangible within the body. That is the **Light of Nature** <term>Light of Nature</term> <note>original: *Liecht der Natur* — the innate intelligence and intuition God placed in the natural world.</note>, the natural wisdom which God placed into the **star** <note>original: *Sydus*</note>, and from the **star** <note>original: *Sydere*</note> into man. Just as one learns to write or read from a schoolmaster—in that regard, the hands and feet are nothing [without the instruction]. But now, these arts cannot be perfected without hands and feet, without ears and eyes, etc. For through the eyes we look into nature, etc. They are **instruments** <note>original: *Instrumenta*</note> through which we accomplish that which is within us, given to us by God as a natural gift. Therefore they are as instruments, without which no man may be created. Since these things must now happen through such means, man is created out of the elements and formed after the image of God into the form

->and form, most fit for use in that which God desires of him; and no more skillful form could be, nor be found, than that of Man alone.<- For his shape and form are skillfully suited for every gift of nature—for the arts and other things—to be used and handled, so that he may do and make with his tangible limbs what God does in the spirit, or what an angel or a spirit does. This the human does with his body and with his **instruments** <term>instruments</term> <note>original: *Instrumenten* — In this context, Paracelsus refers to both the physical limbs and the tools humans use to interact with the world.</note>. For this is the distinction between a spirit and a human: that the spirit is without instruments, whereas the human acts through instruments, insofar as it concerns natural capability. As an **example** <note>original: *Exemplum*</note>: God makes a house; a human can also make one. God has hands and feet in the **Word** <note>original: *im wort* — referring to the creative power of the Divine Logos</note>; the human has them as physical limbs. Also, a human makes another human healthy through effort, which he must bring into the work with his body; God does so with His word without hands or feet. A human walks with feet; a spirit walks without feet. Thus, through the limbs, the art and wisdom of the **Light of Nature** <term>Light of Nature</term> <note>original: *Natürlichen Liechts* — a central Paracelsian concept referring to the innate intuition and secular knowledge granted by God to understand the physical world.</note> are fulfilled, just as the example demonstrates: God wills that trees grow upon the earth, along with other fruits, pears, and similar creatures.

Now, if His will is to be done, the wood must first be present from which the pears grow, for God desires them to come from the wood. It is not that the wood *is* the pear, but the pear is like a spirit within the wood until **corporality** <note>original: *Corporalitet* — the state of having a physical, tangible body.</note> has occurred. And because the pear must have a tangible body, the **elements** <note>original: *Elementa*</note> have been **transmuted** <term>transmuted</term> into wood. That which is tangible has its **body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note> from the other two elements, and everything that is to enter such a body is first a spirit—but not a pure spirit, for such a thing takes on no body. Rather, it is a sub-elemental spirit; this spirit receives and establishes the physical form. For instance, a seed is a natural spirit, but when it is sown, a tree grows out of it; now it exists within its body. Understand the pear from the tree in the same way: it is an elemental spirit at first, and afterwards material in its corporality. Thus, the body of the pear is given out of the two elements, along with this transformation.

In this same way, God now wills that those things should happen which were created by Him in the **Firmament** <note>original: *Firmament* — the sphere of the stars which, in alchemy, influences human talents and the "arts."</note>, such as the Arts, Music, **Mechanical Arts** <note>original: *Artes mechanicae*</note>, **Faculties** <note>original: *Facultates* — specialized branches of knowledge or professions</note>, and various **Religions**. These must happen through a human, as has been mentioned, just as the pear comes through the tree. For there must be something through which the **stars** <note>original: *Gestirn*</note> act, and that is the human alone. Therefore, he is created in such a form so that all the **Great Works of Nature** <note>original: *Magnalia naturae* — the hidden wonders and powers within the natural world.</note> may visibly occur through him and be brought into a physical reality—he who is **forged** from the elements into the form of blood and flesh.

### The Sage Philosophy of Theophrastus Paracelsus ###

->D iiij<-

the maker of all hidden things—and in addition, even what man himself is—is not seen, not even by himself. For just as it was with Jesus Christ: the Jews accepted Jesus, but they did not accept him as being the Christ; that was invisible. It is the same within man; no one sees what the man truly is or what is inside him, except for what his **works** <note>original: *Werck* — in Paracelsus’s view, "works" are not just moral deeds but the tangible results of a person’s craft, art, or scientific discovery.</note> build up. Therefore, man should be in constant action so that he may learn to know himself—what God has given him—and so that others may also see his works and praise and laud God, from whom all things come, are created, and are given. 

He who does not seek hides his treasure in the earth and buries his coin <note>A reference to the Parable of the Talents in Matthew 25:14–30; Paracelsus argues that failing to use one's natural talents is a sin against God's design.</note>. For Christ also did this, making himself known through his works, as he himself spoke: "If you will not believe me—that I am the one you do not see, that is, that I am the Son of God—then believe my works." This is as much as to say: "My works are those which no one is capable of performing except the Son of God alone." In the same way, we should also make ourselves manifest, so that the unbelievers may see in God what God works through man. 

For Christ has given us an example which we should follow, and through our works provide testimony regarding ourselves; for by them we are recognized, and they will follow us as witnesses. Thus, Christ was recognized only as a man. That is a judgment according to what is visible, and according to what is visible, no true judgment can be given. For one man is like another; everyone has ten fingers, everyone has two feet; thus, man should not be judged in such a state—as to who or what he is—but rather he is known for who he is by his works and the powers that proceed from him. By this same means, we know who the Son of God is, what prophets or apostles are, what saints or teachers are, and what comes from God or from nature. 

Thus, through works are those men recognized in whom the <term>Light of Nature</term> <note>original: *liecht der Natur* — the innate capacity given by God to humans to understand the world through reason, science, and experience.</note> resides—what is in each one, and for what purpose nature uses each individual. Thus, through all people, all the <term>mysteries</term> <note>original: *Misteria*</note> of God are revealed in an angelic and natural <term>philosophy</term> <note>original: *Philosophia*</note> and <term>astronomy</term> <note>original: *Astronomia*</note>, so that everything may be made manifest, whether it be in heaven or on earth, in the hells, or in all creatures. For nothing is so secret that it shall not be made manifest. No one recognizes Christ except the one who is drawn to him by the Father; he who is drawn to him is then taught by him. Likewise, no one is taught by the **stars** <note>original: *Gestirn* — refers to the "sidereal" or celestial influence that Paracelsus believed granted humans their specific professional skills and wisdom.</note> unless he is drawn into the stars; he is then taught by the stars. And no one is drawn to those ends unless he comes from them—that is to say, what is of God and of the heavens...

# The First Book / #

...speaks of nature/ and of heaven/ what is of nature/ that speaks of nature/ Just as what is of the devil/ treats of the devil/ therefore we should know/ that both philosophies <note>In Paracelsus’s worldview, "philosophy" refers to the study of the inner workings of both the physical world and the divine realm.</note>/ through man/ are recognized with their powers/ accomplished and completed. Namely the eternal and the natural/ and both may well stand together/ for they both proceed from one God/ and man also from the same. Everything that is now from God/ man may well use/ and complete/ for that purpose God has created him/ and all things in heaven and earth. But man did not receive the form of other creatures, only a human form; however, the essence of those same **species** <note>original: "Specierum"</note> is distributed within him. And even if there is perhaps one virtue in such vermin, there are ten vices alongside it. For what use is the virtue of a wolf—that it provides a good wolf-pelt—when there is nothing else good about it? Would it not be better for us to keep geese and chickens and do without the fox-pelt? What is the use of a virtue that must be maintained with so many vices? Humans are the same: they are good in one thing, but then in ten or twenty vices they are also evil and worthless. That is to say, they are not perfect humans; they mix human virtue with the animal **prime essence**. Now, all these things are created, and however they may be, it is the will of God.

Now, the reason I point this out is this: what does it benefit a man to be pleasing to a woman—which is a virtue, for she should be devoted to her husband—if she has many more vices against the man that destroy such devotion? What use is it if one is only useful to oneself and no one else? What use is the virtue that remains in that person alone, when all things should spring forth for the benefit of one's neighbor, even from our very substance? This is what God wills.

...own kind, without the assistance of the other. Thus it is also to be understood here: the **elemental body** eats and drinks; it needs nothing from the **sidereal body** <term>Syderischen Leib: the "astral" or star-derived body that governs the mind and senses</term> for this, for it does not eat for the sidereal body, but only for itself, maintained by the elemental realms from below. So also a woman eats for herself, and not for the man; the man for himself, and not for the woman.

Thus the body desires bodily works; it desires them for itself, not for the sidereal body, and it builds the elemental body through them, but it does not build the sidereal body. Therefore, **Venus** <note>Referring to the astrological influence of the planet Venus, traditionally associated with lust and procreation.</note> has nothing to do with that matter. The multiplying of the world—that is, the bearing of children—comes from the **corporeal elements**, not from the stars. For whatever is worked there concerns the **corporality** <term>Corporalitet: physical, material existence</term>; now, whatever concerns corporality proceeds from the corporeal elements. 

Therefore, Venus cannot do it; rather, the <insert>voluptuousness</insert> of man does it, not Venus at all. For Venus has one kind of body, and the elements have another. How then can the intangible govern the physical, since the <term>sperma</term> <note>The reproductive seed.</note> comes from the lower elements and not from the upper? How can a spirit make flesh and blood? How can flesh and blood make a spirit? 

Just as little can happen here as has been wrongly supposed. Take an example for yourselves: Man makes a man, but he does not make the soul; the soul also does not make the man. Each has its own particular **creation** and **fabrication**, and yet it is one thing and one man. 

But I wish to instruct you regarding an error held by the astronomers: they believe that just as a spark falling from the flint-and-steel into tinder ignites it so that it burns, so also Venus should be an "igniter" in the elementated body. This is not the case, nor can it be. The reason is: that same spark must have a physical effect within it, and it would have to be something that is flesh and blood. Consider your example of the tinder: the spark from the steel is fire; when it falls into the tinder, it makes the tinder into what the spark itself is—that is, it is fire, and the tinder becomes fire. 

Therefore, in elemental works, there can be no **sidereal co-operation** <note>original Latin: "Coadiutorium," meaning a helping force or external assistance.</note>. Rather, the elementated body cares for itself in what concerns its own body. Likewise, the sidereal body cares for itself in the same way. It is indeed true, however, that the senses and thoughts are governed by the sidereal body. Thus, through the sidereal body, an **object** <note>original Latin: "Obiectum," meaning something presented to the mind or senses.</note> can be presented to the elemental body—such as a woman standing before a man. But such objects generate nothing; they provide **occasions** <note>original Latin: "Occasiones," or opportunities/triggers.</note>, but they are like a shadow on the wall: the shadow indicates a corporality and comes from it, yet the shadow itself is nothing.

Now further, to declare the **slime of the earth** <note>original Latin: "Limum terrae." In Paracelsus's cosmology, this is the "Mysterium Magnum," the primordial material of the universe from which both man and the world were extracted.</note>, as you have until now...

<summary>Paracelsus argues for a strict separation between the physical (elemental) body and the astral (sidereal) body, asserting that physical functions like eating and reproduction are purely elemental and not caused by the stars or Venus.</summary>
<keywords>elemental body, sidereal body, Venus, reproduction, astrology, corporality, Limum terrae, creation, soul and body</keywords>

This page continues the philosophical explanation of man's composition as the "slime of the earth" (Limus terrae), moving from the division of the two bodies to the unified material origin of the human being.</meta>

# The First Book #

...understood <note>Completing the word "vbergestanden" from the previous page.</note> how he is a **mass** <note>original: *Massa*; refers to a primal, undifferentiated lump of matter.</note> and an extracted **fifth essence** <note>original: *quintum Esse*; the "quintessence," the purest and most concentrated form of a substance.</note> from the heavens and the elements. Thus it is further necessary to know why it is called the **slime of the earth** <note>original: *Limus terrae*</note> and not the "slime of the firmament," or "slime of the elements," or "slime of water, fire, or air," or why not "slime of the world," since everything was nevertheless together in one mass. 

The reason is that the earth contains and is the **mass** in itself; the others are not masses. Therefore, it is the nature of the mass—which is to say—that the earth is the ground and **center** <note>original: *Centrum*</note> of all creatures; and [man] is taken directly from the center in which all creatures walk. It has been called **Earth** <note>original: *Terra*</note>, and the Earth is the mass. 

Just as a fire is nothing in itself—the wood is the fire <note>Paracelsus means the wood provides the physical substance that allows the fire to manifest.</note>—yet one does not speak of the wood, but of the fire; there is always one thing that retains the name. Similarly, when many waters flow together into one, they all lose their [individual] names; one alone retains it, and in essence they all come together. When they all come together, they have only one name, which is **the Sea**; as if one were to say, "He made it out of the sea"—that is, out of all the waters that flow into it. 

From this follows the name **slime of the earth**. You should understand the earth in the same way as indicated for the sea: that all things run into it and are buried there. And just as all things are consumed in the sea, so are the creatures consumed in the earth, in their **influences** <note>original: *Influentijs*; refers to the spiritual or astrological forces acting upon a body.</note>, and every **body** <note>original: *Corpus*</note> is consumed by its mother. 

In the same way, wax is a mass in which all medicines are held and made together into a **plaster** <term>Cerotum: a wax-based medical dressing or cerate.</term>. Just as the **ingredients** <note>original: *Ingredientia*</note> and the wax are one thing, and become so, and retain the name "plaster," so it is with the "slime of the earth." Thus, the Earth has been that same mass in place of the wax, into which the ingredients of heaven and earth have been **mixed and joined** <note>original: *comistiert vnd coniungiert*</note>. 

Man is made from this **composite** <note>original: *Composito*</note>. Therefore, as I have described man’s origin and **incarnation** <term>Menschwerdung: literally "becoming-human"; the process of being formed into a person.</term> until now, all of you who deal with human beings should observe him well and not value him so lightly. For he did not spring from a stone; he is indeed made from filth, but such a mixture and composite was in that same filth that no one can fully fathom or reach the end of that noble composition. 

Therefore, you physicians should consider that you must be **true doctors** and not **false doctors** <note>original: *veri Medici* and *Pseudomedici*</note>. Do not deal with the **universal** through your **particulars** <note>original: *Particularibus in vniuersum*; a warning against using narrow, specific remedies to treat the complex, whole nature of the human being.</note>. Instead, you should know what is perfectly appropriate for a physician, and not so lightly or recklessly hand over God's creature—which He created in His own image—to the **butcher's block** <term>Fleischbanck: literally a "meat-bench" or shambles; implies treating the human body as mere meat without spiritual value.</term> for the sake of greed and envy, [betraying] your own honor and oath...

<summary>Paracelsus explains that man is called "slime of the earth" because the Earth acts as the central "mass" or container for all celestial and elemental ingredients. He warns physicians to respect the divine complexity of the human composition rather than treating patients as mere physical matter for profit.</summary>

<keywords>Limus terrae, quintessence, macrocosm and microcosm, medical ethics, composition of man, elements, alchemy of the body</keywords>

### The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus <note>original: *Philosophiae Sagacis Theophr.*; Paracelsus’s title for his work on how the stars and elements influence human nature.</note> ###

...surrendered <note>Completing a thought from the previous page regarding the surrender of human reason to hidden forces.</note>, and the undertaking, in which you must recognize yourselves as ignorant in your own consciences, and that your art is like one who plays in a bran-tub <note>original: *Prenten*; a metaphor for blind chance, like reaching into a barrel of flour and bran—one might pull out something white (pure) or something black (impure).</note>; if he does not hit white, he hits black, or he burns; it is good and evil mixed together. The authorities should also be mindful to approach man with a well-considered spirit, for since the scripture says that the house-father wanted to chop down the tree because it bore no fruit, what did he find in counsel? He should not do it; he should let it stand longer to see if it would yet bear fruit. Thus one should not weigh man so carelessly and hold him in such low regard, he who is so high and well-made, and comes from the highest, from whom all creatures come. For it must not happen precisely today that what God has given to man comes out, but in its own time. He did not want Judas to betray Christ before Christ's time. It is one way today, another way tomorrow. Time gives much, and completes the **gift** <term>donum: a divine talent or natural capacity bestowed by God</term>. Unless it were a tree from which no fruit ever came. For when one is a child, he speaks as a child; but when he becomes old, it is another matter.

Take an example from a potter: when someone breaks only one pot of his, he cannot easily be without anger and revenge; it vexes him and insults him. If more are broken, they must be paid for. How much dearer then will the reckoning be from the highest good <note>Refers to God as the *Summum Bonum*.</note>, that His **handiwork** <note>original: *Handtarbeit*; refers to the human body and soul as the crafted product of God.</note> is thus broken? Therefore let each one take good heed of what killing he has within him, be it in wars, murders, or slayings. You should judge the Son of Man rightly. Also, the **pastors** <term>Seelsorger: literally "soul-carers"; the clergy</term> are to be admonished much more, but at this point—since I am treating only of the natural—I shall omit it. 

With this, I will conclude the origin of man and his unification with the outer world, concerning the natural part of man, and how he is placed among the others, and made into a whole man. It follows hereafter in the second **section** <term>Paragrapho: a chapter or distinct division of a text</term>. So much have I mentioned here in this part, as far as it has touched upon and includes the natural. And all this happens

# The First Book /
## The Fourth Chapter.
### Concerning how many types of Astronomy there are / how many orders / and Processes / and how the same should be recognized / along with their members / and how these same members should be divided into their species.

Since I have endeavored to describe the influences <note>original: *Influents*; the celestial forces believed to flow from the stars into the physical world</note>, concordances <note>original: *Concordants*; the hidden correspondences between the macrocosm (universe) and microcosm (humanity)</note>, and harmonies <note>original: *Conuenients*; the suitability of specific remedies to specific diseases</note> of external things in treating <note>original: *tingiern*; literally "to tint" or "to dye," an alchemical term for transforming or healing a substance</note> and acting upon diseases <note>original: *Morbis*</note>, I have seen fit to divide them into figures, so that the four external tinctures <term>extraneae tincturae: medicinal forces or spiritual essences that originate outside the human body</term> may be understood. Regarding this, you should know that it is very necessary to recognize the differences between these four, and to use not just one figure, but several in sequence—each one derived from the other, with each serving as an interpreter for the one preceding it. This is shown in the most intelligible way so that you may have a pure, clear, and common explanation of all subsequent effects for a localized understanding. That is to say: to establish a figure with its members <note>original: *membris*; the various branches or components of a field of study</note>—meaning how many members each type of Astronomy contains—and furthermore to describe another figure for the species <note>original: *Species*; the specific subdivisions or types</note> of those same members. Following this, a specific explanation of each article will be provided, through which it may be discovered what each influence is, what each member is, and what each species is. In this way, Philosophy <note>original: *Philosophia*; here referring to the study of the secrets of nature and God</note> may be most thoroughly experienced and learned, showing in what order each one stands and is utilized.

->Thus follows hereafter the<-
->first figure.<-

Now, furthermore, it is necessary to know the *species* <note>types or sub-categories</note> of the Members—into how many species each Member is divided—so that the Members may be understood all the better and more easily. Therefore, understand me through this illustration regarding which members and species <note>original: *membra vnd species*; Paracelsus uses these terms to mean the main branches and specific sub-types of his philosophical system.</note> I place and indicate within Astronomy; it has seemed best to me to arrange them in such an order. For he who wishes to be a perfect Astronomer <note>In Paracelsus’s vocabulary, an "Astronomer" is not just a scientist of stars, but a sage who understands the entire relationship between the heavens and humanity.</note> must necessarily understand and recognize them. For the sake of greater understanding, there follows an explanation of what the members and their species signify within themselves, so that the arts of these members may be learned more easily; and the explanation follows hereafter.

## Interpretation of Magic and its species,
## What Magic is, and what a Mage is.

Understand what Magic and a Mage <note>original: *Magica vnd Magus*</note> are in this way: Magic is divided into six species. Now, the beginning of Magic is an interpretation of unnatural signs—to recognize them as God places them supernaturally in the heavens, and yet how they appear and are recognized "naturally" among others, such as the Star of the East over Bethlehem. And in the same way that Christ walked upon the Earth as a man among other men, so too did that Star stand among other stars. And just as Christ was recognized only by his own followers, so these stars are recognized only by the Mages. Thus, Mages are the interpreters of such supernatural signs in the heavens, just as the Apostles were those who recognized Christ; they are appointed to interpret the Word. As Christ says: "There shall be signs in the sun, moon, stars, etc." Thus, the Mages are also the interpreters of all Prophets and of the Apocalyptic revelation. This is the first species of the magical art, and it is called notable magic <note>original: *insignis Magica*</note>.

Furthermore, there is another species of Magic; it teaches the forming of living bodies <note>original: *Corpora viuentia*</note>, as happened in the times of Moses, and it is a transformation from one body into another. Although that transformation did not happen through Magic as it is understood here, but rather through Magic according to the process of the "fourth Astronomy." Otherwise, the species is Transfiguration <note>original: *Transfiguratio*</note>, in the same way that Christ was transfigured and became radiant like the sun. Magic is also to be understood in this way here, and this species is called by its proper name transfigurative magic <note>original: *Magica transfiguratiua*</note>.

Moving further, the third species teaches how to create words which possess all the power that herbs receive from the heavens. As an example: everything that the physician is able to extract from medicine, such [power...]

# The First Book
<meta>catchword: The</meta>

...these species are able to be perfected through words. For whatever the natural order provides of its own accord, art provides as well. And this species is called by its proper name: **Characteristica** <note>The art of using signs, symbols, or "characters" to achieve effects through the power of words.</note>.

Furthermore, note that the fourth species teaches how to make **Gamaheu** <note>original: *Gamaheu*; in Paracelsus's philosophy, these are talismans or stones—sometimes naturally occurring—that possess supernatural virtues.</note>, which perform everything that natural instruments are capable of. Just as a key opens a lock, a sword cuts wounds, or a suit of armor protects against stabbing and shooting—the fourth species of the magical art is able to do such things through art invisibly, whereas nature does them visibly. And this species is called by its proper name: **Gamadreos** <note>A technical term used by Paracelsus to describe the animation or magical empowerment of physical objects to act on their own.</note>.

Furthermore, the fifth species is able to create **Images** <note>original: *Imagines*; these are wax or metal effigies used in sympathetic magic.</note>, and those who are contained within such images become like them. Thus, whatever can be naturally inflicted upon a human being, Magic is also able to accomplish—making a person crooked, or lame, etc., blinding them, and bringing them to **impotence** <note>original: *ad impotentiam*</note>. Nature is capable of doing this naturally. It is also capable of making some healthy again. This fifth species is capable of all of this, and is called by its proper name: **One into the other** <note>original: *Altera in alteram*; referring to the transfer of a condition or state from a magical image to a living person.</note>. Magic is also able to act so that one may hear a voice from across the sea, so that one in the **West** <note>original: *Occident*</note> may speak with one who dwells in the **East** <note>original: *Orient*</note>. For whereas nature is capable of hearing a voice at a hundred paces, this species can do so over a hundred German miles.

Furthermore, just as nature is able, through natural forces, to allow a messenger or a horse to run or travel in a month, this species is able to accomplish the same in a single day. And in summary, what nature is able to do in a year, this art can accomplish in a month, even in the growth of the earth's plants. And this species is called by its proper name: **The Cabalistic Art** <note>original: *Ars Cabalistica*; here Paracelsus uses the term to describe the acceleration of natural processes or the manipulation of time and space, rather than just mystical text interpretation.</note>.

These six species that have now been mentioned constitute the **Magical Art** <note>original: *artem Magicam*</note>; in Latin they are called the **Arts of Wisdom** <note>original: *artes Sapientiae*</note>. For these six species were regarded by those in **Sheba** <note>original: *Saba*</note> in the East, and in the island of **Tarshish** <note>original: *Tharsis*</note>, as the highest wisdom given by God to man in this mortal life. And only the **Sages** <note>original: *Sapientes*</note> who possessed this knowledge were called **Mages** <note>original: *Magos*</note>. Furthermore, all other mortal wisdom was diminished and held to be weaker, while Magic alone was held to be the most excellent and invincible wisdom.

# What Necromancy is, what a Necromancer is, and what should be understood and contained within all its species.

So that you may rightly understand **Necromancy** <note>original: *Nigromantia*; in Paracelsus's system, this is not merely "black magic" but the study of the mortal remains and spirits that persist after death.</note> and the **Necromancer**, note that Necromancy is divided into five species. Whoever knows and understands these five species understands Necromancy and is a Necromancer. It is the second member of **Astronomy** <note>For Paracelsus, Astronomy is the study of the "sidereal" or star-born part of man.</note>. And the first foundation of this member is as follows: When a person dies, and the eternal and the mortal are separated from each other, two mortal spirits remain on Earth which the person leaves behind: the **elementic** and the **sidereal** <note>The "elementic" spirit belongs to the physical body (earthly elements), while the "sidereal" spirit is the astral body or mind that came from the stars.</note>. Now follows the knowledge of the first species: whoever recognizes these two spirits, what they are, and knows their property, essence, and nature, that person knows the first species of Necromancy. It is to be understood in this way: just as an astronomer recognizes a person—how they are disposed and natured, what their character, desire, mind, and will are—or as a doctor may recognize such things, so he who recognizes the spirits of a deceased person in the manner described is perfect in the first species. Its proper name is **Knowledge of mortal spirits** <note>original: *Cognitio mortalium*</note>.

Furthermore, the second species is to be understood thus: whoever can work with, trade with, and command those same mortal spirits so that they fulfill his business, knows the second species of Necromancy. It is to be understood in the same way as when a master works with and commands his servant, who must then perform that task. Whatever is possible for a servant to do in such a manner—provided they are servants and not masters—should be considered according to what his mind was while he was living. And this species is called by its proper name: **The torment of the night** <note>original: *Tortura noctis*; this refers to the compelling or "torturing" of spirits to act during the night.</note>.

Now, further concerning the third species, note that such hovering spirits are born from the **Sidere** <note>The firmament or the stars.</note> in many ways and forms, and they exist and die while hovering in the **Chaos** <note>In Paracelsian physics, "Chaos" refers to the atmosphere or the air as a medium between heaven and earth.</note>. That is, they are born and then consumed again by death; others are born and consumed again, just as we humans on Earth are born and others die. He who recognizes these spirits, just as a doctor recognizes herbs, and can use them as a doctor uses herbs, knows the third species of Necromancy. Its proper name is **Living Meteorology** <note>original: *Metheorica viuens*; referring to the study of living entities within the atmospheric "meteors" or vapors.</note>.

Now, further concerning the fourth species: know that whoever is able to reach into a human being without injuring them—that is, an opening—in the same way as one who reaches into water and takes out a fish, and the water receives no hole; or like one who places something into the water, and it also receives no hole; that person understands the fourth species of **Nigromancy** <note>original: *Nigromantiae*; here referring to a type of "spiritual surgery" or the manipulation of matter through the astral body.</note>. This means he may reach into the body and take something out, or reach in and place something inside. And its rightful name is **Nigromantic Closing** <note>original: *Clausura Nigromantica*</note>.

Therefore, note for the fifth species: he who can and knows how to make a visible body invisible and to conceal it, just as the night with its darkness makes a person invisible, or as if someone were concealed by a wall or the like—since nature and art can make a visible thing invisible through such a medium—so the fifth species of **Nigromancy** is able to conceal a visible body with an invisible one. He who can do this understands the fifth species of **Nigromancy**, and its rightful name is **Nigromantic Blinding** <note>original: *Obcaecatio Nigromanticae*</note>. Thus, know that these five species make a complete **Nigromancer**, and he operates through natural forces. And although these things are hidden from the **lesser light of nature** <note>original: *Minori naturae lumini*; refers to ordinary human reason or physical observation.</note>, they are nonetheless revealed to the **Greater Light of Nature** <note>original: *Lumini Naturae maiori*; refers to the intuitive or divine insight into the inner workings of the cosmos.</note>. Such is **Nigromancy**, and such is the **Nigromancer**.

### What **Necromancy** <note>original: *Nectromantia*; Paracelsus distinguishes this from *Nigromantia*. While the latter deals with astral bodies, *Nectromantia* here focuses on divining secrets through visions or spirits.</note> and what a **Necromancer** is, and their interpretation along with their species.

**A**lso, further note concerning **Necromancy**; it is divided into fourteen parts. Whoever is instructed in these fourteen parts may well use the third **branch of Astronomy** <note>original: *Membrum Astronomiae*</note>. Now know that there are several species, namely **Visions** <note>original: *Visiones*</note>. Regarding these, know the foundation through this example: Just as a lord has a servant, and all his secrets are entrusted to that servant by the lord—now, if one wishes to know the lord's secrets, and the lord does not reveal them himself, it must be revealed through others; thus it must be experienced and recognized through such a servant. To that end, it is proper to investigate the lord's secrets through the one to whom they are secretly entrusted. In this way, understand **Necromancy**: that the secrets of men, and that which they hide, are also known to those who possess such knowledge.

### The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus <note>original: *Philosophiae Sagacis Theophr.*</note>

...not only so that one might imagine, because no one is with him, that he alone knows a thing; rather, there is still something that we humans do not see, which is with us in all our hidden words and works. This "something" can speak with a person and knows how to deal with them; it searches out everything that the person believes to be entirely locked away. Now, there are many species in this branch; however, understand only two ways. Thus, there are only two processes in this branch, even though there are many species; they are completed in two forms. And it is solely an art that discovers the secrets of men, as much and as far as it is possible to know outside of their hearts. For example: whatever a person allows to come further than staying within himself—that which is now already in another's mouth—is not hidden from this art. Whatever he also performs physically likewise cannot be secret. From this it follows: whatever comes before the mouth and out of the hand is manifest to these **Flagae**, and Nectromancers may learn of it.

Now, for an explanation of how the species should be understood: it has been stated that there are only two processes through which such secrets are learned, the visible and the invisible. Regarding how they are to be brought to the point of revealing such secrets—as is well known—one must speak with them according to their pleasure or bring them to it by force, in the same way as a **Secretary** <note>original: *Secretarius*; used here in the sense of a confidential clerk or keeper of secrets.</note> who may be overcome through kindness or through ill-treatment. Now, there are many ways understood to inquire of the **Flaga**, yet the process is one and the same. Nothing is so secret that it shall not be made manifest. If secrets are to be thus revealed, it is necessary that the one who spoke them has made a path through which they may be made manifest. Thus, the art of **Nectromancy** follows: that these **Flagae** must be obedient to the power of this art, and through it, they make things visible through a **Mirror**, **Glasses**, **Coals**, etc. <note>original: *Spiegel, Prillen, Koln*; traditional tools of "scrying" or divination used to focus the mind or trap astral reflections.</note>—and not only themselves, but also that which was hidden by the person to whom the **Flaga** belongs. And where such a thing is not requested visibly through the art, it must nonetheless happen invisibly through their figure...

### What Astrology is, and what an Astrologer is, and what their powers are, along with their types <note>original: *Speciebus*</note>.

To recognize what **Astrology** and what an **Astrologer** is, note briefly such an example: In the same way that one may experience and recognize how here on Earth people run amongst each other—one here, the other there, one right, the other wrong—so you should also know that just as there is a running amongst men, so it is also in the **Firmament** <term>Firmament: the sphere of the stars and the heavens</term>. He who recognizes such running of the stars as well as the running of people amongst each other may well boast of **Astrology**. Yet more is required: that he knows what each one has as an intention in its course, like someone who sends a messenger, and the messenger promises to complete <note>catchword: volendt</note> that same task; now that person knows what the messenger intends to do. Thus should the **Astrologer** also know what work each star takes upon itself, so that he knows the intention of the stars as well as the intentions of men. He who knows such things is an even better **Astrologer** than he who only knows how they run amongst each other. It also belongs to this study to know what they may accomplish and what they may not. For man looks upon much that he cannot complete. Thus you should also understand in the **Firmament** that much is started by the stars that may not—

# The First Book
## What the Signatum and the Signator are, and what the Signature is together with its types.

<image-desc>Ornamental decorative initial 'N' with intricate scrollwork and floral patterns.</image-desc>

There is nothing that Nature has not marked, and through these signs one can recognize what is marked within the thing itself. Thus, there are four **types** <term>types: original: *Species*; the specific categories or branches of the study of signatures</term> that encompass all **signatures** <term>signatures: original: *Signatur*; the outward physical marks or signs that reveal an object's inner purpose, character, or medicinal use</term> within them; and he who recognizes and understands these four may well recognize the **mind** <note>original: *gemůt*; referring to a person’s inner disposition, temperament, or soul-life</note> of man. To understand these signs, know this instruction: The stars have their course, and by that same course they are recognized. In humans, it is also thus, only with the difference that they give man **fixed lines** <note>original: *lineas Fixas*; permanent physical markings on the body, such as those on the palms or face</note> through which one sees and recognizes what the course is. Just as the course of the stars is **tempered** <note>original: *complexionieret*; formed according to a specific elemental temperament or "complexion"</note>, so also are those lines tempered which are like unto it.

Furthermore, understand also this example: as you see that every herb grows in the form that is equal to its nature, so also is man led into that same form which looks like his nature. And as the form indicates what that herb is, so also the **Signatum** <term>Signatum: original: *Signatum*; "The Signed"—the physical body or object that bears the marks of its inner essence</term> indicates who that man is. This happens not according to name, lineage, or the like, but according to the **property** <note>original: *eigenschafft*; the inherent quality or essential characteristic</note> that is within the man. And the art of **Signata** <note>the study of signed things</note> teaches how to give the right names to each thing according to how it is innate to it. Not that a wolf should be called a sheep, nor a dove a fox, but that each receives a name according to what it is itself in nature. 

Upon this, note that Nature has ordained four types herein, which four types constitute the **Signatum Member** <note>original: *Membrum Signatum*; a specific part of the body that serves as a sign</note>. And thus Nature, through these four types, wishes to indicate to the **Signator** <term>Signator: original: *Signator*; "The Signer" or interpreter—the practitioner who reads and deciphers the signatures of nature</term> all natural secrets that lie within man. Since nothing is so secret or hidden that it may not become manifest, it depends solely on recognizing those things that reveal the hidden. From this it follows that **Chiromancy** <term>Chiromancy: original: *Chiromantia*; the art of palmistry or interpreting the lines of the hand to understand character and fate</term> contains the signs of such secrets in three places, as they are placed in the figure. Just as those lines and **veins** <note>original: *Venae*</note> present their indications according to the content of that same sense and mind, so also does the **proportion of the person** <note>original: *Proportio personae*; the physical symmetry and ratios of the human body</note>. 

From this it follows that such a member of **Astronomy** <note>original: *Astronomey*; here used in the Paracelsian sense, referring to the "inner stars" or celestial forces operating within the human body</note> may describe the mind of everyone. ## What the uncertain arts are, what their types contain, and what may be expected from the uncertain practitioner.

There are several arts that have come down to us from the ancients, which have existed for a very long time, as is self-evident; these arts have almost always walked alongside and been current with **Magic** <term>Magic: original: *Magica*</term>. And as it is found, these arts have always been held in great honor and dignity, and the further back one counts toward the beginning, the more honest and certain they were. And although the arts in themselves are not any worse for it, the people and their minds are. Therefore, much depends on what the person is like. I call them **uncertain arts** <term>uncertain arts: original: *Artes incertae*; disciplines like divination or astrology that Paracelsus considers technically valid but currently unreliable due to the corruption of modern practitioners</term> according to how things are in my time. If they were still as they were with the ancients, and the young were like the old, then I would call them **certain arts** <note>original: *Artes certas*</note>. But as the situation is now, the name cannot stand; rather, even what is already certain, and is, and is true, that no one can know nor trust in it. They are wonderful arts, and yet they are not arts. For that is an art which is certainly so, which one well knows, and in which there is no doubt. But this is to be considered here in

They treat great and wonderful mysteries, more so than other branches of astronomy, and much can be understood through them quickly. Now, the foundation of their art is not based on a natural process, but is rather "indirect," appearing just like **divination by lots** <term>divination by lots: original: *Sortilegium*; the practice of foretelling the future by drawing or casting lots</term>, and yet it is no mere game of chance; the hand provides the "lot." Now, every person is a prophet of the **Natural Light** <term>Natural Light: original: *Natürliches Liecht*; the innate wisdom or reason implanted by God in nature and man</term>. Some prophecies are spoken aloud; some are expressed through manner and gesture; some through pointing and showing; some through paintings and figures; and even many more in other ways. Since the hand can create images, forge swords, master all metals and stones, and catch all wild beasts on earth and in the water, why should such things not also happen through the hand in these arts? The hand may well complete this art through its power, just as the mouth can speak a word that is powerful.

Regarding this, know further: since man is himself a born natural prophet, he may well use these **types of uncertain arts** <note>original: *Species artium incertarum*; arts that rely on intuition or subjective signs rather than fixed, "certain" mathematical calculations</note>, of which there are four. And although **geomancy** <term>geomancy: divination by earth or marks made in the soil</term> takes its name from the earth, **pyromancy** <term>pyromancy: divination by fire</term> from fire, **hydromancy** <term>hydromancy: divination by water</term> from water, and **chaomancy** <term>chaomancy: divination by the air or sky; Paracelsus used the term 'Chaos' to refer to the element of Air</term> from the air, the foundation of the art does not come from the element itself. That is to say, it is not the elements that rule or provide the art. Rather, it is true that the arts are completed through the elements, but the art itself comes from man's innate prophetic nature.

In the same way that God has worked much through many kinds of people—both the lowly and the esteemed—it also appears that He allowed His Son to walk the earth in a very lowly state. The Son also chose lowly people to be His **apostles**, and lowly persons have been prophets. Yet, miraculously, through such lowliness, great wonders occurred. Thus, it is also to be understood here in the **uncertain arts** <note>original: *artibus Incertis*</note> that they are prophetic, insofar as nature works through them, whether in geomancy, pyromancy, hydromancy, or chaomancy. It lies in the fact that man is himself of a prophetic nature, and he rules the hand as a blacksmith rules his hammer. Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus [Paracelsus]

### What Adept Philosophy is, and what 
### its types are, as well as 
### its powers and virtues.

To know what **adept philosophy** <term>adept philosophy: original: *Philosophia adepta*; the study of the hidden, celestial forces within nature that go beyond the four physical elements</term> is, first take note of this instruction: All earthly bodies, beyond what they possess from the elements, also carry with them a firmamental power and virtue. Thus, wherever there is an elemental body, there is also a firmamental property. He who now knows what is firmamental within the elementated body, he is an **adept philosopher** <term>adept philosopher: original: *Philosophus adeptus*; a master who understands both the physical and the celestial aspects of nature</term>. And in the same way that the **common philosopher** <term>common philosopher: original: *Philosophus comunis*; a scholar of traditional, physical natural philosophy</term> describes the natural powers of herbs, so too shall the adept philosopher describe the firmamental powers within those same herbs. Although various writers have described such powers in many ways, they did so with such lack of understanding that they did not recognize the distinction between what belongs to the elements and what belongs to the firmament <note>The "firmament" refers to the heavens and the astrological influences of the stars</note>.

Now, such knowledge is necessary, especially regarding medicine. For what is firmamental cannot be treated in an **alchemical** <term>alchemical: original: *Alchimistisch*; referring here to laboratory processes like distillation or extraction</term> manner. But what is elemental, that is subject to alchemical preparation. And it is also necessary to know that whatever the alchemist breaks apart loses its firmamental power. If the firmamental power is to work, no breaking apart must occur <note>Paracelsus suggests that physical processing in a lab can destroy the subtle, spiritual essence of a substance</note>.

Furthermore, know that adept philosophy contains a special art of **composition** <term>composition: original: *Cōposition*; the mixing or blending of medicinal ingredients</term>. Just as one naturally mixes various physical bodies together, so too can the **sidereal secrets** <term>sidereal secrets: original: *Syderischen Archana*; hidden powers or "arcana" derived from the stars (Latin: *sidereus*)</term> be composed. From this follow the names, such as **Celestial Theriac** <note>original: *Tyriaca Coelestis*; a "theriac" was a famous universal antidote; here, a version empowered by the heavens</note>, **Mithridatum of Olympus** <note>original: *Metridatum Olimpi*; a heavenly version of the ancient Mithridatum cure</note>, **Ethereal Powder** <note>original: *Sufuff aethereum*; *Sufuff* or *Zufuff* refers to a dry medicinal powder</note>, and so on. That is to say: just as these are made in an earthly way, so too are they composed in a firmamental way.

Note also further that such firmamental power makes knives and swords with which one can hammer an anvil in two and cut through any metal as if through wax. This art is called the **Art of Swords** <term>Art of Swords: original: *Gladialis*; from Latin *gladius*</term> or the **Art of Striking** <term>Art of Striking: original: *Incusiua*; from Latin *incus* (anvil)</term>. And just as the elemental way makes knives for chopping wood, so the **astral way** <term>astral way: original: *art Astralis*</term> makes knives for chopping iron. Likewise, know that as nature can make natural keys to open locks, so too can adept philosophy make invisible keys. For whatever the elements are able to accomplish through their physical bodies, the **Star** <term>Star: original: *Astrum*; the celestial or spiritual essence of a thing</term> is also able to do in its own essence. This is the **Philosophy of Authority** <term>Philosophy of Authority: original: *Philosophia authoritatis*; a philosophy that commands and has power over matter</term> and it is also **Portable** <term>Portable: original: *Portiua*; possibly meaning a power that can be carried or applied anywhere</term>, for the reason—

What the **elements** <note>original: *Elementa*</note> do is natural; what the stars do is also natural. The elements act like elements; the firmament acts like the firmament. He who is experienced and learned in the elements philosophizes elementally. He who is learned in the firmament philosophizes firmamentally.

Thus are finished the explanations of the nine **sciences of astronomy** <note>original: *Scientiarum Astronomiae*</note>. Following hereafter are the operations that the heaven itself works upon the art of man, as follows below.

### What Divination and its types are.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter D featuring foliage and a central floral motif.</image-desc>
Since nothing is so secret that it shall not be revealed, then that which is most secret is that which is to happen in the future. Thus, there are two ways to experience future things: one is through the natural art, such as **prognostications** <note>original: *Prognosticationes*</note> and **judgments of Astronomy** <note>original: *Judicia Astronomiae*</note>; the other way is supernatural, and also comes to us supernaturally, such as **prophecies** <note>original: *Propheceyen*</note> and **oracles** <note>original: *Vaticinia*</note>. Now, to describe the supernatural future here, **Divination** <note>original: *Diuinatio*</note> is a **member** <note>original: *Membrum*</note> that announces hidden future things. It takes its origin from the one who intends to send those same future things. That same sender allows them to be indicated beforehand as a prophecy and a warning; and this occurs through six processes: that is, through dreams, through **fantasy** <note>original: *Fantasey*; here meaning mental visions or apparitions</note>, through speculation, through the mind, through the senses, and through the voice.

So that you may understand **divinations** <note>original: *Diuinationes*</note> more easily, I will present several examples to you. First, note that **divinations** <note>original: *Diuinationes*</note> appear wonderful and yet so insignificant that they are held in contempt. As when it occurred to **Joseph** in his sleep who **Mary** was, and by whom she had become pregnant. But because dreams are held to be contemptible, no belief is given to the **revelation** <note>original: *Reuelation*</note>, which is then nothing other than **divination** <note>original: *Diuinatio*</note>. Thus, much is divined through dreams, but no one heeds it until it has happened. Know also regarding **fantasy** <note>original: *Fantasia*</note>, that through paintings or images, future works are revealed. This happens when, for instance, strange figures appear in the heavens, or figures encounter one as if they were spirits. All such things are **types of divination** <note>original: *species Diuinationis*</note>; and because people do not know from whence they come, they are despised, and what they signify is mocked. Like the mental images that sometimes occur to someone, and he himself does not know what they mean until they have happened; only then is it recognized. So it is also with **speculation** <note>original: *Speculatio*</note>, when someone undertakes to speculate on a thing—how it will come to an end—and within that same **speculation** the outcome of the matter is found. But because no other basis is there, it is also not believed. Thus it sometimes comes to one

## What Augury is / and what its
## types signify.

Likewise you should also know regarding **auguries** <note>original: *Auguriis*; the ancient practice of interpreting omens from the behavior of birds or other natural signs</note> / that they also take their origin supernaturally / and are solely **presages** <note>original: *Praesagia*; omens or warnings</note> of future things / and indicate them in such a way that is not possible for the natural arts. Thus should the auguries be understood and recognized: they concern mankind for the sake of the coming wrath.

### What Intoxications are, and their types.

Understand regarding the third **member** <note>original: *Membro*; a specific branch or part of a larger system of knowledge</note> and its **types** <note>original: *Speciebus*</note> such a meaning: that in the sum of **intoxications** <note>original: *Ebrietatum*; used here not just for drunkenness from alcohol, but for any state where the mind is displaced from its natural human reason</note>—that is, when a person falls from their **human wisdom** and enters into another, **alien wisdom**. For thus there are two wisdoms: **human wisdom** <note>original: *Humana Sapientia*</note>, and secondly, **alien wisdom** <note>original: *Aliena Sapientia*</note>. Now, human wisdom is that wisdom which God gives to man, through which he lives as a human being and, as a human, recognizes, measures, and understands all things. God has given such wisdom to every person and provided them with it, so that whatever he hears or sees, he may judge and recognize those same things through that same wisdom; thus he will come to the right foundation, through human wisdom, of what each thing is in itself. But **alien wisdom** is to be recognized thus: when a person deviates from human wisdom and takes another upon himself, and according to that wisdom he judges what he sees and hears. That person can never come to any perfect truth in that wisdom, but flies back and forth like a reed in the water; for this alien wisdom is a **dizzying spirit** <note>original: *schwindelgeist*</note> that deafens and maddens against all human nature.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the third "member" of Astronomy, focusing on the concept of "Ebrietatum" (Intoxications). Paracelsus is distinguishing between natural human wisdom and the "foreign wisdom" that takes hold when a person is under a state of celestial or physical intoxication.</meta>

<header>The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus</header>

And in summary, observe such an example between the two wisdoms: Imagine a person who lived as a human with all human wisdom, beyond reproach; then it happens that he becomes drunk and full of wine. At that point, **foreign wisdom** <note>original: *aliena Sapientia*</note> begins, and **human wisdom** <note>original: *humana Sapientia*</note> departs. Now, see what the drunken person does: nothing from human wisdom, but rather from a foreign wisdom, which is nothing other than a mad, senseless, coarse blockhead <note>original: *Filz*; a term for a crude, stubborn person</note>—constantly stubborn, remaining fixed in their hard heads, measuring nothing by the right standard, but according to mad, senseless wisdom.

Therefore, know from now on that there are five **types** <note>original: *Species*</note> under this **branch** <note>original: *Membro*; referring to the third category of Paracelsus's astronomical system</note> which likewise bring foreign wisdom into humans, just as wine brings it into the brain. For there are also **wines** <note>original: *Vina*</note> among the **heavens** <note>original: *Obern*; the celestial bodies or upper spheres</note>; whoever drinks from them falls into a foreign, mad, senseless wisdom, and they judge what they see and hear like drunken folk who judge without any human understanding. 

Thus, one type is called **drunken madness** <note>original: *ebriecata Mania* or *inebriata Mania*</note>; those afflicted boast about the scriptures and interpret everything according to foreign wisdom, translating it perversely. There is also **drunken frenzy** <note>original: *inebriata Frenesis*</note>; these people want to achieve everything with swords and forget human reason, which does not teach such rage. There are also **drunken phantasms** <note>original: *inebriata Fantasmata*</note>, which is a type full of strange pranks; as it is a foreign wisdom, they also have foreign customs and gestures. There is also a type called **drunken imagination** <note>original: *Imaginatio inebriata*</note>; that is, many strange fantasies occur to them, just like a drunken person who thinks the walls are speaking to him, or that the bed is running in circles around him, and he does not recognize himself. 

Finally, there is the fifth type, which is **transformation** <note>original: *Immutatio*</note>; that is, it alters the body and mind, the senses and thoughts. They abandon friend and foe and follow no wisdom but their own; this is **drunken transformation** <note>original: *inebriata Immutatio*</note>. And just as you see when a hundred people are together and all are drunk, no one is of the same mind as the other; each one bends the argument to his own nose <note>an idiom meaning to interpret things to suit one's own whim</note>. So it is also with those who are **intoxicated** <note>original: *Inebriecati*</note> by the **firmamental must** <note>original: *Firmamentischen Most*; "must" is young, unfermented wine, used here to describe raw celestial influence</note>. Therefore, they do not have one wisdom, but each has a particular one, just like every fool—no fool follows another fool. Each one is best pleased by his own way, and they never arrive at a complete truth at any time.

<meta>This page transitions from the third branch of "Intoxications" to the fourth branch of Paracelsus’s astronomical system: "Inclinatum" or Inclination. It explains how the stars can adopt individuals to fulfill certain destinies even if they weren't born under a specific alignment.</meta>

# The First Book /
# What the "Inclined" is / and its Types.

Now know further regarding the fourth **branch** <note>original: *Membro*; referring to the fourth of Paracelsus's five categories of Astronomy</note> that the **stars** <note>original: *Gestirn*; refers to the celestial bodies or constellations</note> sometimes rule a person themselves and draw that person according to their own mind. This is to be understood as follows: sometimes the stars prepare a work and wish to make it manifest through a person, but if no person is present who stands in **conjunction** <note>the astronomical alignment of two celestial bodies</note> with those stars, then they take one up who is like an **adopted son** <note>original: *Filius adoptiuus*</note>. The father owed nothing to this son; rather, what he bestows upon him does not come from friendship, blood, or legal right. In the same way, the **star** <note>original: *Astrum*</note> also chooses an adopted son for itself, through whom it then works as if he were its natural-born son.

Now, take note of this **inclination** <note>original: *Inclinatio*; the celestial "leaning" or influence on a person</note>: it carries out its influencing in six different forms. Namely, once in the **person**—that is, in flesh and blood—in such a way that it creates a particularly pleasant person who is more praiseworthy or more hostile than other people. Furthermore, the **temperament** <note>original: *gemüth*</note> of the person often changes so that this person’s mind surpasses the minds of all others. For in this way **Solomon** <note>the biblical King Solomon, famed for wisdom</note> was an **adopted son** <note>original: *Filius adoptiuus*</note> in terms of his person. 

There are also inclinations that exalt the **spirit** <note>original: *Spiritum*</note>, so that this spirit is above all others in fortune, in schemes, and in all those things that belong to the spirit. Thus was the **Emperor Barbarossa of Swabia** <note>Frederick I (1122–1190), Holy Roman Emperor</note> an adopted son. You should also know regarding inclination in its fourth **type** <note>original: *Species*</note> that the stars sometimes prepare a **doctrine** <note>original: *Doctrin*; a system of teaching or philosophy</note> which they wish to make manifest through a person. So they choose one through whom they complete it. Thus, in doctrine, the adopted sons have been **Albertus Magnus** <note>13th-century polymath and teacher of Thomas Aquinas</note>, **Lactantius** <note>an early Christian author</note>, **Wycliffe** <note>John Wycliffe, the English reformer</note>, and others more. 

Likewise, the stars prepare a particular art, or a particular skill in **commerce** <note>original: *Kauffmanschafft*</note>. And if they have no natural-born son through whom to complete it, they choose one. Thus, an adopted son for art was **Albrecht Dürer of Nuremberg** <note>the famous Renaissance painter and engraver</note>. For commerce, the adopted son is the **Fugger of Augsburg** <note>original: *Fucker*; referring to the wealthy German banking family</note>. 

Also note in the sixth type that the stars sometimes give birth to a physical dexterity, such that it surpasses all others; for such things, the adopted sons are those who can walk upon the tightrope.

# The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus, Page 37

### What the Impression is and its
### Types.

So that you may understand the nature of the <term>Impression</term> <note>original: *Impressio*; a celestial "printing" or influence stamped upon the physical person</note>, and in what form it is to be understood and recognized: it is a power that comes from the <term>stars</term> <note>original: *Astris*</note> and serves only the <term>Elemental Body</term> <note>original: *Elementierten Leib*; the physical body made of the four elements, as opposed to the spiritual body</note>. It works in such a way that it has no fellowship in its form with the <term>Astral Body</term> <note>original: *Astralischen Leib*; the "star-body" or sidereal soul</note>. Instead, it is related to the <term>Elemental Body</term> in the same way that a color is related to a <term>physical object</term> <note>original: *Corpus*</note>. Just as the color and the object cannot be separated, so too the <term>Impression</term> and the <term>Elemental Body</term> cannot be parted from one another.

Now, regarding the <term>Impression</term>, one must understand this specific point: the <term>Impression</term> is born at the moment of conception and grows until <term>birth</term> <note>original: *Partum*</note>, at which point it remains embodied. Furthermore, take note that just as a color on the outside fades and changes over time—such as black, red, or yellow hair that eventually becomes gray or white—so too should the <term>Impression</term> be understood. It is conceived and born with the human being, and with its various <term>types</term> <note>original: *Speciebus*</note>, it conforms to the <term>Elemental Body</term>, advances in age, and transforms along with it.

Now, the <term>Impression</term> of the <term>Elemental Body</term> is the <term>breath of life</term> <note>original: *spiraculum Vitae*</note>. Within this <term>breath of life</term> are the essence and nature of the <term>Elemental Body</term>. And although I have stated that the <term>Impression</term> comes from the stars, you should only view the stars as a <term>means</term> <note>original: *medium*</note> through which the <term>breath of life</term> is substantially delivered to the <term>Elemental Body</term>.

In the same way, a human being is a <term>means</term> who acts according to his nature, through the one who created him. The <term>Elemental Body</term> has no life within it without the <term>breath of life</term>. Now, there are two who inspire this <term>breath of life</term>: namely God, as the one from whom man receives life and those essences that are innate to the body. But there is yet another <term>Inspirer</term> <note>referring to the stars or celestial forces acting as agents</note>; he also inspires the <term>breath of life</term> along with its accompanying essences. 

Mark the distinction between these two "inspirers" in this way: it is exactly like the relationship between God and a <term>physician</term> <note>original: *Artzet*</note>. Consider which one makes the sick person healthy: it is God, not the physician. However, the physician brings about the visible result. It is the same here: who gives the true <term>breath of life</term>? It is God alone. Yet, there is another who carries away the fame for it, and it is upon that agent that people fix their attention.

<summary>Paracelsus defines "Impression" as a celestial influence that acts as the physical breath of life for the elemental body, remaining inseparable from it from conception until death. He uses the analogy of a doctor to explain that while stars are the visible agents of this life-force, God remains the ultimate source.</summary>
