...had. In this, note now that the <term>Impression</term> <note>original: *Impressio*; a celestial influence "stamped" onto the physical body</note> is nothing other than a **Fixed Inspiration** <note>original: *Inspiratio Fixa*; a permanent spiritual "breathing-in" that remains with the person</note>, which is received with conception and with birth. Now, from this Impression follows health or sickness, pleasant customs or pleasant gestures, pleasant works, pleasant wisdom, and foresight; and it receives no more from the stars than as much air as a person needs when they wish to speak. Thus the **Elemental Body** <note>the physical body made of the four elements</note> becomes alive through the Impression, along with death and all that belongs to life.

### What Generation Is, and Its Species.

<image-desc>Large ornamental initial 'A' with scrolling botanical patterns.</image-desc>
Thus you should also know that the branch of **Generation** <note>original: *Membrum Generatio*; the category of creation or coming-into-being</note> has four species under it, namely according to the four elements. Now, the branch of Generation is nothing but the **Communication** <note>original: *Communicatio*</note> that the stars impart to those things made of the elements. Just as the sun imparts warmth to the elements, and without the sun they would all be dead; the sun is the **breath of life of the elements** <note>original: *spiraculum vitae Elementorum*</note>, making everything alive that exists within the four elements. Man and the breath of life make the human being; man is the **Microcosm** <note>original: *Microcosmus*; the "little world" that mirrors the universe</note>, and his breath of life is the **Creator of things** <note>original: *Conditor rerum*</note>.

Now the elements are the **Mothers** <note>original: *Matrices*; the wombs or sources from which things grow</note>, and the firmament is the **Parents** <note>original: *Parentes*</note>; these two give birth to all fruits that grow out of the elements, and the sun is their breath of life. That is, the sun is the breath of life of the things of Nature. Thus Generation is to be understood in this way: that the elements can accomplish nothing without the stars <note>original: *Astrum*</note>. For the elements are the Mothers, the **Sun** <note>original: *Sol*</note> is the **Vulcan** <note>original: *Vulcanus*; the alchemical "blacksmith" or transformative heat</note>, and Nature is the **Craftsman** <note>original: *Fabricator*</note>.

And even though the seeds <note>original: *Semina*</note> lie in the Mother <note>original: *Matrice*</note> and not in the Begetter, consider the egg of the hen: the egg comes from the hen, and not from the rooster. But if it is to generate its **chick** <note>original: *Pullum*</note>, this must happen through the rooster. Thus it is also to be understood here that the Mothers [the elements] have the seed, but they receive the **effect** from the stars, and the **digestion** <note>original: *Digestionem*; the ripening or "cooking" process</note> from the sun, which hatches out the fruits of all elements, just as a hen hatches her eggs. 

So know now how to speak of Generation: that from the element of **water**, all minerals, salts, metals, gems, stones, and rocks <note>original: *Mineralia, Salia, Metalla, Gemmae, Lapides, Petrae*</note> grow and come forth. And **Water** <note>original: *Aqua*</note> is the mother of them all, and the sun hatches all these things out in the water. Likewise, know also of the element of **fire**, that the fruits of this element are also cooked and hatched by the sun. Now the fruits of the element of fire are all...

### What the Soul-less Is, and Its Species.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'V' featuring a bird or dragon-like creature entwined with floral scrollwork.</image-desc> Writing about this branch is somewhat more difficult to understand than the others. But first, you must know what the **Soul-less** <note>original: *Inanimatum*; literally "without breath" or "without soul"</note> is: it is a human being in whom no soul can be found to exist, and of such humans there are six kinds. And although there is one more kind, as will follow later in this paragraph, anyone may hold their own opinion of it. But of the six in which there is no soul, these are the **Nymphs** (water-people), **Giants**, **Lemures** (mountain-people), **Gnomes** (air-people), **Vulcans** (fire-people), and **Shadow-dwellers** <note>original: *Vmbragines*, translated here from the German *schrettlin*, referring to spirits, goblins, or nightmare-inducing creatures</note>.

For just as we humans are created on the earth, yet with a soul, so there are also people without a soul within the four elements, plus two others: the Giants and the Shadow-dwellers. And just as we walk upon the soil and not *in* the soil, upon the water and not *in* the water, outside of the fire and not *in* the fire, and in the same way outside of the air and not *in* the air, so there are **counterfeit humans** in the elements who dwell *inside* the elements and not outside of them—like the **Phoenix** in the fire, or the **Mole** <note>original: *Talpa*</note> in the earth, and so on. No one should be surprised by this, for it will be proven that it is truly so.

However, the Giants and Shadow-dwellers have their dwellings just like humans. So, know regarding their **generations** <note>original: *Generationibus*</note> that it happens as follows: they are born through celestial and elemental **seeds** <note>original: *Spermata*</note> without the **slime of the earth** <note>original: *Limum terrae*; a reference to the biblical clay from which Adam was formed</note>. They are also not "creatures" <note>Paracelsus often distinguishes between "Creatures" made in God's image with souls and these elemental "imitation" humans</note>, but rather they grow just as **dung beetles** <note>original: *Rosszkefer*</note> grow out of horse manure.

## What Meteorology and Its Species Are.

This **branch of the stars** <note>original: *Membrum Astrorum*</note> is **Meteorology** <note>original: *Metheorica*</note>, and its proper name is **Sage Meteorology** <note>original: *Sagar Metheorica*</note>, and not "Lesser Meteorology." Now, this branch contains many species within it, holding names just like "Lesser Meteorology." But so that you understand the difference between both types of Meteorology: know that "Lesser Meteorology" is mentioned in the **branch of generation** <note>referring to natural weather on Earth</note>, but here in this "Sage Meteorology," things are born in the **high Olympus** <note>original: *superno Olimpo*; here referring to the upper reaches of the heavens or the firmament</note>. Take rain, for example: those same rains do not come down upon us as rain, but as a dew or a vapor. Likewise, dews are also created in that same place, etc., but they are poured upon us with a smaller substance, for they are **spiritual** <note>original: *Spiritualisch*; meaning subtle or airy</note> and not **corporeal** <note>original: *Corporalisch*; meaning physical or heavy</note>. They also produce thunder and **lightning bolts** <note>original: *Straal*</note>, yet they do not strike our earth; instead, they make a strike downward, but because of the great distance to the earth, they cannot reach it. Thereafter, they fall down upon the other side of the **globe** <note>original: *Globel*</note>. In this way, stones and other things are found. Similarly, "Sage Meteorology" gives birth to blood, metals, and other such things. It gives birth to **fire-drakes** <note>original: *Dracones*; often used to describe meteors or fireballs</note>, **phantoms** <note>original: *Falones*</note>, **apparitions** <note>original: *Apparitiones*</note>, **likenesses** <note>original: *Similitudines*</note>, **figures** <note>original: *Figuras*</note>, and the like; these come from above so that they enter the **middle spaces** <note>original: *media Interstitia*; the spaces between the celestial spheres</note>. Sometimes they are destroyed, consumed, and blown away by the "Lesser Meteorology." Within this "Sage Meteorology" is the **tincture of metals** <note>original: *tinctura Metallorum*</note>, of gems, and of all colors. From this "Olympus" come the colors; in this "Olympus" sits the **Meteorological Vulcan** <note>original: *Vulcanus Metheoricus*; Vulcan was the Roman god of fire and smithing; here he acts as the celestial craftsman who "forges" the colors and qualities of nature</note>, who is the **creator** <note>original: *genitor*</note> of all **tinctures and colors** <note>original: *Tincturarum et Colorum*</note>, etc. From "Sage Meteorology," the **conjunction of the tincture** <note>original: *coniunctio Tincturae*</note> enters into the **elementary bodies** <note>original: *Corpora Elementata*</note>. # What **New Growths** <note>original: *Noualia*; Paracelsus uses this term to refer to anomalies or "news" in nature, often referring to things that appear outside the standard order of creation</note> are, together with their **types** <note>original: *Speciebus*</note>.

<image-desc>A large decorative initial 'W' featuring interlaced foliage and floral patterns in woodcut style.</image-desc>

Just as every thing is created, and how one thing should give birth to another, God has placed both the sentient and the non-sentient into an order; and it pleased God, and all things were good. Now, however, that same order has further been broken, and many deformities have occurred, or things have happened differently than the way Nature has the order in herself. I do not indicate such things here so that anything should be **prophesied** <note>original: *vaticiniert*</note> from them, but rather they are merely **errors of nature** <note>original: *Errata Naturae*</note>. However, I point this out because the astral nature causes it. 

For example: Nature makes no fools, for it is not her order, nor is it the gift that God has given her; rather, an **error** <note>original: *Error*</note> has occurred which has broken the order of nature. For example: if there were a hundred men sitting in judgment, and each one was to make a statue. Once they are made, none is like the other; the one who is capable makes it correctly, while the ninety-nine others make nothing good. 

Thus Nature possesses the art of how she should make a human being, or any kind of growth. But because there are so many factors that make a human, each one comes and makes its own pattern, by which the work is corrupted. It is just as if a room full of people were sitting in a council; each one wants his advice to be followed, and so a council decision is reached and made that looks just like a fool who has many goiters <note>original: *Kröpff*; a swelling of the neck, used here as a metaphor for a distorted or "lumpy" result</note>. 

Therefore, knowing the nature and property of the stars—that they are not always in equal harmony—there arises a mixed work in the mind and in the body. In this, the **naturalist** <note>original: *Naturalis*; a physician or student of nature</note> should pay close attention: where there is a **monstrous form** <note>original: *Forma Monstrosa*</note>, there is also commonly a **monstrous sense** <note>original: *monstrosus Sensus*; meaning a distorted mind or perception</note>, as is the case with fools, mistletoe, mold <note>original: *Moder*; can refer to decay or parasitic growths</note>, and so on. And where such **monstrous bodies** <note>original: *monstrosa Corpora*</note> are found in the **matters of nature** <note>original: *Rebus Naturae*</note>, in that same place are also the **monstrous remedies** <note>original: *Remedia monstrosa*</note>, which are not to be used as they would be in a **perfect body** <note>original: *Corpore perfecto*</note>. and brings forth / is all for the sake of man. # The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus

**Magic** <note>original: "Magica"</note> has brought such **powers** <note>original: "Vires"</note> just as that same star is in itself, with those same **secrets** <note>original: "Secretis"</note> and **mysteries** <note>original: "Archanis"</note>. It is in the same way as when someone eats a herb: the herb and its powers are within him, exactly as those powers are. So it is also in man, whether much or little, in one person or another. Therefore, take note of this declaration as such a **Proof** <term>Proof</term> <note>original: "Probation"; a demonstration or experimental verification of a truth.</note>. If it is possible to bring poison into a person, or medicine along with its effect, through one person into another, then it is also possible for the **Magical Astronomer** <note>original: "Astronomo Magico"</note> to drive the heavenly powers into a person in the same way.

And so that you understand me rightly, regarding the foundation upon which the **Magus** acts or speaks: this is the born Magus. For just as a Magus can naturally make another Magus—as I have mentioned—know that this also occurs during conception; these are the truly born Magi. And a Magus learns only from the stars, and not from men. Therefore, know that there is more to be understood about Magic than has been revealed until now, and it is this: every art is born with the man; that is, the art and the man are together in the conception. For a man, as a mere man, can learn nothing from others; only Magic learns [directly]. 

And this is assigned to Magic because God does not wish for anything to remain secret or hidden, but rather that everything He has created in nature should be made manifest, so that it may be experienced. Therefore, the commandments and laws are given to avoid doing other things that might hinder such exploration, such as whoring, hypocrisy, **legalistic scribbling** <note>original: "Schreiberey"; likely referring to empty academic pedantry or the deceptive manipulation of texts.</note>, usury, and the like. For whoever occupies himself with such things will no longer be a Magus. 

Therefore, Magic must exist for the sake of **revelation** <note>original: "offenbarung"</note>. If a thing is to be made manifest, it must be given by the one who hid it, to the one who should and can interpret it, and to whom it is granted. Just like the Book of Revelation: no one will ever interpret it unless he be a Magus, whether born or adopted. Any further attempt at interpretation consists of "flying spirits" without foundation—nothing but colors and a painting—making a **pretense** <note>original: "Fucum"; a Latin term for a dye or cosmetic used to disguise the true appearance of something, implying a deceptive facade.</note> out of everything. Christ said: *There shall be signs in the sun, moon, stars, etc.*—and no one will interpret this without Magic. Yet, this Magus is not born from the natural stars, but from the supernatural heaven; that is where the Magi spring from. Now the Magus is born, and Magic is imprinted upon him just as sight is to the eyes and hearing is to the ears. As an example in all Magi who have existed: none of them ever learned...

If the **elemental body** can make another form out of wood, how much more can the **spiritual body** prepare another figure and form out of stone and wood, at which the **elemental body** must marvel? For the **elemental body** seeks its art from the spiritual; however, it receives the lesser portion. The Master is above the Apprentice. 

From this it follows that man himself—just as figures are changed from one to another by a painter—can be transformed by the spiritual master; just as easily, and even more easily, can man be transformed from one thing into another by the spiritual master. And although this does not happen through the stars themselves, but through **human sciences** <term>humanas Scientias: the practical applications of wisdom by humans</term>, it requires a good student who has learned the foundation of the stars well and is himself skillful.

Now observe further the artistic power and property of the spiritual body. Just as a person can change their own color, or disguise and mask their face, much more so can the **spiritual body** do this. For to man [it is] well...

How many have made the blind see and cleansed the lepers? And furthermore, as Christ said, we shall do even more than He has done through **Faith** <note>original: "Glauben"; referencing John 14:12</note>. 

If, then, such great things are possible, how much more might we do the lesser things in Nature through Nature herself? This all happens through God, who has given such things to men. If Nature distributes her art and gives it to those who seek her, sharing her power through the **attractive virtue** <term>attractiuiſche Tugendt: the magnetic power of the soul or an object to draw celestial influence to itself</term>—so that she has the power and might—why then should it not be possible for a **Magus** to bring heavenly influence into an earthly plant? Such a plant then acts according to the power of the Stars, just as one who acts through God performs those same **great works of God** <note>original: "Magnalia"</note>, while he who acts through Nature performs the **great works** of Nature.

For just as the dead are revived through God, so will Nature give power and ability to her **Natural Saints**, who are called **Magi**, to perform powerful deeds. For there are saints in God for the sake of salvation called **Saints** <note>original: "Sancti"</note>, and there are also saints in God regarding natural powers who are called **Magi**. God is wondrous in His saints, both in the Kingdom of God and in Nature; it is not possible for others to do these things, except for those to whom it is specifically given. Thus, the distinction between a **Saint** <note>original: "Sanctum"</note> and a **Magician** <note>original: "Magum"</note> is this: the Saint acts through God, while the Magician acts through [Nature]...

### The Wise Philosophy of Theophrastus 45

**Nature works**; but it has long made me reluctant to write anything about **Astronomy** <term>Astronomia: here referring to the study of celestial influences on the human body and spirit, not just movement of planets</term>, or to speak of it with companions or others. This is because I have considered what great power and strength the celestial influence possesses, and I have weighed the coarseness and the senseless ways of men, who are so utterly impossible to describe, and who—because of **Sophistry** <note>Paracelsus uses "Sophistry" to describe academic or religious learning that is used for profit or ego rather than seeking true, divine, or natural light.</note>, the satisfaction of money, and deadly lusts—cannot grasp it. For the cause of this is that **Astronomy** and its various branches are not recognized. Who could recognize **both lights**? <note>The "Two Lights" are the *Lumen Gratiae* (Light of Grace/Revelation) and the *Lumen Naturae* (Light of Nature/Reason).</note> Who could even speak with such people? For every party follows the malice and fantasies of their own star’s influence, which are always contrary to true wisdom. For just as a **leaven** <note>A biblical metaphor (from Matthew 16:6) for a corrupting influence.</note> fell against the teaching of Christ, so too a leaven has fallen against the teaching of Nature; and thus both lights have been falsified by their Sophists, and no one wishes to judge with certainty. Many judge the **Magical art** <note>original: "Kunst Magicam"</note> and speak of it out of a drunken and full dream—that is, they recognize only their own deception and error. Who would want to learn from them? **Magic** is an excellent discipline and great in its works. But we know that Christ spoke a lasting word: *If you believe, you shall do even greater things* <note>original: "Glaubet jhr es so werdt jhr ein mehrers thun"; referencing John 14:12.</note>. Now, if Christ performed certain deeds, yet promised his disciples they would do more, and if Nature performs certain things through her art, why should we not also do more than she? As they have learned from their parents and ancestors, who said to Christ: "He has the Devil," so must the wisdom of God and Nature be despised by her children. It is created for our sake; therefore, we are powerful within it. The **wise man rules it**, and it does not rule the wise man. If the Scripture is able to do more through faith than Christ did in love toward his neighbor, why then should we not also be more capable than the stars? For the commandment is directed toward us, not toward the stars; and all things are subject to us, just as the disciples of Christ were subject to Christ. Thus, the disciples of Nature can do more than Nature, which sleeps within herself and remains idle until she is awakened in such a way. However, Christians do no more—neither less nor more—for Christ is to them a mockery and a sin, so that no one wishes to apply themselves in faith. So it is in Nature as well; everything passes away with the work of the Sophists, which is the current consumption of the time of Nature. Therefore, **Wisdom** should be within us, through which we rule all things—not only the powers of the **Firmament**, but also all living animals that are stronger than man; these must be under man in the depths of the

It can strike forth / hew, and stab; it can do much more, for such possibilities exist within the Heavens. To understand the cause, notice the example: the Sun has no other property in itself than solely being the highest **degree** <note>original: "Gradus"</note> of natural daylight; and wherever there is daylight, there is also heat, for the daylight is placed within the heat. That is the **magical force and impression** <note>original: "Magica Vis et Impressio"; the way a celestial body "stamps" or exerts its power onto the physical world</note>; and this power is to be understood in another way: that there is a **gradation** <note>original: "Gradation"; an intensification of a quality</note> which exalts the **fifth essence** <note>original: "quintum Esse"; often called the "Quintessence," this is the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance, beyond the four physical elements</note>. This property is proven by the Sun: through a **burning mirror** <note>original: "Feuwerspiegel"; a lens or concave mirror used to focus sunlight to start fires</note>, its heat surpasses our eyes, and our sensitivity cannot endure it. This occurs through the roundness of **crystal** and other similar burning mirrors, which are hereafter called **incensories** <note>original: "Incensoria"; technical term for instruments used to ignite fire using light</note>. These blind the eyes through their shine and ignite, burning and scorching; the Sun can do no more than this here on Earth. In the same way, other **forces** <note>original: "Vires"</note> of the stars may also be increased.

...as the <term>Thief</term> <note>original: "Latro"; a reference to the Penitent Thief on the cross from the Gospel of Luke.</note> entered into Paradise, or how the Rich Man <note>A reference to the parable of Dives and Lazarus, where the rich man is "buried in hell."</note> was buried in Hell. Thus it would be sufficient to know that this error is a mere juggling-trick, in that people think such things are preserved here on Earth, even though Scripture indicates otherwise and [human] fantasy is rejected.

To report to you concerning <term>Necromancy</term> <note>original: "Nigromantia"; for Paracelsus, this refers to the misguided study of or communication with the astral remains of the dead.</note>, understand it in this form: <term>Astronomy</term> <note>original: "Astronomia"; here meaning the study of how the "inner stars" or celestial forces operate within the human organism.</note> proves through itself that the earthly conduct of Man is governed by the stars, and this same [influence] is contained in its own body, and remains in it until it is consumed. However, in the same way that the **Elemental body** <note>original: "Elementierte Leib"; the physical body made of the four elements of nature.</note> loses one limb after another until they are all consumed—first the hearing, then the sight, then movement, and further the voice and speech which vanish along with the others; then the blood, then the **fluids** <note>original: "Liquores"; the vital humors or liquid substances of the body.</note>, then the flesh, then the veins—only the bones remain, which are compared to gold because of their nature and quality. So, note this example: that the **Sideric body** <note>original: "Syderisch leib"; the "star-body" or astral corpse that lingers after death.</note> also loses one piece after another: the understanding, the wisdom, the art, the skill, the beauty, etc. For these are its "limbs," and from these limbs it also loses one after another—now the understanding, then the wisdom, then the art, then the senses, each according to how it existed within it, until they are all consumed and nothing remains of it. And although the bones remain in a human because they are fixed, they too are perishable with time, though last of all. Thus, know of the **Sideric body** and its capability: it cannot hear, nor can it speak; it has no eyes, therefore it cannot see. Furthermore, what could anyone drive out of it? Yet the erring ones undertake to force a thing to speak which was not created for speaking; they want to have something from it which God did not give it. It should answer, it should hear, it should see, it should follow—and not one of these parts is within it. Therefore the Devil delights them, because they seek that which is not in them. It possesses movement because, during life, it moved the **Elemental body**, and through that same body it spoke, saw, and heard. But when they are separated from one another, none of these parts can exist anymore; they are dead and without power. For it moved the **Elemental body** during its lifetime—since there is no movement in the **Elemental body** itself—and thus when it is separated from the **Elemental body**, there is no movement in that physical body. The movement is in the **Sideric body**; therefore it passes away and is dead. But it moves nothing but itself, until its final consumption. The qualities it possesses are those of the heart, which is the **disposition** <note>original: "Gemüth"; the seat of emotions, mind, and character.</note> in

...is in him, possessed by him, and within his power—that is this **Sideric Body**. Therefore, once the **Elemental Body** <note>original: "Elementiert Leib"; the physical body composed of the four earthly elements.</note> has been separated from it, death has arrived; though the Sideric body must be consumed over time. During that time, the human **Mind** <note>original: "Gemüth"; refers to the seat of will, disposition, and earthly desire.</note> is carried forth through this Sideric Body, no differently than a shadow follows a person. Wherever the whole person goes, there too is his shadow; and whatever can be produced from a shadow can also be mastered here in this Sideric spirit. 

If that person was a <term>Speculator</term> <note>original: "Fürkauffer"; literally a "fore-buyer" or forestaller, someone who obsessively seeks worldly profit through trade.</note> and set his heart, mind, soul, and strength upon such things, and was thus seized by death while in the grip of such a fantasy, then it is the nature of his Sideric Body to pursue such profit and <term>Deceit</term> <note>original: "Alfantz"; refers to trifles, nonsense, or dishonest worldly dealings.</note> even after death. That is to say, it attaches itself to those places where such things occurred—not only in matters of trade, but in every single thing where that person’s heart, mind, strength, and soul were focused. 

And mark this above all other points: such spirits follow most of all those whose foundation and heart were set upon worldly pleasure, greed, and the like. But where hearts are not so entirely tied to the worldly, not many such spirits are seen; for such a person walks in God, and his Sideric spirit does not wander, but quietly consumes itself. 

Therefore, no one should be amazed if, after a person’s death, that person’s figure is seen. It is a **Spectacle** of the dead, in which we the living should reflect and philosophize, turning away and desisting from our evil habits, so that after a person’s death, that same body in which he lived does not manifest or become heard until its eventual consumption, exposing that person's shame and vice through its phantasms and shadowy wandering. 

For whatever dies while tied to the worldly in such a mind remains visible—unless that worldly mind is taken away. As soon as that happens, the Sideric Body flies toward the stars into its grave; but if not, it remains by the **Corpse** <note>original: "Cadaver"; the decaying physical remains.</note> and at the place where the mind was focused, for the heart is what governs it.

Therefore, to inform you concerning <term>Necromancy</term> <note>original: "Nigromantia"; for Paracelsus, this is the study or manipulation of these lingering astral shells, which he considers a lower and often deceptive art.</note> as it is in itself: no further power is to be granted to it than what remains before the spirit is consumed. For within the dead Elemental Body after death, one should not seek speech, sight, hearing, or movement; and the longer it lies there, the less is to be found in it. But whatever remains there reveals the "Old Man" <note>A theological reference to the unregenerate, earthly nature of a human being.</note> in his temperament. ...as is then proven in the practice of **Necromancy** <note>original: "Nectromantia"; the practice of communicating with the spirits of the dead.</note> according to the order of the **Nigromantic Process** <note>original: "Nigromantischen Proceß"; a historical term for black magic, often conflated with necromancy in the Renaissance.</note>. Now, they do not consider that they are searching where there is nothing. Something does indeed follow into the Sideric bodies, but it leads to no fruitfulness; yet it happens in this way:

A person who is whole, with the **Elemental Body** <note>original: "Elementierten Leib"; the physical body made of the four earthly elements.</note> and Sideric Body still unseparated, has a nature within them regarding what they like or dislike, what they want or do not want, what pleases or displeases them; they direct themselves according to this and consent to it. Now, his Sideric Body retains this nature. If the Exorcist can use that same liking toward it, the spirit consents to him, but only in the manner of a **shadow** <note>original: "schatten weiß"; as a mere reflection or echo, rather than a conscious, living soul.</note>. But if he uses something offensive against it, he also receives a contrary answer—and yet still only in the manner of a shadow.

That something might be sought and taken from this, or something fruitful found, cannot happen in any other way than this: as if a person had buried a treasure and intended to reveal it before the separation of the two bodies <note>meaning, before death</note>. Then, after death, if it were that same Exorcist to whom the person intended to reveal it, and he were brought to this Sideric Body, the treasure would be revealed to him. But if he is not that person, nothing will be made known to him at that place. 

This does not happen from the **Soul**, or from the **Spirit of Life**, or from the **Eternal**, or from the **Image** <note>original: "Bildtnus"; the divine spark or "imago Dei" in man.</note> which is given by God, but happens solely from the perishable, mortal Sideric Body. For you should know this: just as the Elemental Body must rot and become ashes, so also must the earthly senses and thoughts, powers and the **Mind** <note>original: "Gemůt"; the seat of earthly emotions and will.</note> rot and become as wind. 

But I must inform you regarding the **Conjurors** <note>original: "Coniuristen"; those who attempt to command or "bind" spirits through ritual incantations.</note>, whom I have mentioned before; they want to compel and force through incantations, so that the Sideric Body must do what they want. The power and authority they have over the Sideric Body is like this: they attempt that which is possible nowhere, neither among the Saints nor in Nature. Therefore, such **recklessness** <note>original: "leichtfertigkeit"; a term Paracelsus uses for dangerous, frivolous, or unlearned meddling in the occult.</note> accomplishes only this: that they provoke **Satan**, who otherwise lies in chains; for we are those who tread upon snakes and dragons. ### Proof in the Science of Necromancy
<note>original: "Probatio in scientiam Nectromanticam."</note>

Now, since Christ says that nothing is so secret that it shall not be revealed—although the theologians apply this only to the human heart—the Philosopher may also apply it to the **Light of Nature**. Also look at the animals, which can neither speak nor interpret, yet there is nothing so secret within them that man does not discover it. It follows from this that nothing is so secret that it is not possible for it to be revealed. For God Himself does not wish such things to remain hidden, but rather that they be revealed in His time. Therefore it is right that those very things which make the hidden manifest be held in honor with diligence and learned most industriously. And although it is true that the *theologians* do not want this, it is the fault of their folly and coarse understanding that they attribute to the Devil a thing that is nonetheless from God—an upright Art. So it is that through its natural operation, the natural powers are experienced. For Nature has nothing so secret hidden within her that can conceal itself from the foundation of this Art. Thus the arts should be experienced, discovering what lies in the sea, in mountains, in rocks, in man, and in all corners, whether in the day or in the darkness. Therefore it is necessary that we have knowledge of this art of *Necromancy* and understand and recognize it rightly in its foundation, so that we may learn to experience the wonders and **great works** <term>Great works: "Magnalia," a term for the magnificent, miraculous deeds of God visible throughout the physical world.</term> of God in the natural **mysteries** <note>original: "Mysterijs"</note>. # The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus

Without this <note>The "Light of Nature" mentioned on the previous page.</note>, no one achieves anything, for it is this very light that creates the Art. From this it follows that Nature presents us with arts through which we should seek; and these same arts are not from humans, but from Nature, which acts in a manner similar to this: where there is a heart, there is also a mouth and a voice, and that is the opening of the heart. Thus, where the treasure is, there is also a heart and a mouth—and that [mouth] is the Art. Therefore, its effects are to be sought from Nature, not from humans, for Nature searches within herself for what is in her, and she has an eye that sees into all her secrets. That very eye is **Necromancy** <note>original: "Nectromantia"; Paracelsus distinguishes his "natural necromancy"—the study of the sidereal or "star-born" body—from the "black" necromancy of conjuring the dead.</note>, and within that same eye are the arts of seeking. What is taken from the eye seeks rightly and finds. This eye of Nature is so sharp that no power in Nature can hide so that Nature shall not find it.

For just as no human may hide before God, so too nothing can hide before Nature. Thus God has established an order, so that through such an eye every hidden thing makes itself manifest, just as the Gospel saying holds: *Out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth overflows* <note>original: "Auß völle des Hertzens / laufft der Mundt vber"; a reference to Matthew 12:34.</note>, which is to say: the secrets of the heart open themselves through the mouth. He who hears the mouth, hears the secrets of the heart. So it is also with all hidden things, for there is not one that does not have, instead of a mouth, a **Spirit** <note>original: "Spiritum"</note> which acts as the mouth and chatters what is within it—that is, what lies within the being to whom it belongs. Thus the mouth is an eye that looks into the heart. 

Therefore, we should understand the Art in such a form, that there is no other foundation than to seek solely with the **Light** [of Nature] which is Nature itself; and in that same Light will be found that which is known to no one else. Without that Light, all things remain in darkness, in which nothing at all can be found, but instead produces a **Labyrinth** <term>Labyrinth: In Paracelsian terms, a state of intellectual confusion where one wanders through false theories without ever reaching the "center" or the truth.</term> that can never reach its center. Thus, understand the foundation from which the Art of **Necromancy** flows as it has just been described, so that it should not be abandoned, and much less rejected.

Now there are four main paths of Necromancy, in which four ways Necromancy learns to seek—though there are not only four arts according to these four ways, but rather four types of processes of the arts. However, all are directed toward their kind, just as in medicine there is not only one herb, but many kinds of herbs; not only one medicine for a fever, but many medicines for a fever, and each is as valid as the other. But note the distinction of the four main paths as I have mentioned: the first path is through **Mirrors**, the second through **Crystals** <note>original: "Barillen"; this refers to beryls or lenses used as scrying stones or magnifying glasses to observe natural signatures.</note>. Thus, it often happens that figures are found in wood or stones, or in other such **bodies** <note>original: *Corporibus*</note>, which are contrary to the nature and properties of that wood or stone, etc. Thus, a **presage** is an indication that something is about to befall a person. Likewise, **monsters** <note>original: *Monstra*; in this era, the term referred to any biological anomaly or "prodigy" that deviates from the natural order</note> are often born—whether among birds, cattle, fish, worms, or even humans—at which one must wonder and be horrified; these are all **presages** of a **coming wrath** <note>original: *venturae Irae*</note> upon humanity. Thus should these **auguries** be understood and recognized: they concern humanity because of the **coming wrath**.

# What Intoxication Is, and Its Kinds.

Now, understand concerning the third **member** <note>original: *Membro*; a section or division of his argument</note> and its **kinds** <note>original: *Speciebus*</note>, that in the **sum total of intoxications** <note>original: *summa Ebrietatum*; Paracelsus uses "intoxication" to mean a state where the mind is overtaken by an external influence or ecstasy, not just drunkenness</note>—that is, when a person falls from their human wisdom and enters into another, foreign wisdom. For there are two wisdoms: **Human Wisdom** <note>original: *Humana Sapientia*</note> and, secondly, **Alien Wisdom** <note>original: *Aliena Sapientia*</note>. Now, **Human Wisdom** is that wisdom which God gives to man, through which he lives as a human being and recognizes, measures, and understands all things as a human. God has given such wisdom to every person and provided them with it, so that whatever they hear or see, they may judge and recognize those things through that same wisdom; thus, through human wisdom, they will arrive at the true foundation of what each thing is in itself. But **Alien Wisdom** is to be recognized thus: when a person deviates from human wisdom and adopts another, and according to that [other wisdom] judges what they see and hear. Such a person cannot reach any perfect truth in that wisdom, but flutters to and fro like a reed in the water; for this **Alien Wisdom** is a "spirit of dizziness" <note>original: *schwindelgeist*; a giddy or swirling spirit</note> that deafens and maddens contrary to all human nature.

In summary, take note of this example between the two wisdoms: Suppose there was a man who lived like a human with all human wisdom, blameless; it then happens that he becomes drunk and full of wine, so that **alien wisdom** <note>original: *aliena Sapientia*; foreign or external wisdom</note> begins, and **human wisdom** <note>original: *humana Sapientia*</note> departs. Now see what the drunken man does: nothing out of human wisdom, but rather out of a foreign wisdom, which is nothing but a mad, senseless, coarse churlishness; stubborn and willful, they remain set in their hard heads, measuring nothing by the right standard, but rather according to a mad, uncomprehended wisdom.

Therefore, know from now on that there are five **kinds** <note>original: *Species*</note> under this **section** <note>original: *Membro*</note>, which likewise bring foreign wisdom into humans, just as wine brings it into the brain. For there are also **wines** <note>original: *Vina*</note> among the upper realms; whoever drinks from them falls into the foreign, mad, uncomprehended wisdom, and they judge what they see and hear like drunken fools <note>original: *Bölz*; blocks or clumsy fellows</note> who **judge** <note>original: *iudiciern*</note> without any human understanding.

Thus, there is one **kind** <note>original: *Species*</note> called **intoxicated mania** <note>original: *ebriecata Mania* or *inebriata Mania*</note>; they boast in the Scriptures and interpret everything according to foreign wisdom, **interpreting** <note>original: *interpretirens*</note> it contrariwise. There is also **intoxicated frenzy** <note>original: *inebriata Frenesis*</note>; those who suffer from it want to achieve everything with swords and forget human reason, which does not teach such rage. There are also **intoxicated phantasms** <note>original: *inebriata Fantasmata*</note>; this is a **kind** <note>original: *Species*</note> that is full of strange tricks; as it is a foreign wisdom, they also have foreign customs and gestures.

There is also a **kind** <note>original: *Species*</note> called **intoxicated imagination** <note>original: *Imaginatio inebriata*</note>; that is, many strange fantasies occur to them, just like a drunken man who thinks the walls are talking to him, or that the bed is running in circles around him, and he does not recognize himself. So it is also in the fifth **kind** <note>original: *Specie*</note>, which is **alteration** <note>original: *Immutatio*</note>; that is, the body and mind, sense and thoughts, are perverted within them; they surrender friend and foe and follow no wisdom but their own; this is **intoxicated alteration** <note>original: *inebriata Immutatio*</note>.

And just as you see when a hundred people are together and all are drunk, no one is of the same mind as the other; every one twists the **argument** <note>original: *Argument*</note> to suit his own nose. So it is also with those who are **intoxicated** <note>original: *Inebrieccati*</note> by the **firmamental must** <note>original: *Firmamentischer Most*; "must" refers to young, unfermented wine; here Paracelsus uses it as a metaphor for celestial or astrological influences that overwhelm the mind</note>. Therefore, they do not have one wisdom, but each has a particular one, just like every fool; no fool follows another fool, but each likes his own way best, and they never arrive at any perfect truth at any time.

<summary>Paracelsus compares spiritual or celestial influence to physical drunkenness, identifying five types of "intoxicated" wisdom that cause humans to lose their reason and twist the truth. He argues that these celestial influences, or "firmamental must," lead to fragmentation and error rather than a single, perfect truth.</summary>

## What the Inclined is, and its Kinds.

Now know further concerning the fourth **part** <note>original: *Membro*; a section or member of his argument</note> that the stars sometimes rule a person themselves and draw them according to their own will. This is to be understood in this way: the stars sometimes prepare a work and wish to make it manifest through a human being. But if no person is present who stands in a natural conjunction with those stars, they choose one for themselves who is like an **Adopted Son** <note>original: *Filius adoptiuus*; someone chosen by the stars rather than born naturally into a specific destiny</note>. A father owes nothing to such a son; rather, whatever he bestows upon him does not come from friendship, blood, or legal right. In the same way, the **Star** <note>original: *Astrum*</note> also selects an **Adopted Son** for itself, through whom it works as if he were its own natural-born son.

Now, take note of this **Inclination** <note>the tendency or "leaning" a person has toward a specific craft or destiny influenced by the heavens</note>, that it carries out its influence in six different forms or **kinds** <note>original: *Species*</note>:

First, in the **Person**, that is, in flesh and blood. Here, it makes a particularly pleasant person who is more praiseworthy or even more hostile than other men.

Furthermore, it often changes the **mind** <note>original: *gemüth*</note> of a person so that this person’s mind surpasses all others. **Solomon** <note>The biblical King Solomon, famous for his divinely granted wisdom</note> was such an **Adopted Son** in terms of his person.

There are also **Inclinations** that **exalt the Spirit** <note>original: *Spiritum extolliern*</note>, so that this spirit stands above all others in luck, in schemes, and in all those things that belong to the spirit. The **Emperor Barbarossa of Swabia** <note>Frederick I (1122–1190), Holy Roman Emperor, a legendary figure in German history</note> was such an **Adopted Son**.

You should also know of the fourth **kind** of **Inclination**: that the stars sometimes prepare a **Doctrine** <note>a system of teaching or belief</note> which they wish to reveal through a human being. Thus they select someone through whom they fulfill it. In the realm of **Doctrine**, such **Adopted Sons** have been **Albertus Magnus** <note>A 13th-century polymath and theologian</note>, **Lactantius** <note>An early Christian author and advisor to Constantine</note>, **Wycliffe** <note>John Wycliffe, the 14th-century English reformer</note>, and others.

Likewise, the stars prepare a special **Art**, or a particular skill in **Commerce** <note>original: *Kauffmannschafft*</note>. And if they have no natural-born son through whom to fulfill it, they select one. Thus, an **Adopted Son** of **Art** was **Albrecht Dürer of Nuremberg** <note>The famous German Renaissance artist (1471–1528)</note>. Of **Commerce**, the **Adopted Son** is **Fugger of Augsburg** <note>The Fuggers were the wealthiest banking family in 16th-century Europe</note>.

Finally, note in the sixth **kind** that the **Star** <note>original: *Astrum*</note> sometimes gives birth to a physical skill so great that it surpasses all others. **Adopted Sons** of this kind are those who can **walk upon the rope** <note>tightrope walkers or acrobats</note>. Thus you understand the fourth part and its kinds:

->how the heavenly courses, in their Adopted Sons,<-
->act wonderfully; that is<-
->Inclination.<-

<header>The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus</header>

## What Impression is, and its Kinds.

So that you may understand the nature of **Impression** <term>Impressio: a celestial "stamp" or imprint left by the stars upon the physical body</term>, and in what form it is to be understood and recognized: it is a power that comes from the **Stars** <note>original: *Astris*</note> and serves only the **Elemental Body** <note>the physical body made of the four elements: earth, water, air, and fire</note>. It functions in such a way that it has no shared form with the **Astral Body** <note>the "star-body" or the spiritual/intellectual part of a human</note>. Rather, it is related to the Elemental Body in the same way that a color is related to an object; and just as the color and the object cannot be separated, so too the Impression and the Elemental Body cannot be parted from one another.

Now, regarding Impression, it must be understood as a principle that is born at the moment of conception and grows until **Birth** <note>original: *Partum*</note>, at which point it remains fully embodied. Furthermore, take note that just as an external color fades and changes over time—such as black, red, or yellow hair that later becomes gray or white—so too must Impression be understood. It is conceived and born with the human being, and along with its **Kinds** <note>original: *Speciebus*</note>, it conforms to the Elemental Body, ages with it, and transforms alongside it.

Now, Impression is the **Breath of Life** <term>spiraculum Vitae: the animating force or "divine breath" that sustains physical existence</term> of the Elemental Body. Within this **Breath of Life** <note>original: *spiraculo Vitae*</note> lie the essence and properties of the Elemental Body. And although I have stated that Impression comes from the stars, you should view the stars only as a **medium** <note>a channel or go-between</note> through which the Breath of Life is substantially delivered to the Elemental Body. In the same way, a human being is a medium who acts as he is, through that which he is.

The Elemental Body has no life within itself without the **Breath of Life** <note>original: *spiraculum Vitae*</note>. Now, there are two who breathe this Breath of Life into us: namely **God**, as the one from whom man has life, and those essences which are then innate to the body. But there is yet another "Inspirer" <note>one who breathes life in</note> who also inspires the Breath of Life along with its attached essence. Note the distinction between these two inspirations:

It is exactly like the situation between God and a **Physician** <note>original: *Artzet*</note>. Consider who it is that truly makes the sick person healthy: it is God, not the physician. Yet, the physician brings about the result. It is the same here: who gives the true **Breath of Life** <note>original: *spiraculum Vitae*</note>? It is God alone. But there is another who brings the reputation for it, and it is upon him that notice is 
taken.

## What Generation is, and its Kinds.

So you should also know that the **Principle of Generation** <note>original: *Membrum Generatio*</note> has four **Kinds** <note>original: *Species*</note> under it, namely according to the four elements. Now, the **Principle of Generation** is solely the **Communication** <note>original: *Communicatio*</note> that the stars share with the elemental world. Just as the Sun shares its warmth with the elements—and without the Sun they would all be dead—the Sun is the **breath of life of the Elements** <note>original: *spiraculum vitae Elementorum*</note>; it makes everything living that exists within the four elements. Man and the **Breath of Life** make the human being; man is a **Microcosm** <term>Microcosmus: a "little world"; the idea that the human body reflects the entire universe</term>, and his **breath of Life** is the **Creator of things** <note>original: *Conditor rerum*</note>. Now the **Elements are Wombs** <term>Matrices: literally "mothers" or "wombs," referring to the nurturing environment of the elements</term> and the **Firmament the Parents**; these two give birth to all the fruits that grow from the elements, and the Sun is their **breath of life**. That is, the Sun is the **breath of the things of Nature** <note>original: *spiraculi rerū Naturae*</note>. Thus **Generation** is to be understood in this way: that the elements can accomplish nothing without the **Star** <note>original: *Astrum*</note>. For the **Wombs** are the **Elements**, **Vulcan** <note>the Roman god of fire/blacksmithing, here representing transformative heat</note> is the **Sun**, and Nature is the **Maker** <note>original: *Fabricator*</note>. And even though the **Seeds** <note>original: *Semina*</note> lie in the **Womb** <note>original: *Matrice*</note> and not in the **Begetter** <note>original: *Genitore*</note>, look at the hen's egg: it comes from the hen and not from the rooster. But if it is to generate its **Chick** <note>original: *Pullum*</note>, it must happen through the rooster. So it is also to be understood here: that the **Wombs** contain the seed, but they receive the **Effect** <note>original: *Effectum*</note> from the **Star**, and the **Maturation** <term>Digestionem: in alchemy, the process of slow heating to bring something to maturity</term> from the Sun. The Sun hatches the fruits of all the elements, just as a hen hatches her eggs. Thus, you now know how to speak of **Generation**: that from the **Element of Water** grow and come all **Minerals**, **Salts**, **Metals**, **Gems**, **Stones**, and **Rocks**; and **Water** is the mother of them all, and the Sun hatches all these things within the Water. Likewise, know regarding the **Element of Fire**, that the fruits of this element are also cooked and hatched by the Sun. Now, the fruits of the Element of **Fire** are all

### What the Inanimate is, and its Kinds.

Concerning this **Part** <note>original: *Membro*; referring to a branch of knowledge</note>, it is somewhat more difficult to understand than the others. It is a person in whom no soul can be found to exist; and there are six kinds of such people. And just as we walk upon the earth and not *in* the earth, upon the water and not *in* the water, outside of the fire and not *in* the fire, and in such a manner also outside of the air and not *in* the air; so too there are **counterfeit humans** in the elements who dwell *within* the elements and not outside of them—as the **Phoenix** <note>the mythical bird of fire</note> lives in the fire, as the **Mole** <note>original: *Talpa*</note> lives in the earth, and so on. And no one should let themselves wonder at this, for it shall be proven that it is so in itself. However, the Giants and the Shadow-folk have their dwellings just like humans. So, know regarding their **Generations** <note>original: *Generationibus*</note> that they occur as follows: they are born through **Celestial and Elemental Seeds** <note>original: *Spermata*</note>, without the **Slime of the Earth** <note>original: *Limum terrae*; a reference to the biblical creation of Adam from the dust/clay of the earth</note>. They are also not **Creatures** <note>in the sense of being part of the primary divine creation of ensouled beings</note>, but rather grow just as dung beetles grow out of horse manure.

### What Meteorology and its Species are.

This **Branch of the Stars** <note>original: *Membrum Astrorum*</note> is **Meteorology**, and is called by its proper name **Sagacious Meteorology** <note>original: *Sagax Metheorica*; "Sagax" implies a wise or spiritually significant form of weather study</note>, and not **Minor Meteorology**. Now, this branch has retained many species within itself, bearing names identical to those in Minor Meteorology. However, so that you may understand the difference between the two types of Meteorology: know that Minor Meteorology is mentioned in the **Branch of Generation** <note>physical weather that affects crops and growth</note>; but here, in this Sagacious Meteorology, things are born in the **celestial Olympus** <note>original: *superno Olimpo*; the upper atmosphere or spiritual realm</note>. For example, **Rain**: this same rain does not come down to us as liquid rain, but as a dew or vapor. It also produces **Thunder and Lightning**; however, they do not strike our earth, but rather make a stroke downward. Because of the great distance down to the earth, they cannot reach it; instead, they fall down on the other part of the **Globe**. Thus, stones and other things are found there. Similarly, Sagacious Meteorology gives birth to **Blood, Metals, and other such things**. It gives birth to the **Dragons**, the **Phantoms**, the **Apparitions**, the **Likenesses**, the **Figures**, and the like <note>These terms refer to atmospheric phenomena like fireballs, auroras, and mirages, which Paracelsus viewed as spiritual entities</note>; and these come from above, so that they enter the **middle spaces** <note>original: *media Interstitia*; the layers of the atmosphere between heaven and earth</note>. Sometimes they are destroyed, consumed, and blown away by Minor Meteorology. In this Sagacious Meteorology is the **tincture of metals, of gems**, and of all **colors**. From this Olympus come the colors; in this Olympus sits the **Meteorological Vulcan** <note>original: *Vulcanus Metheoricus*; Vulcan was the Roman god of the forge; here he represents the divine alchemist of the sky</note>, who is the **father** of all **Tinctures and Colors**, etc. From Sagacious Meteorology proceeds the **conjunction of the Tincture** into the **Elemental Bodies**. ## What *New Growths* <note>original: *Noualia*; in Paracelsus's vocabulary, these are "innovations" or "novelties" in nature—specifically biological deviations or growths that occur outside the standard divine blueprint</note> are, along with their *Species* <note>original: *Speciebus*; types or varieties</note>.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter W featuring scrolling foliage and floral motifs.</image-desc>Just as every thing was created, how one thing should beget another—both the sentient and the insentient—God established this in the order, and God was well pleased, and all things were good. But now, furthermore, that same order has been broken, and many "mis-growths" have occurred, or things that are different from the order that Nature has in itself. I do not point this out here so that something should be predicted from it, but rather they are merely *Errors of Nature* <note>original: *Errata Naturae*</note>. I point it out because the Astral Nature <note>the "star-driven" forces that influence biological development</note> causes this. 

As an example: Nature makes no fools <note>original: *Narren*; often referring to people with congenital intellectual disabilities</note>, for it is not its order, nor is it the gift that God has given it; rather, an Error <note>original: *Error*</note> has occurred which has broken the order of Nature. 

As an example: Imagine a hundred men sitting in judgment, and each one is supposed to make a statue. When they are finished, no statue is like the other; the one who has the skill makes it correctly, but among the ninety-nine, none makes anything good. Thus Nature possesses the art of how it should make a human, or any other growth. But because there are so many factors that "make" a human <note>referring to the various competing celestial influences acting upon a fetus or a plant</note>, each one comes and makes his own pattern, and with that, the work is spoiled. It is just as when a room full of people sit in a council: each one wants his own advice to be followed, and so a resolution is passed and made that looks just like a fool who has many goiters <note>original: *Kröpff*; swellings of the neck, used here as a metaphor for an ugly, disorganized result</note>. 

Therefore, know the nature and quality of the stars—that they are not always in total harmony. From this discord springs a mixed work in the mind and in the body, not only in humans but also in those who have feathers <note>birds</note>. *Monsters* <note>original: *Monstra*; biological abnormalities or "prodigies"</note> are produced among the cattle, in the fish, in herbs, in trees, etc., which go against their order, figure, and form.

And he spins, so that the human is brought into another form, and spins him back into the old form. This happens because we are clay and mud; we are nothing other than that. Therefore (as an example), we are transformed as a testimony. When God wills, we are mud and clay again. And as much as is necessary to hold up as an example to us, that much and no more do such **operations** <note>original: *Operationes*; the practical workings or rituals of the art</note> occur.

Therefore, in further testing the accompanying **species** <note>original: *Species*; the various types or outward appearances of things</note>, and in making **sigils** <term>Characteres; symbolic marks or signs used in magic to channel specific influences</term> and **talismans** <term>Gamaheu; stones naturally marked with images or figures, believed to hold celestial virtues</term>, no one should be surprised. For the reason is this: if Nature willingly endows herbs and stones with their own properties, so that they contain **magical powers** <note>original: *Magicas Vires*</note>, how much more does she do so when she is petitioned for it? For the reason is that stones, herbs, and the like cannot be found in all places. For where can one find enough **lodestones** <note>original: *Magneten*</note>? Where enough sapphires? Where can one find everything in the meadows and the fields? It is this deficiency that necessitates the use of **magic** <note>original: *Magicam*</note> here.

From this it now follows that Nature places her powers into words, just as into herbs and roots, and likewise into **talismans** <note>original: *Gamaheu*</note>, and also into images—just as these things are revealed according to the art. These are solely the arts that compensate for the same deficiencies that Nature bears in her growth toward mankind. Thus, notice further that the **Kabbalah** <term>Cabalistica or Cabalia; a mystical tradition involving the power of names, letters, and numbers</term> also makes use of such magical powers, specifically in this manner: Suppose there is a pipe that is a mile long, and someone speaks through that pipe, and at the other end of the pipe stands the listener; then he may [hear] this **sentence** <note>original: *Sententz*; a thought or statement</note>

But so that I may answer you further from the Light of Nature <note>The "Light of Nature" is a central Paracelsian concept referring to the wisdom and knowledge found within the physical world, accessible through observation, experience, and the human intellect, as opposed to the Light of Grace which comes from divine revelation.</note> regarding the potential of the Magi, you should first understand this: Nature is first and foremost a magician <term>Maga; the feminine form of Magus, personifying nature as an active, magical force</term> herself. Sometimes this is through man, acting as his instrument, for a new future judgment against nature; or, through the stars, he can prophesy on his own without the involvement of men. 

When he wishes to signal something, he brings forth those very harbingers, such as comets or visions in the sky—there is no need to recount them here. But that man is a <term>Magus; a practitioner of magic who understands and directs the hidden forces of nature</term>, or may be one, means that he is appointed to it just as a hammer is appointed to smithing. To understand this further, note this example: A physician knows and recognizes all the powers that reside in herbs. Likewise, the **Magus** knows what resides in the stars, and nothing is hidden in the heavens that is not possible to know through **Astronomy** according to its various branches <note>original: *Speciebus*; here referring to the different categories or applications of astronomical knowledge</note>. 

Now, the physician extracts the power from the herbs and calls it a remedy. This remedy is small in weight, yet he holds many meadows and fields in his fist—that is to say, the meadows and fields are not the medicine, but the extract alone is the medicine. In the same way, the Magus can bring many "meadows" of the heavens into a small stone and call it a <term>Gamaheu; a natural stone believed to have astrological or magical properties, often bearing a natural image or "signature"</term>, or an image, or a character. For these things are the vessels in which the Magus preserves the <term>Sidereal Forces; powers derived from the stars (from the Latin *sidereus*)</term> and virtues. 

There is nothing else to speak of or understand here except a <term>Reseruaculo; a reservoir or receptacle</term>. And just as the physician may give his medicine to the sick, and it turns the illness away for him, so too can the Magus bring such <term>Virtutes; virtues or inherent powers</term> into a person after he has extracted them. That is to say, as he is able to grasp them from the stars, so can he also perform them, for good or for ill. The medicine grows anew every year...

# The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus

...and comes with new powers; but the old Nature and the stars have their *exaltations* <note>original: *Exaltationes*; in astrology, the sign in which a planet is thought to have its strongest influence</note> in place of their summer, so that they also reserve their time for themselves, before which is their winter, during which they give nothing; rather, they should be sought in their summer. Thus, Nature is never found empty, but always like a rich man's chest: when it is emptied, it becomes full again, and man puts nothing into it. It is not like the fig tree that Christ cursed, but rather, he who seeks finds. For wherever Christ goes, He shall find what He seeks; if not, it shall be cursed. Therefore, we should watch continually, just as Nature does for us, working without ceasing; this should be an example to us. This [constant work] is not within us humans—as it is in the stars and elements—according to the new creature <note>Refers to the spiritually reborn person in Christian theology</note>; rather, with us, there is neither summer nor winter, but a daily watching and looking out.

No one should marvel that such powers are to be brought down into a medium. For consider the example: the Sun has no other quality in itself than simply being the highest *degree* <note>original: *Gradus*</note> of natural daylight. Furthermore, where the daylight is, there also is the heat, for the daylight is set within the heat. Now it comes down to us—for thus it was created—upon the whole earth, just as all other firmamental stars do. Now, look at its effect and what it does. There are many more such stars that are not so visible. Now, how is it possible that this daylight, with its embodied warmth, might be brought down through man into a *subject* <note>original: *Subiectum*; the material or person receiving the influence</note>? Not at all. For it has a *limit* <note>original: *Terminum*</note> of what it should give us, as do all other stars; for it comes down itself with all its powers, as much as is belonging and ordained to us.

But it is possible that it might be brought even higher through the *Magus* <note>The practitioner of "Sagacious Philosophy" or spiritual science</note> in brightness and heat, yet only so that this happens through what is ordained for us, and that the *body* <note>original: *Corpus*</note> be engaged without being harmed. Take the Sun as an example: how it blinds and burns and ignites—that is the *magical power and impression* <note>original: *Magica Vis et Impressio*; the active force of the celestial body acting upon the physical world</note>. And these powers are to be understood differently, such that there is a *gradation* <note>original: *Gradation*</note> that *exalts the Fifth Essence* <note>original: *quintum Esse*; also known as the Quintessence, the purest and most potent core of a substance</note>. Its quality is demonstrated by the Sun through the burning-mirror <note>original: *Feuwer spiegel*</note>; it surpasses our eyes, and our sensitivity cannot endure its heat. This happens through the *roundness* <note>original: *rotunditet*</note> of the crystal and other similar burning-mirrors, which are subsequently called *incendiaries* <note>original: *Incensoria*; lenses or mirrors used to concentrate sunlight</note>. Through their brilliance, they blind the eyes, igniting, burning, and scorching. The Sun can do no more than this here on Earth; likewise, other *powers* <note>original: *Vires*</note> of the stars may also be increased.

Since the Magus <note>original: *Magus*; a practitioner of natural magic who understands the hidden workings of the universe</note> is thus able to bring down every power of the stars into his designated *subject* <note>original: *Subiectum*; the physical object or person intended to receive the celestial influence</note>—just as a hunter traps a deer in a net, and a fisherman the fish in his net, or as the physician puts medicine into a jar—can he not then create images <note>original: *Bilder*; here referring to astrological talismans or sigils engraved to capture stellar power</note>? These are to be understood in no other way than if one were to ask: can the physician not make an ointment from medicine, or a plaster, or a potion, or a fumigant? In the same way, can the Magus not take a "firmamental" <note>original: *Firmamentischen*; belonging to the heavens or the stars</note> medicine and create an image, a sphere, a stone, or something else? For it is, and should be, equal in *form* to that power. Why should he not be able to create such figures that might aid in health and sickness? 

Indeed, the heavens themselves create figures, as we see in comets <note>original: *Cometis*</note> and halos <note>original: *Halonibus*</note>, in "lances" <note>original: *Lanceis*; spear-shaped meteorological phenomena or meteors</note> and other exhalations <note>original: *Exhalationibus*; vapors or atmospheric phenomena once thought to cause celestial displays</note>. If the heavens can judge over man—moving the natural flesh here and there, and killing it, or laming it, or making it healthy and the like—why then should the Magus not also have this within his power? He is as capable as the physician with his medicine, accomplishing as much as his power allows. 

For the reason, note this example: just as poison and other things—both good and evil, pure and impure—are able to spring from the earth, the heavens are equally capable of the same. The physician takes from the earth; the Magus from the heavens. Why then should it not also happen in those things which are in the stars, just as well as in those which are in the earth? Whether it be in images, stones, herbs, or words, that power is brought into them just like good or evil medicine is placed in jars. 

Thus, magic <note>original: *Magica*</note> is to be understood as nothing other than a "high medicine" which acts solely from the *firmament* and within the *firmament*, whether it be natural or supernatural, as has been sufficiently told until now. All this lies in how the stars carry their *impregnation* <note>original: *impregnation*; the celestial "seeding" or influence</note> and how the *conceptions* <note>original: *Conceptiones*; the structural design or "taking in" of these influences</note> are arranged upon it; according to this, every effect occurs. It is not only that man handles such things, but Nature herself practices them in many ways; for we see clearly that the heavens themselves work good and evil among us. Why should the Magus not also do the same through the heavens, just as the heavens do? For it is in the *firmament*, and it is there so that the heavens may be under man—as much subject to him as leaves and grass. For there it is found what the Prophet says: "You have made all things subject to him, the birds of the heavens, the fish in the water" <note>A reference to Psalm 8:6-8</note>. If these must now be under man, then everything must be under him that may be of use to man; and whatever Nature is capable of, that must be under man. <meta>This page continues Paracelsus’s critique of superstitious beliefs regarding the state of the soul and the astral body after death. He transitions from discussing the power of the Magus to the specific errors of those who misunderstand the nature of the "sidereal body" or the remains of the deceased.</meta>

### *Philosophia Sagax* of Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus von Hohenheim, better known as Paracelsus (1493–1541)</note> ###

The common opinion—that they thus sit in Purgatory or in Hell, and must do penance there until the Last Day <note>original: *Jüngsten Tag*; the Day of Judgment</note>, thereafter to be saved or damned. Man occupies himself with such folly, holding such fantasy for great wisdom, though it is nothing but a shadow, as has been mentioned. However, so that I may further instruct you: three strange orders have thus fallen into error within Necromancy <note>original: *Nigromantia*; for Paracelsus, this is the natural science of the sidereal body, not "black magic" in the modern sense</note>, namely Exorcists, Conjurers, and the "Dead-bookmakers" <note>original: *Todten büchler*; those who use ritual books to perform services for the deceased</note>. 

The Exorcists presume to have power over such sidereal bodies <term>sidereal body: *Syderische Leib*; the "star-body" or astral remnant that remains on earth after the soul has departed and the physical body has rotted</term>, which they call spirits, so that they might speak with them and receive answers to their questions. They forget that a dead thing cannot speak; that is, they wish to act naturally upon the same ground as one might act with a [living] human, expecting it to show all its secrets and reveal them. They believe the spirits should do the same; and yet, there is nothing more to be gotten out of them than what may be observed from the remains themselves through their transformation. Nothing further can come from a dead thing. 

The Conjurers <note>original: *Coniuristen*</note> adjure <note>original: *beschweren*; to bind or command through ritual</note> these same sidereal bodies, forgetting that man has no power to adjure sidereal bodies. From such frivolous hearts it follows that the Devil possesses such sidereal bodies, and thus satisfies their frivolity. For if he can possess a living human, how much more so a dead one in whom there is no resistance at all? And thus these same spirit-conjurers deal with the Devil and not with the human; they are devil-conjurers, not human-conjurers. And they are thus gladdened by the Devil in their adjuration, as much as diabolical joy allows. 

The Dead-bookmakers are those who wish to bring such sidereal bodies into Heaven through their intercession, forgetting that nothing enters Heaven except that which comes from Heaven. They also forget that man may not have his dwelling place after death in such a way—that is, that he remains in the grave or in the air—but rather he has another vessel <note>original: *Behalter*; a place of keeping or preservation</note> in which he is kept until the time of the inquiry, when the great trumpets shall be blown and say: "Arise, ye dead," etc. 

Necromancy does not concern itself with such three strange specters <note>original: *Spectarum*</note>, but rather treats only that which is natural, in the same way that a physician treats medicine. Therefore, know how to distinguish the natural and the supernatural from one another, so that the true ground of Astronomy <note>original: *Astronomia*; here referring to the science of celestial and sidereal influences</note> may be found and recognized. # The First Book #

...as the Thief <note>original: *Latro*; referring to the Penitent Thief on the cross (Luke 23:43)</note> entered Paradise, or as the Rich Man was buried in Hell. Thus it would be sufficient to know that this error is a mere charade—the belief that such beings should be kept here on Earth—when Scripture indicates otherwise and dismisses such fantasy.

To instruct you regarding Necromancy <note>original: *Nigromantia*; for Paracelsus, the study of the sidereal or astral body rather than "black magic"</note>, understand it in this form: Astronomy <note>original: *Astronomia*; here referring to the science of the influence of the stars on the human constitution</note> proves through itself that the earthly conduct of Man is the Stars, and this same influence is contained in its own body and remains within it until it is consumed. However, it is just like the physical body <term>elementated body: *Elementierte Leib*; the physical body composed of the four elements (earth, air, fire, water)</term>, which loses one limb after another until all are consumed. First, the hearing; following that, the sight; then the ability to move; and further, the voice and speech, which pass away along with the others; after that the blood; then the fluids; then the flesh; then the veins. The bones remain, for they are compared to gold, whose nature and character they share.

Note then by this example: the sidereal body <term>sidereal body: *Syderisch leib*; the "star-body" or astral remnant that remains on Earth for a time after the soul has departed</term> also loses one piece after another: its understanding, its wisdom, its art, its skill, its ornament, and so on. For these are its limbs, and of these limbs it also loses one after another: first the understanding, then the wisdom, then the art, then the senses—each according to how it existed within the person—until they are all consumed and nothing remains of it. 

And although the bones remain in a human because they are "fixed" <note>a term from alchemy meaning resistant to change or fire</note>, they too are ultimately perishable over time. So, know this of the sidereal body’s capacity: it cannot hear, nor can it speak. It has no eyes, and therefore it cannot see. Furthermore, what does one hope to drive out of it? When the erring ones then presume and want to force a thing to speak that was not created for speaking, they want to have from it a thing that God did not give it. It is expected to answer, to hear, to see, and to obey, yet none of these faculties remain within it. Therefore the Devil delights in them, because they seek that which is not in these remnants. 

The sidereal body possesses movement only because, during life, it moved the physical body, and through that physical body it spoke, saw, and heard. But once they are separated from one another, none of these faculties can exist anymore; they are dead and without power. For while it moved the physical body during the time of life—since there is no movement inherent in the physical body itself—once it is separated from the physical body, there is no longer movement in that body. The movement resides in the sidereal body; therefore it goes about as a dead thing, and is dead. It moves nothing but itself until its final consumption. The properties it retains are those of the heart, which is the mind...

Therefore, no one should wonder if, after a person's death, the figure of that same person is seen. It is a spectacle of the dead <note>original: *Spectackel der Todten*; an apparition or ghostly manifestation</note>, in which we the living should reflect and philosophize, leaving and desisting from our evil habits. For whatever dies temporally in such a mind is visible—unless that temporal mind is taken away.
