Therefore, to report to you concerning <term>necromancy: *Nigromantia*; for Paracelsus, this is the study of sidereal remnants rather than the conjuring of souls</term> as it is in itself, no further power is to be granted to it than what has not yet been taken away through consumption. For regarding the dead <term>elementated body: *Elementierten Leib*; the physical body composed of the four elements</term> after death, one is not to seek speech, sight, hearing, or movement; and the longer it lies there, the less there is to be found in it. What remains, however, indicates the "old man" in his constitution <note>original: *complexion*; the physical and humoral makeup of a person</note>. So it is also in the sidereal body, where the heart of the deceased person was focused...

Now, they do not consider that they are searching where there is nothing. Something may indeed follow within the **sidereal bodies**, but not toward any fruitfulness; yet it happens in this way: 

A human being who is "whole"—with the **elementated body** <note>the physical body made of the four elements</note> and **sidereal body** unseparated—has a nature within them regarding what they like or dislike, what they want or do not want, what pleases or displeases them; they direct themselves according to this and give their consent. If the exorcist can use that which was pleasing to the deceased person, the spirit will consent to him, yet only in the manner of a shadow; but if he uses something contrary to the spirit's nature, he will also receive a contrary response—and again, only in the manner of a shadow. 

That something might be sought and taken from this, or found to be fruitful, cannot happen in any other way than this: as when a person had buried a treasure and intended to reveal it before the separation of both bodies <note>i.e., before death</note>. If, after death, that same exorcist were the one to whom the treasure should have been revealed by that person, and he is brought to this **sidereal body**, then the treasure would be revealed to him. But if he is not that specific person, nothing will be made known to him at that place. This does not happen out of the soul, or out of the spirit of life, or out of the Eternal, or out of the image that is given after God <note>the *Imago Dei* or divine spark</note>, but occurs solely out of the perishable, mortal **sidereal body**. 

For you should know this: just as the **elementated body** must rot and become ashes, so also the earthly senses and thoughts, powers and mind <note>original: *Gemuͤt*</note> must rot and become a wind. The power and authority over the **sidereal body** is like this: they attempt something that is nowhere possible, neither with the Saints nor with Nature. Therefore, such frivolity achieves only this: that they incite Satan, who otherwise lies on a chain; for we are the ones who tread upon snakes and dragons. And we are the ones who are Satan’s chains, binding him. If we are in such frivolity that we do not allow ourselves to be and remain as such chains, but instead break the rings ourselves—

And yet, they do not speak such words from theology, but from "fantasy" <note>baseless speculation or false imagination</note>, which is their theology; as **necromancy** proves, which reveals hidden things and is specifically ordained for that purpose, and given by God and not by the Devil—through nature, not through the Devil. Thus, through its natural operation, the natural forces are experienced. For nature has nothing so secret hidden within her that can hide itself from the foundation of this Art.

Thus should the arts be experienced: what lies in the sea, in mountains, in rocks, in man, and in all corners, whether in the light of day or in the darkness. Therefore, it is necessary that we have a knowledge of this art of **necromancy** and understand and recognize it rightly in its foundation, so that we may learn to experience the wonderful works and **great deeds of God** <note>original: *Magnalia Gottes*</note> in the natural **mysteries** <note>original: *Mysterijs*</note>. Although the ancients, our ancestors, discovered many kinds of medicines through this art—which we have inherited from them and enjoy the fruits of their discovery—the art has not been used as perfectly as was necessary. # The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus

Without this seeking, no one achieves anything, for seeking itself creates the Art. From this it follows that Nature presents us with Arts through which we should search; and these same Arts are not from men, but out of Nature. Nature acts in a similar way [to a human]: where there is a heart, there is also a mouth; where there is a mouth, there is also a voice—and that is the opening of the heart. So, where the treasure is, there is also a heart and a mouth, and that [mouth] is the Art. Therefore, its effects are to be sought out of Nature and not from men. For Nature searches within herself for what is in her, and she has an eye that sees into all her secrets. That same eye is **Necromancy** <note>original: *Nectromantia*; here Paracelsus uses the term not for dark magic, but for the "sidereal" or star-like power of human perception to see the internal essence of things.</note>, and in that same eye are the arts of seeking. Whatever is taken from that eye seeks rightly and finds. That same eye of Nature is so sharp that no power in Nature can hide so well that Nature shall not find it. For just as no man may hide himself from God, so too can nothing hide from Nature.

Thus God has established an order, so that through such an eye every hidden thing makes itself manifest, just as the Gospel saying holds: "Out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth overflows" <note>A reference to Matthew 12:34 or Luke 6:45.</note>. This means the secrets of the heart open themselves through the mouth; he who now hears the mouth hears the secrets of the heart. So it is with all hidden things: there is not one of them that does not have, in place of a mouth, a **Spirit** <note>original: *Spiritum*</note> which is the mouth, which chatters what is within it—that is, what lies within the thing that it is. Thus the mouth is an eye that sees into the heart. Therefore, we should understand the Art in such a way that there is no other foundation than to seek solely with the Light which is Nature itself. In that same Light is found that which no one knows; without that Light, all things remain in darkness, in which nothing at all can be sought, but which instead produces a labyrinth that can never reach its center. **A**ll that Nature brings forth, she forms according to the essence of the **virtue** <note>original: "Tugendt"; here meaning the inherent power, property, or "potency" of a thing rather than moral goodness</note> that is within it. ...makes it manifest. Therefore, thirdly, through **Divine judgment**—that is, as God himself ordains—the **Heart** comes to light and is revealed for what it truly is. Divine power drives this forth as a warning or a lesson to other people; just as the righteous are known through **righteous Works**, and the wicked through **evil Works**. As He also says: *By their works you shall know them, and by their fruits* <note>A reference to Matthew 7:16: "Ye shall know them by their fruits."</note>. For the works and the fruits indicate what kind of tree it is; and just as no grapes grow on thistles, so little good comes from a **thistle-man** <note>original: "Distelmenschen"; a person whose nature is prickly, harsh, or barren of virtue</note>. I will set aside those two paths—self-betrayal and God’s command to recognize men by their fruits—for experiencing them firsthand requires no special skill, and what God does is plain to the understanding and requires no writing. However, regarding the **Signs** that Nature has presented, I wish to provide further instruction.

In the same way that you see openly when a seed is sown in the earth and hidden within it, Nature drives the secret of that same seed up into the light of the earth, so that everyone sees what kind of seed was lying in that place. In this way, the **Heart** is the seed of the human, and Nature drives the **Body** out of that same seed, so that everyone may see what kind of heart was there. And although a wide and noticeable difference can be understood in flowers and woods—being more easily recognized than in humans—the **Art** <note>original: "Kunst"; here referring to the Science of Signatures</note> still provides enough knowledge for us to recognize them, if we explore and fathom Nature as she opens herself in the **Signed** <note>original: "Signato"; referring to an object that bears a signature or mark of its inner nature</note>, etc.

We humans on Earth learn of everything that lies within the mountains through external signs and analogies; likewise, all properties in herbs, and everything that is within stones. There is nothing in the depths of the sea, nor in the heights of the **Firmament** <note>The sphere of the stars or the heavens</note>, that man must not recognize. No mountain, no rock is so thick that it can withhold and hide what is within it, or keep it from being revealed to man. All of this comes through its **Signed Mark** <note>original: "signatum Signum"</note>. This is before our eyes in the same way as a pear on a tree, which creeps forth from the wood, from the roots, and from the earth, and indicates what is within that tree. For every fruit is a **Sign that has been Marked** <note>original: "Signum Signatum"</note>, through which it is recognized what is within the thing from which it comes.

Thus, nothing can be within a human that is not marked on his outside, through which one may recognize what is within the person who carries that **Signed Mark**. And in the same way that a **Physician** <note>original: "Arzt"</note> has his skill in the knowledge he takes from the **signed mark**, so too does the **Astronomer** <note>original: "Astronomus"; in the 16th century, this included the study of astrology and the influence of the heavens</note from the **Signed**—that is, from what the Heavens place before him.

For nothing exists in the stars that does not have its **marked sign** <term>signatum Signum; the outward mark that reveals an inner essence</term> visible upon it. Just as herbs have their **sign** <term>Signum</term> and the stars have theirs—from which **signs** <term>Signis</term> the physician and the astronomer are created and derive their art—so too is the knowledge of man's inner being recognized through the **marked sign**. This sign is assigned to him by the **craftsmanship** <term>Fabricatio</term> within the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosmus; the "little world" of the human being which mirrors the vast universe</term>. 

He who does not become an astronomer through the **marked sign** is no astronomer; he who does not philosophize through the **marked sign** is no philosopher; he who does not practice medicine through the **marked sign** is no physician. There is a natural **Astronomy** <term>Astronomia</term> that crafts itself within the human being; the **firmament of the Microcosm** is his heaven, his **course** <term>Cursus</term>, his **sphere** <term>Spher</term>, his **ether** <term>Aether</term>, and his **Olympus** <term>Olimpus; here meaning the highest spiritual heights within a person</term>. 

Note further: Nature has made four things manifest to humans, as well as to every living growth; understand it thus: In these four arts, the secrets of hidden, invisible things are recognized and discovered. 

Namely, through **Chiromancy** <term>Chiromantiam; the art of reading signs and lines on the body, not just the palms</term>. This art includes the outermost parts of the "branches" in humans, such as the hands and feet, along with the other streams, lines, and wrinkles of the body—all of these belong together. This is to be understood so: that within the feet, hands, and veins, the **marked signs** <note>original: "Signa signata"</note> are contained. In these, the **Chiromancer** <term>Chiromantes</term> shall be trained, not only to recognize humans through them, but all herbs, stars, and whatever else exists. All things are placed into these **Chiromantic signs**, and **Chiromancy** is the **star of natural things** <note>original: "Astrum rerum Naturalium"</note>. Just as there is Chiromancy in **lilies** <note>original: "Gilgen"</note>—that is, the lily has its "star" according to the nature of the lily—this is the first **kind of marking** <term>Species Signati</term>.

Furthermore, the second part is **Physiognomy** <term>Physionomia</term>, which concerns the form of the face and everything the head encompasses. This art of **Physiognomy** provides the **marking** <term>Signatum</term> of the higher thoughts and senses. For the heart is one thing, and the head is another; and although the head is not the heart, the heart is truly the heart. From this it follows that man recognizes what is in both. 

Thirdly is **Substance** <term>Substantia</term>, which concerns the form of the entire body. This art teaches one to recognize—just as the other two do—what a person's senses, thoughts, and heart intend, and what he is dealing with internally within himself. For Nature herself has a displeasure for an evil inner person; therefore, she marks them in four ways, so that nothing remains hidden or exists that is not made manifest through the **marking** <term>Signatum</term>. 

And fourthly is **Custom and Usage** <term>Mos et Vsus</term>, which refers to the way and gesture with which a person presents and conducts themselves. This applies to other things as well: as in nettles with their burning, or in **Spanish flies** <term>Cantaridibus; blister beetles used in historical medicine</term> with the raising of blisters. Thus, these four things belong together; that is, they constitute a complete knowledge of the hidden, internal...

The physician must recognize the four **species** <term>original Latin: species; here meaning specific types or categories of signs</term>, for then he recognizes the medicine through its form and figure, which is divided into four shapes, as the four arts demonstrate. Thus the physician recognizes the medicine, the astronomer his astronomy, the shoemaker his leather, the weaver his cloth, the carpenter the wood, the miner the metal. Thus, every thing recognizes its **subject** <term>original Latin: subiectum; the underlying material or focus of a craft</term> that is entrusted to its **faculty** <term>original Latin: facultet; a specific branch of knowledge or professional domain</term>.

Thus, it is Nature that reveals what is within every single thing; and he who does not possess such art—to understand these four things and to recognize the secrets of Nature from them—cannot be a **naturalist** <note>original: "Naturalis"</note>, cannot be a natural astronomer, cannot be a natural physician, nor can he be a natural philosopher; nor can he know anything of the secrets of Nature or speak of her **mysteries** <term>original Latin: mysterijs; hidden divine or natural truths</term>. Thus, the foundation enters into our knowledge and understanding, because all things have a seed, and within the seed all things are enclosed; and Nature is the **maker** <term>original Latin: Fabricator; the creative force that builds the physical form</term> into the figure—so she provides the form, which is the essence within itself, and the form indicates the essence, for the essence is invisible. Therefore, these four things belong to **Astronomy** <term>original Latin: Astronomiam</term>, so that in their **conception** <term>original Latin: Conception; the moment of formation or "birthing" of an idea or object</term> they are ordered, made, and joined together. Therefore, their interpretation proceeds from Astronomy, along with the others born under this conception, etc.

Thus, Nature has ordained that the outward signs indicate the inner works and **virtue** <term>original German: Tugendt; in this context, it refers to the specific healing power or spiritual "talent" of a substance</term>; thus it has pleased God that nothing remains hidden, but rather that through the **sciences** <term>original Latin: Scientias</term> everything lying within all creatures should be revealed. Some might wonder why God has ordained such a thing—that man should learn hidden matters through art? Yet the reason is solely so that the body of man might have its exercise or the like, and experience what God has spiritually placed and created within bodies. Therefore, He did not ordain that **science** <note>original: "Scientia"</note> should be unknowable; rather, all secrets are within it, and all virtues are subject to the sciences so that through knowledge we may experience what lies spiritually within all things.

Another example: to whatever purpose a thing belongs, for that purpose it is formed. Just as one who wishes to build a tower and a bulwark gives it the form that is most skillful for standing against the enemy; and anyone who has knowledge of a war-tower sees by its form what **virtue** <note>In this context, "virtue" refers to the inherent power, quality, or functional strength of an object.</note> the tower has within it, and for what it is intended.

Nature does the same to him; she marks the human according to what is in his heart, hanging her signs upon him. By those same signs, one sees the inner mind, just as one sees the carpenter in the house. 

Now, if man is so skillful that he can build himself a castle against all his enemies, and yet he cannot build it without displaying the outer signs, how much more does Nature possess such foresight? When she makes a human, his virtue and mind do not remain silent; instead, a warning is put forward, so that everyone knows how to protect themselves—just as one guards against a gunshot coming from a hidden loophole <note>literally "blind shooting-hole" or embrasure in a fortification</note>. 

Thus, there is nothing in Nature that does not have the **body** <term>original Latin: Corpus</term> matching its virtue. Every diligence should be used so that the form is well recognized, for then the virtue within it—which is its **spirit** <term>original Latin: Spiritus</term>—is also well recognized. In this way, Nature often makes a person crooked whom she intends to use for crooked things; and she makes him crooked so that one may guard against his "crookedness" as one would guard against a hidden loophole. Many such signs exist on humans, all of which proceed from the mind of the heart; and through that mind, they are brought into the form, so that the mind and the form become equal. 

For Nature intends the form of humans, and all that belongs to the **signed object** <term>original Latin: Signato; the physical thing that bears the marks of its inner nature</term>, to be recognizable to the **science of signatures** <term>original Latin: scientiae Signatae</term>. Thus, through the form, one finds what Nature intends to use that human for. Therefore, this art is given from the **Light of Nature** <note>A central Paracelsian concept: the innate wisdom and divine intelligence embedded within the natural world, accessible to human reason.</note> through **Divine Providence** <term>original Latin: diuinam Prouidentiam</term>. For this reason, this art should be held in great esteem and researched with all industry and diligence. For it is a great treasure for a man to recognize what lies in the heart of his counterpart—not only so that I may boast of knowing human secrets, but much more for the natural...

Growths <note>original: "Getwechß"; referring to plants or biological growths</note> are also recognized through the **signature** <term>Signatum: The "sign" or external mark on a natural object that reveals its internal healing properties or purpose.</term>. Thus is the nature of the will: what is intended to dye something black marks itself with black; blue marks itself through blue. If bark is to form on a tree, it marks itself as bark; a leaf marks itself as a leaf; a seed as a seed. And because nettles have a burning fire within them, they also mark themselves outwardly with burning. In this wonderful way, the **Light of Nature** <note>original: "Liecht der Natur"; a Paracelsian concept referring to the innate wisdom or divine intuition that allows humans to understand the natural world.</note> teaches us to recognize the inner heart through the external form, and has established this knowledge as an art. 

However, because many were recognized through this art and many treacherous hearts were discovered, those same people have sought to erase, displace, and obscure it. And thus **Philosophy** and **Medicine** have been grievously deceived and robbed of the ability to experience the secrets of Nature. I am often scolded for speaking out against certain prominent persons; but when I see that they hate their own nature—and the signs warn others of this as well—how can I be well-disposed toward one whom his own father did not favor, and who has become a failed child in his very birth? Therefore, I wished to point this out to you, so that you may hold love for this art and research it, to fathom the hidden treasures of Nature.

### Proof of the Sciences of the Uncertain Arts
<note>original: "Probatio in Scientias Artium Incertarum"</note>

It might seem strange that I present the "uncertain art" as certain and as a true art, since it appears to have no certain foundation or ground. Yet, uncertain things are revealed through it, and nothing should be accepted without a definitive basis. Here lies the most notable foundation: the work itself, which proves itself true. I must acknowledge that the other **particulars of Astronomy** have a constant foundation and visible proof within them; but these uncertain arts, of which there are four, cannot be proven with such visible evidence. But if something further also had a foundation—even if it were not laid out visibly, yet were as well-tested as that which is visible (just as crafts prove themselves through their own works, and do so visibly)—who then could say that such a thing should not also be called an art?

...be. Since something is indeed found in the work which is discovered through these **uncertain arts**, yet not all things were created to be seen visibly, nor are they fundamentally easy for everyone to understand. For invisible things work just as well as visible ones. Now, there is much in the **Light of Nature** <term>Light of Nature: The innate wisdom or divine intuition within the natural world that allows humans to understand hidden truths without formal schooling.</term> that our eyes do not see, and yet it is the natural light. Why does the wind blow? Who can grasp its movement? Yet it blows down trees, walls, and towers. Should there not then be, in such power that moves the element, also a movement in the hands of **Geomancy** <term>Geomantiae: A method of divination that interprets markings on the ground or patterns formed by tossed handfuls of soil, rocks, or sand—here specifically referring to the involuntary movement of the practitioner's hand.</term>? Should there not be a movement in the eyes, since the elements are stirred by movement? It is just the same in man; the movement is great and there is nothing to dispute about it: "the spirit blows where it will," <note>original: "der geist wehet wo er wil"; a reference to John 3:8.</note> who knows from whence or whither? 

Take for yourselves an example of **dowsing rods** <note>original: "Virgulten"; refers to the wooden wands or rods used by dowsers to find water or minerals.</note> that move in the hands; no one sees who drives them, and yet it is natural, for the **mover** <note>original: "Motor"</note> is the **spirit of Nature** <note>original: "spiritus Naturae"</note>, to whom all things are known, and it may move a body according to harmony. Therefore, if a movement occurs in the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosmo: The human being, viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe (the Macrocosm).</term>, it must be caused by another; if by another, then it must be understood from what ground that same thing flows. Much must be granted to movement; movement has performed great works for both good and evil. Movement is the **Divine will**; what it gives depends on the judgment, yet the resulting sentence always falls upon the righteous heart. This is just as man is unequal in himself—one more truthful than the other—so it is also to be understood with the **mover**. Therefore, to have a righteous **mover** <note>original: "Motorem"</note> is to find what is hidden through the **uncertain arts**.

Now further it is to be known: these **uncertain arts** <note>original: "artes Incertae"</note> have a process and figure that are consistent with the natural order, and nothing is to be said against them. But the beginning that comes out of that same figure will not allow itself to be proven by the eyes. But just as the spirit of the image rules the stars, so also is a mastery given to the hands and eyes. And even though something happens through the hands, and also through the eyes, and they both might not be able to justify it—being merely instruments—no further questions should be asked of that which touches and guides the instrument. That is not an art, nor is it praiseworthy to discuss joining hand and hammer together; rather, that is the art which is worthy of praise: the one that guides the hand and hammer and forges that which is called a "Work." Even if one were to say: "**Geomancy** is no art, for there is nothing there but hands and chalk, and making **little dots** <note>original: "Tüpflin"; the points or marks made in geomantic divination.</note> out of them"—I grant that this is rightly said, except for the claim that it should be no art; that I contradict, for the reason:

Where does it come from for the blacksmith, that he makes a horseshoe with his hand and hammer? Not from the hand, nor from the hammer—for hand and hammer are just like hands and chalk in **Geomancy** <term>Geomantia: A method of divination using markings on the ground or patterns of earth.</term>—but what is it that makes the horseshoe? Namely, that which lies hidden in the head, which no one sees, which no one can grasp; that governs hand and hammer. That same thing forges and makes the horseshoe. Since the blacksmith [the true cause] does not reside in the hand or the hammer, but rather in the head—in that which one cannot see—might there not also be something in the craft of **Geomancy** that guides the hand and the chalk? 

Also in **Hydromancy** <term>Hydromantia: Divination using water.</term> the eyes, and **Pyromancy** <term>Pyromantia: Divination using fire.</term>? Must it not be conceded that the **Mover** <term>Motor: original Latin for the "driving force" or "agent" of an action.</term> in all practice is Nature, and man is her medium through whom she works? Therefore his body and his limbs are Nature’s **Instruments** <term>Instrumenta: original Latin for "tools" or "apparatus".</term>. Now, might it not be that a man can do what Nature teaches him and wants from him? Just as she wishes to make a painter out of one, so now she guides his hands to paint. If Nature wishes to work through the **uncertain arts**, can she not guide the hands and the eyes so that the very thing which lies within her might come to be, just as she brings craftsmen to the completion of their work, etc.?

Whether there might not also be something to say here concerning the hidden things in man, which govern something more than just the **elemental body** <note>original: "Elementierten Leib"; the physical body composed of the four elements, subject to physical laws.</note>. It is understandable that the elemental body has no order of its own to be obedient to the non-elemental body, but rather lets itself be used as an instrument. Now, the power within the **Light of Nature** <term>Light of Nature: The innate wisdom or divine intuition within the natural world that allows humans to understand hidden truths.</term> is such that human thoughts can work wondrous things, as is then clearly discovered. Now it is necessary to consider what thoughts are. 

So I tell you in truth: thoughts do what the **stars** <note>original: "Gestirn"; referring to the macrocosmic influences of astrology.</note> and the **Elements** <term>Elementa: The four building blocks of the world: earth, water, air, and fire.</term> are unable to do. Rather, thoughts rule and govern against them all. Thoughts are free and are governed by nothing; in thoughts resides the **Freedom of Man**. These thoughts surpass the **Light of Nature**, for out of thoughts is born a **Mover** <term>Motor</term> that is neither elemental nor **astrological** <term>Astrologisch: Relating to the influence of the planets and stars.</term>. If thoughts are so immensely powerful that they rule the stars and elements through the newborn spirit, should they not then also perform a different work than what the stars and elements are capable of? And yet, they produce a work just as righteous as the hidden thing in the head does with hand and hammer—that is natural. Thoughts make a new heaven, a new firmament, and also a new...

Man is created so powerful that he is more than

# The Wise Philosophy of Theophrastus

He who walks a path finds only what lies upon it; where nothing lies, nothing is found. And when one speaks of the discovery of the **arts** and of all future things of prophecy, who can judge hidden matters? Or be certain of things before they happen, except by confirming all things through **faith**? What proof do the prophets have, other than faith, until the time the event unfolds? And if one wishes to dig deeper, there are even more arts whose origins are harder to prove than simply saying they are "hidden events."

It is evident, and it is so, that God allows much to be revealed, and no one knows how; through "uncertain arts," <term>uncertain arts: practices like divination or intuitive healing that Paracelsus believed were grounded in spiritual insight rather than fixed physical rules.</term> many secrets are revealed. Not that one should question the underlying cause, but rather the will of God, which is revealed in strange ways. For you see well in divination <note>original: "diuintern"</note> how the stars <note>original: "Gestirn"</note> work strangely; so too they work strangely in the uncertain arts. It is not only that the stars act here, but often the stars deliver the judgment <note>original: "Iudicium," meaning the final discernment or astrological interpretation</note>, often it is one's own internal heaven, often the will of God, and often chance. That with which a person is in harmony <note>original: "concordiert"</note>, through that they bring about the effect.

Therefore, it is an uncertain thing, because no one knows who is at work; for flesh and blood can do nothing of themselves. Indeed, flesh and blood are not the man; rather, the **heart** is the man, and within the heart lie the hidden powers. According to what that heart is, so works its perfection, giving a form or figure of its judgment. This figure should not be set down without art; for although the beginning might not be called an art, it delivers its sentence <note>original: "Sententz"</note> through judgment and figure. And since judgment should not be handled without art, the art must provide the conclusion and judge and recognize the sentence. And if more is found in the art than was thought possible to experience, no one should be surprised.

# The First Book
<meta>catchword: sen</meta>

To know what **Adept Medicine** <term>Medicina adepta: A higher form of healing that addresses the influence of the stars and spiritual forces rather than just physical substances like herbs or minerals.</term> is, understand it this way: It deals solely with the diseases we receive from the heavens and those same heavenly influences. For there are two origins from which all diseases grow: one from the **stars** <note>original: "Gestirn"</note> and the other from the **elements**. Thus, there are also two kinds of doctors, two kinds of medicine, two origins, and two effects. Therefore, a doctor should apply himself with such diligence that he clearly knows and recognizes the difference, so that he does not attack a **siderial** <term>siderial: relating to the stars or constellations; here, meaning an illness caused by astrological influence.</term> disease with elemental medicines, nor an elemental one with siderial influence. For where this error occurs, it cannot happen without causing harm.

Thus, **Adept Medicine** is the art that alone provides such knowledge—to know and understand the siderial **infections** <note>original: "Infectiones"</note> and **expulsions** <note>original: "Expulsiones"</note>. For the failure found in medicine today is that doctors do not recognize siderial infections; they fall into error by trying to drive out siderial diseases with elemental medicines, which is contrary to the proper order of medicine.

As an example: The **Plague** <note>original: "Pestilentz"</note> is a disease from the stars, and this same infection presses upon us just as the sun does with its light. Now, an error follows in this disease when men attempt to drive out the Plague with elementalized medicine. This medicine cannot help against the siderial infection, though it may help with the condition that the body receives from that infection—which is then a **physical disease** <term>Morbus Physicus: a natural ailment of the body's elements, as opposed to a supernatural or astrological one.</term>. But what the stars—as the true **principal cause**—strike, cannot be averted here. It is true that elemental medicine helps only as much as a hat helps against the sun; the sun's rays are not removed by the hat, though one may find some protection from them. For in the same way that a fire burns from the outside, so too is the "burning" of a siderial disease to be recognized.

But just as cold and heat can harm the body, so too can the stars; the body is weakened and its strength is withdrawn, except through certain special powers within a human being that resist such infection. From this, it follows that not everyone can be infected. Therefore, know this of **Adept Medicine**: it alone distinguishes siderial diseases from elemental ones and heals them with siderial medicine. For where such understanding is lacking in doctors, great destruction occurs, as is taught and shown in their **practice** <note>original: "Practica"</note>.

Now see what **Adept Medicine** is in its foundation and origin—it is not earthly, dealing only with grass and hay, or kept in jars...

# The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus

An **Apollo** <note>Paracelsus uses the name of the Greek god of light and healing here to represent a divinely inspired or enlightened person.</note> must not learn from men, nor must he act according to elemental and earthly **reasons** <note>original: *rationibus*</note>; for only that which speaks of the things below pertains to what is below, but whatever wishes to speak from above must be learned from above. Likewise, the earthly through the earthly, and the firmamental through the firmamental. The Schoolmaster resides in the place where the subject of his teaching exists.

And the firmamental essence is learned from the Firmament just as easily and naturally as the earthly is learned from the earthly.

## Proof of the Science of Attained 
### Philosophy.

Furthermore, it is also to be known that <term>attained philosophy</term> <note>original: *Philosophia adepta*; the highest form of wisdom which connects the physician or philosopher to the divine secrets of nature.</note> proves itself in this way: it cannot be learned from man, but only from the school where it resides. We must note this well and clearly: there is a difference between learning from man and learning from the source where the thing itself originates. This is the nature of the instruction: how can a man teach me regarding "attained" things if he himself is <term>earthly</term> <note>original: *Terrenus*; meaning belonging to the earth or the fallen material world, as opposed to the spiritual or celestial.</note> and has learned nothing but what is of the earth? 

Therefore, I must seek another from whom I may learn, one who is an Adept. For just as <term>Theology</term> or <term>Justice</term> cannot be learned from anyone else except from Him who alone is God—who is Justice itself—so too can man reach the foundation of attained philosophy just as little. 

Now, so that you understand me on this point regarding what is to be learned from men and what is not: for example, you might say, "Is it not enough that I learn from Paul, and go to school with him, and take from his letters what is necessary for me? For in him I find it all. Likewise, I have other Apostles, and I have the Prophets, and I have the Evangelists. If I now read through these, explore them, and experience them, why do I need to ascend to the <note>This refers to the biblical account in 2 Corinthians 12, where the Apostle Paul describes being "caught up to the third heaven" to receive divine revelations.</note> third heaven or be caught up in ecstasy? Is it not enough to learn from them?" Furthermore, if I learn attained philosophy from someone who has it from the source who is the thing itself, then that is also enough for me. 

Regarding this, understand this foundation: it would be enough and more than enough, for the kingdom of God is among us. But this must also be present: "Without Your spirit, there is nothing in man" <note>original: *Sine tuo numine nihil est in Homine*; a line from the famous medieval hymn *Veni Sancte Spiritus*, emphasizing that human effort is empty without divine grace.</note>. Understand it thus: we have only the literal letter from those who have learned from Him who is the thing itself, and who possesses it, and who knows it. If we now wish to have the understanding in which the entire treasure lies—what those same letters enclose, grasp, and contain—then we must take that further. Namely, we must receive it from Him who learned to put the letters together; for no man can

Man should not presume to interpret or translate any kind of teaching unless he has it from the one in whom the interpretation resides. Therefore, because attained philosophy must be founded in such a way—not to be learned from man, for man does not know it, but to be learned from him who is and knows it—it follows that he must be above man and grasp more than is possible for a man who is <term>earthly</term> <note>original: *Terrenisch*; belonging to the material world or "fallen" nature.</note>.

To understand me well in this <term>section</term> <note>original: *Paragrapho*; a specific part or point of the argument.</note>, consider this example: The herbs, roots, seeds, trees, fruits, etc., and all precious stones that are on earth and in the four elements are nothing other than letters. # The First Book
## Proof in the Science of Mathematics
### Attained Knowledge. <note>original: "Adepta." In this context, "Adepta" refers to "attained" knowledge—wisdom that is not learned from books but through spiritual or natural insight.</note>

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'N' featuring intricate floral and vine patterns inside a square frame.</image-desc>

Now know that there is a difference between **elemental mathematics** and **attained** mathematics—that is, the **sidereal** <note>original: "Syderea"; relating to the stars or the astral realm.</note>. Although I have sufficiently indicated this in the interpretation, yet for the sake of the Proof <note>original: "Probation"; a demonstration of truth or validity.</note>, it is necessary to seek and receive a greater foundation.

Now know, in brief, that **elemental mathematics** <note>original: "Mathematica Elementata"</note> is visible and tangible, possessing a tangible body in which all mathematical forms <note>original: "Species"</note> are carried out. But now, **attained mathematics** <note>original: "Mathematica adepta"</note> also has a visible body, but it is not tangible; it is substantial but without a [physical] body, just as the sun appears in a body of water, or the moon in a well—understand this further. 

The elemental mathematician must use his own labor and make that which he desires himself, completing it with earthly bodies. Without these, he cannot carry out **arithmetic** <note>original: "Algorithmum"</note>, **geometry**, **cosmography**, and so on. Everything must pass through the elements and proceed from the circle, the number, the line, etc. And this must happen through the art that he learns elementally from the outside. For instance, a tree—one sees how it grows; the sun, how it moves; the moon, when it becomes new and full; all of this is elemental. 

But in **attained mathematics**, the stars, the **generated things**, the **created things**, the **essences**, and the **supreme mysteries** <note>original: "Archidoxa"; a term used by Paracelsus to describe the highest or most fundamental doctrines of nature.</note> place themselves into their own spheres, circles, courses, measurements, concave lines, and numbers—according to height, depth, width, and location. Thus, all things stand so perfectly that it would be impossible for an elemental hand to achieve. They stand corporally and substantially, yet intangibly; visible, but without physical substance; measured in every way and in every division with the greatest skill. Thus, all types of mathematics require only the mathematician's eyes, his careful observation, and his understanding of all things. 

In this way, **attained mathematics** is distinct in its powers, essence, and arts from earthly mathematics. Sidereal mathematics establishes and demonstrates things that are impossible for the elemental arts to find, and of which they have known nothing until now—less even than a mere taste. Every proportion, distance, and every aspect—nothing excepted—not a degree, not a minute is omitted, forgotten, or overlooked; rather, everything is there completely, modestly, and so clearly—

How much more in such **attained mathematics** <note>original: "Mathematica adepta." This refers to a higher form of knowledge that perceives the spiritual reality behind physical objects.</note> do things appear essentially. Just as with a person in a mirror, where nothing is left out that is not seen and placed within it, so in attained mathematics all **thickened bodies** <note>original: "Corpora ingrossata"; refers to the dense, physical matter of the world.</note> are removed, and only the **spiritual bodies** <note>original: "spiritualia Corpora"</note> remain.

And observe an example of this: the elements have a form and a body, which has a shape according to what it is. Now the **sidereal** <note>original: "Syderisch"; relating to the astral or "star-like" spirit that Paracelsus believed resided within all matter.</note> also has a form and a body, shaped according to what it then is. Now both bodies are mixed together as one; one sees the elemental [physical] body, but one does not see the sidereal [spiritual] body. For the elemental body is too coarse and too thick for one to be able to see through it. Now, however, pay heed to what follows: if the two bodies can be separated, so that one is seen by itself, un-darkened and uncovered by the other, then one sees how each body stands.

For a greater understanding, take note: gold that lies in darkness is seen by no one; if it lies buried in the earth, no one sees it. But now the **Attained Art** <note>original: "Kunst Adepta"</note> exists so that the night, the darkness, the earth, and so on, may be removed, and then the same thing may be seen brightly and clearly, as it is in itself. This is now attained mathematics, philosophy, and also medicine. The reason I say this here is because of what this example shows: a tree standing in the field has two forms, one elemental and one sidereal; the elemental is seen, but the sidereal is not seen.

Now the sidereal is the gold; the elemental is the night, the darkness, the earth, which covers that which is within it. If now this darkness, the earth, the night is removed—that is, the elemental body, which is the wood—then one sees the sidereal body pure and clear, as this example shows: A block of wood that lies there contains the image of a man, the image of a woman, the image of an animal, or whatever else one wishes; if one takes away that which belongs [to the outer part], then one sees what it is. <note>Paracelsus is using the metaphor of a sculptor: the statue is already "inside" the wood, but it is obscured by the excess material, which he equates to the elemental body.</note> Now, what is taken away is the night and the darkness; the earth has covered what was inside it. Thus, **attained science** <note>original: "adepta Scientia"</note> is that which can separate the "night-body," the dark body, and the earthly nature from the sidereal; and thus the sidereal remains whole and unstained, pure and clear, as represented and made possible by figures and all **geometry**, **cosmography**, **astrology**, and so on.

We only want to see what we see with elemental eyes—that is, the **face of heaven** <note>original: "faciem Coeli"</note>—in which the least art lies. That is the outer appearance; but the greater art is the inner sight. For what does it matter if someone looks at a beautiful young woman’s face on the outside, but does not know her on the inside? How quickly will he be deceived? So too, what does it matter that we look at the earth from the outside and do not know what is within it? What does it matter that we look at the water from the outside and do not know what is in it? If we were to wait until it reveals itself, it would be to our own harm—just like waiting for the young woman to show her malice after she was thought to be as innocent as a sheep. It would be a rough sight indeed. Should we wait until the fish themselves come to the shore? It is just the same.

Therefore, we should not take the outer appearance alone for the art, but rather regard it as a darkness, as a night in which the sun, the glow, and the light lie hidden. Thus we are also compelled to enter into **attained mathematics** and not keep **elemental mathematics** <note>original: "Elementalem"</note> as the whole of the science, nor to only know the **face of heaven**; rather, we must go into the heart, into the mind that is within, and see there what exists. If this is to happen, then the **primordial void** <note>original: "Chaos"</note>, the **shadows**, and the **bodies** <note>original: "Corpora"</note> that darken and cover it will become pure and clear. ### The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus

Thus, there must be a **clarification** <note>original: "Clarificatio." In this context, it refers to a purification or clearing of the mind and senses to perceive spiritual truths.</note>, which is **attained mathematics** <term>Mathematica Adepta: The spiritualized version of mathematics and astronomy that deals with the living essence of the stars rather than just their physical measurement.</term>, and that is what should be used in all branches of **astronomy** <note>original: "Astronomia"</note>, and no other. The mathematician desires to bring all **sidereal courses** <term>Syderische Lauff: The movements and paths of the stars and celestial bodies.</term> into an **earthly globe** <note>original: "jridischen Globum"</note>—into the very body that he himself is, into wood which he also is—and thus he desires that the heavens and their sphere be brought into wood; as it is in heaven, so should it be in wood, copper, and paper. In the same way, the **cosmographer** <term>Cosmographus: A scholar who maps the general features of the universe, including both geography and astronomy.</term> desires that the world be brought onto a cloth, or onto a wall in a **map** <note>original: "Mappam"</note>. Now, such things are **elemental** <term>Elementisch: Pertaining to the four physical elements (earth, water, air, fire); here used to mean "purely physical" or "material."</term> desires, belonging to elemental nature and property; the elemental is also given into the art.

But now, when he looks there in **astrolabes**, in **quadrants**, in **spheres**, **small globes**, etc., it is nonetheless there alone without movement; the movement is not there, and yet movement is the greatest thing that should be there—to know the movement. And even if these instruments move themselves, it is still a dead movement, which is just like a shadow on the wall: it is neither blue nor green. Elemental learning and **science** <note>original: "Scientia"</note> are capable of nothing more than what has just been mentioned. Therefore, they lie only in the **face** <note>original: "in Facie": On the surface or outward appearance.</note> and not in the **heart** <note>original: "in Corde": In the inner essence or core.</note>; they know something from the outside, but nothing at all from the inside.

However, **attained mathematics** gives you a spiritual, visible astrolabe that has its own course, just as the actual path of the stars is—like the sun moves through the water for all to see, so this science proceeds by itself. In this way, instruments should be made so that they show themselves in such a manner, like a thing in a mirror that moves back and forth, moving exactly as the object seen within it moves. And that is the difference between **elemental** and **sidereal mathematics**: the elemental instrument stands there like a block of wood, like a dead thing that one must carry wherever one wants it, whether to the right or the left; it stands there like an image of wood or stone, sticking to the wall like a spiderweb.

But those things belonging to **attained mathematics** have the movement within them, just like their sphere and their **body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> from which they come and whose instrument they are—not only regarding their running, rising, or descending, but also regarding what concerns the cosmographers; that is movable, just as the cosmographer's understanding of the movement of inhabitants should be. So, understand **attained mathematics** correctly in this **demonstration** <note>original: "Probation": A proof or trial.</note>: that it is visible but not tactile, and that if that which obscures the invisible were taken away, the art of attained mathematics would be sufficiently proven. For all things are ultimately brought to proof through the work, and the works must be witnesses in all things. And thus **Magic** <note>original: "Magica"</note> and all its branches must be brought into the work.

# The First Book
## Concerning the Gift of Divination <note>original: "Dono Diuinationis"</note>

Furthermore, it happens that an **astronomer** <term>Astronomus: In Paracelsus's view, an astronomer is not just a scientist who looks at stars, but anyone who understands the "sidereal" or hidden influences acting upon the world.</term> gives birth to himself—just as I have mentioned regarding **Gifts** <note>original: "Donis"</note> and shall mention further—in that Nature herself, without formal **Art** <term>Kunst: Here meaning formal academic study, technique, or acquired skill.</term> or human assistance, performs astronomical effects by herself. These occur without Art and diligence; that is, they reveal themselves without being sought out by man.

Though this does not happen in everyone—that is, in every individual—it occurs only in those who are predisposed to the **stars** <term>Gestirn: The collective influence of the celestial bodies on the earthly realm.</term> in this way. This applies to those who are of a skillful and good nature, well-aligned with the stars, purified, and **appropriated** <note>original: "appropriert" - meaning their nature is specifically suited or "tuned" to receive certain influences.</note>; namely, those who conduct themselves well in eating and drinking. For a drunken state <note>original: "volle weiß"</note> retains no **divination**, and in a state of fullness, nothing is effected, except for what belongs to the nature of drunkenness, which speaks out without thought. Indeed, the stars may well **divine** <note>original: "diuiniern"</note> through a drunken state, but it is a strange occurrence—it will be more numerous and worse than that from a sober person.

However, the influence likes to work through those who are modest in their conduct, and commonly in simple and ignored people whose speech is not held in high regard. For what occurs without formal Art works through simple people, such as the **Prophets** and others besides. But what occurs through Art must occur through skillful people. The Ancients were very diligent in this, ensuring they did not defile their bodies or minds, so that such **operations** <note>original: "operationes" - here referring to spiritual or celestial processes taking place within a person.</note> could be fulfilled in them, whether through sleep, through speculation, or through the mind. For such diligence as the Ancients had revealed great wisdom, art, prophecy, and other things to them—things which do not happen with immodest conduct and gluttony.

For the stars take someone up, and according to how he is disposed toward the arts, skill, and wisdom, the stars then act within him like a schoolmaster toward his pupil. He is a **self-born astronomer** <note>original: "selbsgeborne Astronomen"</note> who directs and brings himself into the heavenly influence. That is to say: when a star is ripe and contains within itself a fruit, a **gift** <note>original: "Dotem"</note>, a work, an art, a sickness, or whatever it may be, it strikes its **connected vessel** <term>Coniunctum: The human being who is "conjoined" or spiritually linked to a specific celestial influence.</term> and works through it. And that same "Coniunctum," which is the human being, does not himself know from whence it comes to him. Thus, the **firmament** itself brings to light in man what man does not seek and what does not lie in his mind. Now, this same **category** <note>original: "Species"</note> is called divining. For while a man practices such firmamental effects without the Art of astronomy, he speaks in a way that he himself does not know how, from where, whither, or whence...

# Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus <note>original: "Philosophiae Sagacis Theophr." referring to the author, Theophrastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus.</note>

and truly more so than all the clever ones. Such people have sometimes been held in wonder by the common folk, just as if they had been **Gods**. For in former times, there were self-born artists and masters—and women too—who accomplished such great things through the influence of the **stars** <term>Gestirn: The collective power or influence of the celestial bodies.</term>, such as the **Sibyls** <note>Sibyllae: Ancient prophetesses credited with divine revelations.</note> and their like, who prophesied and did more than all the clever people; not out of innate wisdom and understanding, but even beyond their own wisdom. Now, you shall understand this same operation in this way: that it reveals itself through sleep, through the spirit, and through **speculation** <term>Speculation: In this context, a form of deep, intuitive contemplation or mental reflection rather than mere guessing.</term>; that is, through such paths to which no one pays any heed.

And where such **divination** <note>original: "Diuination"</note> occurs, one may suspect a plague <note>original: "Plag" — can refer to any great calamity or divine punishment.</note> hanging over the people as a warning, which they nevertheless do not accept, nor deem worthy of accepting, but rather mock and laugh at. In former times among the ancients, divination was held in great esteem. For where a **concordance** <note>original: "Concordantz" — an alignment or harmony between two things.</note> occurred, such that the heavenly influence matched with someone and was accomplished through its heavenly operation—through sleep, the spirit, speculation, thoughts, or the like—the ancients kept a great watch and took careful note of the outcome of that same divining.

But other despisers, whom it concerned, because they did not understand it, gave no credit to such divining or what was spoken; and through such mistrust many people were led astray. Especially those who encountered such **presages** <note>original: "Praesagia" — omens or signs of the future.</note> but did not have the grace of understanding, and because it happened without **Art** <term>Kunst: Formal academic study or technical skill.</term>, they acted only by their own chance. They did not consider that the stars themselves were at work, and that from the stars all things of Nature proceed and are made manifest. For Nature is the tool of her Creator, just as the prophets were. Thus, Divination is not an Art, but a self-grown **operation** which the Heavens themselves make manifest and drive forth, just as the earth drives forth fruit until it falls of its own accord. For when a thing wishes to be or become ripe, it has its messengers who announce it.

There is a common proverb: "My angel told it to me." In this, the operation is called an **angel**, as is the common custom. And this has arisen from the fact that the **Gift of Divination** <note>original: "Donum Diuinationis"</note> is not understood. And it is a **Gift** <note>original: "Donum"</note> for the reason that God Himself, in **Divine Providence** <note>original: "diuina Prouidentia"</note>, ordained Nature to presage such things, and that it should not happen without a medium, but occur through a medium. Thus, the medium is the stars, which here unite with the one who can speak, and who further [carries] that same...

However, it is purely a heavenly operation, though arranged by God in such a manner. Now, the cause and origin of this **divination** <note>original: "Diuination"</note> is this: that man has a **sidereal body** <term>Syderischen Leib: The "astral" or star-born body, which Paracelsus believed was the seat of intuition and dreams, distinct from the physical flesh.</term> within him, which is united with the external stars, and the two converse with one another when the sidereal body is unburdened by the **elemental body** <term>Elementischen Leib: The physical, material body composed of the four elements.</term>. But when the elemental rests, then the dreams come; as the stars operate, so are the dreams and their revelation too, and thus it happens. And according to whether the stars are well-disposed or not, well or poorly prepared, accordingly the dreams come. For as has been mentioned, to the overly clever and self-important person, the stars give nothing. For one's own cleverness drives away the operation of the **firmament** and resists the stars. Therefore, the firmamental operation occurs only in those who give place to the stars.

Many treasures and other such hidden things were also found, and such rare things that almost nothing of the greatest **art** <note>In this context, "Art" refers to academic or learned skill, which Paracelsus often contrasts with natural, divinely-inspired knowledge.</note> could have compared to them. When such an apt sidereal body is found by the stars, and the stars are prepared, then wonderful things are revealed, also in the past and present. Thus women have often prophesied, and old people who were gifted with no academic arts, and just as if in a state of foolishness and simplicity, they prophesied for a long time ahead, which was then also wonderfully found to be true; and these were prophecies, but it is not easy to recognize those through whom nature thus works, for they are commonly people who are least esteemed.

Thus there have also been many learned people who possessed an apt sidereal body and additionally exercised themselves in the **influence**—

Likewise in man, whatever is within him is driven out by the stars—that is, what the stars want to have out of him, without man's own contribution. All of this is **divination** <note>original: "Diuinatio"</note>—all that which men have undertaken in writings regarding wisdoms, cleverness, and the like. But mark further the end of such things and **divination**: since it came from the stars, it has also perished with them—that is, it began with them and ended with them. For the heavens allow nothing to be inherited; they remain within themselves. Therefore, I believe it is not unreasonable to recognize the **stars** <note>original: "Astra"</note> better, so that such things might be anticipated. But because man can do nothing but be vain, he does not understand it. Thus, deception passes from one to another. From this it follows that many are considered holy, and have produced their writings and sermons, and with them **signs** <note>original: "Signa"</note> and the like, which are nevertheless purely a **sidereal** work. They **divine** <note>original: "Diuiniern"</note> their writings, yet there is nothing there but **firmamental** <term>Firmamentisch: Relating to the physical sky or firmament; mundane as opposed to spiritual.</term> operation, which the simple person neither wants to nor can understand. For the crooked serpent **Leviathan** <note>A biblical sea monster, here representing the devil or the force of spiritual deception.</note> takes such perverted stars as an instrument to complete his own deception through them. For in this way, many kinds of teachings are written that are considered great and holy, though they are nothing. For such deceptions fall silent in heaven; they run toward death with them, dying in their own writings, and they are the very ones who falsify and corrupt all religion. Therefore, it is necessary that one recognizes well what the stars work, and to whom that same work is subservient and subject. It has seemed good to me to make this manifest,

Philosophy of the Sagacious Theophrastus

## Of the Gift of Augury.

Now, moving further, you should know about **auguries** <term>Augury: The ancient practice of interpreting omens and prophecies based on the behavior of birds and other animals.</term>, that these occur solely through animals. Through animals, one understands the prophecy of things present, things to come, and other such matters. He who knows how to prophesy with animals, how to understand and recognize them, he is an **augur**. This is a **gift** <note>original Latin: "Donum"</note> that drives itself and is given without human interference; it requires only learning and recognition of when and how such prophecies occur, and by what signs they are to be recognized.

Regarding this, take note that the **stars** <note>original: "Gestirn"</note> are so powerful that they draw and rule even the irrational animals. They lead them so that as much as is possible through a creature may be revealed concerning prophecy and other matters. For the stars drive their influence into the animal’s will. Among simple folk, there is a similar "animal-like" operation as there is in beasts, for an irrational human and an animal are the same thing in the eyes of the stars.

Therefore, know that the stars know all future things; but because they cannot speak, they show these things through form, figure, and the like. Or, they drive the **sidereal body** <term>Sidereal body: Also called the "astral body," this is the part of a living being influenced by the heavens, acting as a bridge between the physical world and the stars.</term> within animals so that they give signs, according to what that specific animal is capable of and its nature. For everything that lives has within it a **sidereal spirit** through which the stars act and work—not only the sentient, but also the non-sentient.

All these things are auguries, occurring whenever something happens in a creature that is against its usual kind and nature. For example, **peacocks** have a specific time to cry; if they cry outside that time which nature has given them, it is a prophecy of some harm that will befall that place or its house. A **dog** that howls more and differently than is naturally "dog-like" also signifies a corpse, a death, or something similar in its house. A **magpie** <note>original: "Aglaster"</note> that sings contrary to its nature is likewise a prophecy of harm or disadvantage.

Understand this in the same way for all animals—ravens, storks, swallows, sparrows, and so on. For this is the most common **proof** <note>original: "Probation"</note>: that the stars have their "body" in all things, not only in humans. And by the power of this body, the heavens work through them and reveal through that animal what [is coming] to those **residences** <note>original Latin: "Domicilii"; here referring to both physical houses and astrological "houses."</note>...

As an example: when a person lies sick and is destined to die, signs of death appear one after another in the body. Likewise, signs also appear in his **horoscope** <note>original: "Figur"</note> and in his **conjunction**, which must break with him. Thus follow the wonders which man brings forth through such things. In ancient times, those who discovered such rare things and had knowledge of **auguries** and understood them were regarded as gods. But **astronomy** teaches that they were not gods, but rather skillful people of the **Light of Nature** <note>The "Light of Nature" is a central concept for the author, referring to the innate, God-given capacity to understand the world through observation and reason rather than just through scripture or tradition.</note>, learned in **auguries**. For God created man in such a way that man, heaven, and earth are united; the **Light of Nature** is entrusted to the heavens, and man is to receive it from them. Therefore, this specific branch of knowledge is a natural art, useful for man to receive, know, and learn; it is a piece and a part of the great wisdom a person ought to possess.

...to instruct. For it is just the same with **states of inebriation** <note>original: "Ebrietatis"</note>.

Now, so that this example may be understood even more easily, take note: A person who is sober has his wisdom as God has ordained it for him. The **Apostle Paul** <note>original: "Paulus Apostolus"</note> considered this well when he said we should not be drunk with wine, for in it is all excess. 

So that this might be well understood, I felt compelled to make this **demonstration** <term>Demonstration (original: "Probation"): A logical proof or examination used to reveal the hidden nature of a thing.</term> of what wine does, why, and by what powers. Accordingly, once the example is finished, I shall show what the stars do in man—for they are a "wine"—and what they effect in man, and where it manifests. This seems to me a fair and necessary reason to reveal, so that it may be understood what the sober do and what the drunken do.

## Concerning the Gift of Impression <note>original: "Dono Impressionis"; the "gift of being impressed" or shaped by a higher divine or cosmic necessity that overrides personal choice</note>

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'N' at the start of the paragraph, featuring intricate floral and leaf scrollwork (acanthus style) within a square frame.</image-desc>

Now, however, beyond that which constitutes Free Will—as **Inclination** <note>original: "Inclinatio"; the natural inner drive discussed previously</note> indicated in the preceding chapter—there is yet another **branch of Astronomy** <note>original: "Species Astronomiae"</note> above all else. This branch breaks and takes away the Free Will, so that a person must do what **Impression** <note>original: "Impressio"</note> wills, and not what he himself wills; and yet it is not a forced thing, and it is called **Predestination** <note>original: "Praedestinatio"</note>. Thus it is as much as saying: I will this here, that you do this, and you do that, and this must be, and must not be omitted. For therein, observe an order in things that must proceed, and that must be completed; and this must happen through those who want another way—they must go there, where they do not want to go. 

Now, to write of this **Gift** <note>original: "Dono"</note>, its **proof** <note>original: "Probation"</note> is first of all to be noted: that a thing is intended to be completed through a person, and yet the person would not do it of his own free will. Therefore, there is **"Compel them to enter"** <note>Latin: "Compelle intrare"; a reference to the parable in Luke 14:23, used here to mean a divine necessity that drives human action</note>, which is **Impression**. **Peter** <note>the Apostle Peter</note> did not want to go where he was **predestined** <note>original: "praedestiniret"</note>—that is his "Impression" here, to go there—but he had to go where "Impression" willed. **Christ** also desired that the "Impression"—that is, **Predestination**—would be taken from him in the Cup <note>referring to Christ's prayer in Gethsemane to "let this cup pass"</note>; but yet, because it was Predestination and **Divine Impression** <note>original: "Diuina Impressio"</note>, he had to proceed through it, and the Cup could not be taken away. 

Thus, as "Impression" is called "Predestination" in the Holy Scriptures, we should understand from this that "Impression" is a powerful accomplisher within the **Light of Nature** <note>original: "Liecht der Natur"; the innate wisdom and functional order of the physical world</note>, serving to fulfill its order. Now Nature has an order, such that men must be blacksmiths, must be farmers, must be millers, must be bakers, etc. Now, man in himself is of such a lazy nature that he would in no way do such things of his own accord; for laziness prevails in man, so that there would be neither baking nor milling. But so that men may be delivered from laziness, and so that their free will—which leads them astray—is set aside, there is **Impression**...

If **Impression** <note>original: "Impressio"; the celestial influence that shapes human behavior</note> did not exist, all things would be neglected, and it would come to the point that a person would put on shoes like a pouch, drink wine in the Hungarian fashion <note>likely a reference to drinking unrefined juice or drinking directly from the source</note> from the grapes themselves, and eat meat unboiled. **Impression** breaks all that; it compels.

Thus God wills that **Art** <note>original: "Kunst"; in this context, it refers to skill, craft, technology, or applied knowledge</note> be used among men on Earth, and that nothing happens without Art. For take note: He has commanded us to pray for our daily bread—not for the seed, but we should pray for the bread. That is to say, after it has come from the field, from the farmer, from the miller, and from the baker; we should pray for it when it is now complete, not for that which is incomplete. Now, if a thing must and shall be complete among us, then it must become complete through our **Art** which we use for it; without it, nothing may become complete. For what use to us is the wool on the sheep if there were no wool-beaters, spinners, and weavers? How could Christ have given wine to his disciples to drink when he said, "Drink, this is my blood," etc., if it had not been brought to the state of wine through **Arts**—such as by tending the vineyard, planting, pressing <note>original: "drotten"; to tread or press grapes</note>, and drawing it off? For Christ did not wish to give wild wine <note>unrefined juice or wild grapes</note> to drink, but cultivated wine. From this, it follows in many ways—though it is not necessary to recount and write down everything that is known here—but as an example: that such a necessity must exist within man. Therefore, since it must be, and **Divine Providence** <note>original: "diuina Prouidentia"</note> has considered this: so that man, because of his innate laziness, would not fail to perform any Art of his own accord—dying instead in the grass and eating all things raw—lest such a thing happen, as is the way with the cattle, God has placed **Impression** into the stars. These urge and drive the lazy man to work, and compel him, so that through **Art**, those things which are created in the **Light of Nature** <note>original: "natürlichen Liecht"; the Paracelsian concept of innate wisdom and the laws governing the physical world</note> for the sake of man do not remain hidden through his laziness. Thus the driver is there, the **Ethereal Impression** <note>original: "Impressio Aetherea"</note>, which compels and urges that progress must be made—to do and to use that which must be. For just as Peter was compelled and girded to go where he did not want to go, and had escaped several times—yet, when the grain was ripe, it had to go to the mill, and Peter had to go there too. # The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus

**Impression** <note>original: "impressio"; the celestial influence that shapes and drives human behavior</note> in its testing is a driver, an infusion of **Art** <note>original: "Kunst"; skill or applied knowledge</note>, of **wisdom**, and of all those things which should and must be in man through the **Light of Nature** <note>original: "Liecht der Natur"; the innate wisdom and functional logic of the physical world</note>. Without this **Impression**, man would do nothing at all.

Now, the things that compel and "imprint" upon man are solely the **power of the superior stars** <note>original: "Potestas superiorum Astrorum"</note>, into which God has placed and given the authority to provide that which is **predestined** <note>original: "praedestiniert"</note> to happen in Nature. Through the order of Nature, such things must happen and do happen. In the same way, the earth would never grow any lavender, **spikenard** <note>original: "Spica"</note>, or cypress if they were not driven out of it by force. Now, what drives them out? Only the sun and the stars; they drive out of the earth what is inside it. Otherwise, the earth is just as surrounded by "laziness" as man is. But the heat of heaven drives it, acting as a **spur** from which all growth must come forth—just like a horseman who drives out of the horse with his spurs whatever is in the horse; otherwise, because of its laziness, the horse would never show any virtue or what is within it. 

In the same way, **Impression** is like wine: wine has a character and a function within it, like a virtue. Thus, whoever drinks too much of it, the wine drives out of him what is in him; wine is capable of that. Here is another example: a man might be lazy and worth nothing at all if there were no **Impression** there that delighted and drove him toward women; by the man’s own nature, it would not happen for a long time. 

Thus, there is always something that drives. And it is no less true that **Imprinting** <note>original: "Imprimiren"</note> reaches over all men, but it does not have power and strength in all men. Rather, it turns out this way: **Many are called, but few are chosen.** This means: you will all be called, but it will not be given to all to have what they would like. There is only a **predestined** number; that number is the one in whom that which the **Impression** has been commanded to do is fulfilled. It follows then: let him who can take, take—that is, he to whom it is given, he does it. 

And just as Christ speaks of three types of **eunuchs** <note>original: "Eunuchorum"; a reference to Matthew 19:12</note>, so it is also to be understood in the **Light of Nature**: there are also three kinds in the world. One soil is fertile; it was able to take [the seed] and has taken it. Then there are rocks that take nothing and have nothing. Then there are the mosses, which also have nothing. So it will also be with men: not all are **predestined** for marriage or for the raising of children. Rather, some are for the Kingdom of God—these cannot be of use to women; some remain sterile by nature so that the population does not become too large.
