Thus, God in His **Providence** <note>original: "Providentia"; God's divine foresight and guardianship</note> has seen to it that not just anyone who wishes to run may do so, or do whatever they desire. Instead, only those are capable who possess the **Impression**. For God desires a thing to be done by the one He has joined to the task, and not by the one who acts out of their own self-will. For no one knows what they truly want, or what will result from their own desires. Although a person may see a path as good for themselves, God does not see it as good. He knows better than man what will become of it over time. It is better that the will remains with the One who recognizes all hearts, rather than with the one who recognizes none of them and follows only their own head—doing whatever they think best.

As an example: Marriage is permitted to everyone in all the world; that is the primary freedom of mankind, which is why brothers and sisters <note>Likely referring to the general "brethren" of the human race rather than literal siblings</note> come together in marriage. But now that freedom is set aside, and it has never pleased God for everyone to be married. He has taken this away from two types: those who are born by nature as **eunuchs** <note>original: "Eunuchi"</note>, and those who are **castrated** <note>original: "castriert"</note> for the sake of the Kingdom of Heaven. To these two types, marriage is not given; rather, they are deprived of it. Those born this way by nature do not concern themselves with it; they do nothing and bear no children. Just as little should those do who are "castrated" for the sake of the Kingdom of God; they may not reach for marriage or bear fruit before God, for it has been taken from them. 

Their fruit does not please God; He wants fruit from them like that of Peter, to whose order they belong: to be girded and led where they do not wish to go—to **martyrdom** <note>original: "Martyrio"</note> and **to the punishment of death** <note>original: "ad supplicium Mortis"</note>—rather than to the breasts of women. This is what pleases God. However, if they do not walk according to their appointed order, it is against their **Impression** and **Predestination** <note>original: "Praedestination"</note>. Yet, there is a **free predestination** <note>original: "libera Praedestinatio"</note> and a **free impression** <note>original: "libera Impressio"</note>, which do not force one to keep the path, but only require one to be and live under the Commandment. This breaks **Free Will** <note>original: "Liberum Arbitrium"</note>. Therefore, the Commandment is **predestined**, as has been stated, under the authority of the Commandment which man does not keep. See now, what does man think—that God would take pleasure in fruit that is born against His order and in the sin of transgressing the Commandment? He only takes pleasure in those who are the "third" <note>Referring to the third category: those who choose celibacy for God</note>.

Thus, understand **Impression** <note>original: "Impressionem"</note> now: that a thing which should and must happen can only be completed by those for whom it is imprinted—that is, by those into whom the **Impression** has been placed, and not by others. As an example: the **Impression** goes

This is just as Christ did, who gave His disciples the power to cast out **devils**. Thus, no one will cast out devils unless they truly have the power to do so. Likewise, no one will make the blind see, the crooked straight, or the lepers clean <note>A reference to the miraculous healings performed by Christ and the Apostles</note>, unless they are among that specific number. Whoever presumes to do more, but is not of that number and yet wishes to do it anyway—their works are without fruit, as is plainly evident.

Therefore, understand **Impression** to be a **Gift** that is driven to happen through those who are deputized, elected, and ordained for that very purpose. One should leave the work to them and not resist it. For everything that is from God and from Nature exists only in those to whom it is given. Therefore, what is from God remains and does not perish; what is from Nature remains in Nature also, and does not perish against Nature’s will.

# The First Book / Of the Gift of Generation
<note>original: "Dono Generationis"; referring to the divine gift or power by which things are brought into being through natural reproduction and physical processes</note>

Although it might well be possible in itself that we humans on earth could all exist without generation <note>the natural process of birth and reproduction</note>—if God alone wished to sustain us for that purpose by His Word—then all generation might not need to exist at all. But now, because God does not will it so, but rather wants it to be this way, so it must also be. And although it is true that it is His Word, and from His Word all things have come to be and been created, they did not remain as a Word, but rather as a **Generatum** <note>original: "Generatum"; a thing that has been physically generated or produced</note>. 

For example: If God wanted to feed us through His Word, we would not need the grain, the field, the mill, or the baker. But it is so arranged that it is indeed His Word and comes from Him, yet there must also be bread from the field, from the mill, and from the baker. Thus, God wills that all things pertaining to us humans be assigned to us in such a form: bread as bread, wine as wine, and likewise with all other natural growths. 

Take an even greater example: Christ gave Peter the keys, gave him the power to bind and to loose, and gave all his disciples the power to drink poison without harm, and that whomever they lay their fingers upon should recover. Now, the power belongs to God alone, and no one is capable of it but God alone; yet this is how He wants to have it. Therefore, it should be sought in the place where it is, and yet nothing is taken away from God, as this example demonstrates. He who is hungry does not flee to God for bread, but to the baker; and even though he takes the bread from the baker, how is God’s power weakened? Not at all. 

The baker takes it from the miller, the miller from the farmer, the farmer from the field, the field from the earth, and the earth from God. And although God Himself could be the baker, the miller, the farmer, and the field, etc., such is His rule, His order, and His **divine institution** <note>original: "Diuina institutio"</note>. And although it is true in itself that Christ Himself is the Rock and not Peter, just as the bread is assigned to the baker, so the Rock is assigned to Peter; yet such is the rule of Christ, that Peter be the Rock just as the bread belongs to the baker. And yet the beginning in all things is God; He is the first beginning. Therefore, where He is the beginning, there He is also the end, and the end shall be measured by the beginning.

Now, what is this lack of understanding when a person says: "I will let God rule, and I will seek no **medicine** <note>original: "Artzneyen"; referring to medical treatment or remedies</note>; if God wants me healthy, He will surely make me healthy." Now, it is no less...

His will is done, whether through medicine or not; but He wants it so that we drive out the disease through medicine. And yet, He is the physician Himself, willing that the disease be driven out by this means or by that means, or by another. Now, since His divine will is such, and He has created medicine from the earth for this purpose, why should a person then set themselves against God and despise His order? When you are hungry, you do not wait for God to feed you directly; you look to the baker and to the kitchen. If you can understand this—that you must seek bread from the baker to quiet your hunger and not wait for a roasted pigeon <note>a German idiom referring to expecting something for nothing or a miracle without effort</note> that God Himself might roast for you and let fly into your mouth—then take heed also of the other ordinances of God: that He will have it so, and not as you wish. He is Lord; in His hand all things stand as He wills, and so we must follow. And even if we intended to ordain things differently according to our own minds, none of us is His counselor or teacher; He is alone. 

Thus, Peter remains a rock <note>a play on the name Peter/Petrus, from the Greek "petros" meaning stone or rock</note> and that which God made him to be; and the earth remains that which God ordained it to be. Thus, from Peter come the fruits of Peter, and from the earth the fruit of the earth. By those fruits we must be satisfied, fed, and quenched in all things that are laid upon us, and nothing there can be skipped over. As an example: if you wish to walk ten miles into a town, you must walk the path and the footsteps one after another, and you cannot skip any. Likewise, if you wish to eat, you must look for bread, and that too cannot be skipped. Therefore, let all know that God has created all things that man needs, and has given him an art <term>Art: here meaning "Kunst," the specialized skill or knowledge of a craft or science</term> to prepare each thing and make it for the best. 

And according to that same order, He wishes to sustain humanity; nevertheless, He holds the power in His hand to let the medicine be useful to you or not, according to His pleasure. He lets bread be available to you or not, and likewise for you to exist or not. And above all this, He may break the order—but man cannot—for He can make bread out of stones, and He can make the stones speak.

Since God has now made such an ordinance <note>original: "Ordinantz"; the divine arrangement of the world</note> by which we are to be sustained, and does not want us to go about so sluggishly and be sustained, but rather that we should give place to and follow the saying where He says:

> In the sweat of your face shall you eat your bread, and you shall eat the labor of your hands. <note>A reference to Genesis 3:19</note>

Now, since our rule is thus, and this is our order, we must stop saying: "If God wills it, He will surely make me healthy; if He wants me to eat, He will surely give me bread." No, not so; He is no baker; He shall...

# The First Book

...we should proceed. Therefore, we should investigate the elements within the things that they show and give to us. For this reason, God has created and given them; these are the books in which we should learn what our eyes prove to us, and not from fantasy and speculation. For what Nature gives <term>substantially</term> <note>original Latin: "substantialiter"</note> and <term>corporeally</term> <note>original Latin: "corporaliter"</note>, that must be experienced in that form; but what is not visible, not tangible, without <term>body</term> <note>original Latin: "Corpus"</note> and <term>substance</term> <note>original Latin: "Substanz"</note>, that has its own other book, as has been frequently mentioned and will be further indicated in the <term>practice</term> <note>original Latin: "Practica"</note> of these <term>gifts</term> <note>original Latin: "Donorum"</note>. Thus, the nature and virtue of this <term>gift</term> <note>original Latin: "Doni"</note> have been sufficiently tested and presented, which is also a <term>member of astronomy</term> <note>original Latin: "Membrum Astronomiae"</note>, and a <term>species of philosophy</term> <note>original Latin: "Species Philosophiae"</note>, for the reason that both parts are united therein: the heaven in the <term>firmament</term> and the <term>globe</term> within the elements.

To make a <term>probation</term> <note>a "probation" in this context is a systematic test or investigation to prove a theory</note> of the <term>inanimate beings</term> <note>original Latin: "Inanimatis"; here Paracelsus refers to beings that are "inanimate" only in the sense that they lack a human soul, not that they lack life</note>, it is necessary to give a good account of how the <term>spirits</term> <note>original Latin: "Lemures"; often refers to night-spirits or ghosts</note>, the <term>shadow-beings</term> <note>original Latin: "Vmbragines"</note>, the <term>gnomes</term> <note>original Latin: "Gnomi"</note>, the <term>giants</term> <note>original Latin: "Gigantes"</note>, and also the <term>wild-folk</term> <note>original Latin: "Silvestres"</note> and <term>fire-spirits</term> <note>original Latin: "Vulcanales"</note> are born. For their birth does not proceed from human order and creation; that is, they are not from Adam. Therefore, they are not counted among the number of humans; and although they may well be human-like, they are nonetheless not in the number of humans. It is also not proven that they are redeemed through Christ by his death, nor are they in any way subject to the commandments of God given to mankind. For to understand them fundamentally, they are a <term>creature</term> <note>original Latin: "Creatur"</note> without a soul, like cattle, but not a human. Therefore, it is necessary to discover well concerning them: what their birth is, where their dwelling is, what their nourishment is, what their death is, what their multiplication is, and what their occupation is. Now, these are wonderful creatures created by God for man to ponder deeply. For one part dwells in the water; no one should wonder at this, that they do not drown and have their life in the water. For an example is found among the fish, whose nature they also share, just as man dwells upon the earth and the chickens with him in one hall and <term>mansion</term> <note>original Latin: "Mansion"; a dwelling place or station</note>. Thus the <term>nymphs</term> <note>original Latin: "Nimphae"</note> and the fish are also together. The <term>mountain-mannikins</term> <note>original German: "Bergkleutlin"; refers to earth elementals or dwarfs</note> dwell in mountains, not outside of them; no one should wonder at this either. ### The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus

In such a manner are also the **Gnomes** <note>earth spirits</note>. The **Salamander** dwells in the fire; it serves as an example that the **Fire-dwellers** <note>original Latin: "Vulcanales"</note> also do not burn in the fire. The **Shadow-beings** <note>original Latin: "Umbratiles", referring here to air spirits</note> dwell in the air; they are an example like the birds, which alone have their dwelling in the air. The **Giants** dwell on the earth, just as humans dwell among humans; they are also an example that they may well live upon the earth. The **Forest-folk** <note>original Latin: "Syluestres", wild people of the woods</note> dwell in the **wilderness** <note>original Latin: "Deserto"; in this context, any uninhabited wild place</note> and do not leave the wilderness; just as wild game may have its joy in the wilderness more than outside of it, so it is also to be understood of the Forest-folk: that their kingdom and dwelling are in such places and regions. And the **Lemures** <note>spirits or ghosts often associated with specific locations or households</note> have their dwelling near humans; wherever a human may be, there Lemures may also be.

Now, it is no less true that these things and creatures have been seen; namely, as the Bible indicates, that in those same times **Giants** also walked upon the earth. Furthermore, **monuments and limbs**, etc., of giants have been found, belonging to both women and men. **Lemures** have also been seen, and it is known that they have served lords. **Nymphs** <note>water spirits</note> have also been seen, both women and men. **Shadow-beings** have also been seen, and specifically more women than men, who were even married <note>to humans</note>. **Gnomes** have also been seen, who spoke with people, gave money, and took their leave. Likewise, diverse **Fire-dwellers** have been seen, existing entirely in the fire and being thoroughly fiery, who were subsequently mistaken for spirits or ghosts. Similarly, the **Forest-folk**—hairy, wild, and shy, without language or speech, having only a grunt. God is wonderful in His works; that must be considered first of all in all things. And afterward, one must consider that not all things were created as **essential beings** <note>beings created directly by God at the beginning of the world</note>, but that over time, the **lineages** <note>original Latin: "Generationes"</note> produced such works. It is not that the giants are a creation like leaves and grass, or like humans and the beasts of the earth. So it is also with the **Nymphs** and other such **kinds** <note>original Latin: "Genera"</note>; rather, they have a birth that resulted and joined together **from the contrary and the incongruous** <note>original Latin: "ex contrario et incongruo"; Paracelsus suggests these beings arise from unusual or "monstrous" biological processes rather than the standard divine creation of man</note>. Therefore, how such a thing happened, and may still happen, is to be described **astronomically** <note>referring to "Higher Philosophy" or the influence of the heavens on matter</note>, along with the philosophers. Only, first of all, it is most difficult to speak of their souls. It cannot be proven that they possess them; instead, they die altogether like cattle. However, it has happened that they have borne children; not as a pair among themselves, but a woman of their kind with a man from humanity. Then nature proves well that bearing children is possible, through many examples that can verify such things. If there is, or becomes, a soul in that same fruit <note>the offspring</note>, it must...

...come from the father, not from the mother; then it may well be included in the number of humans. But it is a strange thing, which is greatly to be wondered at.

You should also know this regarding their birth and origin: that there must be a father and a mother. Now the father is from the **firmament** <note>the celestial sphere or the heavens, which Paracelsus believed provided the "spirit" or "form" of a being</note>, and the mother is from the **elements**, by way of a comparison. The mother of the **Nymphs** <note>original: "Nimpharum"; water spirits</note> is in the element of **Water** <note>original: "Aquae"</note>; the father is in the firmament. The mother of the **Gnomes** <note>original: "Gnomorum"; earth spirits</note> is in the element of **Earth** <note>original: "Terrae"</note>; the father is in the firmament. The mother of the **Fire-dwellers** <note>original: "Vulcanalium"; often referred to as salamanders</note> is in the fire; the father is in the firmament. The mother of the **Forest-folk** <note>original: "Syluestrium"; wild people of the woods</note> is in the element of **Air** <note>original: "Aeris"</note>, as is the mother of the **Giants**; the father of both is in the firmament. The mother of the **Night-spirits** <note>original: "Lemurum"; spirits often associated with specific places</note> is in the element of Air, as is the mother of the **Shadow-beings** <note>original: "Vmbraginum"</note>; the father is in the firmament. Thus these two produce that same **wondrous creature** <term>Monstrum: In this context, a "marvel" or "prodigy" of nature rather than a "monster" in the modern sense</term>, and it takes after the nature of the element from which and in which the mother is; every such creature takes after that same nature. Just as a human is from the earth and desires to return to the same, so it is also with these creatures. Although humans do not live *inside* the earth—which is due to their office and station—the others must all remain within that element from which they originated during their lives. For in death, and after their death, no trace of them is found, except for those creatures that dwell upon the earth like humans, such as the **Giants** and **Forest-folk** <note>original: "Syluestres"</note>, and those who bind themselves to humans and take on a human death—which happens quite rarely. But that which dies within the element of its origin is entirely lost. For their **bodies** <note>original Latin: "Corpora"</note> exist only in life; in death, they are nothing. For then everything melts away like snow in the sun.

Even their bones are nothing; nothing of them is found to remain. They possess human skills and human labors with food and drink, according to the element in which they reside—just as the fish is in the water, the salamander in the fire, and so forth. Such is also their clothing and their dwelling; they are dressed in human fashion with cloth and form, but not with a material body that remains. Instead, their clothing dies with them; just as with a fish, it grows upon them like a skin. And just as the body has no permanence on earth, they also have no permanence—neither themselves nor their clothing. Their dwellings, however, are permanent within the water, the fire, the earth, and the air, as a snail shell demonstrates, which remains even when the snail is no more. And their labor is after the human fashion, and crafted and joined with such great artistry that humans are not capable of such subtle craft, as is evident in itself. And humans should not wonder at such things. For take for yourselves the example of snails, of mussels, of spiders, of tortoises, and of others, who all carry their houses with them—

...exist and grow with them like a skin with an animal, and no one can say what material that same house is made of. Thus, observe regarding the **Gnomes** <note>original: "Gnomis"; earth spirits</note> and **Nymphs** <note>original: "Nimphis"; water spirits</note>, and **Fire-beings** <note>original: "Vulcanalibus"; salamanders or spirits of fire</note>: they have their dwellings within their own elements. The **Gnomes** build houses, vaults, and many strange structures, yet no one knows what the material is. They have a particular type of alabaster, a different kind of marble, and a different cement. Just as spiders have a different kind of linen <note>referring to spider webs</note> and the turtle has a different kind of glue <note>referring to the substance of its shell</note>, so it is in nature; such buildings are found within the earth and elsewhere, including in the waters. The **Night-spirits** <note>original: "Lemures"</note> have no dwelling in a building, but rather only come into the air and vanish with the air. The **Giants** <note>original: "Gigantes"</note> have dwellings and create dwellings; they are most closely compared to humans, for they build alongside humans, speak with humans, and live near humans. However, they do not trade with them, nor do they have any fellowship with them, nor do they have any regard for God, but rather only for what is animalistic. The **Forest-folk** <note>original: "Sylvestres"</note> have their dwellings in forests, wildernesses, and in the caves of mountains. The **Shadow-beings** <note>original: "Umbragines"</note> avail themselves of humans and care for no dwelling or house, for their entire essence is in the air, except for what the **Concordance** <term>Concordantz: A Paracelsian term for the harmonious correspondence or "agreement" between different levels of reality, such as between spirits and humans</term> provides regarding humans; that provides a different order.

But in this **Demonstration** <term>Probation: A section of the text meant to provide "proof" or theoretical evidence</term> it is not possible to write enough about these **Soulless beings** <note>original: "Inanimatis"; beings lacking a human soul</note>. Instead, in the other volume in which the **Practical Instruction** <note>original: "Practica"</note> is contained, nothing shall be forgotten. But here in the **Demonstration**, understand that nature gives birth to and prepares such growths—and perhaps many more types and essences than are known to us on Earth. Yet, however they all are, this is the general summary: that their nature, behavior, essence, housing, and even clothing have no other origin than that of the snail—except that they are formed in the likeness of humans, though they are not human.

But to conclude regarding their **First Matter** <term>prima Materia: The fundamental, unformed base substance from which all things are created</term> from which they came: for the sake of the **Demonstration**, you should note this a little. The mother is the **Element**, the father is the **Firmament** <note>the heavens or celestial influence</note>; from these two comes such a **Generation** <note>original: "Generatio"; the act of bringing forth life</note>. You see this in the dung beetle, the flea, the louse, etc.—how they grow even without [sexual] birth and increase, namely through the **Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> in which they live, and secondly from the **Firmament**. So it is also with these **Wondrous creatures** <term>Monstris: In Paracelsus's vocabulary, a "monster" is a "showing" or a "marvel" of nature's power, not necessarily something evil</term>. The origin of the dung beetle is from horse dung; thus the horse dung and the sun create it. From these two comes a living animal—and not only the dung beetle, but also the May beetle and many other such **kinds of animals** <note>original: "genera Brutorū"</note> that come to be in this way. Thus there is also a **Seed** <note>original: "Sperma"</note> in the **Element**, in the air, etc., which generates such **marvels** <note>original: "monstra"</note> from the sun.

But just as a unicorn lays itself in a maiden’s lap, so they also like to be where there is little worldly understanding. How they are further to be sought and found, and when they are born, and where, and how the operation occurs, and what their power is in the earth, in the fire, in the water, in the air, and otherwise among humans and in the wilderness—all of that is shown by the *Practica* in the second volume. So, although contrary to the mother of the element, the growth is nevertheless so ordained that it does not take after the nature of the mother, but rather after the nature of the **Firmament** <note>In Paracelsian thought, the 'Firmament' refers to the celestial influences that give an object its specific destiny and properties</note>. Where is a child who takes after the nature, essence, and property of his father and does not differ? There is none. For every child is born for this reason: not that he should represent the father in his nature, but rather himself in his nature. And nature wills that the child have something else, and to nurture something else in the child than in the father; therefore it must deviate from that nature into another nature.
Thus all things strike into other essences and properties, rather than being exactly like the nature of the mother and father. This is proven and sufficiently confirmed in the elements—that contrary things grow out of them—as from the water come stone and metal. Now see how different water and stone are to each other, or water and iron. Also how different are the roses and the earth, the earth and the thorns from each other; yet still it is Divine Order.

To understand such things fundamentally is this: All things are specially created as each thing should be, and not otherwise. Since it is thus created, what can the mother give or take from it? Nothing. For the child is not from the mother, nor from the father, but from the **seed** in which the child was created; but so it shall be conceived and born according to the course of nature. Thus many things grow out of the earth, so that by the quality of their **constitution**, they are each unlike the other. and essence, and not from the Mother. From the Mother alone [comes the fact] that they are Earth, and shall become Earth and mud again; otherwise, it brings nothing from the Earth. From the Water they have nothing, except that the **final matter** <term>vltima Materia</term> <note>original: "vltima Materia"; in alchemy, the final form a substance takes at the end of its transformation</note> becomes water again, just as it was in the beginning. For take note: if every thing were to take after its father's nature or its mother's exactly, then there would be only two heads on earth, two wisdoms, two types, two properties. But because it should not be so, but rather the child should be different from the father, from this follows another nature, another wisdom, another property. Thus God wills it, that one person be different from another, and yet all remain in God's order and in His will. It was necessary that **Nero** <note>The Roman Emperor often used as a symbol of tyranny and evil</note> existed; it was necessary that **Pilate** <note>Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor who presided over the trial of Jesus</note> also existed, and also **Judas** <note>Judas Iscariot</note>. Likewise also **Peter**, **Andrew**, **James**, **Stephen**, etc. It was also necessary that the **Romans** existed, also necessary that the **Jews** existed, and necessary that the **Heathens** existed—and each different from the other, and none like the other. 

Thus through such properties, the time of nature shall be consumed; herbs cannot be or become otherwise than how they are—whether good or evil, beautiful or misshapen, thus they must remain, and other things likewise. But man alone is not so: he may become a **Pius** <note>referring to a godly or dutiful person; likely a reference to the ideal of a "pious" man in contrast to Nero</note> out of a Nero, a sheep out of a wolf, and so forth.

Therefore, receive instruction regarding the element of **Fire**, through the examples I have recounted: that contrary things also grow out of it, such as snow out of fire, frost out of fire, hail out of fire, rain out of fire, etc., as is publicly demonstrated in the **Meteorological Works** <term>Meteorischen Wercken</term> <note>refers to the study of atmospheric phenomena and weather according to the natural philosophy of the time</note>. Now their origin is thus: Although fire is hot and dry, it does not always burn; rather, it is hot and dry in its general nature, not that it burns like a wood fire. That [wood fire] is a **changeling** <term>Panckart</term> <note>original: "Panckart"; an archaic term for an illegitimate child or something of impure origin</note> of elemental fire and a **bastard** <term>Bastart</term>, which man should use for his necessity, as his servant. # The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus
### The First Book

[One] finds in the Earth: some things that burn, some that are moist, some that are dry, etc. Thus also the stars are diverse rather than merely hot and dry, even though they exist within the hot and dry [element of Fire]. For example, the **Moon** is the coldest star, and after it comes **Saturn**. If they did not renew themselves and were not born anew, they would become so cold that everything would freeze, so that the Sun itself could not provide enough heat. 

Now, however, as you have understood regarding the property of the Sun—which is more important to consider than the element itself—know this: that in the element of **Fire** <term>Feuwer</term> <note>Paracelsus uses "Fire" to refer to the entire firmament and the stars, not just flames on earth</note> there are such properties within the **seeds** <term>Samen</term> that from certain seeds snow must grow, just as surely as roses, **lilies** <note>original: "Gilgen"</note>, etc., grow from the Earth. No matter what kind of Earth it is, it is the nature of the seed that provides such colors, form, and taste, giving it a nature different from that which the Earth itself possessed. 

In the same way, the properties of the seeds must come forth from the stars in which they lie. Thus, there is a seed whose nature is snow, and that seed is distributed as far as the **firmament** <term>Firmament</term> <note>The sphere of the stars</note> extends. There are also seeds that produce only rain, and this cannot be prevented. Likewise, there are seeds that produce only frost, only hail, only thunder, and other such **growths** <term>Gewechs</term> <note>Paracelsus views weather phenomena as "crops" or "growths" of the heavens, similar to plants on earth</note>, as they then fall down upon us from above and manifest themselves visibly. Now, the elemental effects of Fire are placed on high, to fall down upon us and to distill. Thus, that which did not distill upward distills down upon us. For look at a seed that **ascends** <note>original: "ascendiert"</note> on high, up out of the Earth—a tree, or any thing. Now, it climbs upward and did not descend; rather, it is the way of Nature that what is above shall descend, and what is below shall ascend. Those things below are given into the power of Man, but those above are not. 

The reason for this is that the lower things benefit Man directly, while the upper things do not. However, the reason they were created is that they benefit the fruits of the Earth, which are then useful to Man. Thus the growths of the Earth desire the upper growths of the element of Fire for their nourishment and sustenance. Just as this is presented in the example, you should also know that it is the same in the other **elements**, such as in the **Air**. Likewise, regarding the **Earth**: if a vision comes to one where he runs properly and quickly from a place, it signifies that the **element of Earth** <note>original: "Elementum Terrae"</note> is also in such a state that it is proceeding well in its **operation**. But if he runs as he intends, yet cannot run or cannot move from the spot, it will be the same for the **element** in its **operation**, according to how the **connected person** is affected. Likewise in the element of **Fire**: if it burns properly and carries away house and home, then the **operation** is similarly proceeding. But if it will not burn briskly, then the **operation of fire** <note>original: "Operatio Ignis"</note> is also not brisk. Therefore, one should know that dreams and **visions** should not be applied to the human being as if they were assigned to the person—those, at least, that come from the **elements**—but rather they should be assigned to that which is operating in such a way, from which the **visions** have come. The **Section of New Things** <note>original: "Membrum Nouale"</note> is especially worthy of testing and is also necessary, because nature shows many things in her **mysteries** <note>original: "Mysteriis"</note> that humans should observe and know. For when nature herself wishes to show a **prophecy** <note>original: "Prophetey"</note> and proclaim a **prediction** <note>original: "Weissagung"</note>, she proceeds without any defect and entirely perfectly, from article to article, from one point to another; therefore, such New Things are well worth recognizing. Now such **portents** <term>Monstra</term> <note>In the 16th century, "monsters" were not necessarily scary creatures, but "demonstrations" or extraordinary signs from nature that pointed to future events</note> are made by nature; as she is, so is the work, and understand it in this way. When nature wishes to make a prediction of a thing, how it shall happen, she depicts herself in the **representation** <note>original: "Contrafetung"</note> and acts like a painter or sculptor, and forms a portent that is equal to and will be like that same work; and it is hit upon so well and so similarly, as an image that portrays itself in a mirror, without any hand or addition from humans. Thus nature is a **Craftswoman** <note>original: "Fabricatrix" — nature personified as a female builder or maker</note> who knows the right foundation and the right art of representation, more than all arts are capable of. Although it is true that nature has given no certain interpretation in such portents, nor made a rule thereof, but much lies in chance. Philosophia Sagax of Theophrastus

# Concluding Remarks.

The order that I have maintained until now has pleased me to present in such a manner, and with such purpose as I have now concluded, to prepare these matters. Now, the order is arranged so that I shall describe all the **species** <term>original: "Species" — specific categories or types</term> related to the astronomers, and those things occurring through them—whether by art or through themselves—distinctly according to their order. Since I have been such a worker, it seemed necessary to me to provide an introduction and instruction concerning the origin of mankind, so that one might recognize what fellowship, alliance, and unity the external beings—both the elements and the stars—have with man; this I have explained and described sufficiently, as far as is necessary for astronomy.

Subsequently, it was found that it is necessary not only to describe astronomy and its members, which take their foundation in the **light of nature** <term>original: "Liecht der Natur" — the innate, divine wisdom present in the physical world that allows humans to understand natural laws through reason</term>, but as it turns out, there are even more **genera** <term>original: "Genera" — broad classes or kinds</term> of astronomers who deal equally with astronomical members. Regarding whatever might touch upon the astronomers in any way, I deemed it a necessity to describe those as well. And in addition to those I have now completed in the name of the Lord, there are three other kinds of astronomical effects: two are supernatural, and one is natural, but is accomplished through the supernatural. Thus, I may not describe the two supernatural ones. However, as much as it behooves me to write of the supernatural, I will neglect nothing. Of the first, which is now completed, I have written naturally in the light of nature; the last that is to come, as the first figure indicates, I will describe naturally, for its effect proceeds naturally. 

Now, it is no less important that I instruct you further regarding the reason why I establish four **astronomies** <term>original: "Astronomias"</term>, from which then follow four **magical arts** <term>original: "Magicae"</term>, four **necromancies** <term>original: "Nigromantiae"</term>, four **nectromancies** <term>original: "Nectromantiae" — a specific Paracelsian term often referring to communication with the "sidereal body" or the deceased</term>, four **astrologies** <term>original: "Astrologiae"</term>, four **signified arts** <term>original: "Signatae" — the study of how internal essences are revealed through external signs</term>, four **uncertain arts** <term>original: "Artes Incertae"</term>, four **adept philosophies** <term>original: "Philosophiae adeptae" — knowledge attained through spiritual mastery and insight into nature</term>, four **adept medicines** <term>original: "Medicinae adeptae"</term>, and four **adept mathematics** <term>original: "Mathematicae adeptae"</term>. 

Now, regarding the first, place and space might perhaps be granted to me, and regarding the last, to some extent as well. The middle two might well not please everyone; yet what can I do about that? For mark the reason that drives me: namely, that I intend to provide such instruction through the four **genera of astronomy** to the readers, so that it shall and may be understood what Nature does, and what the Divin...

The First Book

...does, what faith does, what Satan does, so that the natural effect may be distinctively recognized as coming from Nature, and God’s effect may also be experienced as distinct from the others; likewise, what faith performs, and what the devilish works are. If such knowledge is now to occur and be granted, it is necessary that it be accomplished and completed through the proposed process, as I have presented in the figures <note>The "figures" likely refer to diagrams or illustrations Paracelsus intended to accompany his text to explain the relationships between these forces.</note>. 

And although it is so—and I myself confess—that Christ is not an astronomer, nor is God the Father a mage <term>original: "Magus" — here meaning a practitioner of divine or natural wisdom, not a common sorcerer</term>, nor are they at all contained within those things. However, because the works harmonize in the end, it may be said of them: "it is not from this foundation, but from that foundation." 

As an example: regarding what Christ performed, the Jews said he did it through the devil. Furthermore, the devil performs many signs, and it is said: "God has done it," and "it happens through God." Likewise, faith performs much, and if it acts through the devil, then it is said "God has done it"; if it acts through God, then it is said, "it happens through the devil." Or, people say it is all natural, and that there is nothing there but mortal work. 

So that such distinctions may be recognized—what the work of each one is, and from whom each work proceeds and has proceeded—that is the cause that drives me to describe these four works, where each has its own particular function. My goal is to instruct, to distinguish, and to teach the reader well, so that truly each work may be properly recognized and understood from the foundation out of which it runs and springs. 

If I now wish to resolve this (the fact that the Jews said, "He has a devil; he drives out devils by the power of Beelzebub <note>A reference to Matthew 12:24, where Jesus is accused of using demonic power to perform miracles.</note>, the prince of devils") so that the truth may be known, then the natural effect must be present in its astronomy. Thereafter, the astronomy of Beelzebub and the good or evil of faith must also be present. If these are correctly and well described and made intelligible, it follows that Christ may be recognized in his authority, and the power through which his works happen may be understood. 

Thus, nothing can be judged as devilish unless the other three types <term>original: "Genera" — broad classes or categories of knowledge/action</term> are first recognized. Therefore, my intention has been briefly set at the beginning: to describe Nature in her essence, works, authority, and strengths—what she must do regarding the elements and all those things lying within the elements. What power and authority Nature has over mankind, what her power is like, how she proceeds, and how much and to where. Then, it is necessary to describe the power of God and his Son, as well as their Holy Spirit, and what they are capable of regarding mankind...

Now note this example: there are four orders through which the physician may make him healthy. 

The first is according to Nature, according to its own strength, might, power, <term>predestination <note>original: "Praedestination" — the divinely ordained path or potential within a natural thing</note></term> and <term>ordinance <note>original: "Ordinatio" — the structural order established by God</note></term>, just as God has powerfully created them for all sicknesses; that same power the physician may use, and thereby make the sick person healthy. 

Secondly, if he cannot do it within Nature, he may make him healthy through the power of God, such as by the laying on of hands, saying: "Arise, take up your bed, go here or there," or "I see that you see." <note>A reference to the miraculous healings of Christ in the Gospels.</note> Such medicine proceeds without any help, solely through God’s help; no other assistance is used. 

Thirdly, if the physician does not use these two, but rests in faith, then faith splits: one in God, the other in Satan. If he believes rightly according to the content of the Gospel, then a mountain sinks into the depths of the sea; much more easily may he make a sick person healthy. Such medicine requires no help, except God alone in faith. But if he does not believe in God, but his faith stands in the <term>underworld <note>original: "Inferos" — the lower or hellish realms</note></term>, then it follows that this same faith also works through the infernal power, which has an apothecary in which all the <term>mysteries <note>original: "Mysteria"</note></term> of Nature are contained, which they administer. 

Fourthly, if he uses none of these as mentioned, he must act through the devil, without any mediation. If he now acts through the devil, the devil helps him, provided that the permission from God is fully there; for one who lies imprisoned and bound can do nothing without the permission of the lord who bound him. If he is pursued and gives himself over, then he is <term>natural <note>original: "Naturalis"</note></term> and takes the <term>powers of Nature <note>original: "Vires Naturae"</note></term>, and does everything through them. 

To fully and completely understand these four types and fourfold medicine cannot happen in this concluding speech; however, in the order contained in the figure, and in the entire work, it will all be found and experienced, how the origins of all things are and where they come from. Thus it has pleased me to write and to complete my undertaking. And although it is so, that only what is now completed is <term>astronomy <note>original: "Astronomia" — for Paracelsus, this refers to the study of the "inner stars" or spiritual influences rather than just physical planets</note></term>, yet because one thing may be turned into another and added to a foundation where it does not belong, it is not only...

...[that] which comes out of the new Heaven; there are the inner celestial <term>stars <note>original: "Astra"</note></term> that provide them, and bring forth their <term>office <note>original: "Officium" — their duty or function</note></term> into the outer Heaven, into the element of water <note>original: "Aquae"</note>. This is proven by the example of the <term>Great Flood <note>original: "Sündtfluß"</note></term> of Noah, which could not have happened through the natural power of the outer Heaven alone; however, the inner Heaven is capable of it within its own <term>astronomy <note>Paracelsus uses this term to mean the laws and movements of celestial bodies.</note></term>. Thus it also rains fire from Heaven—that is, from the inner Heaven—as happened in Sodom and Gomorrah. Thus stones also fall from Heaven, as well as blood and the like. For the inner Heaven works within the outer; just as when the sun stood still, the inner Heaven had the outer under its governance and in its hand.

Thus it now follows that, because the process and order of the inner Heaven is identical to the outer in its operation, it is now proper that the inner Heaven also be described according to the order of the outer Heaven. That is, it shall be divided into ten parts of astronomy. Likewise into <term>Magic <note>original: "Magia"</note></term>; but there is a distinction between the magic of Nature and the magic of the inner Heaven. Similarly, there is <term>Necromancy <note>original: "Nigromantia" and "Nectromantia"</note></term>, <term>Signata <note>the study of "signatures" or physical signs that reveal the inner purpose of things.</note></term>, and <term>Astrology <note>original: "Astrologia"</note></term>; but with the distinction between the two that the former must give way to the inner. The outer is less than the inner, and as coarse compared to the inner as iron is to gold, a common pebble <note>original: "Küßling"</note> to a <term>carbuncle <note>original: "Carfunckel" — a precious red gemstone, historically believed to emit its own light.</note></term>, or a pot made of clay to a golden vessel. 

Thus one power is always above the other. Therefore, the Star of Christ in Bethlehem was to other stars—as an outer star—what our coals on earth are to it; the fire that thunders is to our fire what our fire is to a warm wind; the <term>Dew of Gideon <note>original: "Thauw Gedeonis" — a reference to the biblical miracle in Judges 6, where dew fell only on a fleece and not the ground, or vice versa.</note></term> is to other dew what our dew is to sloe juice. For the strength of Samson was likewise from the inner Heaven, and is to be compared to our strength as our strength is to a mouse; and thus the <term>Magic of Moses <note>original: "Magia Mosae"</note></term> is to our magic as a copy <note>original: "abconterfeytung"</note> is to the original from which it was copied. 

Other things are to be compared to one another in the same way and with such distinction as these aforementioned examples of both Heavens indicate. Therefore, such distinctions are well worth knowing, and it is proper to reveal to Man from where every generation comes, so that he may contemplate and consider within himself what the meaning of those things is. If there is an operation from the outer Heaven, Man should know, experience, and recognize it down to the smallest <term>iota <note>original: "Jota" — the smallest letter of the Greek alphabet, used here to mean the tiniest detail.</note></term>. Likewise for the operations of the inner Heaven: what they mean and what they are. He who understands this is holier than the Queen of Sheba.

This shortening will occur among those from whom shame and vice spring and come. For they even attempt to lead the righteous astray, and they would succeed if that same day were not shortened in the very hour when they think: "Now we have conquered him." 

For since the righteous person is scarcely saved, it is necessary that he be protected by God from temptation and deception, just as He has commanded us to pray: *Lead us not* (that is, the righteous) *into temptation* (that is, into the teaching of the false), *but deliver us from evil* (that is, from those who act against nature and wish to describe God's teaching, which is intended to be used for both discipline and piety).

Now, it is no less true that we are currently those who have a God of mercy, for He was born and became human, from which follows mercy and the forgiveness of sins. Had He not been born, it would not be possible—given that such vices against God occur throughout the entire common world without exception—for God not to judge according to His wrath every day, as He judged in the **Old Testament** before the time of the birth and incarnation of His Son. But this forbearance and mercy is a testimony <note>original: "Testimonium"</note> that His Son is born, which is why He is henceforth merciful. Those who act well and die in His mercy will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven; but the others will go into the eternal fire in which there is no end.

# Preface
### Z iiij

...be introduced; but only what the theological <note>Refers to the study of divine or spiritual matters as a science.</note> is capable of. For the heaven is that which is the highest, and is ruled by God, and is not given out of His hand. The **outer heaven** <note>The physical, visible universe of stars and planets.</note> is set in its order; it follows that order and fulfills its office as God has commanded it: it creates the day through the sun, and in its absence the night, everything in its proper time. It gives its rain according to its order, summer and winter, and does not exceed its limit. 

The **inner heaven** <note>In this context, the spiritual or microcosmic realm that exists within humanity and connects to the divine.</note>, however, runs its course according to how God wills, and He wills according to how we are; thus it is governed and ordered. If this same heaven is to be described, it is necessary that the description be taken from that same source from which those *impressions* <note>original: "Impressiones"; refers to spiritual or astrological influences imprinted upon the soul or world.</note> originate. He who lays the first foundation of how this **Celestial Astronomy of the higher Divines** <note>original: "Astronomia Coelestis superiorum Diuorum"</note> is to be understood, must follow the explanation from that same foundation; the description must proceed from that alone. 

He who speaks of the influences of heaven is a **theologian** <note>original: "Theologus"</note>, for he speaks of God, and speaks of that which is from God. Even if the simple **theologian** might wish to say that it is not proper for a **physician** <note>original: "Medico"</note>, **astronomer** <note>original: "Astronomo"</note>, or **philosopher** <note>original: "Philosopho"</note> to speak of God, such a thing is said by no one except an enemy of God, who does not want His works to become known to mankind, so that his own personal vices may not be revealed. 

But as Christ says: *Nothing is so secret that it shall not be made manifest.* Therefore, upon this foundation I may well begin to be a **theologian**, so that through God I may reveal that which is hidden to many. No one should distance themselves from this because this or that person might wish to reject my writing. Indeed, because they reject it, it should be written all the more and more gladly; for the external **Light of Nature** <note>A key concept in Renaissance philosophy referring to the innate wisdom or intellect granted by God to understand the natural world.</note> says: "Wisdom has no enemy but the one who is not wise." Likewise, Truth has no enemy but the liar. Thus, he who writes and teaches from God has no enemy but the one who is not from God. 

Therefore, I wish to conclude the preface in this manner, and to proceed in this form according to the order in which I described the **Astronomy of Nature** <note>original: "Astronomiam Naturae"</note> in the first book. However, the distinction of this book is that it is supernatural, concerning the **inner heaven** and not the **outer**. ## The First Chapter.

### Of the origin and birth of the Soul, what its Being, its Spirit, and Nature may also be.

Since you have read in the first book of the mortal incarnation and Matter—that is, that man is not only from the <term>Slime of the Earth</term> <note>original: "Limo Terrae"; a reference to Genesis 2:7, describing the physical material used to create Adam.</note>, but also from Heaven just as much as from the Earth. For what is from the Earth returns again to the Earth, and what has come from Heaven returns again to Heaven. Now, man is not a man only because he is a <term>Microcosm</term> <note>original: "Microcoſmus"; the idea that a human being is a "little world" containing all the elements and forces of the greater universe.</note>, but that which makes a man is set above all things, being from Heaven just as much as from the Earth. For he is created for the sake of Heaven; therefore, he must also have something of Heaven, by which he may reach Heaven. For what comes from the Earth is a beast and dies in the Earth; therefore, it is not enough to know only of that composition—how man is from nature and has been composed into an image of blood and flesh, as has been described. For the "slime" is not sufficient to make a whole man, or to be considered a whole man, as if there were nothing more in man than only what was from nature; rather, that which is from nature is the least of it, but that he is from Heaven, that is above all. 

And as the Scripture says, the spirit (that is, of man) returns again to the one who gave it. That is: from God he is there, to God he goes again; that which is from the "slime of the earth" goes into the earth, from whence it came. Thus there are two parts in man: the form from the Earth, and the spirit from God, which I am treating here in this book. Therefore, know only of the form of the image in which the spirit—which is given by God into man—is kept, harbored, and housed. Thus God first made man from the earth, and thereafter breathed in the spirit through the <term>Breath of Life</term> <note>original: "Spiraculum Vitae"</note>, through which man is capable of [returning] back up, from whence he came. That is: from the mouth of God he has gone forth, to whom he returns again. And note this well: man is otherwise invisible in his being. That is, what man [truly] is, is invisible—not invisible in the way I define the nature of the <term>Sidereal Body</term> <note>original: "Syderiſchen Corpus"; the "star-body" or astral body, which Paracelsus believed was a semi-material link between the physical flesh and the divine spirit.</note>, but invisible because he is a spirit

Although it is true that neither I, nor anyone else, can or may know the image of God as it truly is, we can only know what we may take from Christ and the Scriptures. For they were left to us so that we might learn to understand and recognize the invisible within them, for the image is invisible. But nonetheless, God is the Person; and since there is a Person, there is also an image, for a person cannot exist without an image. And an image is a form and figure; thus, just as man is formed, so too is God formed, after whom man is modeled.

### The Second Book

God does not see [the earthly flesh], but rather the flesh from the **new birth** through Christ—that is what God sees. For Job indicates this and explains it himself; note this well, and in this way: He says, I know that I shall rise again on the last day, and I know that my **Redeemer** lives (that is Christ). The flesh in which he wishes to see Him is the flesh that he will receive through his Redeemer; in the **new birth**, in that very same flesh, he will see Him—that which is born in the new birth. For Job speaks only of the Redeemer, that is, of God the Son, and not of God the Father; he announces Him in his prophecy as his God. Through this it is understood: **I know that my Redeemer lives** <note>original Latin: *Scio quod Redemptor meus viuit*</note>; that is, he knew for certain that Christ lives, and that He would awaken him on the last day, and would again put on his **fur** <note>original: *Beltz*; a common 16th-century metaphor for the skin or the bodily "garment" of the soul</note>, which is his body. That is to say: Not the body of Adam, but the body of the **new birth**, as he says: "and I shall again be surrounded with my skin." This is as it stands in the third [chapter] of John, that we must solely be **born anew**; otherwise, we shall not enter the Kingdom of God. In that same flesh, Job will see Christ our Redeemer, as will all of us who are from God, and in which all the patriarchs were clothed before the creation of the new birth.

And each person shall see this solely with their own eyes—those who shall rise again in God their Redeemer, which is in Christ. Therefore, understand in this paragraph this distinction: that the flesh from the **mud of the earth** <note>original Latin: *Limo Terrae*; referring to the biblical clay from which the first man was formed</note> was not intended by the prophet Job, but rather the future flesh of the **new birth**, which is conceived by the Holy Spirit. All the saints possessed this in prophecy, just as those born of God possess it after the creation of the new flesh. For the last shall be first. Therefore, man should consider where he is at this time, and what he must yet become and should be. For the **composition** of the **incarnation** <term>Menschwerdung</term> is vast, put together from many things into one image, as will follow hereafter—becoming clearer the longer it is studied. 2. Second, the **Sidereal wisdom**, which is the **art** and the **temporal reason** of men. 
3. Third, the wisdom from the **Spirit**, which God gives to man at conception. 

Now, the first two types of wisdom are **mortal**, and have been sufficiently explained. But to speak of the wisdom that resides in the **Third Spirit**, know that it comes from God. Understand then, that because it comes from God, it brings with it **Divine Virtue**, just as the fleshly brings fleshly virtue, and the Sidereal Spirit brings sidereal virtue, and the Divine Spirit brings Divine virtue. There follows hereafter such instruction regarding the virtues of the Divine Spirit. 

Since God intended for man to come into the **Kingdom of God** after death, He also endowed him with such understanding that he can and may comprehend how he should and may reach that Kingdom. As an example: The Sidereal Spirit knows what is in the stars, recognizes all the constellations, and knows how to act and behave so that things go well or poorly for him. In the same way that this knowledge constitutes understanding, know that the equivalent exists in the Spirit given by God: namely, that the **teaching and the Word of God** is the **Firmament** and **Star** <note>original: "Sydus"</note> of the inner heaven.

Now, through the Spirit given to him by God, man understands that same "Star"; for it would not be possible for us humans to know what is in heaven—that is, in the Kingdom of God—if no one had come down from heaven, from that very place and locality, to tell us. We are solely of the earth, and of the earth we speak.

For this reason, he finds nothing and understands nothing; and thus, he shall have nothing.

They must be recognized and understood to the very end, and acted upon and deliberated through; but through drinking, fornicating, and usury, such things do not happen.

# Chapter Two.

## How Man is composed of a mortal body and an immortal body, and how this is to be understood.

<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut initial letter 'D' decorated with scrolling foliage.</image-desc>
I have written until now to sufficiently present the <term>human composition<note>original: "Menschlich Composition". In Paracelsian philosophy, this refers to the complex makeup of a human being, consisting of the physical body (from the elements), the sidereal body (from the stars), and the divine spirit (from God).</note></term>. However, it is necessary that even more be understood, so that, among other things, a person may better know themselves. For what use are pearls to a sow? That is to say: if a person does not know themselves, they are a sow. From this follows what Christ says: "You shall not cast pearls before swine, lest they trample them." This is as much as to say: You apostles should not speak the Gospel to those who are swinish people, for they will only ruin it. 

But a person should not become a sow, for no one is born a sow. Christ testifies to this when He says: "The children are mine, let them come to me," etc. Furthermore, it would be better for someone to have a millstone around their neck and be sunk into the depths of the sea than to offend one of these children. From this it follows: people may *become* swine, and if they are indeed swine, then one should not offer them pearls, for they fall under the curse: "I do not wish them to be converted, lest I save them." 

God bears such enmity against those who are not truly human, but are instead swine and their like: wolves, foxes, adders, dragons, and <term>basilisks<note>original: "Basiliscken". A mythical reptile said to be the king of serpents, often used in this period as a metaphor for extreme toxicity or evil.</note></term>. So that man may know himself all the better, it must be further understood what he is. For the spirit which God has united with the flesh—having created a soul for him—God, our shield, takes in many ways. He does much with man and much for man’s sake, so that, because man has such a short life, he might return within that same short life to the One from whom he came on the day of resurrection.

He emphasizes that while no one is born evil, one's actions and lack of self-knowledge can turn a human into a metaphorical animal unworthy of the Gospel.</summary>

# The Second Book

<note>The text begins by addressing the "Last Day" or the Day of Judgment, a central theme in 16th-century theology regarding how the body returns to God.</note>

Now, based on this, know that after the death of a human being, the person must remain and exist in blood and flesh; thus, on the <term>Last Day<note>original: "Jüngsten tag". The day of final judgment and resurrection in Christian theology.</note></term>, they shall arise as a human being and not as a ghost, entering the Kingdom of God with blood and flesh. Now, it was sufficiently shown in the previous chapter that the flesh and blood which man inherits from Adam does not enter the Kingdom of God; for nothing comes to Heaven unless it be from Heaven. Now, the flesh of Adam is from the earth; therefore, it does not go to Heaven, but becomes earth again, for it is mortal and <term>subjected<note>original: "vnderworffen"</note></term> to death, and nothing mortal enters Heaven.

So also, the earthly flesh cannot come to Heaven, for the flesh is not worthy of it, and is of no use for anything. Whatever is of no use does not enter Heaven, for it is full of <term>wickedness<note>original: "Vnlust". This refers to a lack of divine joy or a state of sinful inclination.</note></term>, vice, and all manner of excess. There is no fire that may purify it so that such wickedness might leave it and it might become capable of ascending to Heaven; for it suffers no fire, nor any <term>glorification<note>original: "glorificierung". The theological process of being transformed into a divine, radiant state.</note></term>, but only that it must completely leave the person—that is, leave the soul—as happens through death, which takes the human being away from the flesh.

Therefore, we should know that the flesh which comes from the <term>seed of Adam<note>The biological lineage of humanity, which in this context carries the stain of original sin and mortality.</note></term> is entirely mortal and of no use at all. But now, a human being cannot come to Heaven unless they are in blood and flesh like a human. For it is by reason of flesh and blood that man is distinguished from the angels; otherwise, they would be of the same essence. However, man is so much more than an angel because he has blood and flesh, and for the sake of man, the Son of God was born, died, and took death upon the Cross, so that He might redeem man and bring him to the Kingdom of God, making him capable of it. This He did not do for the sake of the angels who were cast down from Heaven, but for the sake of man. 

Therefore, man is so much dearer to God than the angel. Upon this, it is now to be known: because man stands in such love toward God, and yet the mortal flesh does not allow him to enter Heaven, Christ has given him a **new flesh and blood**, so that he may be a man in one body, blood, and flesh. And this same flesh is created through the Son; and the creation of the Son enters Heaven, but the creation of the Father does not—speaking here of flesh and blood. For the mortal flesh is from the Father, as Adam and his descendants; that returns again to the place from which it was taken. It would have been otherwise if Adam had not sinned; then the flesh would have remained immortal in Paradise. However, through his breaking of the commandment, it was subjected to death.

From the Latin *incarnare*, meaning to take on flesh. For even if one is a child of God, if they grow into their age and understanding and die without Baptism, they do not have their [resurrected] body. Therefore, Baptism should be the first thing, as Christ maintains: "Unless it be the case that you are born again," etc. Since the Word speaks thus, we must follow Christ and include everything else in the Word that Christ has spoken regarding Baptism and other matters. This is the **Conclusion** <note>original: "Conclusio"</note> of all discourse concerning Baptism: namely, that the first beginning for every Christian shall be to start with Baptism. 

First of all, regarding those born of Christian blood: [this must be done] because of the Incarnation which is created by the Holy Spirit in Baptism, which provides the body for the Resurrection. But those who are not of Christian blood and resist the faith should first be converted in faith; upon their faith, they shall then be baptized, and not upon their unbelief. Through such people, the **Astronomers** <note>In Paracelsus' worldview, "Astronomers" are not just observers of stars, but those who possess divine insight into the spiritual laws governing both the cosmos and the human soul.</note> are born, who speak and know how to tell of God. In that body are the Martyrs; in that body are the dear Saints of God; that is, they exist in the new birth, not in the old birth. The new birth is what makes one alive; in the old, they all die. But the Saints in the old birth are preserved in the Spirit to receive the new birth, and in that same birth, they see God, Christ our Lord and Redeemer. This hope the **Patriarchs** <note>original: "Altvätter"</note> kept in their womb—that is, in their heart—that they would be born again on the Day of Resurrection and would rise in the flesh of the new birth to see their Redeemer, Christ, in a **Virginal body** <note>Paracelsus refers to a body created of "spiritual matter" rather than earthly generation.</note> that is not born of the earth. This is the hope they kept and locked away in their womb.

Now, since God wanted man to be immortal, it followed that the flesh of the earth could not become immortal. For nothing is immortal except what comes down from above. Thus, man was made from the lower elements and not from the upper, in flesh and blood. From this, it followed that God gave him the soul, which proceeded from Himself, because it comes from above. This was so that man would be and remain eternal because of the soul or spirit. Therefore, God breathed life into him—that is, the soul. Life is not the flesh, nor is it in the flesh; rather, it is the soul, and life resides in the soul, for the soul is the life of man. Thus, man was intended to be eternal through the power of the soul. Furthermore, know that man possessed flesh and blood that is not eternal; however, just as a pagan woman becomes a Christian if she takes a Christian man as her husband, so too did the flesh become eternal along with the soul and was placed in **Paradise**. But after Adam broke the commandment—and God did not want His commandments to be broken, neither the least nor the greatest—there followed the separation of the body and the soul from one another.

...the soul has retained its eternity, but the body has fallen from that same freedom into death. Thus, henceforth, flesh and blood are eternal and no longer subject to death for all those who do the will of our Heavenly Father, being just as obedient as Adam was, while being released from that same punishment. Thus, the soul is no longer bare or naked, but it is clothed with the garment of flesh and blood from the Holy Spirit. For a man should be flesh and blood so that there is a distinction between him and the angels; he should be of the flesh and blood that was Christ’s, who descended from heaven. Thus we should also come from above through the new birth into the body from the Holy Spirit, in which the soul remains and from which it may not be separated as long as it walks and lives in the will of God. But if it falls away from God, like Lucifer, then it has that garment for its own eternal damnation; just as for damnation it is to partake unworthily from the hand of Christ, etc. <note>original: "rc." standing for "etc."</note> For food and drink are just like this garment; it is after all one thing, one process, and one essence, the one like the other, and thus remains undivided.

If now such a new birth had not been decided beforehand in the Holy Trinity—which is above all angels in the heavens—how could God the Father have begotten the Son and sent Him into the world? For if the new birth had not been considered, then all that happened through Christ would have been in vain, for man would certainly not come to heaven in his born spirit (which was neither blood nor flesh), but in the Spirit which is blood and flesh. Now, since his natural flesh and blood are from the earth and the elements, Christ could have accomplished nothing with man; it would all have been in vain. Furthermore, the other school is from above; it is taught by Him who is from above, from whom we are, whose blood and flesh we are. He teaches in the newly born body and not in the old; He teaches heavenly wisdom in that same newly born man through Him who is from heaven. From this school come the Apostles, Prophets, and those learned in God, whose fruits and works are their witnesses.

Instead, they must be understood in the Spirit—not in the Spirit by itself, but in the Spirit that is incarnated in flesh and blood. # The Second Book /

now / that the Scriptures should not be interpreted by natural wisdom, nor natural writings by spiritual understanding, but each should give its own wisdom to its own body and be led into its own wisdom, and they should not be interchanged at all, as the fickle spirit <note>original: "schwindel Geist"; referring to an unstable or confused intellect prone to error</note> is prone to do. And although it is true that Nature is not beneath the Scripture, but is rather inclined toward the Scripture of heavenly wisdom, she is nevertheless not capable enough to bring forth the **pearls** <note>In this context, "pearls" refers to the core spiritual truths or the divine essence hidden within the "shell" of the physical world</note>. For the natural body has no business dealing with the Scripture; only the new body, born of the Holy Spirit, is like a pearl compared to gold, or like coals compared to the sun. 

For observe an example: the Scripture says: *You shall feed the hungry, clothe the naked.* Nature also commands this and recognizes that it is fair and should be so, and she interprets <note>original: "glosierts"; to provide a commentary or gloss</note> it in such a way that it should be done for this reason: in case one of us were in such a state, we would also want to receive it from others. Such an interpretation, however, is not the **Gospel Pearl**. Rather, if we do it for the poor, we do it for God—and not just for the poor—but for Christ our Savior, whom Nature in her wisdom does not recognize, nor can she recognize Him. He who now clothes or feeds Christ, Christ in turn feeds him a hundredfold more—not here, but in His kingdom, which Nature does not know. 

Therefore, although the light of Nature does not reject the Gospel, but rather recognizes that it is fairly spoken, it is nonetheless not equal to the **pearl**. Nor is the **pearl** found through Nature, and even less so when it encounters things that are not natural in their workings—where Nature must stand entirely still—such as the **birth from the Virgin** or the **new birth**; of these, Nature in her light has no knowledge. And I say this only so that man may learn to recognize the distinction: how each wisdom should remain alone in its own conduct and keep that conduct within its own body; the wisdom of one body does not understand the other in its interpretation. 

Thus, two wisdoms remain in man: namely, the **Natural** and the **Heavenly**. Following this, there now follows the description of the **Heavenly Composition**, in which man should be grounded and experienced, to know and recognize the same, so that the **Great Works of God** <note>original: "Magnalia Gottes"</note> may be experienced and recognized among us. In this way we should live, for then we live in the will of God. For the two wisdoms of Nature and of Heaven are gifts that God has given to man here on earth to spend his short days. And although there are also two kinds of **Astronomy** <note>original: "Astronomia"; referring to the study of the stars' influences on both the physical body and the spiritual mind</note> which are necessary for man to know, one must especially be used with all one's strength, for in it lies the Christian power and strength—

In this way, the new body is fed and watered from the Rock that gives water, each according to their best drink; that is, a food and drink which is the very Savior who redeemed us, giving Himself. In the new birth, nothing shall be excepted nor forbidden, but rather entirely free. Those who now wish no evil in their hearts, but only everything that is God’s will—know then, what is it that one may do out of free will?

Not stealing, not murdering, not lying, not whoring, etc. All these things are not fruits of free will; rather, the fruits of free will are that one may make a person healthy when he wishes, raise the dead when he wishes, and perform **Divine Works**—that is, the works that Christ performed, so that those same works are also performed [by the saints], and more, as Christ himself says. He who is thus like Christ does what he wishes out of free will: the dead become living, the lepers are made clean, the blind see, the lame walk, etc. And from five barley loaves many thousands are fed, speaking with fiery tongues; they have power from God through Christ to fulfill such a will. That is the human being who has free will.

It is the same with **Predestination**; it is said that the mortal is predestined in predestination, but that is not so. What does God care for the stinking body, which is full of vice, shame, and sin, so as to predestine it or make much of it? He lets it act according to its own will, for good or evil, against its **Conscience** <note>original: "Conscientz"</note> or with its conscience. Why would He want it, if the human does not want it? There are orders and natural effects of the flesh and spirit, of the <term>elements and stars</term> <note>Paracelsus refers to his belief that the physical body is composed of the four elements and influenced by the "astral" or sidereal body (the stars).</note>. Such is their property, their nature, and their essence; thus they do according to their will what they lust after. Since the human is thus, what would God wish to predestine in him? He who does good enters the Kingdom of the Saints; he who does evil, into the hellish fire.
