# The Second Book

[so that] he might receive the Kingdom of God—that is **Predestination** <note>original: *Praedestinatio*</note>. If someone might otherwise become free to be a shoemaker, a locksmith, or a tailor, what is such empty trickery? That is **natural free will**; it is not the kind that we shall speak of here, nor should one say that a person is "predestined" to be a shoemaker. No! Rather, the **Light of Nature** <note>In Paracelsian philosophy, the "Light of Nature" is the innate intelligence or intuition that guides humans in worldly arts and sciences.</note> provides its own order: this one shall make shoes, this one shall do carpentry, this one shall fish. This is an **impression or inclination of natural influence** <note>original: *naturae influentiae Impressio / Inclinatio*</note> and not **Predestination**.

That which the Apostles and Saints did through God, that is **Predestination**. Thus, whatever is of God is **Predestination**; whatever it wills, it performs. So **Predestination** belongs to the one who wills that it go well for him, who prays that he might be granted his request, who seeks so that he finds, and who knocks so that it might be opened to him. If he prays to our Heavenly Father in the name of His Son—whereas for the one who does not do this, so that such things do not happen for him, it is the **predestining** <note>original: *Praedestinierung*</note> that nothing shall be given to him, he shall not find, and it shall not be opened to him. **Predestination is the Judgment of God** <note>original: *Praedestinatio est Indicium Dei*</note>; as every person acts, so shall it be done unto him. He who follows the Flesh acts against God, and his own **Conscience** <note>original: *Conscientz*</note> bears witness and gives evidence against him. Toward whatever is ordained—whether good or evil—there goes **Predestination**; it is the **ultimate judgment of all things** <note>original: *Sententia rerum vltima*</note>. 

Therefore, a person cannot say that through **Predestination** he became a shoemaker, a thief, a whorer, a warrior, a wolf, or a sheep; rather, nature imprinted that upon him. That nature ought to be under the Commandment and be forced to follow its God and Lord, not using all things for evil, but rather in the order that God has commanded. For the commandment carries **Predestination** upon it; that is His judgment. He who does good goes the right way; for him who does evil, **Predestination** leads him on his way as well. Now, according to this **new birth** <note>Spiritual regeneration or the "resurrection body."</note>, **Predestination** is eternal life. Accordingly, it is ordained that it happens to each person according to his will; and where **free will** exists, then whatever it wills is predestined to happen—that mountains move and seat themselves in the sea, and even much more besides.

Since the human being is thus from God, as stated above regarding the **new birth**, you should know that because of this, the human clings to God and God to him, and both have one nature. This is to be compared in this manner: just as a human is from the earth, it follows that he has the nature of the earth within him. So, henceforth in the **new birth**, he is from God; therefore, in such a state, he also has the **nature of God**. And just as the human is from the **sidereal spirits** <note>original: *Syderischen geisten*; refers to the "astral" or "starry" influences that Paracelsus believed governed the mortal mind and body.</note>

## What Heavenly Necromancy is, and what a Heavenly
## Necromancer is.

You should also know regarding **Necromancy** <note>In this context, Paracelsus uses "Necromancy" to mean the art of seeing hidden things or divination, rather than its modern definition of conjuring the dead</note> and the **Necromancer**, that they are to be recognized in the same manner as previously stated. **Natural Necromancy** <note>original: *Nectromantia naturalis*</note> has fourteen **species** <note>types or categories</note>, and the **Heavenly** kind has just as many. Namely, the first is a mirror-vision, and a **spirit** in beryl <note>original: *Barillen*; referring to crystal gazing or scrying using beryl stones</note>, and one in coal, and whatever else appears in the manner of a mirror, to see in them whatever nature has ordained to be seen there. Now, the **Heavenly species** of these things is also established in such a way—though there are three species, only the **method** <note>original: *Modus*</note> changes in the **body of the vision** <note>original: *Vision Corpus*; the manifestation or form the vision takes</note>. Now, the Heavenly kind works thus: if one can see through a wall, seeing what is on the other side in a mountain, what is in the middle, or into a person to see what is in their heart; these **Heavenly Necromancers** need no mirror, coal, or spectacles <note>original: *Prillen*</note>.

Secondly, which is the fourth species along with the three mentioned, natural art teaches one to seek treasures—what is lost, what is hidden, and where it may be. The **Heavenly Little Treasure-seeker** <note>original: *Thesaurinella*; a diminutive Latin term for the art of finding hidden things</note> teaches one to seek the treasure of **Scripture**, what lies hidden within it, and to understand, know, and recognize it. This is not only for the Scripture itself, but to recognize the heart of God toward mankind—His will, purpose, and all intent. It teaches one to understand these things: the Word and the teachings which God hides, not wishing for man to know them, much like one who buries a treasure and does not want another to have it, lest they use that same treasure for their vanity. Thus, much is hidden in Scripture because God does not want us to know everything, since we use the lesser things poorly; how much more so would we misuse the greater things? But he who knows this is a **Heavenly Treasure-seeker**.

Fifthly, **Natural Necromancy** is the seeking again of stolen things. Now, **Heavenly Necromancy** is that which teaches us to bring back to us that which God has taken from us. As He says: "what he has, take from him, and what he has not, take that from him also" <note>A reference to the Parable of the Talents/Pounds in Matthew 13:12 or 25:29</note>. To take back that same taken good is a species of **Heavenly Necromancy**.

Sixthly, there is a species for finding hidden things; that is, things that a person has within himself and does not know. Nature teaches how to find this—for each person, what she has given them, how they should bring it out of themselves and awaken it through art. And in the same way, the **Heavenly** is similar, which teaches the **fruit of God’s gift** <note>original: *Gab Gottes frucht*</note> in man, what He has given him, which otherwise, without the art of **Heavenly Necromancy**...

### Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus [Paracelsus] 124
### What Heavenly Astrology and what a Heavenly Astrologer are.

So, if you now wish to know what **Heavenly Astrology** and a **Heavenly Astrologer** are, you must first know what is natural and how many its **categories** <note>original: *Species*</note> are—namely, thirteen categories. Now, regarding the first, know that the **Supreme Mover** <note>original: *summus Motor*; a philosophical term for the primary force that sets everything in motion</note> is He who moves all things and has them in His power. Thus, although He has given power to Nature, she still remains in His power; so she is not free to do what she wishes, but rather what He wills, in whose hand she remains. Now, in **Heavenly Astrology** <note>original: *Coelesti Astrologia*</note>, it is to be recognized that the **Supreme Mover** is Christ alone, who says: "All power is given unto me by my Father in heaven and also on earth." From this it follows that Christ is the one in whose hand all new astrological effects reside, as he says: "There shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and distress among the nations." <note>A reference to the apocalyptic signs described in Luke 21:25</note> Thus these things are in the new heaven; that same heaven has its Mover, who gives them when He wills, at His pleasure—making them longer or shorter, placing in the heaven whatever He desires. Therefore, just as the old heaven has its **Supreme Mover** in God the Father, so conversely in the new heaven, He is God the Son.

Secondly: he who now knows the course of these same new signs and recognizes their path—that is, where and how Christ, who is their **Supreme Mover**, drives them—he is then a **Heavenly Astrologer** <note>original: *Astrologus Coelestis*</note> in the investigation of the newborn stars. For he knows where the newborn signs intend to go, or **Pestilence**, **Earthquakes**, **Famine**, etc.; how long they will rule, and in which regions, and which people are their **Subject** <note>original: *Subiectum*; the person or entity receiving the influence</note> in which they operate, just as in natural things.

Thirdly: he who knows—since such a new firmament is supernatural—before it and its operation begin, that the **Heavenly Astrologer** should know what its nature is. That is, what it intends to effect and operate within the mortal realm; whether it comes into humans, into cattle, into earthquakes, or into other such things. He who predicts what such a nature is, the same is a **Heavenly Astrologer**, for he knows what the **Supreme Mover**, Christ, intends to work, and how, and against whom.

Fourthly: there is a natural operation, such that one knows what nature operates—that is, comes to an end and accomplishes that which is commanded of it. He who understands this, knows what happens to people... <note>The text breaks off here; the catchword "nommen" indicates the word "hingenommen," meaning "taken away" or "removed."</note>

<summary>Paracelsus defines Heavenly Astrology as the study of supernatural signs and omens directed by Christ, the "Supreme Mover" of the New Heaven, as distinct from the natural astrology of the Old Heaven. He identifies the Heavenly Astrologer as one who can predict divine judgments like pestilence or earthquakes by understanding Christ's will.</summary>

As an example: I see a blacksmith making an iron glowing hot; now I see that same iron being hammered, but I do not yet know in the end what it will become. Or I see a carpenter hewing wood, but do not know what he intends to make in the end from such hewing. Likewise, although there may be pestilence, earthquakes, hunger, war, etc., one can certainly see that something is in the forge <note>original: *Eß*; the hearth of a blacksmith</note> that is hammering there; but no one knows what the end result will be when the work ceases and it is joined and formed. Therefore, he who knows of such a pestilence or similar trial, and what the "house" <note>An architectural metaphor for the final completed purpose of a divine event</note> will finally be, he recognizes **Heavenly Astrology** <note>original: *Astrologiam Coelestem*</note>; that is, he knows when the war will end, when the hunger will end, what has been accomplished then, and what follows—what the labor has produced.

Further, for the fifth point, he knows what the heavenly course works specifically in each person's calling, just as Nature also indicates her own: she inclines this one to fire, that one to water, this one to fiddling, and that one to another thing. Thus, wherever God ordains someone at birth, that person is a **Heavenly Astrologer** <note>original: *Coelestis Astrologus*</note>; that same person knows how to speak of the works God has undertaken, such as the one who was told to begin the birth of John the Baptist—in his life, in his mother's womb—and so it is with others.

For the sixth point: how God accords Himself with man and with all creatures; where He opens His hand and where He closes it; how He behaves toward each one. That is, how with each year, month, day, and hour He is gracious and favorable, and where He is not; where He grants the decline of earthly things, and where He does not; how much, where little, and where great.

For the seventh point: that a **Heavenly Astrologer** <note>original: *Astrologus Coelestis*</note> should know the realms of the new heavens and the old; namely, the Choir of Angels, the Choir of Saints, the Choir of the Trinity, the Choir of Virgins, etc. Just as in Nature the astrologer knows how all earthly heavens are dispositioned in their properties—such as where the "heaven" <note>Here used to mean the spiritual atmosphere or influence of a place</note> is faithful, where unfaithful, where inclined one way or another. For just as each thing has its own special property, so too does every house, city, country, and village. In **Heavenly Astronomy** <note>original: *Coelesti Astronomia*</note> such a thing is called a "heaven"; the distinction of such heavens or spaces <note>original: *spacium*</note> is to be recognized by the Heavenly Astrologer, just as one knows where saffron grows, where wheat, where grain, and so on.

For the eighth point: thus **Heavenly Astrology** <note>original: *Astrologia Coelestis*</note> teaches one to recognize future things, the prophecies of the **New Mover** <note>original: *newen Motoris*; referring to Christ's influence on the spiritual world</note>, and future signs, even as they have appeared. Just as a natural [astrologer] indicates the day and the hour...

...fourth **Sign** <term>original: *Signato*; an outward mark of an inner spiritual reality</term>, namely **Customs** <term>original: *sitten*; refers to one’s innate character or moral disposition</term> and **Habit** <term>original: *brauch*; refers to practiced behavior or usage</term>. ### What the Uncertain Arts are in Heavenly Astronomy, and who that same Heavenly Practitioner is.

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut drop cap letter N at the start of the paragraph.</image-desc>
Now, observe further how the **Uncertain Arts** <term>original: *Artes Incertae*; branches of knowledge like prophecy or divination that seem unpredictable or "uncertain" to human reason</term> (of which there are four) have come into the Light of Nature. The sidereal stars govern these, as far as the **concordance** <note>The harmonious correspondence or "agreement" between the celestial bodies and earthly events.</note> of both allows and inclines toward them.

Now, this is also a member of **Heavenly Astronomy** <note>original: *Coelesti Astronomia*; Paracelsus’s term for a spiritual understanding of the stars that goes beyond mere physical calculation.</note>, but it is not under the stars, nor in the same form as the natural arts demonstrate. Rather, these are supernatural and are not "Uncertain Arts," but **Certain Arts** <note>original: *Certae*</note> for those who use them in Heavenly Astronomy. For this is their foundation: that God does not take the elements to do something through them, but He takes man for Himself and accomplishes it through man. Now, God well knows how He wants to have these things, and so it happens; but the one through whom it happens hopes and yet partially doubts—one person differently from another. Like **Gideon with the fleece** <note>Referring to Judges 6, where Gideon sought physical signs from God to confirm his divine mission.</note>, who was in doubt until the third test occurred; and yet that happened which was supposed to happen. Not only in such a form, but in many other ways, men have prophesied out of **uncertain hope** <note>original: *ungewisser Hoffnung*</note>, and it was not entirely believable to them, yet believable in that God does not fail. However, when such an operation occurred in **Nineveh through Jonah** <note>Refers to the Prophet Jonah, who predicted the destruction of Nineveh, which was then spared by God after the people repented.</note>, Jonah himself was terrified by his prophecy. For according to his word, it did not turn out nor was it completed. Therefore, these are **Uncertain Sciences** or prophecies, because they may happen or not; and if they do happen, the word of God does not fail, only the [pronouncer]...

...announcer <note>original: "ciatori"; likely the end of "pronunciatori" or "anunciatori," referring to one who delivers a prophecy</note>. And that is the reason why we, through a contrite and humble heart, are able to break these things so that they do not come to pass. There are many in these times whose speech is not heeded, though they reveal such prophecies. In those instances, much is reported: some is taken away, some comes to nothing but proceeds on its own, and some becomes even worse. For just as humility and repentance can take away [the punishment], so pride and boasting can increase the total and make it more than it was before. This is the **Heavenly Uncertainty** <term>original: *Coeleſte Incertum*</term> in man, as it has been indicated.

# The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus

Subtlety should be addressed / yet much more **Adept Heavenly Philosophy** <note>original: *Philosophia Coelestis adepta*; the highest form of spiritual wisdom attained through divine grace</note> / which says nothing of that / in which we currently exist / but speaks of that / which we have never seen / but such is our hope / that He / who created us / does not want / any part of us to be lost / but to keep everything. Because that is His word / it is necessary / that we pay attention to more than just the mortal life / and to His **Adept Philosophy** <note>original: *adeptam Philosophiam*</note> / and provide for that / which we have considered at the last / so that one may have rest / and work well / and live in joy / without sorrow / when the mortal flesh leaves him. For in mortal flesh no rest is to be sought / only misery and need. Therefore we must seek another flesh / that gladdens us / in which there is joy / and such a joy / that also pleases God / just as it pleases us. So now, although much joy is found in the **mortal light** <term>original: *tödtlichen Liecht*; the temporary understanding of the world before death</term> / and nature gives it to all those / who seek it / easily found in the **Light of Nature** <term>original: *Liecht der Natur*; the divine insight given to humans to understand the physical and sidereal world</term> / various trades / arts / learning / skills / reason / prudence / how much more will the degrees be surpassed / of which I spoke at the beginning of this chapter / that one will be enlightened in one thing / and another in another.

Now, however that may be / if we consider the **earthly philosophy** <note>original: *jridischen Philosophiam*</note> / we find / that nothing is with us / only dust and filth / nothing near us / but bickering and strife / misery and weeping. And if we rightly consider / what we are from Adam / what do we find there / but anger / weeping / teeth-gnashing / and hate / and all discord / and that there is nothing in this life. Why then would we seek much in the body / where nothing is to be sought? and attribute much to that same body / which is not capable of those same things? Yet it is fitting / that we remind ourselves / that through **patience** all things shall be overcome / until the mortal body has died / and passed away / and thereafter seek in the [spiritual] body that which we desire to live in / and fulfill in the same / all those things / that the **Philosopher** <note>Paracelsus often uses this term to refer to a seeker of divine truth or Christ as the source of all wisdom</note> commands / and devote ourselves to them / that is / that we should think of **Paradise** / in which the **new world** is / another fruit / another office / another order / another life / another heart and Father in the same place to philosophize / and to hold forth that same **Philosophy of the New World** / as I may do / as in the Light of Nature / but I await the conclusion of my hope / and my consolation / as soon as I—according to the content of my hope through faith toward Him / and in Him / who has redeemed me—will sufficiently experience that same place / along with others / after my resurrection. Therefore know / that the **Heavenly Philosophy** <note>original: *Philosophia Coelestis*</note> is ordained for this purpose / so that we can say nothing of it

### What **Heavenly Adept Medicine** <note>original: *Medicina Coelestis adepta*</note> / and what an **Adept Physician** <note>original: *Medicus adeptus*</note> is.

Now the distinction between the two medicines / **Heavenly** <note>original: *Coelestisch*</note> and **Mundane** <note>original: *Mundanisch*</note> / is divided from one another such / that the Mundane—whether **attained through divine grace** <note>original: *adepta*</note> / or not—proceeds through natural order and powers / but the Heavenly proceeds without the herbs and stars at all. Specifically like this: If an Apostle lays his fingers upon the head / then the sick person is healed. Likewise / if he speaks to a dead man / "stand up and live" / then he lives / In short / that all powers flow from the Word / and that the Word has all power within itself / and so much more / that all of nature in its powers is not capable of so much / as is found in a single Word. This power is **Heavenly Medicine** <note>original: *Medicina Coelestis*</note> / and does / what nature cannot do / that is / nature makes no dead person living / no leper clean / no dead eye see / no fatal **hemorrhage** <term>original: *Profluuium*; a pathological flow or discharge of fluids, often blood</term> does it make healthy. All this **Heavenly Medicine** does through its word. So you should now know / that **Heavenly Medicine** has no field on Earth / in which it grows / or lies / except only in the **new body** <note>the spiritual body of the soul that Paracelsus believes is distinct from the physical flesh</note> / in that same body all words have power and progress here on this Earth / so that it does / what the person wants / who is of the **new birth** <note>original: *neuen geburt*</note> / in that same person are the powers. For they do not work in the mortal body / only in the eternal one / also not in nature / but only in the heavenly. Therefore know / even though a human does / what Peter / Paul / etc. have done / yet in the same person it must further be considered / that they do not have it from the mortal body / or from its powers / but from the living body / born of the Spirit. From that same body / and in that same body the powers go and exist / even though the old body is also there / yet it has nothing to do with it. ## What *Heavenly Attained Mathematics* is,
## and what a *Heavenly Mathematician* is.

Now look at the Siderial <note>relating to the stars or the "astral" body</note> **Mathematics** and the **Mathematician**; and even if you look at all of it well and marvel greatly at the works of God, it is still all vanity and nothing, and worth nothing. For Solomon has spoken (though not of himself): all things are nothing but vanity—that is, base—and so it is. The reason is this: he spoke of the mortal, and not of the eternal. Since he spoke of the mortal, man should concern himself with it in such a way that it serves as a warning <note>original: *witzung*; a lesson or cautionary advice</note> not to build anything into the body in which there is nothing but baseness; instead, he should seek the **new body**, in which there is no *vanity* <note>original: *Vanitas*; emptiness or worthlessness</note>. Therefore, I want to show you at this time—now that you have read about the natural—how to also recognize the supernatural: what **Heavenly Mathematics** and the **Heavenly Mathematician** actually are.

**Heavenly Mathematics** is such that Paul says: *O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God!* <note>original: *O altitudo diuitiarum Sapientiae et Scientiae Dei*; Romans 11:33</note>. Since Paul, who saw much, esteemed it so highly, how could I then be a <term>geometrician</term> <note>original: *Geometer*; one who measures the earth or heavens</note> and measure the height of the heavenly firmament and its internal workings <note>original: *Bergwerck*; literally "mines," here meaning the hidden structures of the heavens</note>, or be a <term>cosmographer</term> and <term>geographer</term>? For Paul says: *How unsearchable are his judgments!* <note>original: *Quam incomprehensibilia Judicia eius*</note>. How then can I say more about it, when he who saw more than I remains silent at this time? 

But I also hope there is much to be seen with certainty. However, I will state the reason why I know nothing more to write here regarding **Heavenly Mathematics** than this: to learn and recognize all things solely from the **new body** and from that same spirit which is in the new body. For the new body has its light, as does the natural; but the new is eternal, while the old is mortal. Furthermore, the mortal spirit is not instructed or experienced in the eternal; rather, like must be among its like, then all goes well. To provide instruction on what **Heavenly Mathematics** is: it is such that if we are to know the highness of God and have a good knowledge of that world, it must come solely from the heart, from the foundation, and from all our powers, in such a way that God himself enlightens us to experience these things. We will not arrive at certain knowledge <note>scientific or empirical proof</note>, for it is impossible even for the angels, and impossible even for the **new body**; for God reserves so much for Himself. Note an example: in the natural world, great secrets are hidden from us which we cannot reach; how much more so in that which [contains] such natural...

The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus [Paracelsus]

natural secrets have been ordained to be hidden from humanity. He has kept His secrets hidden in Heaven and remained silent. To speak in human terms, however—by the light of the sent spirit and through the natural blood in which the <term>worm of conscience</term> <note>original: *Vermis conscientiae*; the persistent internal moral voice or the gnawing of guilt</note> resides—much is indicated and made known. Specifically, humanity should consider that there are many different dwellings in the Kingdom of God. For as He says: "In my Father's house are many mansions" [John 14:2]. We find an example of this on Earth, where there are countless dwellings, no two exactly alike. Just as they differ in type, property, nature, and essence, so too is it in the Kingdom of God. And since it is written, "Our Father, who art in Heaven," this proves that God is God and Lord in all these dwellings, and no one else, for "Heaven" and "dwelling" are one and the same. 

Thus is <term>Heavenly Cosmography</term> <note>original: *Cosmographia Coelestis*; the study or description of the map of the heavens</note> understood. From this, we distinguish <term>Geography</term> <note>the mapping of the earth</note> from <term>Heavenly Mapping</term> <note>original: *Coeligraphia*; literally "writing/mapping of the sky/heaven"</note>. We also understand that humans are divided into different types according to the nature of these Heavens and dwellings, and are assigned their essence according to the will of God in the eternal body of the **new birth**. All this shall come to pass after the Judgment has occurred and the sentence is passed, when the parties are separated—one to the Kingdom of God, the other to Hell. Every person's works will follow them: namely, those who have done Divine works will go to the Kingdom of God, while those who have performed <term>Pharisaic works</term> <note>works done for outward show or legalistic hypocrisy</note> will go into eternal damnation.

## The Fifth Chapter.

### How the Heavenly Powers Create and Bestow Certain Members Without Human Petition.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial V containing two figures in 16th-century costume.</image-desc>

Following this, it should henceforth be known that things are accomplished not only in the previously mentioned **Heavenly Operation** according to a <term>predestined order</term> <note>original: *praedestinierter ordnung*</note>—such as **Heavenly Magic**, **Heavenly Science**, **Heavenly Necromancy**, and so forth—but we should also know that there are **Heavenly Gifts** <note>original: *Coelestia Dona*</note>. These are not part of the "predestined science" mentioned regarding certain "members" <note>likely referring to specific classes of people or spiritual faculties</note>. Rather, there are many members that God gives of His own accord: as He wills, to whom He wills, through whom He wills, and when He wills. For here you must understand that the **Heavenly Power** <note>original: *Potestas*</note> has an order; that is, the "**Let it be**" <note>original: *Fiat*; the creative command of God</note>. is not just an image; rather, the <term>Fiat</term> <note>original: *Fiat*; Latin for "let it be done," referring to God's creative command in Genesis</note> is everything that belongs to the image, affects the image, or is related to it. For example: a man gives his son away in marriage and secures his wedding for him. In the conclusion of the legal marriage contract, the man says: "so shall it be." That statement is the *Fiat*. It encompasses not only the marriage itself, but also the property attached to it, a peaceful life, friendly conduct, and the like. In this same way, the human being is created above all to be an image—an image and the wisdom belonging to it, full of grace and full of truth. This is all the *Fiat*. This is now the <term>Praedestinatum</term> <note>original: *Praedestinatum*; that which is predestined or pre-ordained</note> *Fiat*; that is, that which is attached to the *Fiat* and shall not depart from it. Those who dwell in the new world—those of the new body—exist within this *Fiat*, along with their nine <term>Heavenly Members</term> <note>original: *Membris Coelestibus*; the spiritual limbs or components of the resurrected, eternal body</note> in the predestined order. Now, above this predestination is a free will in God, for the Scripture says: <note>original: *Spiritus ubi vult spirat*</note> "The Spirit breathes where it wills" [John 3:8]. From this it is understood that even where <term>Predestination</term> <note>original: *Praedestinatio*; the divine foreordination of all that happens</note> might not seem sufficient, one should not stop there. Rather, God is unbound; He Himself is the free will, and there is no other. He makes what He wills and breaks what He wills; He may create and then destroy again; He may forbid or permit; He may give to one and nothing to the other—this to one person, and something else to another. From this follows a certain truth: that out of the free will of God, which exists in God alone, something is granted to humanity that lies outside of Predestination. This thing, accomplished through the human being, is something greater and more wonderful. For Predestination maintains the established order. Therefore, from this point on, it is necessary to begin [addressing] those same things that come from the spirit of free will, which "breathes where it wills," and no one knows where it comes from or where it goes. In this way, <term>Heavenly Philosophy</term> <note>original: *Coelestis Philosophia*; the study of divine and eternal truths as opposed to natural ones</note> is understood at its very foundation, as I proceed here just as I did in the Light of Nature. ## What <term>Celestial Divination</term> and the <term>Celestial Diviner</term> are.

<note>original: *Diuinatio Coelestis* and *Diuinator Coelestis*</note>

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial letter 'W' featuring interlaced foliate and vine patterns.</image-desc>
Just as you have six types of divination in the <term>Light of Nature</term> <note>The "Light of Nature" is a central Paracelsian concept referring to the innate intelligence within the natural world and the human mind's ability to perceive it</note>, so it is here in Celestial Divination. And just as the Light of Nature reveals its own effects and makes known through man those secret things which cannot be experienced by humans through their own power—or which might remain unrevealed due to human ignorance—the Heavens also accomplish such things through <term>Celestial Gifts</term> <note>original: *Donis Coelestibus*</note>. 

For example: suppose something heavenly is meant to happen within a person, but this heavenly event has no prophet, no apostle, and no messenger to carry it out by word or deed. In such a case, it occurs in the form of "Divination." However, whatever occurs in the form of divination is commonly prone to error and is uncertain to accept—as God intends it to be—and is difficult to understand until after it has come to pass. 

Thus, the Book of <term>Revelation</term> <note>original: *Apocalypsis*</note> is a "divination from dreams" <note>original: *ex Somniis*</note>, as were the <term>Dreams of Daniel</term> <note>original: *Somnia Danielis*</note> and other similar visions, such as the dream of Joseph the Just. These are a special working that comes from God. But blessed is he who understands them! <term>Caiaphas</term> <note>The Jewish High Priest who, according to the Gospel of John, inadvertently prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation</note> spoke, saying it were better for one man to die for the sake of the people than for the whole nation to perish. He did not have the understanding of this speech within himself; rather, he was "divining" through this Celestial Wisdom. 

Furthermore, if someone fantasizes about celestial things and has no prior foundation in them, yet reaches the fundamental truth—so that in his mind, in his imagination, and in his speculation there is something heavenly—then it is true and righteous, even if it is not yet understood. For in this way, many of the <term>Great Mysteries of God</term> <note>original: *archana Magnalia Dei*</note> are discovered. But because these things are so high, man lets them fall away and remain apart from him. 

Just as a painted image resides in one's heart, so too can the spirit become something that does more than what is possible for a mind in a living body—such as walking into fire, into death, into fear, or into darkness. Many saints did this even among enemies, as David did against Goliath. All such things, which are contained within "Divination," come from divine power and might. If man were perfect, as he ought to be, he would be capable of these things himself as often as he wished. But because he clings more to the <term>Old Birth</term> than to the <term>New Birth</term> <note>Paracelsus refers to the "Old Birth" as the carnal, earthly nature of Adam, and the "New Birth" as the spiritual regeneration through Christ</note>, these things are revealed to him only in the manner of shadows. Only after the event has occurred is it understood; otherwise, there is no understanding in them.

## What <term>Celestial Divination</term> is, and likewise the <term>Celestial Diviner</term>.
<note>original: *Coelestia Auguria* and *Augurator*</note>

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'N' featuring intertwining vine work and foliage. At the bottom center of the page, there is a symmetrical printer's ornament consisting of floral and leaf-like scrollwork in a diamond shape.</image-desc>

Now, just as in the <term>Light of Nature</term> <note>The innate intelligence within the natural world that allows humans to perceive physical truths</note> divinations proceed from the firmament, they also occur out of Divine Order and Revelation within those things through which the divination fulfills its effect, according to the essence of Nature. For example, there are birds used in divinations—of which enough has been reported—and so birds are also governed by the eternal Heaven, through which that same divination occurs. It may also happen through animals or <term>Portents</term> <note>original: *Monstris*; in this context, unusual natural occurrences or "monsters" acting as omens</note>, such as with the donkey of Balaam <note>A biblical reference to Numbers 22, where an animal sees an angel and speaks to its master</note>, and in many other similar instances. Thus, it is also a form of divination when birds appear—be they pleasant or unpleasant or other such signs—not arising from nature, but from Heavenly Revelation, given to man as a sign and for a deeper understanding than he possesses or can have within himself.

But because man is not properly clothed in the <term>New Birth</term> <note>A spiritual regeneration or "becoming a new man" in the Christian sense</note>, or is not "born anew," he has no understanding of these things. Instead, he looks at such signs like a calf staring at a gate <note>A traditional German idiom (wie ein Kalb ein Tor ansehen) describing someone looking at something with total confusion or stupidity</note>. It is not only that they regard them in this way and do not understand, but it is common for them to despise and mock these signs. Just as Christ was despised by the Jews, people today say: "Why does God not send us a true Prophet or Apostle who explains by word of mouth what the divination is meant to signify?" They do not wish to consider that no prophet will be sent to them if they refuse to read and understand the ancient ones; if they ignore the past, they will remain lacking. 

But everything that God specifically ordains and gives out of love for the instruction of man is for the most part nullified, despised, and mocked. Such a <term>Great Wonder</term> <note>original: *Magnale*; a term used by Paracelsus for a great act or "magnalia" of God</note> is held in no higher regard than the Jews held Christ when they said: 

> "If you are the Son of God, then climb down from the cross. You could make others healthy and save them, but you cannot save yourself." 

Therefore, the more a thing is esteemed by God, the more it is mocked by men. In this way, the grace of God is withdrawn from man and he is made blind. But great heed should be paid, for there are <term>Prophetic Signs</term> <note>original: *Prodigia*</note> that never fail, except in how they are regarded by those who see them.

He emphasizes that if humanity ignores ancient wisdom and these natural portents, they will receive no further prophets.</summary>

## What **Heavenly Intoxication** is, and likewise the **Heavenly Intoxicator**.
<note>original: "Ebriecatum Coeleste" and "Ebriecator Coelestis"</note>

Now, just as it is known in the **Light of Nature** <note>The innate intelligence within the natural world that allows humans to perceive physical truths</note> how a person becomes drunk from wine, so it is also with the stars. In such a state, a person speaks out what is within them and is far more capable than at other times when they are sober. But when the effects of the wine fade and the influence of the stars passes, they return to their former state and remember nothing more. In this same way, one distinguishes what is within man as <term>Heavenly Intoxication</term>; that is, the person speaks from the power of that intoxication and does not understand themselves, even though they speak of magnificent things. Many have spoken in the manner of dreams, delivering divine wisdom through heavenly powers without understanding it themselves—such as **Jesus Sirach** <note>Also known as Ben Sira, the author of the Book of Ecclesiasticus, regarded here as a vessel for divine wisdom</note>, who was a **Heavenly Intoxicator**, as was **Solomon**. For they themselves did not understand their own words; they spoke from a heavenly drunkenness and heavenly wine, understanding only while they were filled with that "wine." Once the "wine" departed and was withdrawn from them, the meaning became incomprehensible even to themselves.

And in the same way as the **Apostles**, when they spoke through the **Holy Spirit**, the common people said they were "full of new wine and must." <note>A reference to Acts 2:13, where witnesses to the Pentecost mistakenly thought the Apostles were drunk on fermented grape juice rather than divine inspiration</note> Thus, the Holy Spirit is understood to be a "wine" and a "must" in its effects. Therefore, we should know that what is spoken from the **Heavenly Must** is heavenly wisdom, while what is spoken from earthly wine is an earthly thing. 

Now, this occurs in many different ways. There are some who, in the **Light of Nature**, fall into a "divine trance" <note>original: "Taubsucht," literally "deaf-sickness," used by Paracelsus to describe an ecstatic state where one is deaf to the physical world</note> and into many departures from common natural wisdom. In doing so, they abandon wisdom as it is commonly known and employ a special manner and way. We should also know that such <term>Heavenly Intoxicators</term> <note>original: "Inebriecaris Coelestes"</note> reveal themselves in various forms. In short, they appear to be drunk and full of wine, yet they are not; they have consumed no drink. This is why people even said of [Christ]: "He has a devil and speaks through him," <note>A biblical reference to accusations made against Jesus in the Gospels</note> when in fact it was Divine Wisdom speaking, and neither a devil nor wine. 

Therefore, a person should not judge unless they have knowledge of who is speaking and what is being said. However, because man is so inclined that he does not wish to speak from the **new body** <note>The spiritual or resurrected body</note> but only from the **old** <note>The mortal, earthly nature</note>, he is for that reason robbed of true understanding. He does only that which is innate to him from the Earth, which then misleads him into damnation. For although man is indeed earthly, he ought to belong to the eternal kingdom...

### What **Heavenly Inclination** is, and what the **Incliner** is.
<note>original: "Coelestis Inclinatio" and "Inclinator"</note>

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'A' featuring foliage and scrolling vine patterns.</image-desc>
Furthermore, to know what **Heavenly Inclination** is, take for yourselves an example of how the stars <note>The "Firmament" or "Stars" in Paracelsian thought represent the natural forces that shape a person's character and talents at birth.</note> influence and incline a person toward specific things, giving them a desire for them. Thus, one is drawn to metals, another to stones, another to wood, another to agriculture, and another to hunting; they are seized and embodied by a particular love for these things. Know also that through such love which a person holds, an "inflow" <note>The process by which external celestial influences enter the human mind.</note> occurs, so that such things are discovered and thought out—just as all things and arts have been invented. In the same way, you should also note that from the **Eternal Heaven**, an influence and inclination of this kind goes into humans, so that one is inclined toward one love and another toward a different one; each to a particular gift, just as God inclines them.

For He is the **Incliner**, and He inclines them out of love. Thus, one has love for his death, another for his cross, another for the resurrection, another for teaching, or for this or that article of the **Gospel**, so that each article has its own particular measure—just as the faith was articulated among the twelve **Apostles**, just as the four **Evangelists** wrote in four ways, and as the **Prophets** had specific articles, distinct from the others. ### What **Heavenly Impression** is, and 
### the **Heavenly Impressor**.

Now, however, beyond what was mentioned before, there is **Impression**. According to the **Light of Nature** <note>Paracelsus’s term for the innate intelligence within the natural world and human reason.</note>, Impression is well-explained: it compels, pushes, and forces. Where Impression exists, the proverb is false: "**The wise man shall rule over the stars**" <note>original: "Vir sapiens dominabitur Astris." Just as iron must be, which happens through Impression and not Inclination; copper must be, and Impression is its mother; gold must be, it is a son of Impression. For Impression creates stone, metal, herbs, and all things.

If, then, Impression exists in nature, so there is also an Impression in Heaven, which also creates what it desires and how it desires it. Heaven is the **Impressor**; the work is the **Impression**; and that through which it happens is the **Athanor** <note>A type of furnace used by alchemists to maintain a steady heat; here used as a metaphor for the cosmic "engine" of creation.</note>. Thus, as Nature does this, she has **Created Seeds** <note>original: "Semina creata"</note> within her, and without them, she can accomplish nothing.

These are <term>Heavenly New Tidings</term> <note>original: "Coelestia noualia"</note>, and they appear only in the <term>Reformations</term> <note>original: "Reformationibus"; referring to divine renewals or corrections of the world’s spiritual state</note> which are ordained to happen out of Divine <term>Providence</term> <note>original: "Providentia"</note>.

Thus it has seemed good to me not only to describe natural forces, but also the Heavenly that works within us—not that this alone is enough, but rather it is only the second part, and it becomes complete with two more parts. For it appeared good to me—since four ways are set before man and he is engaged in four ways—that he should also know in which way he wanders, acts, or lives; for great attention must be paid there. This is so that <term>Nature</term> <note>original: "Natur"</note> does not love too intensely, but loves only so much that even more joy and love may be given to the Heavenly. And not only that these two should each fulfill themselves in their own way, but also that the third part be complete—that is, the powers that come out of <term>Faith</term> <note>original: "Glauben"</note>, so that they are present entirely perfectly without any intermediary, through works and deeds. Now, since we are to live and wander in these three here on Earth, and thus consume our time here, it follows thereafter that <term>Satan</term> is the enemy of man; he wishes to prevent man from reaching the place from which he himself was thrust out, and to which the Kingdom is promised to us. He would gladly bring us into disgrace before God so that it might happen to us as it did to him. He attempts this in many ways: he falsifies the works of Nature to deceive us; he falsifies the Heavenly works; he also falsifies Faith; and in all these things he lies in wait with power wherever he may lead astray. Therefore he performs signs in nature, signs in heaven, signs in faith—but false ones. How such things occur through him, the fourth volume will teach you to recognize. This is my intention: that God shall be given what belongs to Him, and the Devil what belongs to him—that is, that we have such an understanding through which we may know what is of God and what is of <term>Satan</term>, to separate such works from one another, and to give such works to each to whom they belong. As in the new body we belong to God; in the mortal body we belong to the flesh, which is to say, to natural <term>Righteousness</term> <note>original: "Iusticia"</note>. Now henceforth it will be necessary to set down the <term>Tests</term> <note>original: "Probationes"</note> concerning the <term>Heavenly Members</term> <note>original: "Coelestia membra"</note> as well as the <term>Gifts</term> <note>original: "Dona"</note>, one after another, as they are tested.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'D' with ornate scrollwork and floral patterns within a square frame.</image-desc> We must first properly recognize the example of what <term>Heavenly Magic</term> <note>original: "Magica Coelestis"</note> effects. I bring in this example of Moses here so that you should understand it in this way: I only wish to test the <term>Magic of Moses</term> and of the followers of Moses, and of all those who are Heavenly Magi, and in this manner. For Heavenly Magic is not an art, but solely <term>divine power</term> <note>original: "Potestas diuina"</note>. If He says "do this," and the person does it, then it is already accomplished. Now the light is to be tested: whatever God wills, that happens; yet it lies further in faith and in not doubting, as Abraham did, and as others did—provided that we do it and perfectly believe what God commands, so that it be so and not otherwise. Whatever happens thus out of the command of God, through the faith of the one to whom it is commanded, that is Magic. As when the children of Israel went through the sea with dry feet; that happened through the faith that stood in the command of God. But this Magic was not given to Pharaoh; therefore he drowned with his people. That the fleece of <term>Gideon</term> <note>original: "Gedeonis"; referring to the biblical sign where a wool fleece was alternately wet and dry</note> became wet and remained dry, he was a Magus; for in him was the faith that what God commanded would be so and could not fail. That Jonah lay in the fish was <term>Heavenly Magic</term>; thus is Heavenly Magic proven: in that which God wills, it happens through the means that is faith.

plea. But to speak of this here is not my intention, but rather to explain it more fully at its proper place. ### The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus

So it has also come to pass that holy men have not been able to disguise themselves, any more than dogs and cats could; the reason for this is that God wants everyone to be not as man desires, but as His Divine Will is. Therefore, nothing depends on these conflicts, for they achieve nothing; everyone remains in the gift that God has given them, and so His Will is fulfilled. For this reason, it is also not good that we all become physicians, nor good that all be apostles, all prophets, or all martyrs; rather, let each one carry out his <term>Office</term> <note>original: "Officium"; referring to one’s specific duty, calling, or vocational role</note>. And if they cannot get along with one another, what does it matter? It is their own folly. For why should the physician be an enemy to the apostles? Or the apostle to the natural physicians? Each one makes his sick healthy, those whom God has entrusted to him; in doing so, he does the will of God. Their bickering does not enter into the Scripture. What does it matter to the Moon that it shines less brightly than the Sun? How is the Sun better than the Moon? What does it matter to the stars that the Moon is larger than they are? If each does what God has commanded him, it is enough; their quarreling does not affect these things. One thing must be so, the other thus; and so it is with every thing.

### Proof regarding the Celestial Signature and the Celestial Signer.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'N' featuring intertwining scrolling foliage and vine patterns.</image-desc>
Now, the first proof of this **Section** <note>original: "Membri"; literally 'member' or 'limb,' referring to a specific part of the book's argument</note> is this: that we truly know that Nature marks her own and leaves not even the least thing unmarked. In the same way, the **Celestial Signature** also acts, marking her own as well. Thus, every person can be recognized for who they are in their heart. This is a necessary knowledge for everyone—for all people—for he who possesses this knowledge knows where he might be burned and where not <note>A metaphor for having the discernment to know who to trust and where spiritual danger lies.</note>. Now, hear further concerning this proof: Nature marks her own with diligence, and these same signs open up the natural heart of man. Furthermore, the **Celestial Mark** <note>original: "Signatum"</note> marks its own by their fruits and works; through these, they are recognized. Christ testifies to this: "by their fruits and works you shall know them" <note>Referring to Matthew 7:16.</note>. That is, whether they are from God, out of God, and in God, or not. Now, the **Celestial Mark** has been sufficiently proven through Christ, showing that the heavenly mark consists in works and is to be sought in fruits, and not in the signs of the body—such as in the hair, stature, form, or the like. Rather, it stands in the fruits alone. Through these, a person is just as clearly revealed for what they are, even more than Nature is able to show. For though Nature has the power to mark the character of a land through the "air"—distinguishing, for instance, the Italian from the German by their hair, because the air in that place turns it black, while in others it makes it red or yellow—so too do the forms of men differ. Some follow the fashion of **Ethiopia** <note>original: "Aethiopia"</note>, particularly in the nose; others in the mouth, as in **Calicut** <note>original: "Calecuta"; a major port in India, used here as a representative example of distant peoples with distinct physical features</note>. And thus, there is a distinction in all prominent and notable things—a different nature in the person, in the hair...

# The Second Book #

Christ says: You **brood of vipers**—now, they are not vipers in their physical person, nor are they wolves in their person; but the clothing is sheep-like, and the heart is wolf-like. For man is a <term>Composite Creature</term> <note>original: "Animal Compositum"; a being made of multiple different natures or elements</note>; as is his nature, so he composes himself **from very many colors, skins, customs, and riches** <note>original: "ex quam pluribus coloribus / pellibus / moribus / diuitijs"</note>. Because much rascality is hidden within them, so it is with the <term>brood of vipers</term> <note>original: "Otterzucht"</note>—it is not that they *are* vipers, but rather their behavior. He who then recognizes the **fruits of the adder** <note>original: "Frücht der Nater"</note> recognizes these traits among men as well; not by the form, image, or figure, but by the behavior, that is, by the fruits of the same.

Likewise, Christ says: You are the **lights of the world**. Not tallow candles nor waxen ones, but lights by which the **new birth** is shaped here on earth in this darkness, so that the darkness is not surrounding us. Therefore, I test the <term>Celestial Signature</term> <note>original: "Coelestem Signaturam"</note> solely in the works and not in the outer image. For the image of man is after God’s likeness, but the heart of man is not like God’s. Therefore, it is not the image, but the heart that should be examined.

Although it is also true that clothing indicates the human heart—thus, if a person dresses differently than nature teaches them to dress. One who dresses according to nature dresses according to the work they were born into, and what is suitable for it. But he who wishes to achieve his secret aims through clothing, and not from the heart, those are **sheep's clothing** <note>original: "Schaffskleider"</note>. For they are not made to look predatory, murderous, or warlike, so that the heart and the person might be known immediately, but rather in the manner of sheep, so that they are not recognized. But they are deceived by those who recognize sheep's clothing through the <term>Celestial Signature</term>. For such people can guard themselves against them.

Thus, every person should know what good fruits are, so that they know how to guard themselves against the hidden heart. And as a test of good knowledge, these are the good works: namely, to **lay hands on the sick** so that they become healthy, without payment. Also, that they feed the hungry and clothe the naked, and all of this out of the love we have in God, and thereafter, according to nature, to love our neighbor as ourselves. If this comes from the heart, as you would wish it from another, then you are certainly without any deceit. Otherwise, it is impossible that you are not a wolf, whether in the spiritual or worldly state. For there, all men are tested. For this reason: if the **merchant** <note>original: "Kauffmañ"</note> gives as he would wish to be given to, he is righteous; if the **innkeeper** <note>original: "Weinschenck"</note> gives as justly as he desires from others, he is righteous, and the like. These are the good works. Thus, know from now on that the <term>Celestial Signature</term> <note>original: "Coelestis Signatura"</note> is tested through Christ alone, and Christ points solely to works, and shows them in such a way that they [the false ones] are wolf-like...

# The Second Book
## Proof regarding the Uncertain Celestial Arts

<meta>catchword: first</meta>

That a human being should hold an uncertain thing in their hand is somewhat vexing. Now, however, because man possesses much in the way of temporal goods, yet has no assurance or certain constancy in anything according to his own intentions, how can he then expect to find any certainty in invisible things? Since he cannot possess the visible with certainty—and not only the visible, but even that which has physical substance falls from his hand—how much more so that which is "flying" <note>This likely refers to ethereal or spiritual influences, such as the movements of the stars or the wind</note>, in which there is no substance? Therefore, even if a thing is not always certain because one cannot keep hold of it, how can one do anything about a thing that falls away by chance? A man holds a sword; it falls from his hand, even though he is strong enough to hold it; nevertheless, it happened. If such things are not certain in the natural world, how then could invisible things always be held in the hand according to every person's whim, to be used however another person desires and wants?

Now this is a <term>Probation</term> <note>original: "Probation"; here meaning a "proof" or a "trial" of one's understanding</note>, showing that things do not have to turn out as man wants; rather, they must turn out as He wills, in whose hand man stands. How can man then say, "I am certain"? Because man lacks much, it is true; he is uncertain; he does not know the hour of his death, nor of his life or his health. Thus, if he does not know these things, he knows even less of the Arts and of celestial matters. For he was created without a "fore-certainty." 

But now, since there are such uncertain Arts within the <term>Light of Nature</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for the innate wisdom and functional knowledge found in the natural world, as opposed to divine revelation</note>, we must also find uncertain Arts in the celestial <term>Astronomia</term> <note>original: "Astronomia"; this encompasses both astronomy and astrology as understood in the 16th century</note>. I must give you an example: You know that God has an intention and a daily operation toward man. Now, such an intention of God’s does not always move forward; it also sometimes moves backward or sideways. How then can anyone call a matter certain, since an intention is not certain to end as planned, but is broken within itself? For God created man, and man pleased Him well; yet in the end it did not turn out well, but God Himself "failed" <note>The author is suggesting that from a human perspective, the intended perfection of Creation was disrupted by the Fall</note> in that which should not have failed Him. Who then at that same time possessed a certain Art that would not have failed? For instance, if someone had said: "Adam is in Paradise; he will never come into the world, for God Himself led him into Paradise." Now, that person would have had to fail in his prediction, and it would not have been successful for him. For however much God looks upon a thing, He also faces resistance from the Devil, who is a "Disrupter" to Him in all things; and He permits him. Who then can know for certain what will happen tomorrow? Even if he were an angel from God, he would know...

<summary>This page argues that human knowledge is inherently limited and uncertain, especially regarding celestial arts like astronomy, because even God's intentions can be disrupted by human fallibility or the Devil's interference.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the inherent uncertainty of human knowledge and the "Uncertain Arts." While the previous page established that humans cannot even hold onto physical objects with certainty, this page extends that logic to divine prophecy and natural laws, arguing that the interplay between the heavenly (certain) and the earthly (uncertain) creates a world of unpredictability.</meta>

->**The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus**<-

...not. Therefore, the **Celestial Arts** and **Sciences** <note>original: "Coelestes Artes / und Scientiae"</note> are also uncertain; for even if one knows God’s will, he cannot proclaim it as a certainty. This is because there are many <term>impediments</term> <note>original: "Impedimenta"; obstacles or hindrances</note> and obstructions that may break it. 

For example, Jonah was supposed to tell those in Nineveh what he did, and he spoke it as a certainty; yet it did not happen. It was not certain, for he was hindered by the fact that the people of Nineveh repented; at 그 point, his command was no longer in force. Similarly, if someone says to a sinner: "You are damned," it appears to be so, for the Scripture empowers and declares it. However, the one who speaks cannot be certain, because the cause of repentance and sorrow takes the damnation away and breaks the judgment of the Scripture. 

Therefore, none of these things are certain; everything is in doubt—that is, regarding the future. What is past is certain in itself; what is before one's eyes is likewise certain. But in matters of the future, nothing is certain, for God allows Himself to be made "uncertain" and lets His purpose be broken. How much more must we mortal humans on Earth expect uncertainty? There are not so many arts in nature that are so certain of their outcome as they are assumed and intended to be. 

Consider how a fire is supposed to burn and consume an object. Yet, how many saints have there been where the executioner made a "certainty" into an "uncertainty," so that the fire did not cause harm? How often is someone sentenced to death with certainty, yet it does not happen? Likewise, many are judged certain to die from sickness, yet that too is uncertain. 

In summary, whether it be in nature or in the heavens, as long as the world stands, all things are uncertain. For mixing a certainty and an uncertainty together cannot indicate anything certain. The heavenly is certain, but the earthly is not. When these two come together, one makes the other uncertain and leads it astray. But when the perishable passes away, then it is entirely certain, for nothing else can then exist.

Take an example from the <term>Natural Light</term> <note>original: "natürlichen Liecht"; Paracelsus’s term for human reason and the knowledge gained through observation of the world</note>: A prince or king undertakes a business. Now, people say, "the heart of the king stands in the hand of God." But let one say what they will—no matter whose hand it stands in—the king must endure the practical maneuvers made by those who encounter the very dealings the king has in mind. 

Thus, know of all things: there must be a firm intention if a thing is to be certain and not fail; it depends on the one in whose hand it lies. But all things here on Earth are not held in such firm hearts; rather, everything is like a reed that blows wherever the wind pleases. I must speak only of one man whose affairs became certain: that is John the Baptist, the baptizer of Christ. Now, he himself was upright in his dealings; but how is it that one who acts with justice and right... because he had not looked upon his uncertainty...

Therefore, since we do not even know what we are, and no one can truly know himself except God, that is the reason why all things are uncertain. Whatever wishes to be certain must wait until the Day of Resurrection; the verdict given to each person then will be certain.

### Proof regarding Attained Celestial Philosophy.

<meta>This page continues from page 145, where Paracelsus argued that human knowledge is limited and uncertain in our current mortal state. ### The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus (1493–1541).</note>

We can know nothing of the new world; we only know what is to come for this mortal world. That, however, is not **philosophy** <note>original: "Philosophia"</note>, but something else. Now, as for what **Celestial Philosophy** <note>original: "Philosophia Coelestis"</note> is for us now in this world, we should understand it in this way. I say this: We humans on earth may not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God. I mention this because the foolish man says there is no God. Why does he say this? Only because he knows nothing but gluttony and drinking. 

Now there are two kinds of people: those destined for salvation and those for damnation. Both must live on bread—that is, from that which they came from. One part lives from it toward damnation, the other toward salvation. Each part, however, must possess both **Attained Celestial Philosophy** <note>original: "Philosophiam adeptam Coelestem"; Paracelsus uses "adepta" to describe wisdom gained through spiritual practice or divine grace</note> and **Terrestrial Philosophy** <note>original: "Terrestrem"</note>. For not alone by bread, but also by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God—thus is our food and life. It is not from the earth, but from God through His Word. If the Word were not there, and only the bread by itself, then the earth would be our God. But no—not from the earth, but from God, through His Word. 

Now this is enough for this **proof** <note>original: "Probation"</note>: that we humans do not live from natural philosophy alone, but also from the heavenly. And although bread grows from the earth, it is yet the food of man—not for life nor for health. It is bread; its power within the bread is the Word of God. Our life here on earth, in both the mortal and the immortal aspects, comes from that same Word. For even if the sinner or the fool says: "No, I eat from the earth; there is no Word," he is effectively saying: "I say there is no God." 

What is on earth that does not have its blessing from God? Now the **Blessing** <note>original: "Segen"</note> is the Word, and the Blessing is life. As soon as that is taken away—when God withdraws His blessing—that thing immediately begins to wither and decline. This is how rich people become beggars, how fields dry up, and how hail strikes the garden. Even if there is enough bread and the tongue has all the pleasure it desires, if God takes His blessing, it is nothing but poison and eternal sickness, here and in the next world, which no physician can or may help. 

And regarding this proof, no one should wonder at my saying that it is not only what is from the earth that sustains man, but the Word from the mouth of God along with it. For **medicine** <note>original: "Artzney"</note> is a medicine and is earthly; it can do nothing by itself unless God be in it. Therefore, God heals the sick—not the earth, nor the elements. It is written in the **Gospel** <note>original: "Euangelio"</note> that the disciples used oil and anointed the sick with it...

He defines Celestial Philosophy as the understanding that human existence relies on this spiritual power rather than just earthly matter.</summary>

I must tell you an example: You see that we are all taught, so that each person is capable and knowledgeable. Now, what is it that makes everyone "taught"? It is nothing unless that learning comes not from the flesh, but from God. For it must be fulfilled that every person shall be taught by God. Since this is so, the **Natural Light** <term>original: "Naturlich Liecht"; the innate human capacity for reason and understanding the physical world</term> is nothing on its own; instead, it must proceed from God. For if that is sufficient, what then is bread that is without the Word of God? It is without power.

Now look at an example. Christ says: *This is my body, this is my blood.* <note>original: "das ist mein Leib/ das ist mein Blut"</note> Furthermore: *Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood...* etc. Now this is spoken according to **Celestial Philosophy** <note>original: "Coelestem Philosophiam"</note>, and according to that same philosophy, it is understood in this way: you should not think that by merely eating the bread and drinking the wine it is finished, as if you were only sustaining earthly flesh and blood. Rather, remember that with this bread you also eat and drink the **Eternal Bread** that is *within* the bread—namely, that from this same bread your eternal flesh grows, and from that drink, your eternal blood.

In summary, we should not only fill the belly, which belongs to the earth, but we should also enjoy the food of the eternal body, the newborn body. Therefore, the bread is bread for itself, and the Word in the bread is also a bread—not baker's bread, but Divine Bread that God himself baked. Thus we must recognize **Attained Celestial Philosophy** <term>original: "Philosophiam adeptam coelestem"; wisdom gained through spiritual practice or divine insight rather than mere study</term>, in that it does not teach us to understand the earthly alone, but it also teaches us to understand the eternal. That is, to eat eternal food with the mortal, within the mortal, here in this mortal life. And what we eat of the Eternal here in this mortal life remains in us, and we in Christ, as the **Second Adam** <note>In theology, the "First Adam" brought death; the "Second Adam" (Christ) brings eternal life</note>—that is, the Adam of the new birth.

Now, if we strive in all things for what the **Natural Light** gives us, we find nothing else but an earthly thing. There is absolutely nothing in the earthly, but it is in the Word. For he who commanded the sun to stand still, who created it to move—the sun has its power from that same Word. And as long as the Word lives and wills, so long is the sun in its power. Thus we all live from the Word: the earthly and the heavenly. Therefore we can—

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the limits of Natural Philosophy, transitioning from the previous page's focus on the Eucharist and the "Natural Light" to the necessity of recognizing God's sovereignty over natural substances like herbs.</meta>

# The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus

...not say, "there is no God"—that is, "since we have bread from the earth and wine from the vine, what need have we of God?" Both the wicked and the good receive their nourishment and life from the Word, though not all for eternal life. So that something of the eternal may also be considered, **Celestial Philosophy** <note>original: *Philosophia Coelestis*</note> must be undertaken by us. We should not write of earthly things like herbs alone, but also write of the eternal and the heavenly—that is, of Him in whose hand all things reside. 

Thus, if someone writes of **Chamomile** <note>original: *Camillen*</note> and its power but forgets Him who made it, he tells a lie about it. This creates false prescriptions in medicine, for a foolish physician wants to do exactly what nature does in the chamomile, yet he does not consider that the chamomile stands in the hand of God; it acts as He wills, not as nature wills. This misleads many a physician, for he relies upon the herb and the seed and not upon God. If it were only as Nature dictates, it would be a certain trade. But no: the One on high wants it according to His own mind and will. For this reason, He taught us to pray:

> **Thy will be done** <note>original: *dein Will geschehe*</note>

—that is, His will, not Nature's will, even though Nature is very capable and highly gifted. Rather, the will of Him who is the **Master of Nature** must be done. Know also this proof: that natural philosophy alone is not enough to know; one must also know the supernatural. This is how God works with His creation.

## Proof of Attained Celestial Medicine
<note>original: *Probatio in Coelestem Medicinam adeptam*</note>

<image-desc>Decorative ornate initial 'N' with scrolled floral and leaf patterns.</image-desc> Now, it is no less true that the medicine which comes through the Word of God—without any intermediate means—is the highest medicine, given specifically by God. This has been proven many times through the saints, for they have made the blind see, the dead live, the lepers clean, and much more besides. Therefore, because this proves itself, it may well be called **Attained Celestial Medicine** <note>original: *Medicina Coelestis adepta*; "Attained" refers to knowledge or medicine reached through divine grace or spiritual mastery</note>. 

However, a further knowledge is necessary to have: namely, that "Attained Celestial Medicine" is that which heals the sick when Nature is not able. That is, it heals those illnesses which are created solely for the sake of **God's Miracles** <note>original: *Wunderwerck Gottes*</note>, through which God is praised and honored. Just as when the question was asked of Christ: "Who is this man born blind? Has he sinned, or his parents?" Then Christ said: "No, neither he nor his parents, but rather so that the glory of God might be revealed through him." Since this sickness has no other origin than what has been stated, it follows that this blind man was subject to no [natural] medicine, but alone to the **Celestial...**

# The Second Book

**Heavenly.** <note>original: *Coelest.*, likely an abbreviation for Heavenly/Celestial Medicine</note> The woman who suffered from a **flow of blood** <note>original: *profluuio*; a reference to the woman in Mark 5:25-34</note> for twelve years and had consumed her wealth among the physicians, and no one was able to help her; from this it follows that her illness belonged to **Heavenly Medicine**, not to the natural. There are still many such illnesses in the world at this hour, where Heavenly Medicine alone must act, and not the natural. For illnesses are thus divided into two kinds: into Nature, and into the Heavenly powers. Therefore, understand now that Heavenly Medicine proceeds without a natural body—simply: "take up your bed and go," etc. 

Now, it is no less true that God does not wish His saints to be revealed, but rather He hides them. From this it follows that, contrary to the form of natural medicine, many are healed who could not be made healthy by Nature. Therefore, it is a great thing regarding the secrets of God: He works as He wills, in whom He wills, and when He wills. For this reason, He commanded us to seek, knock, and ask, for the cause that we cannot achieve all things through Nature, but daily need His help; therefore we should daily ask and seek Him, so that what Nature cannot give us may be given by Him. In this, we should know that we can be perfect in no matter without such prayerful help. For the **Word** must run alongside it; the reason being that no element would be anything if the Word had not made it. Likewise, there would be nothing of all creatures if the Word were not there. Thus, even at this hour, everything is nothing unless the Word is also there, for it is the life and the power. Where that is the medicine, there is **Attained Heavenly Medicine** <note>original: *Himliſche Medicina adepta*; 'Adepta' refers to medicine perfected through spiritual insight</note>. 

It is said, and it is so: whatever illnesses are born into a person, ingrained by Nature, are not subject to natural medicine—such as those born blind, mute, deaf, and the like. So too are there several more illnesses which are also like this and not of Nature, such as **leprosy** <note>original: *Auſſatz*</note> and its various types. Now, whoever wishes to heal them should seek nothing in Nature, but <insert>n</insert> <note>The inserted 'n' completes the word 'sondern' (but)</note> seek in Heaven; there lies the power. Therefore, the physician should be listened to, for God works through him—even if he does not know it, even as he sleeps—and gives him the medicine from the earth and the Word from above, without which nothing can happen. 

Now mark this regarding the **Plague** <note>original: *Peſtilentz*</note>: it too is an illness not at all subject to Nature, but only to Heavenly Medicine, along with the [earthly] medicine. Now the question is: if the Word alone makes one healthy, why not just as well through **Means** <note>original: *Media*</note>? Such as through **diaphoretics** <term>diaphoretics: medicines used to induce sweating to expel toxins</term>; that is, why is the Word not equal in all things, so that one might take the nearest thing at hand and help him with it? That is such a
