The reason is that where a sickness exists, there are two origins: one from Nature and the other from Heaven. The Word <note>The Divine Word or *Logos*</note> heals the heavenly ailment, while the natural heals the natural. Therefore, the **Plague** <note>original: *Pestilentz*</note> is a two-fold sickness originating from Heaven—thus requiring **Heavenly Medicine**—but when it corrupts the physical nature, that corruption must be healed naturally. This is the reason why those means that accord with Nature should be employed.

In this way, God also taught His prophets differently—one for prophecy, another for something else. He did the same with His angels—one for this task, another for that. So too with His apostles and His evangelists, maintaining order in all things. It is the same with medicine: each kind has its own particular essence, and each is ordained for a specific purpose; to that purpose, its power is given. Thus, you should now understand this **proof** <note>original: *Probation*</note> of **attained medicine** <term>medicina adepta; medicine reached through spiritual mastery and divine insight rather than just physical study</term>. In the manner described, it is **heavenly** <note>original: *Coelestis*</note>, so that in all things the heavenly influence must run alongside, and it must be present in all things as that which concludes and performs the work.

### Proof of Attained Mathematics
### Heavenly.

<image-desc>Ornate decorative initial 'V' with complex floral and foliate scrolling motifs contained within a square frame.</image-desc> To write of **Heavenly Mathematics** is a dangerous undertaking. For the reason is: who among us is truly a **Cosmographer**, a **Geographer**, and a **Geometer**, along with all the other branches? However, as much as is necessary for me to test them here, it is thus: it is possible for a human to grasp the entire world in a single fist, and all of it with a complete foundation and good knowledge. Now, since this is so—as it is found in the **Light of Nature** <term>the internal wisdom or "blueprint" within all created things</term> and proves itself—it must also be so here. And so that you may understand it, it is this: to bring Heavenly Mathematics into one's fist, there must first be the one who illuminates that same Mathematics, for the natural light cannot understand it. 

But because we do not live by the natural light alone, but by the **Word of God**, it is indeed possible for us to reach the foundation and understand **Heavenly Mathematics**. Even though we are in mortal flesh, that which is **Living** <note>the divine spark or life-force</note> is with us, which then speaks and works out of us with all its power. Now, **Heavenly Cosmography** <note>the study of the spiritual structure of the universe</note> is nothing other than seeing the human in **Hebron** <note>original: *Ebron*; in Paracelsan thought, this refers to the spiritual or "limbic" state of the first human, Adam, or the site of his creation</note>; the angels have another view. Likewise, **Geography** is nothing other than describing the Land in which there is no sin. He who wishes to take up **Geometry** here can measure nothing, for there is no beginning,

no end, and no one knows of any middle point. Therefore, **Heavenly Mathematics** <term>Coelestis Mathematica; the study of the divine order and celestial proportions</term> is to be held in high regard by the mortal body, so that it may find a greater understanding and seek another. Now you see the **proof** <note>original: *Probation*</note> in this way: since there is neither beginning nor end, it is proven that no art <note>here meaning a human skill, science, or branch of knowledge</note> provides anything at the boundaries. Everything is without beginning and without end; how can man, within the **natural light** <note>The "Light of Nature" refers to human reason and earthly knowledge as opposed to divine revelation</note>, reach out beyond that?

If we are to think of these things, this alone is the foundation: that not the **creatures** <note>created beings and physical objects</note> but God is to be contemplated. When He is measured, then all is measured—and that is as impossible for the **new body** <note>the spiritual or resurrected body</note> as it is for the old. As far as **Heavenly Mathematics** is concerned, the proof is that it is without end, where no one should direct their thoughts either to the **Alpha** <note>original: *A.*</note> or to the **Omega** <note>original: *O.*</note>, neither to the beginning nor the end. And just as little can **Mathematics** be fathomed in its **Cosmography** <term>the mapping of the general features of the universe</term> and **Geography** <term>the study of the earth's features</term>, and more besides, just as little as God Himself can be fathomed; for there He is all in all, with nothing excepted.

## The Conclusion.

<image-desc>A large decorative drop cap 'I' featuring floral and vine motifs within a square woodcut border.</image-desc>

YOU have understood me thus far in the **Heavenly Proofs** <note>original: *Probationibus Coelestibus*; these refer to the methods of testing and validating celestial and divine knowledge</note>. Now, nonetheless, many might raise opposition here. For who can shield himself from everyone? Since words are so swift, as are the thoughts of men—and in addition to all that, what truly resides in peace? All things are in discord <note>original: *vnfried*; referring to strife, unrest, or a lack of peace</note>, whatever they may be. Firstly, God created us all, and through His creation, He brought discord and unrest upon Himself, as is evident. If God Himself lives in discord, and no peace is kept for Him, then you should also know that man—His creature—will be even less spared from being touched by discord and unrest. Did He not overlook His own Son? He had to submit to discord; He will lay the Cross upon us all and see in it that which is His will, regardless of what our own will might be. Therefore, I pay little heed to this, especially in these times in which I live. For in these current times of mine, there is so much discord that the very things that are now discord were peace in the days of my parents, and what are now peace were then discord. And however it may be in all things, it is the **Oppression of Nations** <term>Pressura Gentium; a biblical term (Luke 21:25) referring to the distress and anxiety of people during tumultuous times</term>, nothing else than one against the other, and no one is safe in his bed, nor with his companion at a meal, nor at his plow in the field. If the beds are not safe, nor those in the mill, nor he at the plow, who then is without a **harassing devil** <term>Fegteuffel; literally a "sweep-devil," a term for a tormenting spirit or a source of constant, sweeping vexation</term>? I can well reflect on all this myself—that I am not exempt, but must also carry the Cross. Therefore, I allow the objections to my **Philosophy** <term>Philosophiam; here referring to Paracelsus's specific system of natural and divine knowledge</term> to happen for now; it is for the best. The time will come when they will rest and sleep within me. Let it go now as it will; there are many things; many are called, but few are chosen <note>A reference to Matthew 22:14</note>; everyone may cry out, but few cry out to any use. They may all pray, but few are granted their requests; everyone does his part, so I also do mine; everyone follows his own **straight path** <note>original: *fadenrecht*; literally "thread-straight," like a plumb line</note>, and I follow mine. Now, despite all this, let everyone test what his cry is and what his straight path is; and according to how he tests himself, let him cry out and let him lead his straight path, for in this it will lie: how everyone stands in the **Striking of Saturn** <term>Fulmination Saturni; an astrological/alchemical term referring to the harsh, purifying, or destructive influence associated with the planet Saturn</term>. It is no less so in the **Light of Nature** <term>Liecht der Natur; the innate human capacity to understand the physical world through reason and observation</term>; it also has many enemies, and everything within it is set against each other; this is caused by personal ambition, luxury, and pride. Yet there are only two ways: the just and the unjust, and man in his pride will not judge which belongs to the side of the just or the unjus—

<header>The Second Book</header>

...than to consider all this, beyond which there is nothing else. Now, nonetheless, no one should consider himself right or victorious, but rather recognize himself as a sinner; thus the spirit of humility enters him, teaching him to distinguish between what is just and unjust, so that he may fare well. But all this is ignored; only as far as the head's circle <note>The "head's circle" refers to the limited scope of human intellect or ego-driven logic</note> reaches is reason sought, which is an evil. In my time, much is said about spiritual things, yet it is all Pharisaic <note>The author uses "Pharisaic" to describe religious hypocrisy or a rigid adherence to the letter of the law without spiritual life</note>; that this same spirit is so easily recognized causes me to write much. I am not eloquent, for as soon as I speak one word, ten people are there who speak a thousand, and I please none of them; therefore, silence suits me well. For the good man will fall away from me [if I speak too much], but if I speak little, he remains, for he respects my writings and measures them by the judgment of Him who gave them; with Him I win, but with those who seek speech and chatter from me, I lose. Thus has my grace been given to me by God, in which I remain and shall die.

That heavenly power should be called an **Astronomy** is offensive to many, except for those from whom God has not taken away grace. Why should I not posit **Heavenly Magic** <note>original: *Coelestem Magicam*</note>, seeing as God is a **Magician** <note>original: *Magus*</note>? Not in His person, but through His own [people]; yet He is the first, the other is the other; God is not called "Magician," but rather the one to whom He gives the gift is. But why not also speak of a **Necromancer** <note>original: *Nigromanticus*</note>, since God presents the **subject of necromancy** <note>original: *Subiectum Nigromantiae*; here, the author likely refers to the study of the soul and the spiritual realms after death</note>? Should one then not speak of the same? Certainly, yes. Likewise also **Nectromancy** <note>original: *Nectromantia*; a specific term used by Paracelsus to describe a godly form of spiritual perception or communication with the "inner man"</note>, which flows from God Himself. Therefore, for the sake of the name, it should be worth nothing, yet it is worth so much gold that no one could pay for it. For he who is a **Nectromancer**, or **Magician**, or **Heavenly Necromancer**, is a saint.

Similarly, in **Heavenly Astrology** <note>original: *Coelesti Astrologia*</note>, there is a similar understanding: that God did not hand everything over to the **firmament** <note>The "firmament" refers to the literal sky and stars, which were believed to influence human fate</note>; He kept some for Himself, so that He might be a Master over all and not let it out of His hand. Who then should mark the people more justly than God? Is His sign not more than the natural one? Yes; therefore it is all the more necessary that He Himself marks them, for He fails with none; He hits the mark precisely, and after Him it is good to judge; there, no one lies. So it is with the **Uncertain Arts** <note>original: *Artibus Incertis*; these are the divinatory arts like palmistry or physiognomy, which the author argues are only "uncertain" when practiced without divine insight</note>. When we wish to be most certain, we find ourselves most uncertain; thus it must go the way another intends.

So it is in **Heavenly Philosophy** <note>original: *Philosophia Coelesti*</note>: How can man have a greater **Philosophy** than from God into the **New Birth** <term>new Geburt; refers to the spiritual regeneration or transformation of the soul through divine grace</term>? What we deal with in the natural world is but darkness—yet not the darkness of damnation, but rather that of the **Light of Nature** <term>Liechts der Natur; the innate wisdom and potential within the created world that allows man to understand the physical universe</term>, which is still in God's hand, and in which no one angers God. What, too, is our medicine? He who is capable in it, all...

<header>The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus</header>

[The physician] recognizes herbs and roots, all diseases, etc., and acts according to the extent of his knowledge; what further is there to deal with here, except only that the physician is against the patient, and the patient is against the physician. In that world <note>Paracelsus refers here to the eternal realm or the state of grace, contrasting it with the "mortal" world of earthly medicine</note>, it is not so with his medicine; rather, the medicine that flows from God is immediately present, so that the physician is holy and the patient is blessed. There, the practicing of medicine is good; and Nature—what is she? Nothing. Even if we know her, she is nonetheless nothing more. For as soon as we die, it is all over, and there is nothing more. Therefore, let that [medicine] be of value which has no end, no beginning, no middle, and is eternal. 

This has caused me to write, and not to neglect it; not only that I should use my pen once, but to renew it a second time, a third, even unto the seventh time—as gold is purified through the fire—thus also to purge, examine, and look closely. This seems good to me: not to fly before one has wings <note>original: *nit fliegen vor den Flügeln*; a proverb meaning one should not attempt great things before being properly prepared or matured</note>. A rose is a beautiful ornament, but it must have a full year until it comes to the shrub, to the umbel <note>original: *Dolden*; the botanical cluster where flowers form</note>, and finally to the blossoms. So it is with all other things: he who would mistake the shrub for a rose would have no rose and does not know it; he who would take the bud for the rose and break it off—what does he have? But he who awaits the time until Nature draws it out and it grows to its appointed term <note>original: *Termin*; the natural or predestined time for completion</note>, he has a rose. 

Since Nature acts thus, how much more does the Heavenly act over Nature? Therefore, no one should boast before the time, but rather measure the time; for nothing becomes ripe before its season. He who does not recognize the time proves to be an errant man and a deceiver; he breaks off what is not ripe and takes what is not commanded of him. Thus, I wish to have tested these **Probations of the Heavenly Members** <note>original: *Probation Membrorum Coelestium*</note>, and to further present the **Heavenly Gifts** <note>original: *Dona Coelestia*</note> in their proper place; and so, for this time, I have done enough with the **Probations** <note>original: *Probationibus*</note>.

# Wise Philosophy of the
## Great Astronomy / concerning Infernal Powers / according to the capacity of Nature /
### By the well-grounded and proven Doctor of both Medicines <note>Paracelsus refers to himself as a doctor of "both medicines," meaning both the physical medicine of the body and the spiritual/hermetic medicine of the soul.</note>, Philippus Theophrastus Paracelsus.

# Preface
### To the Fourth Book of the Great Astronomy of Theophrastus Paracelsus.

<image-desc>A large decorative initial 'A' featuring intricate floral and scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>

As I have written for you the three parts of my Great Astronomy, in which I have presented the secrets of hidden things—namely, the power of the natural light <note>The "light of nature" is a central Paracelsian concept referring to the innate wisdom and divine knowledge embedded within the physical world.</note> in Astronomy—and further, how Celestial Astronomy acts in an astronomical manner, together with the Astronomy of Faith: now, hereafter, is the fourth part. This is the Astronomy that tells how the Infernal Astronomical influence manifests itself and carries out its effects. Now, first of all, I wish to give you instruction here in this preface that it is not against the Faith, nor against the power of the Order of Creation, to say that the Devil (or his followers) should be able to accomplish the nine species of Astronomy. It is not that he or his followers cannot be <term>Magi <note>original: Magi; here meaning practitioners of natural magic who understand the hidden properties of the world.</note></term>, for they may indeed be <term>Mages</term>: nor that they should not be <term>Nigromantici <note>original: Nigromantici; traditionally "black magicians," though in the 16th century this was often a general term for those dealing with forbidden spirits.</note></term> without sorcery—that is, without falsehood. Or likewise <term>Nectromantici <note>original: Nectromantici; likely a variation of necromancy, specifically the art of communicating with the spirits of the dead or "astral bodies."</note></term>, just as such species manifest in the other three branches [of astronomy]. They are also <term>Astrologi <note>original: Astrologi; astrologers.</note></term> and recognize and understand <term>Astrologiam <note>original: Astrologiam; astrology.</note></term> at its foundation. They are likewise subject to <term>Signatis <note>original: Signatis; things that have been "signed" or marked.</note></term> and <term>Signaturis <note>original: Signaturis; the "signatures," or physical outward signs that reveal the inner character and virtues of a thing.</note></term> just as much as Man or the Beast is; for the distinctions among them [the infernal spirits] should and can be recognized just as well as the distinctions among Men and among the Beasts, where one sees who is black, red, small, large, and so on.

Paracelsus uses this term to describe occult or speculative practices like magic and alchemy that lack the fixed certainty of divine law but still operate through natural forces.</note> as we are—and even more certainly so, for the spirit is more understanding than the flesh. Thus, in the same way, they are to be recognized in all the matters of the philosophers. Likewise, regarding **mathematics** <note>original: "Mathematicam"</note>, they are in no way ignorant. Since they are so highly learned in such **operations** <note>original: "Operationibus"</note> and are capable of conducting, managing, and accomplishing them, there is a reason why this is possible for them. It is clearly evident that it is necessary for man to know such **effects** <note>original: "Effectus"</note>, and it is proper that he experiences this.

For why does man live on earth, if not solely to be experienced in the works of God, and to see how all things have proceeded from God? And although the Devil, along with his **infernal** <note>original: "Infernalischen"</note> legions, is set against God and His people, it is nonetheless sufficiently proven that he pursues us like a roaring lion, each according to his own nature. To a merchant, he is a merchant; God is also a merchant to the merchant. Know, however, that one is from the Devil, the other from God. Thus, the Devil is a king to the king, a prophet to the prophet, an apostle to the apostle, and a doctor to the doctor. Therefore, there are two kinds of kings, two kinds of prophets, two kinds of doctors, two kinds of apostles, and so on: the righteous one in God, and the false one in the Devil.

Therefore, it is necessary that man—that every individual—carries the knowledge within his understanding of what is from God and what is from the Devil. Likewise, regarding those who are divine royal rulers and divine prophets, and those who are the devilish ones: man should recognize and understand them. For it seems to me entirely and utterly useful that a merchant should recognize the Devil, and that everyone should know how the Devil teaches a merchant, a doctor, or a prophet, and by what means he catches and snares them. It seems to me of great necessity that such knowledge should dwell within man, so that he is not led by the Devil into any kind of evil, through which eternal **damnation** <note>original: "Verdamnuß"</note> might await him.

For take note of an **example** <note>original: "Exempel"</note> from me: when a person is young, he learns from the elder and listens to the elder, for the elder leads him onto his path. Now, if it is possible for one human to lead the young onto the right path or the evil path, depending on who that person is, it is far more possible for the Devil, who is even older than mankind. Indeed, the oldest man is but a child in the cradle—even younger, younger than in his mother’s womb—compared to even the youngest devil. Therefore, the Devil knows the arts of good and evil very well; he abandons the good and turns it into that which is otherwise good...

Now, the Devil can also do this, and even better than man has learned his sustenance from God. That is to say, he can teach man to support himself through idleness; he can teach him to gain ten guilders where, according to God’s teaching, he must be content with ten kreuzers <note>The guilder was a gold coin of high value, while the kreuzer was a small silver coin; Paracelsus is illustrating the leap from modest necessity to greedy excess.</note>, and much else besides. Likewise, he can do this not only among **merchants**, in **handicrafts**, or in **trades**, but he can also teach where Christ says to the **Apostles** that they should carry neither staff nor bag, etc., yet he teaches them to have donkeys to carry these things for them. And where Christ says, "eat what is set before you," the Devil can teach that everything must be set before them, both cooked and raw. Where He says, "You are Peter," etc., the Devil can teach that another person may also be understood by this <note>A likely critique of the Papacy, suggesting the Devil interprets the "Keys of Peter" to justify the power of later institutional leaders rather than the humble apostle.</note>. It is impossible for me to write out everything that he can pervert and teach contrary to and beyond what we have from God, so that everything is pushed to an even sharper extreme.

These are the reasons why I desire to describe these things: so that man may understand in his mind and conscience whether or not he is practicing his office <note>original: "Ampt." This refers to one's God-given vocation or duty on earth.</note>—which God gave him on earth—according to God’s will; for therein lies the danger of eternal death. For only look at the Devil’s wisdom in the cunning of his craftsmen, and what he now does with the **tailors**: God and Nature teach us to make clothing for necessity and according to humility; then comes the Devil and teaches the tailor to make clothes of vanity <note>original: "vppigkeit." Refers to luxury, excess, or sinful pride in appearance.</note>, saying it is for the "prosperity" of the world, and he adorns man and woman. Thus, the prosperity of God and Nature must be despised, while the Devil’s prosperity must be accepted—deemed right for the nobility in their way, right for the citizenry in their way, for the peasants likewise, and for the priests and monks as well, each in his own particular masquerade <note>original: "Gugelfuhr." Literally a "hood-track," used historically to mean a farce, a ridiculous proceeding, or a deceptive disguise.</note>. The Devil does this among the tailors alone, and they do not reflect on it; they ought to know not to act beyond the adornment of God and Nature. Indeed, all men forget that single verse where the Prophet says:

What else is this verse but that all men should have one figure, one form? Thus, it should rightly be so under the tailor. Yet it does not stop with the tailor alone; it is the same with the **shoemaker**: shoes for women, those for men, those for the wives of princes, those for the nobility, those for the citizens' wives, those for the peasant women—and yet they are all equally women. So it is also with men’s shoes: now they are slashed, made of velvet, or made of gold, and these one is forced to buy, etc. Now, take note: this is true not only with these, but with all handicrafts. Therefore, reader / read the following astronomical philosophy of the infernal powers / so that you may recognize / and know / what infernal power and might are / and act accordingly / and guard yourself against error.

### How the Hellish Spirits were created.

As you have read in the first part concerning the composition of mankind / from what they are made by God the Creator / namely that He existed before them / and before man was / all things had been created / and from that creation man was made / that is / from the <term>slime of the earth</term> <note>original: "Limo Terrae." In the Vulgate Bible, this refers to the "dust of the ground" from which Adam was formed (Genesis 2:7).</note> / which is to say / man is made from a material substance. Here, however, in this place / concerning the creation of the infernal ones / there is no corporeal matter for the body / but only the word / which is invisible / has created them. Now first of all, take note / if we wish to know the beginning of the infernal ones / then we must first know / the origin and beginning of the angels. For in the same way / as from the earthly man comes the newborn of heaven / and another the newborn of hell : So it is here in this place also to be understood / that the angels were created beautiful and good / beyond all beauty : However / there is nothing / that is created and gifted by God / that is not nonetheless set into service / if God withdraws His hand from them / As an example : Judas was an apostle / when God left him because of the cause he gave <note>The text suggests Judas’s own actions provided the "vrsach" (cause/reason) for God to withdraw His grace.</note> / then he despaired / and hanged himself / and burst asunder in the middle. Peter, he remained steadfast / to him He gave the keys to heaven / and did not take them back / for Christ himself prayed for him / that his faith would not fail in the sudden crisis <note>original: "im gehesten," referring to a sudden, precipitous fall or a moment of extreme trial.</note> / therefore those / whom God sets before Him / they go out along that same path / but those who are not of that same order / they remain in watching / fasting / and praying / so that God does not lead them into temptation / as happens to all creatures and creations / if they do not watch / pray / and fast / then God withdraws His hand from them / letting them fall into adultery / theft / murder / idolatry / pride / arrogance / and then the hand of God falls upon them.

Therefore know that I indicate this / so that [you know] the infernal ones were not created as infernal beings / but as angels / but when no fear of God arose in them / they were then cast out / and what they had was taken from them. Now for the sake of a greater understanding / before I set down the beginning of the angels / you shall understand and know this example : Namely /

<header>The Fourth Book / The Second Chapter.</header>

## That Lucifer and his followers were cast out on account of pride.

Now, it is no less true that man, being merely human, cannot grasp anything outside of this world regarding the punishment of those who are in the Kingdom of God, or those who have been cast out from the Kingdom of God. For no one can speak of higher things—unless he be taught by the Spirit <note>original: "nisi per Spiritum doceatur"</note>—save from those higher realms themselves. Yet, as much as analogy and experience allow, and as long-standing history and revelation suggest, it is well understood that in heaven, just as on earth, there was initially both good and evil: sin and sinlessness, the pious and the impious, the righteous and the unrighteous. 

Where God drew the line between the evil and the good in His kingdom is unknown to man; however, that it is true has been sufficiently demonstrated here on Earth. This is so, even though it is a marvel that in the House of God—which God created for Himself according to His own pleasure—He created angels who were not perfect, pure, or without sin, but instead fell into such significant sin. One might judge that such a sin was greater than those of <term>Sodom and Gomorrah</term> <note>Two biblical cities destroyed by divine judgment; the author suggests the angelic rebellion was an even more profound transgression.</note>, or even the world that was swallowed by the <term>Great Flood</term>. 

What kind of <term>spiritual body</term> <note>original: "Corpus Spirituale"</note> it was in which such sin resided within the heavens, man cannot fathom. He knows only what he experiences of himself: for flesh is flesh—diseased, besides—and made from <term>mire</term> <note>original: "Koth," literally filth or mud; used here to describe the lowly material of the human body in contrast to the celestial substance of angels.</note>, and to mire it shall return, which is why man is born in sin. 

But in heaven, it is a different matter; the angels were not made from such mire, but rather, as one might judge, from the purest of the pure. Yet, for all that, a significant number of them fell into such sin that all the Hells are filled with them. Therefore, man should consider this: that in all His creatures to whom He gave reason, God allowed a "split path" to exist, as an analogy for their journey. It is as if God had said: "Now, I am alone and have no one with me; I will create a company for myself, servants, and so on. They must possess reason and recognize my will. However, so that I may see what is steadfast and what is not, I will leave them their freedom and watch how my creatures conduct themselves toward me. Those who hold fast, I shall keep; those who do poorly, I shall cast out." Observe then, that all creatures to whom...

<header>The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus</header>
<meta>catchword: The</meta>

...to whom God has given reason, are placed into such <term>temptation</term> <note>original: "Temptation"</note> in heaven just as much as on earth. Now, because reason stands in such temptation—and reason is placed so precariously upon the branch of a tree that the wind tosses to and fro, never enjoying a single steady hour, but rather existing only to prove itself—it follows that in such moments God withdraws His hand. He leaves reason to its own will. This <term>free will</term> <note>original: "freyer Wille"</note>, which is not held in the hand of God, is truly free: it either falls or it stands.

Consider this example of free will: no one is truly free except the one who has no master. He who does not have God as a master—that is, God does not hold him in His hand but instead lets him remain (or stand) free—it follows from this that he may do as he wishes. This is how the trial proceeds, which is why we on earth were taught by Christ to pray: *Lead us not into temptation.* For temptation is when God withdraws His hand from us, lets us stand free, and leaves us to our own free will. We pray that we do not fall while in that state; therefore we ask: *Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.* This "evil" is nothing other than the condition of standing in our own free will.

The angels stood in this very same condition. One part of them acted wisely; they looked upon their Creator and did not give themselves over to wickedness. The other part, however, raised themselves up in <term>pride</term> <note>original: "Hoffart"; in this context, it refers to a delusional self-importance that forgets one's dependence on the Creator.</note> and forgot and abandoned God their Creator, who had made, created, and ordained them. As the Psalmist says: "You have abandoned the one who created you, and have forgotten God your Creator." <note>A reference to Deuteronomy 32:18, commonly attributed to the "Psalmist" in a general liturgical sense during this period.</note> Because he abandoned God and forgot his Creator, God cast him out into <term>Tartaros</term> <note>original: "Tartaros"; a Greek term for the deep abyss of punishment, here used to describe the exile of fallen angels.</note> and kept the pure ones with Him.

### That the Good Angels Were Preserved on Account of Their Humility.

Now, it is no less fitting to provide a better instruction regarding the matters mentioned; namely, that <term>Reason</term> <note>original: "Vernunfft"</note> shall have the understanding of good and evil, and the choice of which it desires, in such a way that God merely withdraws His hand and allows Reason to act as its own Law. Now, it is to be noted in this regard that Reason must be somewhat united with the <term>Holy Spirit</term>; for where the Spirit is not, Reason is bare and weak. In and of itself, Reason is no different than that of a beast, even if it possesses great understanding, great wisdom, ingenuity, and cleverness; yet it is only that wisdom which is foolishness before God.

Now it is also to be known that even the wisdom of the angels is nothing but foolishness before God, unless it be united with the Holy Spirit. This was proven when the angels stood in the free will of the <term>Trial</term> <note>original: "Examination"</note>. There, the hand of God was withdrawn just enough so that they might recognize themselves—each one as he truly was, at the very core. But the Light was not in them; only their own self-knowledge remained, which then deceived some—namely, the wealthiest and most highly gifted angels. These took such great pleasure in themselves that they believed they did not need God and were above Him. 

The others—namely the poorest (as is easily recognized)—remained in <term>Humility</term> <note>original: "Demut"</note>, which is why they kept their place and remained. As the Blessed Virgin says: *He has cast down the mighty from their thrones* <note>original: "Er hat verstossen die mechtigen vom Stul"; a reference to the Magnificat, Luke 1:52</note> (that is, Lucifer, as the mightiest angel) *and has exalted the humble*—that is, the poor angels of humility, whom He placed in the stead of the others. 

For this is proven here on Earth: that wealth is often set against God; it breeds <term>Pride</term> <note>original: "Hoffart"</note>, contempt for the source from which it came, and disobedience and ingratitude toward the one who created and gifted it. Regarding this, it is now to be noted: if God withdraws His hand, it is nothing other than Him taking the Holy Spirit from a person and letting them act according to their own pleasure within their own Reason. Where the Holy Spirit is not, there is <term>Free Will</term>; for where the Holy Spirit is, there all things must proceed according to the Holy Spirit. Yet there is also a Free Will in those who have the Holy Spirit; they possess the Divine

Wisdom—now you love that same wisdom—does not come from the teaching of the Holy Spirit by free will alone, but it is a prepared free will toward the good, and the choice to hold to the good and not to evil. For those from whom the <term>Holy Spirit</term> is entirely withdrawn—such as the damned—they also possess a free will, but it is used for evil: to do whatever they desire, such as murder, stealing, deceiving, etc. 

But the true free will is that which stands in the <term>Trial</term> <note>original: "Proba," a crucible or test of quality</note>, in the temptation through one's own <term>Reason</term> <note>original: "vernunfft"</note> without the Holy Spirit. Therefore, I maintain and point out that the Holy Spirit was not present with the angels during their <term>Examination</term> <note>original: "Examination," the period of testing for the angels</note>, nor was He given to them then. But it is well-incorporated into our faith that, subsequently, the Holy Spirit was given to the righteous, remaining, humble angels; for He is the <term>confirmation</term> <note>original: "confirmierung"</note> and the constancy that does not yield. 

Therefore, no angel will yield anymore hereafter, for the light of the Holy Spirit is with them. Just so is it proven among us on Earth: regarding the Apostles who were with Christ, it was said of them after their own Trial, "I will have you with me, so that where I am, there you shall also be." Christ sealed this in such a way after His Ascension, when He gave them the Holy Spirit; with Him, He confirmed them. Previously, it was not found that they possessed the Holy Spirit; they certainly had command and power from Christ, but they stood in their own Reason. Because of this, they were not always understanding, and were sometimes too weak in faith or too little enlightened. 

As an example, Thomas did not want to believe, and Judas became a traitor. But after the sending of the Holy Spirit, all things were enlightened within them and ignited in Love, so that hereafter no weakness in faith, no lack of eternal wisdom, and no misunderstanding was ever found in them again; rather, they were perfect in all the will of God. 

Thus it is also to be understood regarding the proven angels: that subsequently the Holy Spirit was given to them, so that they never depart from God in eternity. Just as the Apostles did not depart from Christ—leaving behind wife and child, father and mother, fields and meadows, and everything, even the body at the last—hereafter in eternity, without end,

# The Fourth Book
## The Fourth Chapter.
### That Satan has transformed his angelic wisdom into a hellish and devilish wisdom for all manner of evil.

<image-desc>A large woodcut ornamental initial letter 'S' decorated with intricate scrolling floral and vine motifs.</image-desc>

Concerning the infernal spirits who have been cast out. Now, it is further to be known that since Lucifer is no longer in Heaven, but has been cast out of Heaven into the infernal regions—the reason for which has been sufficiently stated—you should know further that his beautiful radiance and angelic nature have been overturned. Out of chalk has come coal; out of a carbuncle <note>A red gemstone, historically believed to glow with its own internal light.</note> has come dung <note>original: "Quark," here referring to something worthless or foul.</note>. Therefore, whatever God gives, or has given, without <term>Confirmation</term> <note>original: "Confirmation," the act of making a state permanent through the Holy Spirit.</note>—that is, without the sealing of the Holy Spirit—all of that can be turned back, namely, away from God. For it has not been fully released out of the hand of God, but still stands in God's hand. 

However, whatever God gives after Confirmation, He never takes back; for He has given it after the <term>Examination</term>, the <term>Trial</term> <note>original: "Probierung," the testing of the angels' character.</note>, and the Confirmation. He also entrusted the little sheep <note>A metaphor for the faithful or the souls of the blessed.</note> to them after the Confirmation, and He does not take them back from them. Therefore, I say this: that Lucifer, the chief originator of the hellish spirits, possessed nothing "confirmed," but rather, during his Trial, he fell into his <term>Pride</term> <note>original: "Hoffart," a specific type of arrogant, high-minded vanity.</note> and into lies against God. He never acted with any truth before God while he was in Heaven. For Christ Himself says: He was a liar from the beginning and never stood in any truth. 

This means that Christ testifies that he [Lucifer] began lying while still in Heaven and never practiced the truth. From this it follows that the very thing he took upon himself against God—the lie—is that in which he was "confirmed" by God: to remain a liar eternally. From this it follows that he remains a liar, and since lies cannot exist in Heaven—only the truth—he had to be removed from Heaven. 

Thus, upon him was placed a garment that befits a liar, just as a rope is placed upon a thief or a wheel <note>The "breaking wheel," a common and brutal instrument of execution for murderers in the 16th century.</note> is given to a murderer, etc. This is now his thieving, lying nature: that he has lost his radiance and is clothed and transformed into the "radiance" of a thief and a liar, so that nothing angelic remains in him or his followers. From the day now comes darkness; he who was the light became the night; and out of a sun came a dark, terrifying heap of coal. He has thus been thrust into the <term>Elements</term> <note>The physical realm consisting of earth, water, air, and fire.</note>; he wanders in the sun's brilliance, he wanders in all bodies <note>Physical objects or organisms.</note>, yet the sun is of no use to him,

# The Fourth Book
## The Fifth Chapter
### Concerning the Dwelling Place of Evil Spirits

<image-desc>A large ornamental decorative initial letter 'E' at the beginning of the text, featuring intricate foliage and scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>I must present to you an example of the dwelling of the devils, and specifically this: You see before us—it is visible—that the sun gives us the day; it gladdens both the sensible and the insensible through its shine, and we thank God and praise God in His works; for thus has God given and created it for us humans. Now, regarding this, you also know that creatures have a use of the sun’s shine according to what they are; namely, the good rejoice in it, but the wicked are terrified by it, for the wicked know how to receive nothing useful from the sun. Like <term>rotten wood<note>Paracelsus often uses decaying organic matter as a symbol of things that have lost their "life force" or "balsam."</note></term> and earthworms, to whom the sun is of no use at all. 

Now note this: the sun shines and gives its power into all <term>bodies<note>original: *Corpora*</note></term>, even into the <term>center<note>original: *Centrum*</note></term>, through and through, in the same way as through a glass. Thus its power passes through the sea, down to the very bottom; likewise through the earth, through and through, to the lowest foundation; likewise through the air throughout its whole body; likewise through the fire, through and through. And it passes through all <term>generations<note>In alchemy, "generation" refers to the natural formation or growth of substances.</note></term> that come from the elements, such as the metals, the mountains, the stones, the cliffs, wood, and whatever is there, so that in the midst of them there is nothing where the sun’s power is not present. 

For against the sun’s power, all bodies are like glass. And although our eyes do not perceive this, but rather they appear as <term>dark bodies<note>original: *Tenebrosa Corpora*</note></term>, yet before the sun they are all <term>transparent<note>original: *Diaphona*</note></term> and <term>clear<note>original: *Perspicua*</note></term>, just as the air is in all things and passes through them. I tell you this example for this reason: where the sun is, there are the devils; where creatures are, there are devils; for the entire circumference of the creatures is the world, and it is <term>Hell<note>original: *Helle*. Paracelsus posits a provocative theory that Hell is not a distant underworld, but a spiritual state existing within our own physical world.</note></term>. 

But now, just as the world gladdens the creatures—as the plants of the earth rejoice toward heaven, and all <term>rocks<note>original: *Petra*</note></term> rejoice toward heaven and because of the day, and so also all other creatures, humans, and whatever exists, rejoice in the day—so it is with the devils. Though they are also in the day, that same day is a darkness to them; they see the sun and are terrified by it. What gladdens humans and creatures is a sorrow to them; what is good for humans is contrary to them, as the example demonstrates: 

One man lies imprisoned in a tower facing death; another is outside the tower and dancing. Now see how far apart these two are. The one who is led out to the gallows is terrified by the day and nothing gladdens him anymore; the other dances and has joy. Both are under one sun, but [he is] not...

# The Sagacious Philosophy of Theophrastus

## The Eighth Chapter

->Concerning the <term>meteors<note>original: *Metheoris*; in the 16th century, this referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including rain, wind, and lightning, not just falling stars.</note> and storms made by devils, and from what <term>simples<note>original: *Simplicibus*; the basic, unmixed ingredients of nature.</note> they are made, and how they make them.<-

Now, it is no less true that among the evil spirits, actions also occur—namely, that they can produce thunder, showers, hail, snow, wind, rain, and also strange figures in the sky, and many more such pieces. This is to be understood in the same way as we on Earth have all the tools for what we require, so that we may work in metals, in stones, in wood, and in all other things; for there is nothing that is not suited to an art or trade, being ordained for some purpose. Thus, we are to practice our skills on Earth in this manner. Now, just as it is in that place, it is also to be understood regarding the <term>firmament<note>original: *Firmament*; the sphere of the sky and the air.</note> that those things which are in the heavens—and the fruits before him—also grow in the firmament just as well as those from the earth. Just as foliage and grass grow out of the earth up toward the heavens, conversely, rain, dew, thunder, hail, etc., all grow in the firmament and out of the firmament, and descend down to us. And just as the grass from the earth has its order and customs, so in the same way, these <term>meteoric impressions<note>original: *Metheoricae Impressiones*; the physical manifestations of celestial forces in the atmosphere.</note> also stand in order within the firmament. 

So, if something is to grow out of the earth, it must have its beginning in that from which it grows, such as the seed, the root, etc. Likewise, there is also a being in the heavens or the firmament from which the rain grows, as well as snow, hail, lightning-bolts, thunder, frost, and so on. Now it must be known that the beginning from which a thing grows should be well considered here, for the reason is this: if we know from what "seeds" the thunder is made, and the rain, and the hail, and everything else, then we can surely know and recognize from what causes the Devil and his spirits are able to make such weather. For this is the "Meteoric Philosophy": that from these things, "firmamental impressions" are born—namely from Salt, from Sulfur, and from Mercury. These three are composed by Nature, and according to how they are joined, the <term>generated thing<note>original: *Generatum*</note> is then formed, which the <term>Archeus of the Firmament<note>original: *Archeus Firmamenti*; the "inner alchemist" or governing natural force that directs the growth and separation of elements in the sky.</note> separates and prepares. # The Fourth Book

...and does to it that which belongs to it, so that which is meant to come of it, shall come of it. In this same way, the evil spirits make such weather, lightning bolts, frost, and other things that would not have happened through nature alone but would have remained undone. Just as the stones would remain lying there and never become a tower if the stonemason did not exist, so it is with these spirits. But because these spirits know all the secrets of nature, its arrangements, and what things are made of, it follows that it is as possible for them as it is for nature itself. However, know then that God does not always permit this, but rather hinders it. For if such things were not within the power of God, we would not be able to remain living on Earth. Nevertheless, it does not happen without cause when such devilish storms occur. In addition to the damage they do, they are a <term>presage<note>original: *Praesagium*; an omen or sign of a future event.</note> and a <term>judgment<note>original: *Judicium*</note> of a shameful future calamity. For whatever omens the devil gives, it is his joy that the omen should be directed against mankind. As the work is, so shall the omen be; the omen reflects the master who makes it. 

Otherwise, it has not yet been experienced that the devil and his spirits can act or intervene in such things in any other way than by signaling future things—showing that what is to come will be as foul as the one from whom it comes. Therefore, it is of great necessity that the works that come from the hand of God are well understood, as well as those that come from the hand of the devil. **B**efore the undertaking of this book is fully concluded, it is necessary to know the concordance of evil spirits with God, with the angels, the saints of Paradise, with humans, with cattle, and with all plants that the elements provide. Thus it is also with the saints, and likewise with humans, as is then evident when he possesses and misleads them, turning them away from good intentions; and he also misleads and possesses the cattle and other creatures of the four elements. If such things were not obvious and grasped beyond all doubt, no one would believe that the Devil should speak with Christ and so boldly resist him in temptation. This is therefore a reason why we should recognize and know that the Devil, although he was once an angel who knew God well, has been robbed of his light so that he no longer has knowledge of anything in heaven, except for what he learns through temptation. ## The Tenth Chapter.
### On the Concordance of the Dead and Evil Spirits.

<image-desc>Ornate decorative woodcut initial 'N' featuring floral and leaf scroll motifs within a square frame.</image-desc>

**NOW** it is also necessary that the **concordance** <note>agreement or spiritual connection</note> of the devils, which they have with the dead, be well understood. Although I mention this in other places as well, it is nevertheless necessary to remind you of it here at this very foundation in this beginning. For the reason is this: you see that often dead bodies <note>original: *Corpora*</note> are or become different, contrary to nature, than nature is capable of in those same bodies; also that sometimes spirits walk, and the like. Now, all this is not to be rejected [as impossible]; for the cause is: he who dies in the Lord is blessed, and to the blessed, nothing further happens. 

But whatever does not die in the Lord, dies in the Devil. Now, the Devil can also make "saints" in his kingdom; he knows how bodies are to be preserved from decay <note>original: *feule*</note> better than man does; he knows the right balm. Therefore, he may well take one of his own and preserve him thus, and for the living, who are also his, arrange a deception. He may also do something else: that is, to manage according to the person—to go about after a person’s death in that same person’s spirit, or in that of another. 

For although one says: "Everyone goes where they belong, immediately to Heaven or to Hell"—this is not a true statement. Everyone goes into a **holding place** <term>holding place: *behaltnus*; a transitional state or location where souls are kept before final judgment</term>. Namely, before the death of Christ, they went into a special holding place; after the death of Christ, there are other holding places—namely, those who die in the Lord go into Paradise, and those who die in Satan go into his chest [or coffer], even until the Day of Judgment. 

Thus, the Devil, who is still here on Earth, and who also has the "held soul" on Earth, can very well move the held person about within that same chest or garden. Likewise, through such "held" people, he can create the "saints" of his kingdom who perform signs <note>miracles or omens</note>. All of this will be found in his **proofs** <note>original: *Probationibus*; demonstrations or trials</note>, showing in what way such a thing is possible. 

But man should know that in such a place, this fellowship with the Devil should be understood: that, in short, he stands beside them continually and tempts them without ceasing. But as for those who are not of his kind—he is within them, leading them according to how he himself thinks best to achieve further deception. For instance, he might touch a prophet in such a way that the man would have to be put in chains, like the madmen <note>those possessed by demons</note> in the presence of Christ; but it is more useful to him that he does not have a madman of a possessed person, but rather one...

# The Eleventh Chapter.
## On the Order and Distinction of Spirits.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'N' featuring floral patterns and scrolled foliage.</image-desc>

**NOW** it is no less true—and it is also publicly evident—that there is an order in Heaven among the angels, one greater than the other, one for this command and another for that; so too on Earth there is an order, one over the other and one under the other, so that nothing is without an order, lest everyone be for himself, but rather subject and obedient to the other. Only among the saints is it not so; they require no order or authority <note>original: *Obrigkeit*</note>; each does what he should do without a superior. Therefore the saints are exempt and free, but the angels are not; they are under God as servants. The saints are not servants, except that Christ is their Head, in whom they rejoice and remain in unity. Now these orders are to be understood thus: that one is an authority under which the others are, and they must be ruled by one Head, so that there are not many heads, but only one Head, though many members or "tails" <note>This likely refers to subordinates or followers trailing behind the leader.</note>. Now, if there were sinners in Heaven <note>Paracelsus refers here to the angels who rebelled while still in the celestial realm.</note>, it is necessary that there also be an Emperor in the same, who is God. Therefore, he [Lucifer] still holds his power among his own in Hell, following that same order. For Christ says: "He has been a liar from the beginning" <note>A reference to John 8:44.</note>; there He speaks only of the highest Devil, who led the others astray, and says that he is also a "Father of Lies." All this proves that he alone stands as the highest.

Accordingly, the other devils also have power; for it was in the name of the devils that Christ was accused of driving out the devil. Likewise, the "legion" of devils that Christ drove out of the possessed proves that there are other devils who carry out their specific duties. For just as the Holy Spirit should be in us, so the Devil and his followers intend to be in us in His place; that is the sin which will never be forgiven <note>The "unpardonable sin" or blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, which Paracelsus here equates with being spiritually occupied by the devil's order.</note>. Thus there is a power among the devils, just as there is in Heaven and on Earth: one devil over all, who has command over the others. Furthermore, there is also the other order, which truly belongs to wisdom: that there is a special council and assembly of devils [to decide] with what cunning they may swindle and deceive mankind. This wisdom is **infernal**; and just as in Heaven wisdom exists alone in Christ for eternal life, so in Hell it exists for damnation and death. Thus you now know the two orders of Hell and

# The Fourth Book / The Twelfth Chapter.

### How and by what path the devils learn to recognize man, and what they are not able to recognize.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'E' at the beginning of the text, featuring ornate floral scrollwork within a square border.</image-desc>

It is also necessary that we know how the devils have a distinction in their understanding regarding mankind. Namely, they recognize man, but not through devilish cunning; rather, they only know what they see, just as one person who sees another steal or kill knows well what the other has done. Because the devils are spread throughout all the world like the rays of the sun—for there is but one sun in the whole world—they therefore know what someone does in the **West** <note>original: *Occident*</note>, and they are able to announce it in an instant in the **East** <note>original: *Orient*</note>. 

However, man should not regard this more highly than as something quite possible for them; it is nothing other than that they see it from the person and are able to act further. Thus, they see not only the actions of man, but also all the growth of the Earth—whatever is there that can be seen. Now, I have previously shown in a chapter how nothing is hidden in mountains or in stones that they do not know, because a spirit is transparent. Yet it is not the same with man, such that the devil might see into him in that same way. He well knows man’s natural essence, his <term>Anatomy</term> <note>In this context, the physical structure and internal workings of the body.</note>, his <term>Imagination</term> <note>original: *Fantasey*; the faculty of the mind that produces images and desires.</note>, and his entire natural light. But whatever concerns the Heavenly aspect therein, he does not know that. 

Rather, we should know that the devil learns of this by observing the thoughts behind outward works and signs. He also dares to use "arts" to try and experience man’s light of Eternal Wisdom, attempting to learn about man through <term>Magic</term> <note>original: *Magiam*</note>, <term>Necromancy</term> <note>original: *Nectromantiam*; specifically the conjuring of spirits or the dead.</note>, <term>Geomancy</term> <note>original: *Geomantiam*; divination by means of Earth or patterns in the soil.</note>, and <term>Astrology</term> <note>original: *Astrologiam*</note>—just as we on Earth learn the Light of Nature through such arts. In this way, he wishes to learn about us as well, but it cannot be. It is as impossible as if we were to attempt, through <term>Scrying</term> <note>original: *Berillisticam*; the use of crystals or beryl stones to see hidden things.</note>, to see God in Heaven—where He is, when, or what He does—or to search for Paradise. All of that is impossible. 

Just as little is it possible for the devils to see a man’s Christian heart, which is closed off toward God. Yet they are so plagued [by curiosity] that they cannot desist from such arts, and they falsely imagine they understand the whole man, which is not true. It is indeed true that if someone intends to steal, the devil knows it, or other such things that are against God. For noting such matters is commanded to his <note>The devil's</note> **Chancery** <note>original: *Cankley*; Paracelsus uses the metaphor of a government office or court record-room to describe how sins are logged.</note>; he is the accuser,

and he knows what every person lacks; but what is within a Christian heart, which is sealed by God, that he is not able to learn. Therefore, know that they themselves have <term>Astronomy</term> <note>original: *Astronomiam*</note> among them; namely, as soon as a child is born, they calculate its <term>Nativity</term> <note>original: *Nativitet*; an astrological birth chart or horoscope.</note>, and they are very skilled and certain in this. Because of this, they track that same child according to what is found in the <term>Judgments</term> <note>original: *Judicijs*; the astrological prognostications or "sentences" derived from a birth chart.</note>. For instance, the temptation of **Christ** <note>original: *Christi*</note>, where **Satan** tempted him, arose from the "stone" <note>In Paracelsian thought, "stone" often refers to a foundational celestial or spiritual influence, or perhaps the star of Bethlehem itself.</note> that was found above **Bethlehem**, and from the history that took place there. That same stone was not natural; therefore, he [the devil] was not able to judge it, yet he followed **Christ** because of it, and it was a cause for **Herod** wanting to kill the child. For he [the devil] expected nothing good from **Christ**, nor did he have a fixed opinion of him until he had tested him, as he also does in possessed people, etc. He acts in this same way with other children; thus, where there are children who are born with turbulence—such as **Alexander the Great** <note>original: *Magnus Alexander*</note>—it is a sign of a strange birth in which the devil rejoices, because much discord will happen through that same child, in which he finds joy.

But now, consider further that the beginning of this book, describing <term>Infernal Astronomy</term>, has sufficiently established the beginning and has been sufficiently presented in general. But from now on, to deal with it <term>specifically</term> <note>original: *particulariter*</note>, it is necessary to complete the same, so that the infernal power may be well understood and recognized.

### The Thirteenth Chapter.

### Concerning the <term>Members</term> <note>original: *Membris*; the individual parts or branches of a system.</note> of Infernal Astronomy.

Now, so that I may present to you the end of this first beginning, the more easily to understand the infernal wisdom and power, know that there are nine <term>Faculties</term> <note>original: *Facultatet/Facultates*; branches of study or specialized powers.</note> among them. Namely, they divide themselves into nine parts, and thus through nine such faculties, they are those who understand how to use everything that is against mankind. Therefore, so that it may be more easily understood, I have set it into a figure [diagram] for the sake of brevity as a <term>Memorial</term> <note>A mnemonic aid or summary reference.</note>. Although such a figure stands clearly in the first book, where it is then also most easily understood; however, how the figure is in itself, is thus:
